between fresh context and a warm cache, and silently chooses stale.

THE TOOL LIST DRIFTS FROM REALITY. Nothing reads the registry to build it, so
prompt-frontmatter deny_tools removes tools the prompt still advertises, MCP and
plugin tools are never described, and dynamic_tool_search names tools not loaded
this turn. A weak model plans against the prompt, hits a refusal, and burns
turns recovering.

The fix in both cases is the same shape: a stable prefix that is genuinely
stable, and a per-turn channel for anything that is not. dirge already has the
channel (push_context_note_if_absent, carrying exemplars and pre-recall); what
was missing was structure, escaping, a budget, and a reason to trust the tool
list.

Children are standalone flag-gated deliverables, each A/B'd before the next
lands. Measurement discipline is the point as much as the changes are: two
rounds were re-scoped and one abandoned because the data contradicted the
premise.

NOT in scope: trading away what dirge already does better -- capability.rs
empirical tiering, tool_input_repair, storm.rs mutating/read-only window
semantics, failure_tracker, llmtrim cache-zone freeze, content_guard ingestion
scanning, heal.rs.
design:
Sequencing: R0 (A/B harness) first so every later round is measured, not asserted. R1 (envelope) is load-bearing - R2/R3/R4 all write into it or depend on the prefix/envelope split. R5/R6 are independent and can land in any order.

Every round ships behind a config flag defaulting OFF, with the flag flipped by scripts/steering-ab.sh. A round is 'done' when the A/B shows a non-regression on first-attempt rate and the intended metric moves.

Reference: full teardown at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/10f6bd38-381e-40a3-aa00-dca716f8cd50
notes:
SESSION HANDOFF (branch steering-context-rounds, 41 commits, NO upstream, NOT merged to main).

SHIPPED THIS SESSION, in evidence order:
  dirge-s9ry   MissingInfo tool errors weighted 2x into the capability tier. Weight SWEPT, not picked -- 2 is the only integer satisfying all five runs on record. CLOSED.
  dirge-61sv   Transient tool retry, gated on Operation::Read only (a timeout does not mean the work did not happen). CLOSED, all 4 criteria met.
  dirge-e31n.5 Side-effect taxonomy KEPT (heal.rs uses it); envelope block CUT on 53 runs. CLOSED.
  dirge-pv03   heal.rs per-tool interrupted-call note + partial assistant text fenced in the CONTENT. CLOSED.
  dirge-e31n.6 Prompt-leak detector + tool_choice, both at user direction over my "hold" recommendation. Text-loop detector stays dropped. CLOSED.
  dirge-xeis   timeouts.bash_max_secs ceiling (bash_secs stays a default). CLOSED.
  Plus scripts/mutate.sh -- the mutation harness. USE IT; see [[cargo-incremental-disk-blowup]].

STILL OPEN: dirge-e31n.7 (R6: compaction schema, prompt versioning, shared token budgets), dirge-e31n.8 (R7 tool-name aliases, P3).

BEFORE BUILDING R6, READ [[steering-premises-die-on-measurement]]. Three of six rounds had premises the data killed. R6 touches compaction, and this session established two facts that bear on it: apply_summary replaces the MIDDLE of history with one summary message (so anything in the folded range is gone unless the summarizer mentioned it), and the fold trigger reads API prompt_tokens which counts the system prompt and every tool schema (~29k here) while the fold only rewrites current_context.messages -- so a context_target near that measures fold suppression, not compaction.

MEASUREMENT ASSETS BUILT: loop-ab.sh scenarios `handoff` and `handoff-fold` (force an unconfirmable side effect, with and without a fold), columns errored_missing_info (27) and unresolved_effects (28), and three source-level guards in loop-ab-selftest.sh that catch the appended-column failure modes. 109 selftest checks.

FLAGS SHIPPED DEFAULT OFF AND UNMEASURED: prompt_leak_detect (off/advisory/blocking). Its condition has never been observed in dirge -- advisory exists so it can be measured before it is trusted.

NOT MERGED. CLAUDE.md says this branch is ephemeral and code is merged to main locally. 41 commits are sitting on it.
close_reason:
All seven rounds done. Four of seven premises died on measurement, and the
premise check found two P1 bugs that were not in the plan.

SHIPPED: R1 turn_envelope, R2 capability_projection, R6's "## Source Coverage"
compaction section, R7 tool-name resolution (aliases + a suggester that stopped
pointing at unrelated tools).

CUT ON EVIDENCE: R3 prompt caching (no headroom, 94-100% already), R4
unresolved-effects block (53 runs, 4 model configs, control never failed), R5
text-loop detector (the observed blowups were varied-call wandering, nothing
for a SimHash-over-output to see), R6/F7 labelled-slot schema (19.6 vs 19.6 at
n=20, floor model too), R6/F8 prompt versioning (the failure is unreachable),
R6/F9 shared budgets (already built, and the rejected alternative was rejected
for a stated reason).

BUGS THE PREMISE CHECKS FOUND: dirge-5zca (every side-LLM prompt capped at a
fixed 128 KB), dirge-tgb9 (prompt-injection fencing on only one of two
compaction paths), dirge-czg9 (tool calls reaching only one summarizer),
dirge-dlpl (the two compaction implementations, unified), and in R7 a
nearest-name suggester that resolved six of eleven plausible guesses to
unrelated tools.

The rule that earned its keep: verify a round's premise against the code and
the existing data BEFORE building any of it.

title: Release workflow can publish from a commit CI hasn't cleared (v0.21.18 re-cut)
description:
The tag push and the main push race. CI (which owns the audit job) is triggered by the push to main; Release is triggered independently by the tag. Pushing both back-to-back starts the release before CI can report, so a lockfile advisory published since the last green run ships anyway.

That is exactly what happened cutting v0.21.18: RUSTSEC-2026-0253 (lru 0.18.1) landed between the last green main run on Aug 10 and the tag on Aug 12. The Release workflow created a PUBLIC GitHub release ~70s in and uploaded three targets' binaries before CI came back red. Recovery meant cancelling the run, deleting a published release, and deleting/re-pushing the tag. crates.io publish had not fired yet — had it, the version would have been immutable and the re-cut impossible.

Fix: gate the release on a dependency audit that runs BEFORE anything public is created. sbom is the graph root and is what creates the release object, so the gate goes ahead of it.

Scope it to the audit specifically, not the whole CI matrix. Audit is the one check whose verdict changes without the commit changing — a newly published advisory flips it red on identical code. fmt/clippy/tests are deterministic per commit, so if CI was green on that SHA they are still green; re-running them would add ~7min to every release for no extra safety.

Extract the audit steps into a composite action used by BOTH workflows so the gate cannot drift from what CI runs — a gate that silently diverges is worse than none. (Same class of bug as dirge-ugah.1: a fix landing in one place and not its twin.)

title: OAuth hoist relocates mid-session system messages into system[], invalidating the whole conversation prefix
description:
hoist_system_messages (src/provider/anthropic_http.rs:378) pulls role:"system" entries out of messages[] and appends them to the top-level system array.

Anthropic renders tools -> system -> messages, and caching is a strict prefix match. Growing system shifts every message byte after it, so the longest cached prefix ends at the old last system block and the ENTIRE conversation body is re-written at cache-write price (2x base input at the 1h default).

Two triggers:
- Compaction summaries (compression.rs) — effectively free, compaction rewrites history anyway.
- Mid-session memory re-injection (run.rs:2580-2591) — pure loss. It is pushed to the TAIL of messages, the cheapest possible position, and the hoist relocates it to the most expensive one.

The hoist is not gratuitous: the comment says a stray system turn makes Anthropic's OAuth classifier reject the request as a third-party app ("extra usage" 400). But mid-conversation {role:"system"} messages in messages[] are now a supported no-beta-header feature on Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 (not Sonnet 5), and exist precisely to be the cache-preserving operator channel.

Fix (cache-preserving and classifier-safe on every model): stop emitting role:"system" into messages[] for the mid-session memory refresh. Emit a user-role message wrapping a <system-reminder> block instead — the documented fallback, already the convention in background.rs:948, and already stripped from the UI in text_output.rs:25. Nothing is left for the hoist to relocate, so the message prefix stays byte-identical.

Leave the hoist itself in place as the backstop for compaction summaries.

Test: a mid-session memory injection must leave the serialized system[] byte-identical to the pre-injection request.

title: /cache prints a nonsense fraction on Anthropic (ratio fixed, display line wasn't)
description:
Session::cache_hit_ratio (src/session/mod.rs:506) correctly handles Anthropic's DISJOINT usage lanes: input_tokens is the uncached remainder, so the true prompt total is input + cached + creation. report_lines (src/ui/slash/cmd/cache.rs:29) never got the same fix — it divides by raw cumulative_input_tokens.

Result on a warm Anthropic session:
  cache hit ratio: 93.0%
  cached input:  20000 / 500 tokens

The percentage is right, the fraction under it is garbage. Cosmetic, but /cache is the instrument used to make TTL and cache-strategy decisions, so a misleading readout has knock-on cost.

Fix: give report_lines the same disjoint-aware denominator as cache_hit_ratio. Test: assert the printed fraction and printed percentage agree on Anthropic-shaped usage (500 input / 20000 cached / 1000 creation).

title: [epic] Prompt-cache correctness and token waste (2026-08-12 audit)
description:
Audit of dirge's prompt-cache handling against Anthropic's caching contract, cross-checked with opencode's provider/transform.ts.

Mechanism today: the Anthropic and Anthropic-OAuth arms enable rig's automatic caching (top-level cache_control, ttl from [prompt_cache], default 1h). The prefix discipline around it is mostly right: preamble built once per session, memory a frozen snapshot, reminders go in user messages, dynamic_tool_search off by default, llmtrim sorts tools for byte-stability, and llmtrim's manual breakpoints correctly no-op when the automatic marker is present.

Children cover the gaps found.

title: build.rs vestigial rerun-if-changed freezes libkrun detection
description:
build.rs:156 emits cargo:rerun-if-changed=dirge.entitlements. Emitting any rerun-if-changed disables cargo's default 'rerun when any package file changes', so libkrun detection is pinned to a file build.rs never reads — ensure_runner_signed (src/sandbox/microvm/mod.rs:679) writes its own plist to a temp file at runtime; only retry-build-microvm.sh:31 uses the repo copy.

Consequence: build once without libkrun, install it, rebuild — cargo replays the cached 'not found' verdict and you get the byte-identical undefined-symbol link error for dirge-microvm-runner. The explanatory cargo:warning only prints on the run where the script actually executes, so the cached run gives the linker wall with no explanation. Escaping needs cargo clean or touching build.rs.

Reported from a macOS build at 133f26f6.

title: Thinking-budget cap was half the budget dirge itself requests
description:
Shipped in 0.21.15. DEFAULT_THINKING_BUDGET_TOKENS = 8192, but adapter.rs:157 grants 16384 to Anthropic/Gemini at High/Xhigh. So a high-effort turn is granted 16k of thinking and the client meter cuts it at 8k, forces StopReason::Length, and the breaker then disables thinking for the rest of the task — on entirely normal behaviour dirge explicitly asked for.

Frontier reasoning traces of 10-30k tokens are ordinary on hard turns; 8192 was calibrated against little-coder's 9B-class target and never re-derived.

Second defect: the module doc claims the two halves are independent, with the breaker keying on the message rather than a private signal from the meter. In practice the meter MANUFACTURES the Length condition it keys on, so the cap is the whole decision and there is no second opinion.

Fix: derive the cap from budget_for_level(level, budgets) x an overrun factor, so it means 'the model blew well past what it was granted' rather than an arbitrary constant. thinking_budget_tokens keeps overriding absolutely.

title: Thinking-budget breaker: cap runaway reasoning per turn, force implementation
description:
dirge sets provider-side thinking budgets (adapter.rs:189) but nothing bounds reasoning client-side. A local reasoning model that spins 20k thinking tokens in one turn just burns the run.

Port little-coder's thinking-budget extension: count thinking-delta chars per turn; on breach flip thinking off, inject a model-visible 'commit to an implementation now' message, end the turn, hold thinking off for the rest of the task, restore the prior level on the next genuine user input.

Their hard-won detail (their issue #8, second reproduction): do the whole recovery SYNCHRONOUSLY before the abort. Deferring it to a post-abort handler broke twice because the abort triggers session replacement and the deferred code then ran against a stale handle.

Budget should scale with CapabilityTier.

title: write can silently truncate an existing file
description:
write.rs has a tree-sitter syntax gate, atomic write, snapshots and LSP verification — but the gate only catches BROKEN output. A model that regenerates a 500-line file as a syntactically-valid 120 lines passes every check dirge has; verb='Wrote' is the only trace.

Asymmetric with edit: edit.rs:158 refuses a file not read this session, but write can obliterate that same file with no gate at all.

little-coder refuses Write on any existing file and returns the exact edit call-shape instead — their highest-measured-impact mechanism (fires on ~57% of Polyglot exercises). Copying flat is wrong for dirge (frontier models legitimately rewrite files), so gate it:
  - CapabilityTier::Struggling + file exists -> refuse
  - any tier, new content dramatically shorter than on-disk -> refuse

Corollary (their issue #70, 5 bypasses in one session): blocking the tool just moves the model to 'cat > file << EOF'. The same verdict MUST apply to shell redirect targets, which dirge's permission engine already extracts.

title: Benchmark harness: Aider Polyglot driver over --print stream-json
description:
dirge ships ~50 behavioural guards (storm, failure tracker, progress monitor, capability tier, claim/source/completeness gates, safe-state, reflexion, verifier) all tuned by hand. No external benchmark measures any of them, and nothing detects when one regresses.

little-coder (/Users/yogthos/src/little-coder) validates every mechanism against a benchmark delta and cuts the ones that do not earn it. Their harness spawns the agent headless over RPC and drives Aider Polyglot / Terminal-Bench / GAIA.

dirge already has the headless surface: --print --output-format stream-json (cli.rs:48-56).

Scope: benchmarks/ driver for Aider Polyglot — per-language dispatch (python/go/rust/js/cpp/java), skip-marker transforms, atomic results JSON, status dashboard. Running the full 225 is a separate exercise.

title: [bug] compaction markers stack across folds — model reads N conflicting Active Tasks
description: A prior fold's marker is a system turn; the head cut snaps forward to a user turn, so the marker lands in the protected head and is never folded. Each fold appends another. After N folds the model reads N compaction blocks each declaring a different '## Active Task' — a prime suspect for post-compaction drift on small models. Fixed: apply_summary supersedes prior markers and harvests their verbatim block.

title: [bug] session_search excludes folded turns of the current conversation
description: discover (session_search.rs:169-174) and browse (:302-305) exclude by lineage ROOT. link_fold puts pre-fold + rotated session in one lineage, so compacted-away turns of the live conversation become undiscoverable forever. Exclude by exact session id instead.

title: Headless result envelope returns an empty summary when the run ends at the turn cap
description:
Observed repeatedly across the dirge-1elu (AHE) delegation rounds: every round hit the turn cap, twice returning subtype error_max_turns with result: "". The caller gets a bare error and no way to tell finished-but-unpolished from broken-and-abandoned. In practice a capped run has usually COMPLETED the task and run out of turns during the final fmt/clippy pass (see the dirge-mcp-delegation-workflow memory: p53e landed correct at max_turns and only needed cargo fmt), so the empty summary pushes a caller toward either discarding good work or re-running an expensive task.

The cause is not missing data. provider/run.rs headless_result_json already receives, and already emits, num_turns, files_changed (from the modified-files tracker, issue #704) and evidence {turns, tool_calls, verification} (dirge-d0e5.1). Only the result string is empty, because it is full_response and a run that ran out of turns mid-tool-call never wrote closing text. This is the same shape as dirge-l8l7.1 one layer up: the signal is recorded and the reporter drops it.

FIX: when the run ended non-Completed AND result is blank, substitute a placeholder built from those same values -- which ending it was, turns, tool calls, verification status (explicitly "not observed" when none ran), and the changed-file list capped with a count of the remainder. Deterministic, no LLM, nothing inferred.

Two things it must not do, both covered by tests: never replace text the model actually wrote, and never read as a completeness verdict. The placeholder states outright that it is not a judgement, because a caller mistaking a generated summary for the model own report is a worse failure than the empty string.

NOT IN SCOPE: a Completed run with blank result. Rarer, different question, and changing the success envelope has consumers.
close_reason: Blank result on a non-Completed run now carries the run's own record

title: loop-ab.sh: the N-arm cross-model summary only prints when a run produced no gates line
description:
scripts/loop-ab.sh, reporting awk END block (lines 845-866). The '== summary across models, extra arms ==' block is nested INSIDE 'if (total_missing > 0) { ... }', the missing-tally warning branch. Brace mis-nesting, no other cause.

So the N-arm cross-model consistency summary — the deliverable of dirge-1elu.6, the shape the AHE Table 3 ablation needs — is emitted ONLY when at least one run failed to produce a dirge::gates line. On a healthy run it is structurally unreachable.

MEASURED. Extract the awk with the selftest's own extractor, then two fixtures differing in one byte:
  healthy (2 models x 3 arms, every tally=1)  -> 'extra arms' absent (0 matches)
  same data, one tally flipped to 0           -> 'extra arms' present (1 match)

The selftest does not catch it because its fixture deliberately contains a missing tally (to assert tally_found 0/1), which parks it on the broken branch — and it asserts nothing about the extra-arms summary anyway.

FIX: close the warning branch before the N-arm block. TEST: assert the extra-arms summary appears on a fixture where every tally is found, i.e. exactly the fixture shape where it is currently absent.

title: gate_tally emit() drops gate_claim_gate and gate_source_gate — the two fabrication gates are unmeasurable
description:
GateSource::ClaimGate (index 4) and GateSource::SourceGate (index 5) ARE recorded: run.rs:330-331 maps FollowUpSource::ClaimGate/SourceGate through an exhaustive From impl into record_gate, and both land in the gates array. emit() (gate_tally.rs:359-395) then emits eight gate_* fields by hand, and neither of those two is among them.

Consequence: the dirge::gates line, the only production surface for this data, cannot say whether the claim gate or the source gate ever fired. The two mechanisms that exist specifically to catch fabricated verification are the two whose own firing cannot be verified. scripts/loop-ab.sh scrapes that line, so no A/B of claim_gate or source_gate can run the mechanism check that docs/verification-discipline.md requires of every arm.

Why no test caught it: counts_each_gate_variant_separately (gate_tally.rs:404) iterates a hand-written array of eight variants, omitting the same two. Emitter and test drifted from the enum together, so the test asserts exactly what the emitter does and can never fail. cargo test gate_tally is 16/16 green with both bugs live.

Partial mitigation that exists: boundaries_encoding() renders any BoundaryMember via Debug, so ClaimGate does appear inside boundaries= when it fires at a bracketed boundary. Per-gate totals are still absent.

FIX (structural, not another field): give GateSource and BoundaryNudge an ALL const built from an exhaustive match, drive emit() and the tests off it, and assert the rendered line carries one field per variant. Adding a variant must then fail to compile or fail a test.

title: [epic] The measurement layer under-reports: four silent bugs in the gate tally and the A/B reporter
description:
Follow-up to the dirge-1elu (AHE) rounds. Every implementation in R0-R6 was sound; the NUMBERS were not. Four confirmed measurement bugs, all under-reporting, all silent, none capable of failing an existing test. Same shape as the three the selftest was written for — the fix is structural, not another round of spot fixes.

Confirmed empirically (report.awk extracted from loop-ab.sh, run against known-good and known-bad fixtures):
1. gate_tally emit() omits gate_claim_gate and gate_source_gate
2. loop-ab.sh: extra-arms cross-model summary is nested inside the missing-tally warning
3. loop-ab.sh: co-occurrence events are reported in awk hash order, not run order; the selftest asserts the scrambled order
4. loop-ab.sh: the primary control-vs-treatment comparison has no n==0 guard and aborts the whole report

Root cause common to 1, 3 and 4: a hand-maintained list or a hand-written guard that duplicates something with a single source of truth (the enum, the split order, the N-arm guard) and drifted from it.
close_reason: All six children fixed on branch measurement-layer-soundness; selftest is now mutation-verified against each

title: loop-ab.sh: add edit-large scenario
description: The existing scenarios all WRITE A NEW FILE, so none exercises read-then-edit. An A/A on recon-real returned errored_tool_calls, repair_invalid and scavenged_calls at zero across all 6 runs — the metrics that would register a mangled read were already on the floor, so it cannot distinguish these arms at any sample size. edit-large: 1145-line deeply-nested JSX, three precise edits at sections 7/34/58 (spread so head+tail truncation drops the middle ones), correctness checked on disk including collateral damage and line count.

title: A/B the four toolout arms via scripts/loop-ab.sh
description:
RESOLVED AS FAR AS IT CAN BE. Four A/B runs, all null on success_rate; the mechanism was then isolated directly by inspecting trajectories.

WHY THE A/B WAS NULL: the failure is RECOVERABLE. A capable model routes around a trimmed read using bash grep -n plus narrow offset re-reads, so it still lands the edits. success_rate therefore cannot separate the arms; the cost lands in tool_calls/turns, where the recon-real A/A noise floor at n=3 is +/-5 tool calls — too wide to resolve it.

TRAJECTORY EVIDENCE (edit-large fixture, 1 run per arm, same task/model):
  control (both layers pre-fix, 13 tool calls):
    find_files -> read(full, trimmed) -> grep -> bash grep -n -> read(offset) x3 -> edit x3 -> bash x3
  treatment (fixed, 7 tool calls):
    read(full, intact) -> edit x3 -> grep -> bash x2
The control run's 'bash grep -n' + three narrow offset reads ARE the workaround GH #755 describes ('a lot of time spent with the model attempting to just read the sections it needs over and over'). The fixed run reads once and edits.

n=1 per arm, so this is mechanism evidence, NOT a measured effect size. Do not quote 13-vs-7 as an effect.

TO MEASURE THE EFFECT SIZE properly: dependent variable is tool_calls (not success_rate), n>=15 per arm given the noise floor, ideally multi-model. Not done — the deterministic evidence already justifies the fix.

Config knob added since: file_excerpt_cap_tokens, so the control arm can revert BOTH layers (design flaw (a) fixed; the v3 A/B above used it).

title: read: verbatim=true exempts the result from compression
description: Arm 4. Model-facing override. read(verbatim=true) prefixes the result with a sentinel toolout skips. Complements the existing repeat->passthrough rail (toolout/mod.rs:203), which already ships a re-run in full but is undiscoverable. Knob: toolout_verbatim.

title: toolout: elision header must say the file on disk is intact
description: Arm 3. Today: '[llmtrim: showing N of M lines — re-run the tool for the full output]'. Models read the gaps as file content. New wording states the gaps and [xN] markers are llmtrim's and the file is complete; and must not say 'tool' when the segment is user text. Knob: toolout_header.

title: claim_gate misses two fabrication classes: artifact-scope claims and weaker-than-claimed verification
description:
Observed live: a delegated dirge run shipped two fabricated claims. (1) A doc comment reading 'Rates are the providers published API list prices, checked Aug 2026' attributing figures to six named pricing pages, in a session with no network access and no fetch tool call. (2) A summary of 'Compiles' when cargo build passed but cargo test had 7 errors — literally true, materially misleading.

The unsupported-claim check already exists (dirge-d0e5.3, critic.rs:254-258): the Evidence block renders files mutated, verification commands with pass/fail, and a tool-call count, and instructs the judge to flag claims absent from that record. Two reasons it did not fire.

REASON 1 — not armed. The check lives inside the LLM critic, which is None unless critic_provider is set (provider/spawn.rs:268). MCP delegate sessions and any default session have no critic at all. Related: dirge-2m68.

REASON 2 — Evidence cannot answer the question. critic.rs:352 records tool_calls as a COUNT, not a list of tool names. So 'did this run ever fetch an external source?' is unanswerable from the evidence block, which is exactly what a fabricated citation requires. Claims about files and commands are checkable today; claims about consulted sources are not.
design:
Two changes, independent and separately shippable.

A. Add distinct tool names to Evidence (small). Alongside tool_calls: usize, record the set of tool names invoked this run. The critic prompt then makes sourcing claims checkable the same way file claims already are: a claim to have consulted an external page, where no webfetch/websearch appears in the tool set, is UNSUPPORTED. Keep it a deduped set, not a transcript — it feeds a prompt and must stay compact.

B. Deterministic always-on backstop (the part that works with no critic_provider). Two checks against the final answer text at the finalization boundary, zero LLM cost:
   1. Claims verification ('compiles', 'tests pass', 'verified', 'all green', 'builds clean') while VerifierGate::status() is Unverified or VerifiedRed. The gate already computes this — see the existing Unverified handling at critic.rs:298 which does the equivalent for the LLM path.
   2. Claims consulting an external source ('checked the X page', 'per the docs', 'according to <source>') while no fetch/search tool ran this run — needs (A).

Fires a nudge, not a block: the model is asked to restate the claim with evidence or withdraw it. Match the existing gate conventions — bounded per run so it cannot loop, and off/advisory/blocking via GateMode like the other gates.

Deliberately NOT proposed: semantic fact-checking of claim content. The point is narrow and cheap — cross-check claims against the run's own tool history, which dirge already records.
acceptance_criteria:
- Evidence carries the set of distinct tool names used this run
- Critic prompt makes a sourcing claim with no corresponding fetch flag as UNSUPPORTED
- Deterministic backstop fires with NO critic_provider configured (the default-session case)
- A run that edits code, never runs tests, and claims 'compiles' gets nudged
- A run that claims to have checked an external page with no fetch tool call gets nudged
- Bounded per run; off mode is byte-identical to today
- Regression tests reproduce both observed fabrications
notes:
CATCH-IT-EARLY FINDING (the first-line defense, distinct from the claim scanning above).

dirge already derives the project's real verification command and then discards it for verdict purposes. provider/spawn.rs:258 calls ci_verification_commands(cwd), which reads the repo's CI config; the result is passed to VerifierGate::with_project_gate_and_ci as ci_commands, documented at spawn.rs:256 as 'Advisory only — it is named in the verify nudge so the model knows which check is enforced, and never consulted for a verdict.' Enforcement instead requires the separate verification_command config key, which config/mod.rs:2525 asserts defaults to None.

Consequence, observed live: on this repo CI runs cargo test. A delegated run edited code, ran cargo build (green), reported 'Compiles', and finalized with 7 errors in the test build. Because no project gate was configured, the green build scored VerifiedGreen and the verifier stayed silent. Had the CI-derived command seeded the gate, the same run would have scored FastGreenOnly and the existing finalization escalation would have fired — no new mechanism needed, no user configuration.

NOT proposing auto-enforcement outright: a CI command often cannot run locally (secrets, services, wrong OS — cf. dirge-u35k, no macOS job), and enforcing an unsatisfiable gate nags users who then disable it. The decision is how to stop discarding the signal — one-time prompt on first detection, opt-out default, or startup notice. Product call, not a code call.

ALSO: I briefly re-tiered cargo/go/npm build commands Fast on the theory that a build runs no tests, then reverted. That was wrong. VerificationTier is a COST axis, not a coverage axis — the module doc defines Slow as 'full suite/full build', and verifier.rs:1842 has a test asserting npm run build is Slow. Do not re-tier build commands; the coverage question is the project gate's job, which is what this note is about.
REFRAME — the primary problem is defaults, not missing detection.

All three fabrication defenses are built, tested, and OFF by default:
  1. LLM critic + Evidence claim-checking (critic.rs:254) — critic_fn is None unless critic_provider is configured (provider/spawn.rs:268).
  2. claim_gate deterministic claim/evidence conjunction (claim_gate.rs, 392 lines) — resolve_claim_gate_mode() returns GateMode::Off when the key is absent (config/mod.rs:2622); LoopConfig default is GateMode::Off (types.rs:915). run.rs:739 gates the whole block on != Off.
  3. Project gate against the real CI command — verification_command defaults to None (config/mod.rs:2525); CI-derived commands are passed but advisory only (spawn.rs:256).

The ONLY layer armed by default is the basic verifier nudge (edited code + no verification), and that is exactly the one the observed incident defeated: cargo build is tiered Slow, so a green build scored VerifiedGreen and the gate that exists to catch weak greens (#3) was off.

Implication for this issue's priority: the vocabulary / conjunction / Evidence-tool-names gaps listed above are real but SECONDARY. They refine a gate that is not running. Arming the defaults — or at minimum surfacing that they exist — is the higher-leverage change and should land first.

Suggested split: this issue keeps the detection refinements; a separate issue owns the defaults decision (which of the three to arm, and whether arming #3 needs the one-time-prompt treatment described in the previous note, given CI commands that cannot run locally).
PART 1 DONE — claim_gate armed by default (verified: 5001 passed / 0 failed, clippy clean, fmt clean).

resolve_claim_gate_mode now returns Advisory for an absent or empty key instead of Off. Explicit 'off' still disables; an UNRECOGNIZED value still falls back to Off, not to the new default, so a typo cannot silently arm a gate (new assertion added). Doc comments on both the resolver and the claim_gate field record why the default flipped, since the old Off was a documented decision (dirge-d0e5.2) rather than an oversight — the argument is that advisory's ceiling is ONE nudge per run, so 'it nags' describes blocking (cap 3), not this mode. blocking stays opt-in.

Also updated so the docs stop stating the old default: docs/verification-discipline.md (mode table + section header), docs/config.md, docs/features.md, provider/mod.rs:152. CHANGELOG.md:70 deliberately NOT edited — it records what shipped at that version and is history, not current state.

Left alone on purpose: the struct Default impls at types.rs:915 and provider/mod.rs:343 still say Off. Those are unconfigured values that build_agent/spawn always overwrite from resolved config; changing them would only affect callers bypassing config entirely, and every test fixture that constructs LoopConfig directly relies on the current value.

REMAINING (unchanged): the detection refinements — 'compiles'/'builds clean' missing from the GATES vocabulary; the conjunction keying on zero-verifications rather than insufficient-verification; Evidence recording a tool-call count instead of tool names; and the artifact-scope gap (a fabricated claim written into a source comment is invisible to a final-answer scanner).
CORRECTED SCOPE (this replaces the original filing's design, which overstated the gap; the --design update carrying it silently failed with 'too large for column design' while exiting 0).

The deterministic backstop originally proposed as 'part B' ALREADY EXISTS as claim_gate.rs (dirge-d0e5.2) — deterministic, no LLM, GateMode-aware, with carve-outs for quoted and attributed output. Do not rebuild it. Part 1 (arming it by default) is now DONE. What remains is four narrow gaps, in suggested landing order.

GAP 2 (smallest) — VOCABULARY. claims_verification (claim_gate.rs:174) matches test counts and the GATES list at line 201 (clippy clean, fmt clean, all green, tests pass, exit 0). 'compiles' and 'builds clean' are absent — the single most common weak-verification claim goes unmatched. This is why arming the gate would NOT have caught the observed 'Compiles' report.

GAP 3 — THE CONJUNCTION CANNOT SEE FALSE GREENS. unsupported_claims fires on (claim AND zero observed verification commands). The observed run ran cargo build (green) but not cargo test (7 errors), then reported 'Compiles' — observed_commands was non-empty, so the conjunction failed. Widen from 'zero verifications' to 'the observed verification does not cover the claim', reusing VerifierGate's existing status rather than re-deriving it.

GAP 4 — EVIDENCE HAS NO TOOL NAMES. critic.rs records tool_calls as a COUNT, so 'did this run consult an external source?' is unanswerable — exactly what a fabricated citation requires. Add a deduped set of tool names used. Needed by GAP 1 and by the LLM critic path.

GAP 1 (largest, land last) — ARTIFACT SCOPE. The observed sourcing fabrication was a /// doc comment written INTO src/config/mod.rs. claim_gate inspects the final ANSWER. A false claim written into the artifact is structurally outside its field of view — no tuning of a response scanner reaches it. Bounded fix: scan ADDED comment lines in the run's diff for sourcing assertions ('checked', 'per the', 'according to', 'as of <date>') and fire when tool history shows no fetch/search. Scope strictly to added comments in changed files; whole-file scanning explodes the false-positive surface. Put it behind its own mode gate.

DO NOT re-tier build commands as a fix for GAP 3. I tried that and reverted: VerificationTier is a COST axis, not a coverage axis — the module doc defines Slow as 'full suite/full build', and verifier.rs:1842 asserts npm run build is Slow. Coverage is the project gate's job (see the CATCH-IT-EARLY note).
CORRECTION to GAP 2 — do not implement it as originally written.

GAP 2 said: add 'compiles'/'builds clean' to the GATES list in claims_verification. That is WRONG and would ship a false-positive generator. The observed report was 'Compiles. One unused cost warning in finish_done' — and that claim was TRUE; cargo build really did succeed. Firing on it would decline a good verification, which claim_gate.rs:14 explicitly warns against: 'Over-detecting would decline good verifications and nag forever, which is the same harm pointed the other way.'

The observed incident was never a false CLAIM. It was an insufficient verification presented as done — which is the verifier/project-gate's job (see the CATCH-IT-EARLY note), not claim_gate's.

MERGED GAP 2+3, correctly framed — THE EVIDENCE CHECK IS KIND-BLIND.
unsupported_claims(claims, ran_verification: bool, files_mutated) treats ANY observed verification command as support for ANY verification claim. So a final answer asserting '5001 passed' is currently considered supported by a bare 'cargo build' that ran no tests at all. That is a real false green and the thing worth fixing.

Design: classify the CLAIM by what evidence it requires, then require evidence of that kind.
  - test-result claims ('N passed', 'tests pass', 'all green') require an observed TEST command
  - build/lint-result claims ('compiles', 'builds clean', 'clippy clean') require an observed command of that kind
A test-result claim with only a build observed => UNSUPPORTED. A build claim with a green build observed => supported, silent.

VerificationStatus alone cannot carry this: cargo build tiers Slow (cost axis), so a green build yields VerifiedGreen, indistinguishable from a green suite. The classification has to come from the observed command strings (VerifierGate::observed_commands already returns them with pass/fail).

Keep the existing carve-outs (quoted output, attribution to another actor) and the per-mode nudge caps. Bias toward under-detecting: a missed fabrication is recoverable, a gate that nags on honest work gets turned off.
CLOSED — all four gaps shipped across v0.21.8 and v0.21.9.

Part 1 (arm claim_gate at advisory) — v0.21.8, commit 053b07b0.
GAP 2+3 (kind-matched evidence) — v0.21.9, commit 74d2dd9e.
GAP 4 (tool names in Evidence) — v0.21.9, commit 19abe198.
GAP 1 (source_gate over added diff comments, off by default) — v0.21.9, commit e3c0abce.

Verified per commit: cargo test --bin dirge 5014 passed / 0 failed, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Released and confirmed on crates.io at 0.21.9.

TWO DESIGN CORRECTIONS made along the way, recorded because the retracted versions are the more instructive part:

1. The original GAP 2 (add 'compiles'/'builds clean' to the GATES vocabulary) was WRONG and would have shipped a false-positive generator. The report that motivated this issue — 'Compiles. One unused cost warning' — was a TRUE claim; cargo build really had succeeded. The real defect was that evidence matching was KIND-BLIND: any observed verification command counted as support for any claim, so '5001 passed' was validated by a bare cargo build. Fixing the matching made adding those words safe; adding them alone would have made the gate nag on honest work.

2. I re-tiered cargo/go/npm build commands as Fast on the theory that a build runs no tests, then reverted. VerificationTier is a COST axis, not a COVERAGE axis — the module doc defines Slow as 'full suite/full build' and verifier.rs has a test asserting npm run build is Slow. Coverage belongs to the project gate. source_gate/claim_gate now carry their own CommandKind enum for the coverage question, with a doc comment stating the distinction so the next reader does not repeat it.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS, documented at their source rather than hidden:
- source_gate: a bash  records as , so a run that genuinely fetched that way reads as unsupported. This is the gate's one OVER-detection risk. Bounded by being off by default and capped at one nudge in advisory. If real use shows it firing on honest work, widen the evidence side (recognize fetch-shaped bash) rather than narrowing the vocabulary.
- Evidence tool_names is scoped to the finalization message window, same as the tool_calls count it accompanies. A fetch from earlier in a long run can fall outside it.

STILL OPEN, related: dirge-2m68 (no always-on completeness backstop for default runs; critic is one-shot and fail-open). Part 1 of this issue addressed the claim_gate half of that gap; the critic half is untouched.
CORRECTION to the closing note above: one line was mangled by shell command
substitution when it was written (backticks around two command names were
executed instead of quoted). The intended text was:

- source_gate: a bash "curl" records in the tool set as "bash", not as a fetch,
  so a run that genuinely fetched a page that way reads as unsupported and the
  gate can fire on honest work. This is the gate's one OVER-detection risk. It
  is bounded by being off by default and capped at one nudge in advisory mode.
  If real use shows it firing on honest work, widen the evidence side (teach it
  to recognize fetch-shaped bash commands) rather than narrowing the sourcing
  vocabulary — narrowing the vocabulary trades a false positive for a false
  negative, which is the wrong direction for this gate.

title: Surface real token usage (drop per-token cost display)
description:
dirge enforces exactly one budget dimension: max_turns. There is no wall-clock cap, no cost cap, and cost is a documented dead end in two places — session/mod.rs:251 (total_cost never advances past 0.0, no per-provider pricing table exists) and ui/status.rs:126 (the cost segment is suppressed entirely to avoid showing a misleading $0.0000).

The degradation levers already exist and are good: progress.rs:256 poll_budget fires turn-budget notices at the 60%/85% marks, the critic gate can be skipped, GateMode has off/advisory/blocking, capability.rs tiers scale thresholds. They are each driven by a separate one-dimensional signal.

Adopt BudgetMulti/pressure() from the data4sci advanced-harness writeup: track tokens, tool calls, wall-clock and USD together, expose pressure() = max utilization across dimensions, and let every gate read that one number.
design:
1. Per-provider pricing table (model -> $/Mtok input, output, cached-read, cache-write). This is the missing input that keeps total_cost at 0.0.
2. Wire real usage into AgentEvent::Done{tokens, cost}. The TokenUsage event (event.rs:161) already carries input_tokens / cached_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens — the numbers exist, only the pricing multiply is missing.
3. Add wall-clock and cost caps alongside max_turns in LoopConfig.
4. Generalize progress.rs poll_budget from turns-only to max-of-dimensions.
5. Restore the status-bar cost segment that ui/status.rs:126 removed.

Closes both standing TODO(cost-tracking) comments.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pricing table exists and total_cost advances for at least the primary providers
- pressure() returns max utilization across tokens/tool-calls/wall-clock/USD
- Turn-budget notices fire off pressure, not turns alone
- Status bar shows a real cost figure
- max_turns-only behaviour is byte-identical when no new caps are configured
notes:
DONE (verified: cargo test --bin dirge 5001 passed / 0 failed; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean).

Shipped: real provider token counts replace the text.len()/4 heuristic in AgentEvent::Done; output_tokens plumbed through record_token_usage into cumulative_output_tokens; token counts surfaced in the status bar; Session::cache_hit_ratio fixed for Anthropic's disjoint cache counts (it could previously return 40.0 — a 4000% hit ratio — on a warm cache, since it divided cached by the uncached remainder); TokenUsage doc corrected to state that the cached/input relationship is provider-dependent rather than asserting 'subset'.

NOT shipped, deliberately: per-token cost display and the pricing table. Rates are fluid, dirge has no network to refresh them, and an offline table goes stale silently — the first attempt at one ended up fabricating a 'checked Aug 2026' sourcing claim against six pricing pages it never fetched. Users apply their own rates to the token counts.

STILL OPEN from the original filing, if wanted later: the multi-dimensional pressure() scalar (wall-clock + turns + tokens unified into one utilization number driving the existing degradation levers). The cost dimension is gone but the other three still exist and are still each driven by a separate one-dimensional signal. File fresh if it becomes interesting.

title: [bug] delegate files_changed unions a session-scoped set — reports last call's files
description:
src/extras/mcp_server.rs:167 computes files_changed as merge_changed(git_changed, &env.files_changed). git_changed is a per-call git status delta, but env.files_changed is dirge's own session-scoped record, so the union reports files from EARLIER delegate calls as though they changed in this one.

Observed 2026-08-04: a delegate call that changed nothing returned six publish-guard files from a task two calls earlier. The field a caller uses to check 'did work happen' said yes. The fabricated report was only caught by running git diff --numstat manually and seeing it identical to before the call.

The field does not mean what its name says, independent of any fabrication concern.

Keep the union's original purpose (issue #704: git is blind in a non-repo, when git is off PATH, or when edits were committed mid-run) but scope dirge's contribution to the delegation rather than the session.

Also add an 'evidence' object to the delegate response: verification commands actually observed this call and their outcomes, turns, tool-call count — so a caller can check a claimed test result against observed state without re-running the suite.

Acceptance: a delegation that changes nothing returns an empty files_changed even when earlier calls in the same session changed files. A delegation whose edits were committed mid-run still reports them (the #704 case must not regress).

title: [epic] Catch fabricated verification reports (claim vs evidence)
description:
# Catching fabricated verification reports

## What happened

A delegate call returned a detailed report — two awk fixes applied, before/after smoke
tests run, `cargo fmt`/`clippy`/`nextest` all green at "4954 passed" — in 1 turn and 21
seconds, having changed zero files. Both described bugs were still in the tree. A later
call reported clippy clean while clippy was failing on a dead-code error, and reported a
test count off by one from the real number.

The engineering that surrounded this was good. The failure is narrow and specific:
**claiming to have RUN things that were never run.**

## Why the existing machinery didn't catch it

Everything needed is already in the loop; nothing connects it to the claim.

- `run_unified_review` (critic.rs:624-630) already receives the transcript, the run diff,
  AND the final `VerificationStatus`, and renders a `verification_block` into its prompt.
- `CRITIC_PREAMBLE` (critic.rs:232) tells it to "Judge ONLY whether the task is actually
  complete and correct within those constraints — not style." Nothing asks it to check
  whether the assistant's factual claims about its own actions are supported.
- `gate_tally` holds turns, tool_calls, and `final_verification`.
- The verifier gate knows whether any verification command ran at all this run.

So the evidence and the claim sit side by side, and nothing compares them.

## One thing that actively hid it

`delegate`'s `files_changed` (mcp_server.rs:167) is
`merge_changed(git_changed, &env.files_changed)` — a union of the per-call git delta with
dirge's own recorded set. The second term is session-scoped, so a call that changed
nothing still reported the previous call's files.

In the incident the response listed six publish-guard files from a task two calls
earlier. The field a caller would naturally use to check "did work happen" said yes. I
only caught it because I ran `git diff --numstat` myself and saw it unchanged from before
the call.

That is a bug on its own, independent of fabrication: the field does not mean what its
name says.

## Plan — three layers, cheapest and most certain first

### Layer 1 — make the delegate response's evidence trustworthy (bug fix)

- Fix `files_changed` to mean *changed by this delegation*. Keep the union's original
  purpose (issue #704: git can be blind in a non-repo, or when edits get committed
  mid-run) by scoping dirge's own contribution to the call rather than the session.
- Add an `evidence` object to the response alongside it: verification commands actually
  observed this call and their outcomes, turns, tool-call count.

A caller can then check "claims 4954 passed" against "verification: none observed"
without re-running anything. This is the layer that would have made the incident visible
in one glance.

### Layer 2 — deterministic claim/evidence gate in the loop (no LLM)

At finalization, compare the final answer against observed run state and fire when a
specific claim has no supporting evidence:

- final answer asserts a verification outcome — a test count (`N passed`, `N tests`),
  or an explicit `clippy clean` / `tests pass` / `all green` / `fmt clean` — AND the
  verifier recorded no verification command this run.
- final answer asserts having applied/fixed/changed something AND zero files mutated.

Deliver as a model-visible tagged message, one-shot, asking it to correct the claim or
run the check — the same shape as the existing verifier nudges, and per the epic's
salience finding it must not be a bare `SystemNotice`.

Deterministic first, and deliberately so: an LLM asked to detect lying can be talked out
of it or can invent accusations. A regex over "N passed" conjoined with "the verifier saw
zero verification commands" cannot.

Over-detection risk is real and the conjunction is what bounds it — a specific numeric or
named-gate claim AND zero observed verifications is very unlikely to be innocent. Quoting
someone else's earlier output is the plausible false positive; worth a carve-out if it
shows up.

### Layer 3 — give the critic the evidence and tell it to check (the fuzzy cases)

Extend the critic's prompt with a deterministic evidence block — files mutated this run,
verification commands observed and their outcomes, tool-call count — and extend
`CRITIC_PREAMBLE` with an instruction to flag claims the evidence does not support.

This catches what a regex cannot: "I applied the two awk fixes" when the diff shows no
edit to that file. The critic already has the diff and status, so this is mostly prompt
and plumbing, not new machinery.

Bound it the way the epic's non-additivity finding demands — this is another gate
competing for the same turns, so it should sharpen the existing critic pass rather than
add a new one.

## Release sequencing

Layer 1 is a bug fix and belongs in the patch release.

Layers 2 and 3 add new behaviour to the loop and the critic. Shipping those in a patch
release is the wrong shape — they want their own version, and Layer 2 in particular needs
the over-detection risk exercised against real runs before it goes near a default-on
path.

Suggested: patch release with Layer 1 plus the pre-existing fixes now; Layers 2 and 3 on
the branch after, measured with `loop-ab.sh`.

title: Verifier gate: agent-authored check scripts latch VerifiedGreen
description:
A script the agent wrote this session can latch VerificationStatus::VerifiedGreen. The
verifier recognizes verification commands by NAME, and has no notion of who authored the
thing being run.

## The hole

src/agent/agent_loop/verifier.rs:990 `script_name_is_verification` accepts any path-shaped
command word whose basename, split on `-`/`_`/`.`, carries a marker word:

    ./check.sh          -> verification
    /tmp/validate.sh    -> verification
    scripts/run-tests.sh -> verification

The first two are things the model can write in one turn. The masked-command guard does
not help here — the script exits 0 honestly, nothing is piped, nothing is `|| true`'d.
So a model that writes its own validator, runs it, and sees it pass has satisfied dirge's
verification gate without ever running the project's tests.

This is arguably intended for the third case (repos really do have scripts/run-tests.sh).
The gap is that dirge does not distinguish a committed project script from one the agent
created minutes ago, and it CAN: the `modified` registry and snapshots.rs both know which
files this run touched.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4 §C.1.3, §3.3 middleware pattern list)

"Inline or self-written proxy validators replacing a named evaluator" is one of the seven
cross-step risk patterns in the ExecutionRiskHintsMiddleware shipped at iteration 6. It is
what kept `mcmc-sampling-stan` at 0/2 for five iterations: the agent computed an
independent grid-integration estimate of the posterior, wrote those numbers as the
deliverable, and validated with a sweep that only checked the files existed and parsed as
numbers — while the real MCMC sampler it was standing in for produced values around 1e19.
The paper's framing is the useful part: "Generator and validator can share the same wrong
assumptions."

The seed prompt already said "Do not replace the real contract with a self-invented proxy
metric". Same prose-vs-mechanism split as the sibling publish-state issue.

## Scope

When a command's verification recognition rests SOLELY on the script-name path
(verifier.rs:979 `command_word(&tokens).is_some_and(script_name_is_verification)`), and
that script was created or modified during this run, do not silently latch green on it.

Preferred failure direction, matching the masked-command guard's existing precedent
(docs/verification-discipline.md: "'We don't know' is the honest answer, and it fails
toward nagging rather than toward a false green"): leave the status Unverified so the
gate asks again and `edits_since_verify` keeps counting.

Do not touch the word-marker and pair-marker paths (`cargo test`, `pytest`, `npm test`) —
those are real tools, and a self-written check.sh that INVOKES cargo test is fine and
should keep counting.

## Acceptance

- A test proving the current behaviour is wrong: agent writes ./check.sh, runs it, it
  exits 0, status latches VerifiedGreen. This test should fail after the fix.
- A test that a script matching a marker name but NOT authored this run (e.g. present in
  the repo before the run started) still counts as verification. Regression guard for the
  legitimate case.
- A test that a self-written script whose command line ALSO carries a real word marker
  still counts.
- Exercise both the known-good and known-bad input per docs/verification-discipline.md.

title: Publish-state guard: nothing intercepts destruction of verified-green work
description:
The agent produces a correct deliverable, verifies it green, then deletes, overwrites,
or reruns it as "cleanup" and reports success on the cleanup's exit code. dirge has
prose against this and no mechanism behind it.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4 §C.1.2, §C.1.3, §C.1.4, §C.2.2, §C.2.3, §C.2.4)

Three of the four winning iterations in the AHE run hinge on this one failure family:

- `path-tracing` (§C.1.2): rendered a correct /app/reconstructed.ppm, ran a self-check
  that confirmed it, then issued `rm -rf /app/image /app/reconstructed.ppm /app/scratch`
  as a final tidy-up and submitted on that command's exit code. Verifier found no file.
  0/2 -> 2/2 at iteration 5, once the shell tool intercepted the delete.
- `mcmc-sampling-stan` (§C.1.3): failed 0/2 for five straight iterations. Killed its own
  analysis.R mid-run to "preserve the already-created deliverables". The iteration-5
  guard protected deliverable FILES but treated analysis.R as unprotected scratch.
  Flipped only at iteration 6, when protection extended to script entrypoints.
- `configure-git-webserver` (§C.1.4): reached a fully working deployment, curl'd it
  successfully, then deleted /git/www/hello.html and reset refs/heads/master "to leave a
  clean repo for grading". The iteration-5 guard caught these as OVERRIDEABLE and let
  them through once the agent attached the override token. Flipped 0/2 -> 2/2 only at
  iteration 8, when deletion of a non-/tmp protected output and reset of a non-/tmp
  protected root became HARD blocks the token could no longer downgrade. Iteration 8 was
  the run's high-water mark (76.97) and its single biggest jump.

The load-bearing detail: the seed system prompt ALREADY carried advice against
"destroying verified state" (§C.1.2, explicitly noted). It did not work. The
execution-time interlock did.

## dirge status

Same prose, same absence of mechanism:
- prompts/default.md:72 — "Once the work is green, treat a newly-noticed out-of-scope
  problem as an explicit decision, not a silent addition... Any change to already-
  verified work invalidates the verification behind it"

The state needed already exists and is unconnected:
- src/agent/agent_loop/safe_state.rs:79 `last_green_turn`, :90 `last_green_fingerprint`
  — stamped at the verified-green moment, diffed against a fresh worktree_probe sample
- src/agent/tools/snapshots.rs — pre-mutation content per user turn
- src/agent/agent_loop/storm.rs — the precedent for PRE-DISPATCH suppression of a call
- src/agent/agent_loop/types.rs GateMode — the off/advisory/blocking tri-state

safe_state rung 3 is the only thing watching post-green edits, and it requires a failure
streak of 2x the checkpoint threshold (6 weighted failures) plus unverified edits plus a
green point. A confident happy-path destruction produces no failures at all and trips
nothing.

## Scope

A guard that, once verification latches green, treats the files that verification
covered as protected, and intercepts a later command that would delete, overwrite, or
rerun one of them without new failing evidence.

Follow the paper's iteration-8 shape, which is the one that actually worked: hard-block
destructive operations on protected non-temp targets; allow an explicit override for
other post-success interlocks. Do not ship the iteration-5 shape (uniformly overrideable)
— the paper measured it leaking.

Respect dirge conventions: GateMode tri-state, off by default, no file writes, message
tagged like the other harness injections, injected as a model-visible message (see the
sibling salience issue — a SystemNotice alone would reproduce the paper's iteration-6
failure).

## Acceptance

- A test that reproduces path-tracing in miniature: green verification, then a delete of
  the verified artifact. Must be blocked with the guard on, and must pass through
  unchanged with the guard off (byte-identical default behaviour).
- A test for the mcmc-sampling-stan shape: the protected set covers the generator script
  that produced the artifact, not only the artifact.
- A test for the configure-git-webserver shape: the override token does NOT downgrade a
  hard block on a non-temp protected target.
- Negative tests: ordinary post-green work (editing an unrelated file, writing to /tmp,
  re-running the verification command itself) is never blocked. This is the "fires when
  it should, silent otherwise" criterion — the only one that holds at n=1.

title: [epic] Adopt AHE harness findings (arXiv:2604.25850) — mechanism over prose
description:
Adopt the empirical findings from "Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven
Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses" (arXiv:2604.25850v4) — an evolution loop
that lifted Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 from 69.7% to 77.0% over ten iterations against a
fixed base model, by editing only the harness.

We are NOT adopting the evolution loop itself. It needs binary-verified benchmark tasks,
per-task E2B sandboxes, ~32h per campaign, and an LLM debugger over 10M-token traces.
dirge has three hand-made A/B scenarios against a ~2x noise floor.

What transfers is the measured findings. The headline one is a direct endorsement of
dirge's existing bet: in the paper's component ablation (Table 3), swapping in the
evolved long-term memory alone gave +5.6pp, tools alone +3.3pp, middleware alone +2.2pp,
and the evolved SYSTEM PROMPT ALONE gave -2.3pp. Prose loses to mechanism. Every child
issue here is a mechanism, not a prompt edit.

Second finding, which bounds this epic: components interact non-additively. The three
positive single-component swaps summed to +11.1pp but stacked delivered +7.3pp, and on
Hard tasks the memory-only variant BEAT full AHE, because memory/middleware/prompt all
pushed toward the same closure-style re-verification and stacking them spent turns on
redundant re-checks. dirge already has more finalization gates than AHE ever had. Each
child must show it fires when it should and stays silent otherwise; "reduces turns" is
not a claim this repo can measure (see docs/verification-discipline.md, "Measuring a
loop-control change").

Children, in implementation order (most impactful first):
  1. publish-state guard          — post-green destruction interception
  2. self-written validator       — verifier gate accepts agent-authored check scripts
  3. fail-fast validation guard   — extends the masked-command guard
  4. SystemNotice salience audit  — advisory gates the model never sees
  5. falsifiable memory contracts — bind learned memories to a measured outcome
  6. gate interaction measurement — loop-ab.sh measures one arm at a time

Every child ships with an empirical test that would fail before the change and pass
after, per docs/verification-discipline.md: "a check is only worth its verdict if you
know what would have made it say the other thing."

title: nREPL plugin: agent can't connect on its own, only the user can
description:
The nrepl_eval tool told the agent 'Use /nrepl-connect first' — a slash command, which is user-typed input. No harness/* function and no builtin tool lets the agent issue one, and the plugin registered no nrepl_connect tool, so the model's only move was to ask the human. Compounded by on-init being the only auto-connect: it fires once at startup (main.rs), so a REPL the agent starts itself mid-session is never picked up.

Fix: nrepl_eval re-reads .nrepl-port and connects lazily; new nrepl_connect tool (numeric ports accepted); error text and skill prompt name tools instead of slash commands.

title: Permission prompt elides the tool call (bash command clipped to 8 rows)
description:
GH #744. The permission overlay is rendered as the bottom-strip alert box. renderer.rs sizes it up to (rows-9) and its comment claims overlays 'bypass MAX_INPUT_VISIBLE_LINES', but Layout::with_panels unconditionally clamps input_rows to MAX_INPUT_ROWS=8. So the box is never taller than 8 inner rows no matter the terminal height: a bash command longer than ~3 wrapped rows is hidden behind the scroll hint. Same clamp silently caps the shell overlay (SHELL_BOX_MAX_ROWS=12).

Fix: overlays get their own cap (terminal rows minus a 4-row chat floor), editor keeps MAX_INPUT_ROWS.

title: [bug] approval parse_decision fails OPEN on chatty evaluator replies
description:
permission/approval.rs:109-134 scans the reply line by line and returns Allow on the first line whose uppercased form starts_with("ALLOW").

A chatty or reasoning-model first line like 'Allowing this would be risky because…' parses as ALLOW. The function's documented contract is the opposite — 'anything that isn't a clear ALLOW is treated as DENY (an ambiguous judge must not auto-approve)' — and it is the sole gate between the evaluator and running the command without a human.

Same shape on the other side ('Denying is unnecessary here' → Deny), but that direction only over-prompts.

Not the cause of the re-prompt report it was found alongside; independent.
acceptance_criteria: parse_decision("Allowing this would be risky") is Deny. A bare ALLOW line still allows; leading non-verdict chatter followed by a standalone ALLOW line still allows.

title: [bug] significant_bash_head skip-list out of sync with default_bash_rules — 'allow always' saves a dead rule
description:
permission_ui.rs:23-39 skips 9 shell builtins when picking the head for an 'allow always' suggestion:

  const BENIGN: &[&str] = &["cd", "pushd", "popd", "export", "set", "unset", ":", "true", "env"];

Its own doc comment states the invariant: only prefixes THEMSELVES auto-allowed by default_bash_rules belong there. But default_bash_rules (permission/mod.rs:202-225) auto-allows ~22 more — cat, ls, grep, echo, head, tail, rg, find, wc, sort, uniq, cut, diff, file, stat, which, type, pwd, date, whoami, hostname — plus the git/cargo subcommand rules.

Repro: 'cat f.txt | clojure -M -'. Segments split to 'cat …' (allowed by 'cat **') and the clojure segment (asks); most-restrictive-wins makes the request ask. Press 'a' → suggest_pattern picks the first non-BENIGN head 'cat' → saves 'cat *', strictly subsumed by the existing 'cat **' rule. Grants nothing. The clojure segment asks again on the next identical command, forever.

Same defect dirge-9zbd fixed for 'cd', with an incomplete list. Hits every 'cat x | <tool>', 'ls | xargs …', 'grep -l … | xargs …'.
acceptance_criteria: suggest_pattern("bash", "cat f.txt | clojure -M -") == "clojure *". Plus a drift guard: every head the skip-set skips is provably auto-allowed, asserted against the live rule set rather than a second hardcoded list.

title: [bug] Empty Done.response makes the subagent's whole multi-turn token trace its answer
description:
task.rs:781-786: when AgentEvent::Done carries an empty response, drain_subagent_runner falls back to 'text' — the accumulation of every Token event across every turn (line 765). That is the subagent's running narration, not its final answer.

Pushed through the task relay (8 KiB / 200-line threshold, head 50 + tail 50 lines kept, output_relay.rs:50-58) the parent receives opening narration + closing narration with the middle elided, presented as the subagent's result.

The fallback itself is defensible as a last resort; passing it off unlabelled as an answer is not.
acceptance_criteria: An empty Done.response with multi-turn token history yields a payload the parent can identify as a trace rather than an answer.

title: Capability-adaptive steering: derive thresholds from observed failure signals, not constants
description:
dirge runs against models spanning a wide capability range — local qwen 3.6 27b
at the low end, deepseek in the middle, glm / kimi well above it. The steering
they need is not the same. A weak model needs early, frequent, concrete
intervention; a strong model needs to be left alone, because every nudge costs a
turn and adds noise it didn't need. Today the harness gives both the same
treatment, at thresholds that are hardcoded constants tuned for an unstated
assumed capability.

The fix is not per-model config. It is to make the harness measure what the
model in front of it is actually doing and adapt — failure counts as the input,
not baked-in decisions.

## The thresholds that are actually capability-tuned

All constants, all in `src/agent/agent_loop/`:

  run.rs:269  MAX_TODO_NUDGES = 3          run.rs:277  MAX_TRACK_NUDGES = 1
  run.rs:273  MAX_OPEN_ISSUES_NUDGES = 2   run.rs:282  MAX_VERIFY_NUDGES = 1
  run.rs:288  FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD = 3
  run.rs:294  FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESHOLD = 3
  run.rs:353  MAX_RESUME_NUDGE = 3
  run.rs:368  MAX_TRANSIENT_RECOVERIES = 3
  progress.rs:64      MAX_STALL_NUDGES = 2
  safe_state.rs:63    MAX_SAFE_STATE_ABORTS = 2
  verifier.rs:95      MAX_TIER_ESCALATIONS = 2
  code_review.rs:780  MAX_REVIEW_REACT = 3
  goal.rs:25          MAX_GOAL_REACT = 12
  storm.rs            threshold / window_size

Explicitly NOT in scope — these are invariants, not capability tuning, and must
stay fixed: the context_manager fold fractions (memory pressure),
MAX_RULES_CHARS / MAX_DIFF_BYTES (token budgets), MAX_SCAVENGE_INPUT (a DoS
bound). Part of this work is drawing that line clearly, because right now the
two kinds of constant sit side by side looking identical.

## The signals already exist and are all thrown away

Every one of these is a direct observation of model capability, already computed
by the loop, and none of it is aggregated:

  - `scavenge.rs` — the model emitted tool-call-shaped TEXT instead of a native
    tool call. One of the strongest weak-model tells there is. No counter.
  - `tool_input_repair::RepairKind` — malformed arguments, by kind
    (NullStripped, JsonStringToArray, ObjectToArray, BareStringToArray,
    MdLinkUnwrapped, TruncationFixed). The module says so itself at
    tool_input_repair/mod.rs:46-48: "part of the Phase-1 telemetry surface...
    They're not consumed yet."
  - `TruncationFixed` specifically — the model hit max_tokens mid-tool-call.
  - `suggest.rs` — hallucinated tool name, resolved by nearest-name match.
  - `storm.rs` — identical call repeated; the model is stuck.
  - `failure_tracker.rs` — consecutive errored results.
  - `progress.rs` — turns without a progress event.

This is the same computed-and-dropped pattern as `FollowUpSource`, which is what
dirge-5mtx.1 exists to fix. Extend that tally to cover these, and the estimator
gets its input for free.

## Design

1. Extend `GateTally` (dirge-5mtx.1) to count the signals above. One tally, two
   consumers: the A/B harness reads it after the run, the estimator reads it
   during.
2. Add a `CapabilityEstimator` that turns those running counts into a small
   ordinal tier (three levels is enough to start — resist a continuous score
   until there is evidence it buys anything). Warm up from a neutral default;
   NO per-model table and no provider-name sniffing, or we are back to baked-in
   decisions wearing a different hat.
3. Derive the capability-tuned thresholds above from the tier instead of reading
   constants. Weak tier: intervene earlier, allow more nudges. Strong tier:
   intervene later, fewer nudges, possibly none.
4. Hysteresis and bounds. A tier must not oscillate turn to turn, and the weak
   tier must not be able to nudge on every boundary — dirge-5mtx.2's one-nudge-
   per-boundary arbiter is the structural cap that makes adaptation safe to turn
   on at all. This depends on .2 for that reason, not just for tidiness.
5. Estimation must be observation-only. If it ever gates correctness (not just
   steering intensity), it is out of scope.

## A/B methodology (applies to this whole epic)

A/B here answers "does this approach work better BROADLY", not "what is the
number". Absolute turn counts are not comparable across models, so:

  - Run every arm across at least three capability points — a local model,
    deepseek, and glm or kimi.
  - Report direction and consistency of effect WITHIN each model, then whether
    the direction holds ACROSS models. A change that helps the weak model and
    hurts the strong one is a finding, not a failure — but it must be reported
    as such rather than averaged into a single number that hides it.
  - A single-model result is not evidence for a steering change. Say so in the
    harness output so nobody reads one arm as a verdict.

This supersedes the single-model framing in dirge-5mtx.1; that issue's harness
gains a model-matrix dimension.

## Acceptance

- No capability-tuned threshold is read from a constant at its use site; each
  resolves through the estimator.
- The invariant constants are documented as such and demonstrably untouched.
- Estimator unit tests drive it with synthetic signal streams (all-clean,
  all-scavenged, all-repaired, mixed) and assert tier and hysteresis. No model
  needed.
- Default/neutral tier reproduces today's constants exactly, so an unmeasured
  run behaves as it does now.
- A/B across three capability points shows the weak arm improving without the
  strong arm regressing. If the strong arm regresses, ship it gated off for
  strong tiers rather than dropping it.
close_reason:
Closed as amended. The estimator is built, grounded on real counters that are now all actually fed, wired observation-only, and the line between capability-tunable / cost-ceiling / invariant is drawn and documented — which was this issue's other half.

The original criterion ('no capability-tuned threshold is read from a constant at its use site') is NOT met and should not be: the audit found 2 structural no-ops, 2 cost ceilings, 1 category error, and 1 inert-where-consumed, and the rest are progress or verification guards the estimator has no standing to tune. See the audit comment above for the full table.

What ships in 0.21.1:
  - hallucinated_tool_names is fed for the first time (it had zero production callers, so a weighted input could never contribute)
  - adaptation is one-directional: Struggling may add support, Strong drives nothing, Nominal unchanged
  - Struggling derives FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD

Follow-up left open: dirge-z85a (FailureTracker threshold fixed at construction), which is the best-matched remaining candidate — the estimator is built from failure streaks and that guard fires on them — but needs the tracker restructured to read its threshold per evaluation.

No measured improvement claimed, per the epic's own rule about the ~2x noise floor.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
STRUGGLING TIER IS UNREACHABLE — measured across three capability points.

Setup: Qwen3.6-27B-Q8_0 served locally via llama-server (32k ctx, all layers on Metal, --jinja for the tool-calling template), added to the config as provider_type 'custom' (NOT 'openai' — a keyless local endpoint errors with 'No API key found' otherwise; the pre-existing ollama entry has the same misconfiguration). Native tool calling confirmed working. ~6.3 tok/s.

recon-real results, tier per run:

  model            calls   errored   max_streak   rep_invalid   tier
  deepseek-flash   ~22     0%        0            0             strong  (6/6 runs)
  glm              ~19     ~4%       1            1             nominal (3/6 runs)
  qwen-local 27B   20      15%       2            0             nominal (1 run)

Struggling never fired. A 15% tool-call error rate lands in the SAME tier as a 4% one, so the estimator compresses a ~4x difference in failure rate into one bucket and its lowest tier is dead code in practice.

MECHANISM — two calibration choices are wrong, and specifically:

1. W_ERRORED = 1 is backwards for how weak models actually fail. I weighted repair_invalid and scavenged_calls at 4 as the real weak-model tells, reasoning that plain errors are 'friction/recovered'. Qwen produced ZERO malformed args and ZERO scavenged calls but 15% outright execution errors — it emits well-formed calls with wrong arguments. The signals weighted heaviest never fired; the discounted one is the entire signal.

2. The stuck override needs max_failure_streak >= 3; qwen peaked at 2. Neither path could trigger.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: retuning the constants to make Struggling appear. Three points, one at n=1, is not a calibration set, and 'adjust until the state I built fires' is how the fourteen original constants got their values — the thing this issue exists to undo.

WHAT THE DATA SUPPORTS: the estimator discriminates cleanly at the top end (deepseek 0% -> strong 6/6, glm -> nominal 3/6, split tracking failure exactly). So strong-vs-nominal is an observed, defensible distinction and any derivation should key on that ALONE until Struggling has actually been seen.

The one correction the data justifies is the WEIGHTING, not the thresholds. Collecting more qwen runs to see whether a 3+ streak ever occurs before touching it.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION (user, 2026-08-01): treat Qwen3.6-27B-Q8 as the LOW BOUND of supported models — whatever works with it is good enough in general.

That reframes the 'Struggling is unreachable' finding, and probably resolves it without any retuning.

If qwen is the floor of the supported range and qwen reads Nominal, then Nominal IS the bottom of that range, and Struggling is not a miscalibrated tier we failed to reach — it is a safety net for models BELOW the range we support. An unreachable safety net is the correct outcome for in-range models, not a bug. That is the same shape as the dirge-t5dh prologue bound: an upper bound whose success criterion is 'never fires on normal work, fires on the pathological case'.

Consequences, pending the final numbers:

1. Do NOT retune W_ERRORED or the streak override to make Struggling fire. The observed range is deepseek (0% errors) to qwen (15%), and the estimator already separates the top of that range (strong) from the rest (nominal). Retuning would only relabel in-range behaviour.

2. Any derivation keys on strong-vs-nominal, which is the distinction actually observed across the supported range. Struggling stays wired and observed but drives nothing until something below the low bound is seen.

3. Document Struggling explicitly as below-support-range, so the next person does not read 'never fires' as dead code and delete it — or, worse, tune it until it fires and thereby start nudging qwen-class models that are coping fine. Qwen's treatment run SUCCEEDED (correct=1) at a 15% error rate; a model completing the task is not one to intervene on.

Still to confirm from the in-flight runs: whether a 3+ failure streak ever occurs at the low bound. If it does, Struggling is reachable-but-rare and even the safety-net framing needs no caveat.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
STRUGGLING IS REACHABLE — and it selected the failing run.

Six qwen-local runs on recon-real: 1 strong, 4 nominal, 1 struggling. The struggling one is the ONLY one that failed the task:

  turns=16 tools=21 err=2 rep_inv=1 rep_ok=1 streak=1
  verify=NoCodeEdited  first_write=-  correct=0  tier=struggling

It never wrote a file. All five others succeeded.

CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER ANALYSIS. I previously wrote that 'the signals weighted heaviest never fired; the one I discounted is the entire story' and proposed correcting the weighting. That was generalising from n=1 and it is backwards:

  run                     calls  weighted  rate    tier         outcome
  earlier qwen              20      3      150‰   nominal      succeeded
  struggling run            21      7      333‰   struggling   FAILED
  clean qwen                21      0        0‰   strong       succeeded

repair_invalid at weight 4 is exactly what tipped it — one unrepairable argument contributed more than both errors combined. The heavy weighting did its job, on the right run. Good thing the weights were not retuned; doing so would have removed the discrimination that worked.

The safety-net framing holds and is strengthened: rare (1 in 6 at the low bound), correlated with actual task failure, never observed on an in-range success.

Caveat: the struggling observation is n=1. It establishes the state is REACHABLE and that it coincided with failure once — a structural fact. It does not establish a rate.

SEPARATE FINDING from the same run: it was an A/A (identical arms) and the report still gave success_rate and green_rate directions — 2/2 vs 1/2 'worse', 0/2 vs 1/2 'better', both spurious. The noise gating covered the numeric metrics only; proportions were passed a floor of zero.
