Fixed in 9d679627 using a 1/n floor (one run flipping is the smallest movement the sample can express), verified against these exact rows.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
PARTIALLY DONE. The estimator is built, grounded on real counters, wired observation-only, and now derives ONE threshold (FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD, 9efe2135). Struggling is validated as reachable and correlated with task failure.

Still outstanding against this issue's own acceptance criteria — 'no capability-tuned threshold is read from a constant at its use site':

  run.rs      MAX_TODO_NUDGES, MAX_OPEN_ISSUES_NUDGES, MAX_TRACK_NUDGES,
              MAX_VERIFY_NUDGES, MAX_RESUME_NUDGE, MAX_TRANSIENT_RECOVERIES
  progress.rs MAX_STALL_NUDGES, stall_threshold, prologue_cap
  safe_state  MAX_SAFE_STATE_ABORTS
  verifier    MAX_TIER_ESCALATIONS
  code_review MAX_REVIEW_REACT
  goal        MAX_GOAL_REACT
  storm       threshold / window_size

Note that several are budgets of 1 (MAX_TRACK_NUDGES, MAX_VERIFY_NUDGES, MAX_PROLOGUE_NUDGES), where scale_budget floors at 1 and scale_threshold cannot go below 1 either — so tier scaling is a NO-OP for them and wiring it would be theatre. Worth auditing which of the list can actually move before doing any of them.

The one that landed was chosen because Strong-direction scaling there is unambiguously safe (more latitude for a model with zero observed failures). Each remaining one needs the same argument made individually; they are not a batch.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
Input this issue was waiting on is now landed: dirge-5mtx.5 labelled every finalization-gate budget cost-ceiling vs re-fire-guard, on GateStates itself (src/agent/agent_loop/gate_state.rs). Cost ceilings (code_review_reacts/MAX_REVIEW_REACT, goal_reacts/MAX_GOAL_REACT) bound LLM spend and must not be tier-scaled upward for a Struggling model — that is exactly the case where a weaker model would burn the most. Re-fire guards are the ones a capability estimate could legitimately move.

Still outstanding here, and worth auditing BEFORE any batch work: several of the ~13 remaining thresholds are budgets of 1, and both scale_threshold and scale_budget floor at 1, so tier scaling on them is a literal no-op. Wiring them up would look like progress and change nothing. The audit is 'which of these can actually move under either scale fn', not 'replace the constants'.

The broader constant taxonomy from .5's revision comment also lands here: context_manager fold fractions are memory pressure, MAX_RULES_CHARS / MAX_DIFF_BYTES are token budgets, MAX_SCAVENGE_INPUT is a DoS bound. None of those are capability-tunable, and right now they sit next to the ones that are, looking identical.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
THRESHOLD AUDIT + POLICY CORRECTION. This resolves the 'no threshold read from a constant' criterion by amending it on evidence, the same way .5's was.

## The audit

Computed every constant against both scale functions (base -> struggling/nominal/strong):

  MAX_TODO_NUDGES            3 budget      4 / 3 / 1
  MAX_OPEN_ISSUES_NUDGES     2 budget      3 / 2 / 1
  MAX_TRACK_NUDGES           1 budget      1 / 1 / 1   NO-OP
  MAX_VERIFY_NUDGES          1 budget      1 / 1 / 1   NO-OP
  MAX_RESUME_NUDGE           3 budget      4 / 3 / 1
  MAX_TRANSIENT_RECOVERIES   3 budget      4 / 3 / 1
  MAX_STALL_NUDGES           2 budget      3 / 2 / 1
  MAX_SAFE_STATE_ABORTS      2 budget      3 / 2 / 1
  MAX_TIER_ESCALATIONS       2 budget      3 / 2 / 1
  MAX_REVIEW_REACT           3 budget      4 / 3 / 1
  MAX_GOAL_REACT            12 budget     18 / 12 / 6
  FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD 3 threshold   1 / 3 / 4
  FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESH  3 threshold   1 / 3 / 4

Findings:

1. TWO ARE STRUCTURAL NO-OPS. MAX_TRACK_NUDGES and MAX_VERIFY_NUDGES are budgets of exactly 1, and 1*3/2 truncates back to 1 under the floor. Wiring them would look like adaptation and change nothing. Now pinned by a test so it is a documented property.

2. TWO ARE COST CEILINGS and must not scale up. MAX_REVIEW_REACT and MAX_GOAL_REACT each bound LLM calls; Struggling->4 and ->18 means MORE spend on the run already in trouble. Labelled as such by .5 on GateStates.

3. MAX_TRANSIENT_RECOVERIES is a CATEGORY ERROR. It bounds recovery from transient mid-stream network errors. That is a property of the connection, not the model. A capable model on a flaky link needs the same 3.

4. FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESHOLD CANNOT ADAPT AS WRITTEN. It is consumed once at FailureTracker construction (run.rs:2053), at run start, when the tier is always Nominal by warm-up. Deriving it there is inert. Making it adaptive needs FailureTracker to take a changing threshold -- filed separately rather than bolted on.

## The policy correction — the important part

I removed the FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD derivation and made Strong scale identically to Nominal. Adaptation is now ONE-DIRECTIONAL: the tier may add support, never remove it.

The reasoning is structural, not statistical, so it holds at n=1. CapabilityCounters observes tool-call mechanics ONLY -- errored calls, repaired args, invented names, scavenged text, storms, streaks. Not one field moves based on whether the model verifies its work, checks the right gate, or makes progress. So a Strong reading is evidence about argument hygiene and nothing else, and cannot license relaxing a guard that fires on progress or verification.

The epic's own record is the counter-example, twice over. Both failures worth having a guard for came from models this estimator reads as Strong:
  - dirge-t5dh, the 60-turn reconnaissance thrash: deepseek-flash, 0% tool-call error rate. Flawless mechanics, zero files written.
  - dirge-w2de, the wrong-gate green: same tier.

The original argument ('extra latitude for a model with no observed failures cannot cause a nudge storm') is true and still gets the risk backwards -- it relaxes verification pressure on exactly the class of model that produced the only verification failures on record.

GENERAL RULE now in the module docs: a signal may only tune a guard that fires on the same thing the signal measures.

## Amended acceptance

'No capability-tuned threshold is read from a constant at its use site' was written before the audit and is not achievable or desirable as stated: 2 cannot move, 2 must not move for cost, 1 is a category error, 1 cannot adapt where it is consumed, and the rest are progress/verification guards that the estimator has no standing to tune. What ships instead:
  - Struggling derives FAST_VERIFY_EDIT_THRESHOLD (verify sooner).
  - Nominal and Strong are bit-identical to the pre-estimator constants.
  - The line between capability-tunable, cost ceiling, and invariant is drawn and documented, which was this issue's other half.

Not claiming a measured improvement. Per the epic's own rule, this is a structural argument; the ~2x noise floor makes it unmeasurable at any affordable n.

title: [bug] Verifier latches green on any passing command; no notion of the project's real gate
description:
The verifier latches VerifiedGreen on any recognized build/test command that
passes, with no notion of what the project's ACTUAL gate is. A green run of a
weaker command suppresses the "verify it works" nudge and reports the work as
verified when the real gate would reject it.

## Observed

2026-07-31, delegating dirge-5mtx.1 to dirge on deepseek-flash. The agent wrote
a new module, ran `cargo test --bin dirge gate_tally`, got `7 passed; 0 failed`,
and reported success.

This project's gate is `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with
`RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"` set globally (.github/workflows/ci.yml:14, :55).
Under that gate the same code produced SIX hard errors — every public item in
the new module flagged `dead_code`, because nothing calls it yet.

`cargo test` does not set RUSTFLAGS, so the agent saw them as warnings. It
noticed exactly one of them (`emit` is never used), reasoned explicitly that it
was acceptable, and cited `#![allow(unused_imports)]` in `mod.rs` as precedent —
an attribute that covers the re-export block and has nothing to do with dead
code in a module. So the failure was not carelessness: it verified, got green,
and reasoned its way past the one signal that leaked through.

Severity is real: this lands broken code on a branch with a green self-report,
and the next agent in the chain trusts it.

## Which guard should have caught it, and why it didn't

`verifier.rs` tracks "did a build/test command run, and did it pass". `cargo
test` is a recognized verification command and it passed, so the run latched
`VerifiedGreen` and the finalization nudge stayed silent. The verifier is
working as designed; the design has no concept of a project-specific gate.

The tiered split from dirge-uw2l.2 (Fast vs Slow) already models almost exactly
the distinction needed — "something cheap passed" vs "the real thing passed",
with `FastGreenOnly` already escalating at finalization. It just classifies by
COMMAND SHAPE (is this a typecheck? a full suite?) rather than by what this
repo actually requires to merge.

## Mitigation

Teach the verifier the project's real gate, and treat anything less as the
existing `FastGreenOnly` tier rather than green:

1. Resolve a project gate command, in order of reliability:
   a. explicit config key (`verification_command`) — authoritative when set;
   b. CI workflow files — this repo's gate is plainly readable from
      `.github/workflows/ci.yml`;
   c. nothing found -> behave exactly as today (no regression, no false nag).
2. When a gate IS known, `VerifiedGreen` requires that command to have passed.
   A lesser green maps to `FastGreenOnly`, which already escalates once
   (advisory) or twice (blocking) at finalization. No new message type needed.
3. Surface the resolved gate in the mid-run fast-verify reminder, so the model
   is told WHICH command counts rather than left to pick one.

Deliberately not proposed: running the gate automatically. It can be slow and
have side effects; the point is to stop calling a run verified when it isn't.

## Acceptance

- Test: gate known + only a lesser command passed -> `FastGreenOnly`, not
  `VerifiedGreen`. Fails on today's code.
- Test: gate known + gate command passed -> `VerifiedGreen`.
- Test: no gate resolvable -> behaviour byte-identical to today.
- Test: CI-workflow resolution actually extracts this repo's gate from
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- A/B via dirge-5mtx.1's harness: on a scenario whose fix introduces a
  clippy-only violation, the treatment arm should not finalize as verified.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: PART 1 landed (f8f8b509): config-driven `verification_command`, (program, subcommand) signature matching, downgrade to FastGreenOnly when the gate hasn't passed. Off by default; unchanged when unset. PART 2 — auto-resolving the gate from CI workflow files so it protects a default config without opt-in — is still open, and is what would have made this catch the original incident without anyone configuring anything.

title: [bug] Progress monitor can never fire on a run that never produces: unbounded exploration prologue
description:
The progress monitor cannot fire on a run that never produces anything. Its
stall counter arms only on a progress event, so a run with zero progress events
stays in the "exploration prologue" forever and the guard is structurally
incapable of reporting it.

## Observed

2026-07-31, delegating an implementation task to dirge on deepseek-flash.
60 turns, 8m26s, ZERO files written, no errors, no repeated calls. The agent's
own account when asked: "I was over-reconnoitering instead of writing... one
oversized parallel batch (40+ grep/read calls) mapping run.rs... I just kept
re-reading the same regions through overlapping grep/read/read_minified/sed
calls instead of locking the small design and writing the file", which the issue
text had already fully specified.

Live config at the time: `progress_stall_threshold: 4` (ON), `max_agent_turns:
1000`, `file_touch_threshold: null`, `failure_reflection_threshold: null`.

## Root cause

`ProgressTracker::record_turn`, progress.rs:130-154:

    let progressed = todos closed || new file mutated || verification went green;
    if progressed { inner.armed = true; inner.barren_turns = 0; return None; }
    if !inner.armed { return None; }   // <-- unbounded prologue
    inner.barren_turns += 1;
    ...

`armed` starts false and is set ONLY at line 137, inside the `progressed`
branch. Zero progress events => `armed` never becomes true => line 141 returns
`None` on every boundary for the life of the run.

The arming rule is deliberate and its rationale is sound as far as it goes
(progress.rs:37-41): "A run that opens with twenty reads is exploring, not
stalling, and must not be nudged for it... Without this the monitor would fire
on every research task." The bug is not the rule — it is that the prologue it
creates has NO upper bound. Exploring for 20 turns is fine; exploring for 60 (or,
at this config's cap, 1000) is the exact "busy but not converging" failure the
module was written to catch, and it is the one case it cannot see.

No other guard covers it: storm needs identical repeats (calls varied), the
failure tracker needs errors (all succeeded), safe-state needs a failure streak
(none), and the file-touch tracker — which WOULD have caught 40 reads of one
file — is off by default.

## Mitigation

1. Bound the prologue. After `prologue_cap` boundaries with zero progress events
   of any kind, emit a checkpoint even though the tracker never armed. The
   message must be DISTINCT from the stall message: a stall means "you were
   producing and stopped", this means "you have not produced anything yet".
   Wording should push toward the smallest possible first write rather than more
   analysis. Bound it like `MAX_STALL_NUDGES` so it can't spam.
2. Default `prologue_cap` to a generous multiple of `stall_threshold` (3x is a
   reasonable start) so genuine research is untouched, and let it be configured
   independently.
3. Consider counting TOOL CALLS without progress, not just turn boundaries. The
   observed run did 40+ calls inside ONE turn, so a turn-granular counter scored
   it as a single barren turn. This is the same granularity bug already fixed
   once in the verifier (25d05324: `edits_since_verify` counted tool calls, so a
   batched `apply_patch` with four operations registered as one edit, making the
   threshold unreachable for any model that batches). Same class, different
   counter — and models that batch aggressively are exactly the ones that thrash.

## Acceptance

- Test: a tracker that never sees a progress event emits the prologue checkpoint
  at `prologue_cap` and not before. This test fails on today's code.
- Test: a run that produces early and then stalls still gets the STALL message,
  not the prologue message — the two must not collapse into one.
- Test: genuine research (reads only, under the cap) is still not nudged.
- The prologue checkpoint is bounded per run.
- A/B against dirge-5mtx.1's harness on a reconnaissance-heavy scenario:
  turns-to-first-write should drop. If it doesn't, the message wording is wrong,
  not the trigger.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: REVISED by dirge-5mtx.7. Drop the proposed 'prologue_cap defaults to 3x stall_threshold' — that is exactly the baked-in decision the adaptive-steering work is removing. The prologue bound should derive from observed signals (turns and TOOL CALLS without a progress event, weighted by the capability tier), so a weak model gets pulled out of reconnaissance early and a strong model doing genuine research is left alone. The turn-vs-tool-call granularity point in the original write-up stands and matters more under adaptation, since the observed thrash was 40+ calls inside ONE turn.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
Fix landed (99e48884). First A/B on the new `recon` scenario, GLM, n=2, max_turns=40.
Control = progress_prologue_cap 9999 (effectively the pre-fix behaviour); treatment = cap 3.

  metric        control          treatment      delta
  turns         17.0 (15..19)    8.0 (7..9)     better
  tool_calls    17.5 (17..18)    7.5 (6..9)     better
  first_write   8.0 (7..9)       5.5 (5..6)     better
  success_rate  2/2 (100%)       2/2 (100%)     flat
  green_rate    1/2 (50%)        2/2 (100%)     better

Turns and tool calls roughly halved, first write ~30% earlier, and no correctness cost — success stayed 2/2 in both arms, which is the thing that would have made this a bad trade. Green rate also went up, though at n=2 that is one run and not worth leaning on.

NOT yet evidence: single model. Multi-model run (glm + deepseek-flash) in flight; per dirge-5mtx.7 the direction has to hold across capability points before this counts, and the interesting question is whether the weaker model benefits MORE (expected) or whether a low cap interrupts it while it is doing legitimately necessary reading (the risk).

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
MULTI-MODEL A/B — the single-model GLM result did NOT hold. Recording the negative result.

recon scenario, n=2, max_turns=40. Control = cap 9999 (pre-fix behaviour), treatment = cap 3.

GLM:            turns 15.5 -> 8.0 better | first_write 9.0 -> 6.0 better | success 2/2 -> 2/2 flat | green 2/2 -> 0/2 WORSE
deepseek-flash: turns 6.5 -> 9.0 WORSE  | first_write 2.0 -> 3.0 WORSE  | success 1/2 -> 2/2 better | green 2/2 -> 1/2 WORSE

Three things fall out.

1. MY CORE ASSUMPTION WAS BACKWARDS. I expected the weaker model to thrash more on reconnaissance and so to benefit more from a bound. The opposite: deepseek-flash already writes at first_write=2 — it dives straight in and never enters a long prologue at all. GLM is the one that reads more before writing. So 'weaker model => more recon thrash' is false, at least on this scenario. A bound that helps the stronger model actively interrupts the weaker one before it has oriented, costing it turns (6.5 -> 9.0).

This is the single most useful input to dirge-5mtx.7 so far, and it argues the adaptive direction is real but NOT along the axis I assumed. The estimator cannot simply map 'weak model -> intervene earlier'.

2. GREEN RATE GOT WORSE IN BOTH MODELS — the only direction consistent across models, and it is a regression. GLM treatment ended Unverified and VerifiedRed; deepseek 1/2. Plausible mechanism: the prologue message says write something now and iterate, but says nothing about verifying, and treatment runs are much shorter — the model writes, considers the nudge satisfied, and finalizes. Caveat: n=2 per arm is two runs, so this is suggestive, not established.

3. THE ARMS DID NOT TEST WHAT SHIPS. I chose cap=3 to make the effect visible; the shipped default is 24. Neither arm tested the default, so none of this licenses a claim about default behaviour. Re-running 9999 vs 24 at n=3 across both models now.

Status: fix stays (the structural hole is real and dirge-t5dh's premise is unchanged — a run that never produces could never be reported at all). But the TUNING is unvalidated and the green-rate signal needs chasing before this is called done.

title: ClassifyFn: constrained judge verdicts, non-overlapping answer sets
description:
Every judge gate generates free-form text and recovers a boolean by substring
matching. Paper §4.2 (CompletionCondition) argues the opposite: constrain the
answer to a fixed set, and choose set members that don't compete.

## Live problems

`goal.rs:128-150` — `parse_goal_verdict` returns UNMET only if the FIRST line
contains `GOAL: UNMET` or `GOAL:UNMET`. A judge answering "The stop condition is
not satisfied because..." parses as MET and the run finalizes. Fail-open on
ambiguity IS deliberate (goal.rs:125-127: "failing toward finalization so a
flaky judge can't trap the loop") and the preamble biases toward MET on
uncertainty (goal.rs:48-49) — but the parse widens the fail-open set far past
"genuinely unsure" to include "said UNMET in different words".

`critic.rs:221-247` — `parse_verdict` works only because `INCOMPLETE` is tested
at line 229 before the COMPLETE fallthrough at line 246. `COMPLETE` is a proper
substring of `INCOMPLETE`. This is exactly the surface-form competition the
paper describes; it is correct today purely by test ordering.

There are three separate parsers with three separate conventions:
`parse_goal_verdict` (goal.rs), `parse_verdict` (critic.rs:221), `parse_unified`
(critic.rs:335).

## Change

Add a `ClassifyFn` beside `CriticFn`, built by the same plumbing
(`build_judge_fn`, provider/build.rs:700 — one shared client, per-call preamble):

    type ClassifyFn = Arc<dyn Fn(String, &'static [&'static str])
                          -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<usize>> + Send>> + Send + Sync>;

Returns the INDEX of the chosen option, so callers never string-match. Implement
by constraining the model's answer — structured output / tool-call with an enum
schema where the provider supports it, single forced token otherwise. Fall back
to the existing free-text path (and its documented fail-open) when a provider
supports neither, so this can't make a working setup worse.

Answer sets must not nest. Concretely:
  goal:   MET / SHORT       (not MET / UNMET)
  critic: DONE / GAPS / UNSURE  (not COMPLETE / INCOMPLETE / ABSTAIN)

Then collapse the three parsers onto one path: the classifier picks the verdict;
free-text generation is used ONLY for the detail body (the bullet list of gaps),
which is what it's actually good at. That is the §7 split — classification and
response as separate calls — applied to dirge's own judges.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: a judge that answers "not met", "Not Met.", "UNMET", "the goal is
  not satisfied" all resolve to the same verdict. Today only one of those does.
- Unit tests: no answer-set member is a substring of another (assert it, so a
  future edit can't reintroduce the trap).
- Provider without constrained-output support falls back cleanly; behaviour
  identical to today.
- A/B (.1 harness): on the incomplete-work scenario, measure verdict accuracy
  against hand-labelled ground truth — free-text parse vs constrained. Expect
  the gain to show up as fewer false-COMPLETE finalizations. If it doesn't move,
  the parse was not the bottleneck and .4 should be reconsidered too.

title: Boundary arbiter: at most one harness nudge per turn boundary
description:
The finalization boundary is a proper fallback node: `poll_finalization_follow_up`
(run.rs:536) polls gates in strict priority and returns the FIRST non-empty
source, at most one per finalization. Its doc comment (run.rs:525-534) calls
itself "the single authority for finalization precedence — previously four
separate `if follow_up.is_empty()` blocks inline in the outer loop [dirge-vcsn]".

The mid-turn boundary never got that treatment. In one iteration of the inner
loop, all of these can fire and stack:

  run.rs:2447-2459  track-work reminder      -> pushed to context + new_messages
  run.rs:2464-2478  fast-verify reminder     -> pushed
  run.rs:2487-2515  progress stall OR budget -> pushed
  run.rs:2787-2789  poll_steering_and_reminder ->
                      run.rs:77-81   user steering (N messages)
                      run.rs:82-84   file-touch reminder
                      run.rs:91-98   safe-state msg OR reflection checkpoint

Up to five harness messages plus user steering before a single assistant turn.
The mutual exclusions that DO exist are ad hoc and local:
  - safe-state replaces the reflection checkpoint (run.rs:85-98), with a comment
    explaining that emitting both would be contradictory ("diagnose and retry"
    vs "abort and re-plan").
  - progress emits stall OR budget, never both (progress.rs).

And the priority reasoning is already written down in prose but not enforced:
run.rs:2480-2486 says the progress monitor "runs LAST of the boundary nudges so
the cheaper, more specific ones (track work, fast verify) get first say — a
stall checkpoint is the broadest message of the three and shouldn't pre-empt
them" — then emits all three anyway.

## Change

Introduce `poll_boundary_nudge`, the mid-turn twin of
`poll_finalization_follow_up`: strict priority, returns at most ONE harness
message plus its `BoundaryNudge` source (from .1).

Priority (narrowest/most-specific first, matching the existing prose):
  1. safe-state abort        (rung 3 — supersedes everything below)
  2. reflection checkpoint   (rung 2)
  3. track-work reminder
  4. fast-verify reminder
  5. file-touch reminder
  6. progress stall
  7. progress budget

User steering is NOT part of this — it's input, not a nudge. It keeps its own
path and continues to be injected alongside, and `had_user_steering` must keep
driving the turn-budget reset (dirge-st8r, run.rs:2801).

Deleting the two ad-hoc exclusions is the point: safe-state-vs-reflection
becomes ordinary precedence, and stall-vs-budget can stay inside progress.rs or
move up — decide during implementation, but only one of them should encode it.

## Risk

A nudge that used to co-fire now gets deferred a boundary. That is the same
intentional trade the finalization gate documents at run.rs:528-532. The budgets
are separate per source, so a deferred nudge is not a dropped one — but confirm
that in tests, because the whole point is that a suppressed nudge still fires
later when its condition still holds.

## Acceptance

- At most one `BoundaryNudge` per turn boundary, asserted in `run_tests.rs`
  for a synthetic turn that trips track-work + fast-verify + stall at once.
- Existing tests for each individual nudge still pass unchanged.
- Off-mode / no-guards config is byte-identical to today.
- A/B (.1 harness): the recovery scenario and the incomplete-work scenario show
  no regression in success rate and no increase in mean turns. Hypothesis worth
  testing explicitly: fewer, more specific nudges -> equal or better success at
  equal or lower turn count. If turns go UP, the priority order is wrong — say
  so in the issue rather than shipping it.

title: Gate telemetry + reusable loop A/B harness
description:
Prerequisite for the rest of the epic: we can't claim any loop-control change is
an improvement without a way to measure it, and right now nothing counts gate
firings at all.

Two halves.

## Gate telemetry

`FollowUpSource` (run.rs:303) already names every finalization gate, but it is
returned and dropped — nothing aggregates it. The mid-turn nudges have no
equivalent enum at all; they're bare `push` calls at run.rs:2447-2515.

- Add a `BoundaryNudge` source enum mirroring `FollowUpSource`, covering:
  track-work, fast-verify, progress-stall, progress-budget, file-touch,
  reflection-checkpoint, safe-state.
- Add a per-run `GateTally` counting firings by source for both enums, plus
  turns taken, tool calls, errored tool calls, and final verification status.
- Emit it once at `AgentEnd` as a structured tracing event on a dedicated
  target (`dirge::gates`) so the harness can scrape it without parsing prose.
  No UI surface — this is instrumentation, not a feature.

## A/B harness

Generalize `scripts/code-mode-ab.sh`, which already has the shape we want
(isolated DIRGE_CONFIG_DIR/DIRGE_DATA_DIR per run, config-key override, N
repeats per arm, fixture-derived ground truth, correctness gate). It is
hardcoded to one flag and two metrics.

- Extract the run/isolate/compare machinery into `scripts/loop-ab.sh` taking
  arbitrary `key=value` config overrides per arm.
- Report per arm: task success rate, mean turns, mean tool calls, mean errored
  tool calls, mean input/output tokens, and the full GateTally breakdown.
- Scenarios need to exercise the loop's failure modes, not just bulk I/O. Add
  at minimum: a task that fails midway and needs recovery; a task the model
  will plausibly declare done while incomplete; a task ending in a genuine
  clarifying question. These are the cases .2/.3/.4 change behaviour on.
- Keep `code-mode-ab.sh` working (rewrite it as a thin caller, or leave it
  alone if extraction gets hairy — don't break an existing tool for tidiness).

## Acceptance

- `scripts/loop-ab.sh` runs both arms of a no-op config change and reports
  near-identical metrics (sanity: the harness itself adds no bias).
- GateTally is asserted in unit tests for a synthetic run with known firings.
- Non-goal: CI integration. This is a local measurement tool; provider calls
  cost money and are non-deterministic.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
REVISED for capability-adaptive steering (dirge-5mtx.7).

Two changes to this issue's scope:

1. GateTally must also count the CAPABILITY signals, not just gates and nudges. These are all already computed by the loop and all currently discarded: scavenge fired (model emitted tool-call-shaped text instead of a native call), tool_input_repair RepairKind counts by kind, TruncationFixed specifically (hit max_tokens mid-call), suggest.rs nearest-name hits (hallucinated tool name), storm suppressions, failure-tracker streaks. tool_input_repair/mod.rs:46-48 already says its telemetry surface 'is not consumed yet' — same computed-and-dropped pattern this issue exists to fix. One tally, two consumers: the harness reads it after the run, the .7 estimator reads it during.

2. The harness gains a MODEL MATRIX dimension. A/B here answers 'does this approach work better broadly', not 'what is the number'. Absolute turn counts are not comparable across models. Run each arm across at least three capability points and report direction + consistency of effect WITHIN each model, then whether it holds ACROSS models. A change that helps the weak model and hurts the strong one is a finding to report, not something to average away. A single-model result is not evidence for a steering change, and the harness output should say so.

Available capability points (config as of 2026-08-01): ollama (local, weakest), deepseek / deepseek-flash, glm, kimi. Main provider is currently glm.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: Harness hazard found while using it: loop-ab.sh invokes $BINARY (default target/debug/dirge) live, once per run. Any concurrent `cargo build`/`cargo test` during a multi-model A/B — which takes many minutes — swaps or locks the binary mid-experiment, so arms silently run against different code. Fix: copy the binary into $WORK once at startup and invoke the copy, so the experiment is pinned to the build it started with. Cheap, and it removes a whole class of invalid result that would be very hard to spot afterwards.

title: [epic] Loop control unification: one boundary arbiter, constrained verdicts, state-derived preconditions
description:
Source: Kelley, "Behavior Trees Enable Structured Programming of Language Model Agents"
(arXiv:2404.07439). Read against `src/agent/agent_loop/` on 2026-07-31.

The paper's structural claim — priority-ordered fallback nodes where exactly one
branch fires per tick — is something dirge already converged on at the
finalization boundary (`poll_finalization_follow_up`, run.rs:536, consolidated
under dirge-vcsn). Two other claims did NOT land, and both are load-bearing:

1. §4.2 CompletionCondition — score a FIXED answer set instead of generating
   free text and parsing it, and pick answer options that don't compete for
   probability mass ("surface form competition").
2. §7 — the paper's only hard empirical result. Same models, same task:
   self-policing inline gave 23-80% defense success (Table 1); splitting
   "classify the situation" from "act on it" into separate calls gave
   95.8-100% (Table 3). Models classify a situation far better than they act
   correctly on it inline.

Against that, three gaps in dirge's loop, plus the refactor they imply:

- The MID-TURN boundary is a stack, not a fallback. Up to five harness messages
  can land before one assistant turn (run.rs:2447-2515 pushes three; run.rs:2787
  -> poll_steering_and_reminder adds three more). Only two ad-hoc mutual
  exclusions exist, both hand-written and local.
- Judge verdicts are free-text generation plus substring matching.
  `parse_goal_verdict` (goal.rs:128) requires literally `GOAL: UNMET` on line 1
  — any rephrasing silently reads as MET. `parse_verdict` (critic.rs:221)
  depends on `INCOMPLETE` being tested before `COMPLETE`, and COMPLETE is a
  substring of INCOMPLETE: correct today, one reorder from silent inversion.
- Gate predicates read `new_messages`, which accumulates across re-entries, so
  every gate needs a hand-tuned one-shot budget to compensate. The code already
  says so at run.rs:795-800.

Scope: enhancement AND refactor. Each child both fixes behaviour and collapses
an ad-hoc mechanism into a shared one. Every behavioural child ships with an
A/B measurement against the harness in .1 — no child lands on "looks better".

Children, in dependency order:
  .1  A/B + gate telemetry harness           (prerequisite for all others)
  .2  Boundary arbiter: one nudge per turn boundary
  .3  ClassifyFn: constrained judge verdicts
  .4  awaiting_user_response as a classifier (depends on .3)
  .5  State-derived preconditions; retire per-gate budgets

Related pre-existing issues that this epic's .5 should subsume or close out:
dirge-q7vw (judge error records fingerprint, suppressing retry), dirge-mu46
(dedup skip also skips completeness re-judgment). Both are gate-lifecycle bugs
with the same root cause as .5.

Adjacent but NOT in scope: dirge-2m68 (no-critic default backstop).
close_reason:
All six work children resolved. Shipped across 0.21.0 and 0.21.1 via PRs #739, #740, #741. The failure-mode log (dirge-5mtx.6) was detached rather than closed — it is a living record meant to outlive this epic.

WHAT THE EPIC SET OUT TO DO: replace hardcoded steering thresholds with capability-adaptive ones, on the premise that models span a wide capability range and the harness should measure and adapt.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: the constants survived almost entirely intact — but measured, with the one derivation that shipped backed by a structural argument, and with the estimator's authority explicitly bounded. Three findings drove that:

1. EVERY FAILURE WAS A VERIFICATION FAILURE. Six for six; not one was a steering failure. The premise that steering was the weak point was wrong, and the deliverable became docs/verification-discipline.md — the project gate, the CI advisory, the masked-command guard, the exploration-prologue bound.

2. THE NOISE FLOOR IS ~2x. An A/A calibration produced 18 vs 36 turns from identical config. At n<=3 nothing of the size proposed is measurable, and one earlier reported win was retracted. The operating rule became: prefer changes whose success criterion is structural, because those hold at n=1.

3. THE ESTIMATOR MEASURES TOOL-CALL MECHANICS, NOT COMPETENCE. It cannot observe whether a model verifies its work or makes progress, so it has no standing to relax guards that fire on those. Both failures worth having a guard for came from models it reads as Strong. Adaptation is now one-directional: it may add support, never remove it.

The habit that produced every real finding was refusing to change a constant without evidence and going to get the evidence instead — which repeatedly meant not making the change.

FOLLOW-UPS OPEN: dirge-z85a (FailureTracker threshold fixed at construction), dirge-9m05 (--all-features clippy debt), dirge-a9pc (release channels silently skipped), dirge-jbhz (macOS microvm check drift). Plus dirge-5mtx.6 as the standing log.

title: RAX R2: progress monitor — stall + budget signals (agent_loop/progress.rs)
description:
Paper 4.4: dominant late PS failure was 'operating correctly but unable to find a plan within the allocated time limit since its search was thrashing' — a non-result within budget, not an error.

Every dirge guard keys on errors: storm needs identical calls, failure_tracker needs errored results, context_depth needs repeated same-file touches. Successful+varied+useless calls trip nothing until max_turns hard-stops.

- new agent_loop/progress.rs, self-contained like failure_tracker.rs
- fed the Outcome stream via LoopGuards (one classification point per activity.rs design note) + todo/modified-file deltas
- progress events: todo closed, new file mutated, tier red->green
- stall signal: N turns successful calls with zero progress -> replan checkpoint
- budget signal: 60%/85% of max_turns -> visible notice inviting triage (paper 4.1: RAX had explicit measured envelopes; dirge's budget is invisible to the model)
- None config = loop unchanged

PARENT
  ↑ ○ dirge-uw2l: [epic] Adopt DS1 Remote Agent (RAX) findings into the agent loop ● P1

CARRIED FROM R1: staleness gap. Verifier status stays VerifiedGreen after a green suite even if more edits land afterwards — today's gate has the same property for any verification. Tracking edit-after-verify belongs here: 'edits since last green' is exactly a progress/staleness signal, and verifier.rs will already have the edits_since_verify counter R1 adds.

title: RAX R1: verification tiers — fidelity pyramid in verifier.rs
description:
Paper 4.2: cheap tier gets volume, expensive tier gets nominal only; licensed by identical interfaces across tiers. Plus: developers front-line testing during integration found most bugs, formal high-fidelity testing found few.

Today verifier.rs asks one binary question (did A build/test command run and pass) only at finalization. cargo check and cargo test --all-features are indistinguishable.

- VerificationTier {Fast, Slow} beside is_verification_command
- VerificationStatus tier-aware: fast-green/slow-never-run distinct from nothing-run
- mid-run one-shot at turn boundary when code edits accumulate with no fast-tier command since
- finalization escalates: fast-green + slow-never-run -> run the full suite
- config verification_tiers: off|advisory|blocking, default advisory; off = byte-identical

title: RAX R0: prompt guidance — input-divergence, boundary tests, assumption ledger, concurrency evidence
description:
Prompt-only, no code. prompts/debug.md, prompts/code.md, prompts/default.md.
- debug.md Phase 0: observed != expected -> confirm inputs/env/versions match assumptions BEFORE hypothesizing about logic (paper 5: PS was solving a different problem because the spacecraft goals file differed from the testbed).
- code.md: replace generic 'check for edge cases' with boundary-derived tests: enumerate conditions in the changed code (comparisons, thresholds, empty/None, loop bounds), case at/below/above each; state residual risk + fallback where uncovered (paper 4.4: 25 boundaries -> 88 cases -> 2 bugs, 0.5% residual + contingency).
- code.md: concurrency evidence rule — passing tests are not evidence of absence for shared mutable state/async ordering (paper 5: race deadlocked in flight after thousands of clean ground runs).
- code.md + default.md: assumption ledger — name assumptions before implementing, say which were confirmed at verify (paper 4.4: turn durations assumed <=20min, actually >1hr).
- default.md: late-run conservatism — out-of-scope fix found after work is green is surfaced as a decision with specific lines, not silently absorbed (paper 4.3 CCB). Does NOT mean suppress.

title: [epic] Adopt DS1 Remote Agent (RAX) findings into the agent loop
description:
Source: Nayak et al., 'Validating the DS1 Remote Agent Experiment' (ISAIRAS'99), ~/src/dirge-code/rax-results-isairas99.

Structural lessons from RAX that dirge's loop is missing. Five rounds:
- R0 prompts: input-divergence-first debugging, boundary-derived tests, assumption ledger, concurrency evidence, late-run conservatism
- R1 verification tiers (fidelity pyramid, paper 4.2)
- R2 progress monitor (thrashing = no result within budget, paper 4.4)
- R3 safe-state abort (EXEC failure ladder rung 3, paper 2)
- R4 horizon replanning + goal triage + residual handoff (paper 2, 3.1b, 3.4)

title: dynamic_tool_search hides read/write/edit/bash — model can only reach write_todo_list
description: GH #734. With dynamic_tool_search: true the request ships exactly 3 tool defs (task_status, tool_search, write_todo_list) — verified off the wire. ALWAYS_ON_TOOLS (src/agent/tools/tool_search.rs:65) omits every core file tool, so a model asked to write code to disk sees one write-shaped tool: write_todo_list. Fix: put the core loop tools in the always-on set.

title: No-op compaction still rotates the session and repeats forever; the min-savings guard is #[cfg(test)]
description:
A fold that frees nothing still rotates the session id, rebuilds the agent, saves, fires on_session_switch, and prints 'context compacted: N -> N tokens'. Nothing suppresses the next one, so it repeats every turn. Observed live at ~6 second intervals with identical before/after counts (12081 -> 12081, 12567 -> 12567, 13076 -> 13076).

Three compounding defects:

1. The documented min-savings guard does not exist in release builds. src/agent/agent_loop/context_manager.rs:93 declares HISTORY_FOLD_MIN_SAVINGS_FRACTION = 0.3 under #[cfg(test)], so it is compiled out of the binary. Its only other references are the module doc (line 26, which describes it as a live guard: 'skips a fold whose head wouldn't shrink the log by at least that fraction') and a const assert at line 935. The decision function never consults it. Presumably #[cfg(test)] was added to silence a dead-code warning instead of wiring the guard up — the doc has described a guard that was never implemented.

2. decide_after_usage_with_threshold (context_manager.rs:593) is a pure function of prompt_tokens / ctx_max. There is no savings check and no memory of whether the previous fold accomplished anything. already_folded_this_turn only prevents a second fold WITHIN one turn, not the same futile fold on every subsequent turn.

3. The trigger and the remedy measure different things. The ratio uses the API's prompt_tokens, which includes the system prompt and all tool schemas. The fold only rewrites current_context.messages, and the reported tokens_before/after are estimate_messages_tokens(messages) — messages only. When the fixed overhead alone approaches ctx_max, no fold can move the ratio, but the loop keeps trying. That is exactly the 12081 -> 12081 signature: the ratio was high because of system+tools, while the foldable history was already minimal.

Also: run.rs:1220 emits ContextCompacted and calls compression::rotate_session_id() unconditionally at the end of the pass, including for SummaryOutcome::Skipped (CompactionKind::PruneOnly). A pass that changed nothing should not rotate the session, spend a summarizer call, or emit the event.

Suggested fixes:
- Drop the #[cfg(test)] and actually enforce the min-savings guard, or delete the constant and the doc paragraph so the code and docs agree.
- Skip the rotation/event when the pass produced no reduction (tokens_after >= tokens_before and outcome is Skipped).
- Add a back-off: after a fold that freed less than the min-savings fraction, suppress further folds until the token count moves materially, so an unfoldable fixed overhead degrades to one warning rather than an infinite loop.
- Consider warning when system+tools alone exceed the fold threshold, which is the actionable signal for the user (trim MCP tool surface / raise context_target).

Found while investigating runaway compaction on a k3 session; dirge-9jy7 is the reason the threshold was crossed in the first place, but this is what turns a wrong window into an infinite loop.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: Companion: dirge-9jy7 (k3 resolves to a 128k window instead of its real 262144, which is what pushes this session over the fold threshold in the first place).

title: Kimi k3 missing from context_window_for_model: compaction uses 128k instead of 262144, folding every turn
description:
Observed live: a k3/kimi session rotating every ~6 seconds with zero reduction ('context compacted: 12081 -> 12081 tokens'), session after session.

Two divergent sources of truth for a model's context window:

1. src/config/mod.rs:1507 context_window_for_model — a hardcoded ~42-entry SUBSTRING table (deepseek/glm/claude/gpt/gemini/llama/mistral/qwen). No kimi, no k3, no moonshot entry. 'k3' contains none of the keys, so it returns None and run.rs:1667 falls back to 128_000.
2. src/llmtrim/data/model_context.json — the 299-entry models.dev snapshot, which DOES have "k3": 262144 (also kimi-for-coding: 262144). Exposed as llmtrim::context_window (src/llmtrim/mod.rs:217), but its doc says 'Used by the CLI's breakdown occupancy view' — the compaction engine never consults it.

So the whole budget ladder runs against 128_000 for a model whose real window is 262_144. docs/config.md already documents the 262144 figure, added by #724 — the provider shipped without a corresponding entry in the table the compaction path actually reads.

Effect: the fold threshold lands at 0.75 * 128_000 = 96_000 real prompt tokens, which for this user is ~37% of the true window. With 6 MCP servers plus dirge's built-in tools, the system prompt + tool schemas alone are a large fixed overhead that compaction cannot touch (it only rewrites current_context.messages). Once that fixed overhead plus a small history crosses 96k, EVERY turn folds, no fold can get below the line, and the session rotates forever. See dirge-8bnp for why a no-op fold is not suppressed.

Fixes, in order of preference:
1. Have context_window_for_model consult the models.dev registry first and fall back to the substring table. One source of truth, and every future model gets a correct window without a code change. The registry is already embedded and refreshed by tools/refresh_context.py.
2. At minimum add kimi/k3 entries to the table. Leaves the two-source divergence in place for the next provider.

Note the substring matching is itself fragile: keys are matched with m.contains(key), so a short model id like 'k3' can never match and a long one can match the wrong key.

Found while investigating runaway compaction after releasing 0.19.27.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: Correction: the companion issue for the no-op fold loop is dirge-kq3a (the description references a placeholder id). dirge-9jy7 is why the threshold is crossed; dirge-kq3a is why crossing it becomes an infinite loop.

title: CI has no macOS job: the dead-tty watchdog suicide shipped in two releases undetected
description:
0.19.24 introduced the dead-tty watchdog and 0.19.25 shipped it again. Both were unusable on macOS — every TUI session exited 129 within seconds of startup — and nothing caught it, because:

1. ci.yml runs ubuntu-latest and windows-latest only. There is no macOS job at all, for build or test. macOS is a shipped release target (aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin in release.yml) and a Nix bin.nix platform, so it is a first-class target with zero CI coverage.

2. The regression test the fix added (input_reader.rs::live_controlling_tty_is_not_dead) opens /dev/tty and returns early if that fails. CI runners have no controlling terminal, so it is a silent no-op there. Even adding a macOS job would not catch this class of bug unless the test runs under a pty.

3. Nothing exercises 'dirge starts up on a real controlling terminal and stays up'. That is the single assertion that would have caught this, and it is cheap: fork a pty, exec the binary, assert it is alive N seconds later. The inverse (close the primary, assert teardown) is equally cheap.

Suggested work:
- Add a macos-latest job to ci.yml. Build at minimum; tests if runtime allows.
- Convert the /dev/tty regression test to allocate its own pty (openpty) instead of depending on an ambient controlling terminal, so it actually runs in CI.
- Add a pty-based startup smoke test to the suite: process alive after N seconds on a live pty, and exits on hangup when the primary closes. Working scripts from the 0.19.26 release verification are a starting point — they reproduced the bug against 0.19.25 and confirmed the fix.

Filed while cutting 0.19.26 (fix: #731, thanks @nikolap).

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
Verification scripts used to cut 0.19.26. Both reproduce against 0.19.25 (FAIL) and pass on 0.19.26. Confirmed on the actual shipped aarch64-apple-darwin release artifact, not just a local build.

tty_smoke.py — process must STAY ALIVE on a live controlling pty (catches the POLLNVAL false positive):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Smoke test: dirge TUI must stay alive on a real controlling pty.

Regression guard for the macOS dead-tty watchdog suicide (PR #731): 0.19.24
and 0.19.25 exited 129 about 250ms after startup on macOS because poll(2) on
/dev/tty always reports POLLNVAL there.

Usage: tty_smoke.py <path-to-dirge> [seconds-to-wait]
Exits 0 if the process is still alive after the wait, 1 otherwise.
"""
import os
import pty
import sys
import time

binary = sys.argv[1]
wait_s = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3.0

pid, master = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.environ["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
    os.environ.setdefault("LINES", "40")
    os.environ.setdefault("COLUMNS", "120")
    os.execv(binary, [binary])

# Drain the pty so the child never blocks on a full buffer.
os.set_blocking(master, False)
deadline = time.time() + wait_s
while time.time() < deadline:
    try:
        os.read(master, 65536)
    except (BlockingIOError, OSError):
        pass
    time.sleep(0.05)
    done, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    if done:
        code = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
        print(f"FAIL: dirge exited after {wait_s - (deadline - time.time()):.2f}s "
              f"with code {code}")
        sys.exit(1)

print(f"OK: dirge still alive after {wait_s:.1f}s on a controlling pty")
os.kill(pid, 9)
os.waitpid(pid, 0)
sys.exit(0)
```

tty_hangup.py — a REAL hangup must still tear down (catches over-correcting the above):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Counterpart to tty_smoke.py: a REAL hangup must still tear dirge down.

The macOS fix (PR #731) makes tty_is_dead ignore POLLNVAL. This checks it
didn't go too far the other way — closing the pty primary must still be
detected and exit the process.

Usage: tty_hangup.py <path-to-dirge> [settle-seconds] [teardown-timeout]
Exits 0 if dirge exits within the teardown timeout after the primary closes.
"""
import os
import pty
import sys
import time

binary = sys.argv[1]
settle_s = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 6.0
teardown_s = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 15.0

pid, master = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.environ["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
    os.environ.setdefault("LINES", "40")
    os.environ.setdefault("COLUMNS", "120")
    os.execv(binary, [binary])

os.set_blocking(master, False)

# Let it come up, and confirm it survives (otherwise we'd be testing nothing).
deadline = time.time() + settle_s
while time.time() < deadline:
    try:
        os.read(master, 65536)
    except (BlockingIOError, OSError):
        pass
    time.sleep(0.05)
    done, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    if done:
        print(f"FAIL: dirge died before the hangup, code "
              f"{os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)}")
        sys.exit(1)

# Hang up: close the pty primary.
os.close(master)
t0 = time.time()
while time.time() - t0 < teardown_s:
    done, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    if done:
        code = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
        print(f"OK: hangup detected, dirge exited {code} after "
              f"{time.time() - t0:.2f}s")
        sys.exit(0)
    time.sleep(0.1)

print(f"FAIL: dirge still running {teardown_s:.0f}s after the hangup")
os.kill(pid, 9)
os.waitpid(pid, 0)
sys.exit(1)
```

title: Subagent profile model not cross-provider routed (GH #711)
description: Coordinator-dispatched subagents fail when the active provider differs from the profile's pinned model family. main.rs builds a profile's pinned model with client.completion_model() on the ACTIVE client, so `model: glm-5.2` under a Codex/ChatGPT client 400s. /model cross-routes via resolve_model_switch; the profile path never consults it. Secondary: the provider 400 body is never logged.

title: retry: parse X-RateLimit-Reset (GH #718) — OpenRouter 429s storm through the daily quota
description:
GH #718. OpenRouter 429 bodies carry no Retry-After; the reset lives in the error JSON as metadata.headers.X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch MILLIS). retry_after_from_error_msg (src/agent/recovery.rs:205) only knows retry-after-ms / retry-after / retry_after / RFC-7231 date, so it returns None and every 429 falls back to plain exponential backoff.

Two consequences, both visible in the reporter's log:

1. per-minute limit: reset was 42s out, budget is 1+2+4+8+16 = ~31s over 5 retries -> budget dies before the window rolls. Run-level recovery (MAX_TRANSIENT_RECOVERIES=3, run.rs:222) then restarts the whole 5-retry budget, and /retry restarts it again. 44 wasted requests in ~2.5 min.

2. because X-RateLimit-Reset is unparsed, the RateLimit->UsageCap promotion in classify_error (recovery.rs:464, wait > MAX_IN_RUN_RETRY_WAIT=300s) never fires. The free-models-per-day 429 has a reset ~14.9h out and is retried like a transient blip. The wording ('free-models-per-day', '1000 free model requests per day') also misses the usage-cap substring list at recovery.rs:434.

Net effect: 118 x 429 across ~16 min, and the storm burned the entire 50/day free quota in under 3 minutes (log shows the error flip from free-models-per-min to free-models-per-day at 09:06:52).

Fix: teach retry_after_from_error_msg about x-ratelimit-reset (disambiguate epoch-millis / epoch-seconds / relative-seconds / duration strings like '2m59s'), clamp to [0, cap]. That feeds both the backoff and the UsageCap promotion for free. Also widen the usage-cap substrings for 'per day'/'per-day'. Separately consider a session-scoped throttled-until latch so the agent turn, summarizer and post-session stages stop hammering independently.

title: Finalization gates override a pending question to the user (critic/todo nag until the model guesses)
Raw NUL byte in source permanently blocks every edit to the file
description:
tree-sitter's lexer treats byte 0 as end-of-input, so any file containing a raw NUL parses as truncated and check_syntax reports an ERROR at the first form. syntax_gate then rejects EVERY write/edit/edit_lines/apply_patch to that file, forever, with a location that has nothing to do with the edit.

Repro: (clojure.string/replace s #"[\r\n\t<NUL>]" "") in a .clj file
-> 'Syntax check failed: 1 error(s) detected by tree-sitter. syntax error at 3:1: (defn clean [s]'
The delimiter scanner says BALANCED, so no actionable summary is appended - the model gets a bogus line:col on a valid form and starts counting parens by hand.

Real-world: scanned 30296 lisp files under ~/src; 142 rejected, 3 of them false positives - ALL THREE are NUL-byte files (apparat/src/clj/apparat/media/storage.clj, apparat/src/clj/apparat/cells/login.clj, metabase/test/metabase/search/appdb/index_test.clj). Embedding a raw NUL is the normal way to write it in Clojure (no \0 string escape).

Not Clojure-specific - affects every tree-sitter language.

Fix direction: detect NUL in the candidate before parsing and skip the tree-sitter gate (fall through to the delimiter scanner, which handles NUL correctly), rather than reporting a phantom syntax error.
acceptance_criteria: A .clj file containing a raw NUL byte can be edited; delimiter-scanner feedback still applies; regression test

title: Syntax gate auto-repair silently re-nests Lisp forms
description:
repair_delimiters (src/semantic/syntax_validator.rs) appends missing closers at EOF and re-validates with check_syntax. For Lisp that re-validation is vacuous: ANY balanced paren arrangement parses, so a mid-form dropped closer gets 'repaired' into a structurally different file that parses fine.

Repro (validate_or_repair on /tmp/x.clj):
  (ns app.core)
  (defn f [x]
    (let [y (inc x)]
      (println y
      y))
  (defn g []
    (f 1))
-> Repaired: ')' appended at EOF, so (defn g ...) is now nested INSIDE (defn f ...). Written to disk; the model only sees '[auto-repair] auto-closed 1 unclosed delimiter(s)' appended to a SUCCESS message.

The dirge-p1ws LSP rollback cannot catch this: no manager/no server for .clj returns Ok early, and even clojure-lsp would not flag the re-nested form as an error - it is valid code.

Fix direction: for languages where the grammar cannot distinguish nesting (lisps), require the repair to be structure-preserving (e.g. top-level form count / first-column opener count must match pre-edit), or refuse to auto-close and reject with the precise hint instead.
acceptance_criteria: A mid-form dropped closer in a .clj file is REJECTED, not silently closed at EOF; trailing truncation of the LAST form still auto-closes; regression test in syntax_validator.rs

title: LSP servers (rust-analyzer) orphaned on signal exit — setsid detaches them, only Drop reaps
description: rust-analyzer is spawned via child_guard::detach_session (setsid: new session, no controlling terminal, own process group). The ONLY thing that kills it is ProcessGroupGuard::drop -> kill(-pgid, SIGKILL), which requires Rust destructors to run. Because setsid detaches the server from dirge's terminal, terminal-delivered signals (SIGHUP on terminal close, SIGINT/SIGQUIT to the foreground group) never reach it. So when dirge dies WITHOUT running Drop — SIGTERM (kill), SIGHUP (terminal/tab close), a real SIGINT — rust-analyzer is orphaned and keeps indexing (1GB+ RAM). dirge has NO signal handler anywhere (verified: no tokio::signal/ctrlc). Normal interactive /quit and clean --print/--loop returns DO drop the manager and reap the server; this is strictly an abnormal-exit leak. Same gap affects MCP servers, DAP adapters, and bg-shells (all setsid + Drop-only kill; DAP shutdown_active_session and bg-shell kill_all run only on the normal return path). Fix: global child-pgid registry + a tokio::signal reaper (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP) that kill(-pgid) all groups, restores the terminal, and exits. Relates to dirge-8m69 (graceful LSP shutdown handshake).
close_reason: Global child-pgid registry in child_guard + tokio signal reaper (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP) that kill(-pgid) all detached groups, restore the terminal, and exit 128+signum. Covers LSP/DAP/MCP-client (shared ProcessGroupGuard auto-registers) plus bash + mcp_server guards. src/signal.rs::install_reaper wired early in main. Was: setsid detaches servers from the terminal, so signal-death (no Drop) orphaned rust-analyzer.

title: agent_loop: checkpoint-reuse fold returns old-list index — snapshots spliced at wrong position
description:
src/agent/agent_loop/run.rs:957 with compression.rs:794-809 and run.rs:1180-1182 (logic). The checkpoint-reuse fold returns SummaryOutcome::Succeeded(cut) where cut is an OLD-list index, but Succeeded(idx) is documented (run.rs:727-731) and consumed by restore_working_files (run.rs:1180: (summary_idx+1).min(len)) as the NEW-list index of the inserted summary — which on this path is always 0 (apply_checkpoint_summary produces [summary] + messages[cut..]). The inline path correctly returns Succeeded(start). Incremental checkpointing is default-on, so this is the common fold path: with cut > n/2 the post-compaction file snapshots insert at the END of the list (after newest messages); with cut <= n/2 they splice mid-tail, potentially between an assistant tool_use and its toolResult — breaking the orphaned-pair invariant and risking a provider 400. Secondary: ContextCompacted.first_kept_index carries two different meanings per path.
Fix: return the new-list summary index (0) on the reuse path; document first_kept_index semantics. Audit item 3.

title: renderer: remove_chat never loads next snapshot — surviving chat history overwritten
description:
src/ui/renderer.rs:1187-1198 (logic/structural). remove_chat never calls load_active() when removing the ACTIVE chat, and its only call site (ui/mod.rs:2228, Ctrl+X CloseChat) always passes the active index. After chats.remove(idx), active_chat indexes the next chat's snapshot but the hot fields (buffer/source/scroll/selection) still hold the closed chat's content — screen keeps showing the closed chat. Next switch_chat save_active() writes the dead content into the surviving chat's snapshot slot, permanently replacing its history.
Fix: load_active() after removal (and see companion issue on subagent chat-index maps). Audit item 2.

title: ui: shell-exit drain clobbers is_running — double agent run
description:
src/ui/mod.rs:3113 (logic). Shell Exited else-branch (!! invisible or interrupted ! run) runs drain_interjections!() then unconditionally sets is_running = false, clobbering the true that install_into just set when the queue was non-empty. Status shows idle during the drained run; a second prompt takes the not-running submit path and install_into overwrites agent_rx/agent_abort/agent_interject/agent_cancel — the first runner's JoinHandle is dropped, giving two concurrent agent runs with interleaved side effects. Ctrl+C can't cancel the drained run (abort branch at 1768 requires is_running), and Ctrl+C on empty input exits the app mid-run. The other three drain sites (3933, 4033, 4114) correctly do not force false.
Fix: only set is_running=false when the drain didn't spawn (match the other sites). Audit item 1.

title: Wavescope entropy audit remediation (2026-07-11)

title: Alert-overlay scroll clamp uses pre-Layout height; long permission command unreachable
description: src/ui/renderer.rs:973-989 vs src/ui/tui/layout.rs:119: tui_redraw sizes the overlay rows=wrapped.clamp(1, rows_q-9) (bypassing the 8-row cap) and computes alert_max_scroll with inner_h=rows, but render_frame -> Layout::with_panels clamps input_rows to MAX_INPUT_ROWS=8 so the painted inner height is 8. On a 30-row terminal an 18-row alert head gives rows=19, no overflow, alert_max_scroll=0; the painter shows 6 head rows plus a 'more lines, scroll' hint but alert_scroll_down clamps to 0 -- the keys do nothing and the command tail is unreadable before approval. Re-opens dirge-coy3/#587. Fix: compute alert_max_scroll from the post-Layout-clamp inner height (or drop the clamp for overlay bodies).

Test overlay_scroll_geom_uses_painted_height. Integration RED skipped (tui_redraw probes real tty, no size-injection seam).

title: Anthropic token refresh overwrites Claude Code credentials file, dropping its other fields
description: src/provider/anthropic_oauth.rs persist_credentials_to_path (167-174) writes ~/.claude/.credentials.json as exactly {claudeAiOauth:{accessToken,refreshToken,expiresAt}} via save_json_0600 -> full overwrite. That is Claude Code's own file; its real claudeAiOauth object carries extra fields (scopes, subscriptionType, ...) and possible sibling top-level keys. A mid-session dirge refresh (wired at client.rs:322) drops them all, and since the refresh token is single-use and now rotated, Claude Code is left with a stripped credential it may reject. Contrast auth/store.rs save_openai (148-180) which preserves unknown fields and sibling providers. Fix: read-modify-write, merge the three fields into the existing object.
close_reason: Fixed on p1-review-fixes: persist_credentials_to_path is now a read-modify-write merge that updates only dirge's three fields (via serde_json::to_value, no hardcoded keys) and preserves other claudeAiOauth fields + sibling top-level keys. No lock re-acquire (caller holds it). Test persist_preserves_foreign_credential_fields.

title: Inline critic/goal/code-review judge calls have no timeout and can freeze finalization
description: src/agent/agent_loop/critic.rs run_judge! (55-66), code_review.rs (852-934), run.rs (389-395,474-490): side-LLM judge calls on the finalization path have no timeout at any layer; run_oneshot (provider/summarize.rs:193-243) drains a stream with no chunk or overall deadline. Contrast the compaction summarizer and background checkpoint which are bounded by explicit 120s timeouts (run.rs:738-743,975) precisely because a provider that stalls without erroring freezes the session. With code_review_mode=Blocking (or critic/goal gate armed), a judge provider that opens a stream and stops emitting freezes finalization forever; two-pass review gives two chances. Fix: one shared bounded-judge helper (timeout + fail-open) mirroring COMPACTION_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT.

title: Resume-after-failure gate re-issues permission-denied and storm-suppressed tool calls
description: src/agent/agent_loop/run.rs poll_finalization_follow_up (304-320): last_action_failed_and_stopped (237-262) checks only tr.is_error and does not exclude permission denials or storm-breaker backfill results. (A) user denies a bash call -> error 'Permission denied by user' -> model stops and asks -> gate injects a [resume] nudge -> model re-issues the denied call, re-prompting/auto-denying up to MAX_RESUME_NUDGE(3) times; contradicts Outcome::Denied (activity.rs:47) and critic [DENIED] handling (run.rs:2465). (B) storm give-up backfills is_error:true results (tools.rs:1011) then the give-up narrative (run.rs:1934) matches the gate; guards.reset_turn (1450) cleared the storm window so the re-issued call executes again. Fix: exclude permission-denial and backfill/guard-stub results, or skip the gate after a storm give-up.

Resume nudge no longer re-issues denied/suppressed calls; a mixed tail with a genuine error still arms. Tests: false_on_permission_denial, false_on_suppressed_backfill_stub, true_on_genuine_error, true_when_mixed_denial_and_genuine.

title: JSON-RPC write timeout leaves a partial frame and silently desyncs the stream
description: src/jsonrpc_client.rs:156-174 (and notify 206-215): on WRITE_TIMEOUT or write error the pending entry is rolled back but inner.closed is never set and the transport is not torn down. The encode_frame future is dropped mid-write (timeout wraps it), leaving a truncated Content-Length frame in the pipe; the next request writes a fresh frame at the wrong byte offset. Peer stalls >10s (indexing/GC/swap), recovers, and from then on every frame boundary is desynced while closed stays false and callers keep retrying on the corrupt stream (LSP and DAP). Fix: on write timeout or any partial-write error, mark closed, drain pending, tear the transport down.
close_reason: Fixed on p1-review-fixes: request/notify now call fail_transport() on any write failure or timeout — sets inner.closed and drains pending — so a partial frame can't leave the stream open for a desyncing next write. Test write_failure_closes_transport with self-contained mock Protocol/writer/reader.

title: Compaction summary serializes block-array tool results as empty strings
description: src/agent/compression.rs serialize_turns_for_summary (677-695) reads content only via .as_str(); production tool results are block arrays ([{type:text,text:...}]) so they serialize as empty. Same class as dirge-u5ka, already fixed in content_chars (196) and content_text (375) but missed here. run_compaction_pass_with_focus (agent_loop/run.rs:938) feeds live messages straight in, so every tool result (errors, command output, file paths) reaches the summarizer as '[i] toolResult: '. Recall eval passes only because its fixtures are scalar strings. Fix: use content_text() here.
close_reason: Fixed on branch p1-review-fixes: serialize_turns_for_summary now routes content through content_text() so block-array tool results are flattened instead of serialized empty. Test serialize_turns_includes_block_array_tool_results.

title: Read-cache hit returns pre-injection-guard content, defeating the scanner
description: src/agent/tools/read.rs:463 caches the pre-guard text (info) and the cache-hit path at line 259 returns it verbatim without guard_untrusted_result. Scenario: model reads a poisoned file (first result fenced, or body withheld under InjectionScanMode::Block per content_guard.rs:441); reads the same unchanged file again same cache generation -> raw un-fenced content enters context, defeating Advisory fencing AND Block-mode withholding. The default_note prepend is also lost on hits. Fix: cache the guarded output, or apply guard_untrusted_result on the hit path too.
close_reason: Fixed on p1-review-fixes: read.rs now guards the body BEFORE caching (cache.set stores the guarded value) and applies the per-request note via with_note() on both the hit and miss paths, so a cache hit is fenced/withheld identically to a miss. Test cache_hit_returns_guarded_body_not_raw.

title: Background review: idle avatar while is_running=true strands queued messages (#621)
description: Two busy-indicators desync. is_running:bool governs send-vs-queue; the avatar face (^_^)=AvatarState::Done is set unconditionally at handle_done top (done.rs:170). After finalization the plugin done_phase early-return and the /plan drive_plan_review path keep is_running=true while painting Done, and set agent_interject=None. User sees idle face, types a message, it queues (is_running=true) but the interject signal is dead and finalize (which drains) was skipped. On completion several paths drop the queue without dispatch: handle_error clear (error.rs:111), done_phase None arm (mod.rs:3716 flips is_running=false without draining), non-draining Retry relaunch. Fix: (1) don't paint Done at done.rs:170 unconditionally — only when going idle; show a busy face on paths that keep is_running=true. (2) done_phase None arm should route through finalize_idle_turn to drain. GH #621.

title: cargo install dirge-agent fails: rig caret pin drifts onto breaking patch
description: Published dirge-agent 0.19.1 depends on rig with a caret constraint. rig ships breaking API changes in patch releases (0.37.0 -> 0.37.1 added required Text.additional_params), so cargo install (no --locked) resolves the newer rig and fails to compile with E0063. #615 upgraded main to rig 0.39 but is unpublished and still uses a caret (^0.39), so it will recur on the next rig patch. title: Ghostty: unthrottled focus reassert causes ~1min MCP-log/render stall
description: Ghostty echoes focus events (ESC[I/ESC[O) whenever ?1004h (focus reporting) is enabled. dirge's sole FocusGained handler calls renderer.reassert_modes_light(), which re-emits TERMINAL_MODE_REASSERT (includes ?1004h) UNTHROTTLED. On Ghostty this is a tight feedback loop: ?1004h -> FocusGained -> reassert -> ?1004h -> ... saturating the UI select loop and starving MCP-log notification paints for ~1min. iTerm2 doesn't echo focus-on-enable so it's instant there. Confirmed empirically: MCP servers themselves start in <0.35s regardless of TERM; the delay is 100% display-side. force_terminal_reassert already throttles (500ms) to break exactly this loop (renderer.rs:248-252 documents it); the light path lacks the guard. Fix: throttle reassert_modes_light on last_mode_reassert.

title: F1: skip full scrollback rebuild on no-op/duplicate terminal resize
description: Every crossterm Event::Resize (input_reader.rs:122, dims discarded -> UserEvent::Resize unit variant event.rs:256) unconditionally calls renderer.rebuild() (mod.rs:1536), which re-parses markdown + re-wraps EVERY source block in the scrollback (renderer.rs rebuild(), up to 20k rows). No dimension-change guard, so duplicate/spurious resizes (crossterm emits dupes; some terminals fire Resize on focus) do a full rebuild for nothing. Fix: forward the new (cols,rows) on Resize and skip rebuild()+repaint when unchanged from the last handled size.
close_reason: Merged in PR #608: UserEvent::Resize carries dims; handler skips rebuild+repaint on unchanged size.

title: Read-injection scanner: scan untrusted tool results (read/MCP/websearch) for prompt-injection at ingestion
description: dirge fences bash(!)/webfetch output but read-tool, MCP, and websearch results enter context unscanned (chokepoint RigToolAdapter::execute rig_tool.rs:194; read.rs:432, mcp/tool.rs:294, websearch.rs). Port GSD read-injection-scanner's 4 detector families (standard injection, summarisation-survival, markdown-link exfiltration, invisible-Unicode incl. U+E0000 Tag block). Shared pure scanner module + tri-state config (off/advisory/block, default advisory); advisory fences+annotates, block opt-in on >=N high-severity. Reuse/extend content_guard (memory_db.rs:272).
