description: semantic/adapters/bash.rs:162-175 treats compound_statement/if_statement/while_statement/for_statement/case_statement/function_definition as opaque single segments. { rm -rf /tmp/foo; } matches no per-command rule and falls through to Allow. is_complex (line 127) doesn't flag these either. Mirror opencode shell.ts:127 using descendantsOfType('command') — recurse into every command descendant.

title: C2: webfetch SSRF via HTTP redirects
description: tools/webfetch.rs:270-273 builds reqwest client without redirect::Policy::none() or custom policy. validate_url_host_safety runs once on initial URL; 30x to RFC1918/169.254 is silently followed. Install custom redirect::Policy::custom re-running validate_url_host_safety on each Attempt::url().

title: C1: apply_patch uses unresolved path after perm check (symlink-swap risk)
description: tools/apply_patch.rs:251 calls check_perm_path (not check_perm_path_resolve), then apply_create/update/delete/rename operate on raw user-supplied path. Other tools (read.rs:161, write.rs:88, edit.rs:133) route through resolved_path. H12 fix didn't propagate. Thread check_perm_path_resolve per op and pass resolved string into apply_*.

title: H1: propagate AbortSignal into JanetLoopTool::execute
description: JanetLoopTool::execute takes _signal and drops it. Plugin tool handlers run unboundedly inside spawn_blocking holding the PM mutex; the user's Ctrl+C/Esc has no effect until the handler returns. Phase-6 wired AbortSignal into native tools; plugin tools must too.\n\nFix: race the spawn_blocking join against wait_for_cancel(signal) (same pattern as the phase-6 wrapper in builder.rs). On cancel return Err("cancelled"). Document that Janet is single-threaded so handlers can't be preempted — only joined. Plugin authors should keep work bounded.

title: C1/C2: fix customType wrapper + add e2e bridge test for renderer dispatch
description: Phase 9d renderer lookup uses wrong JSON nesting level — payload.get('type') against the {role,content} wrapper always returns None, so registered renderers never fire end-to-end. Smoke test calls invoke_message_renderer directly with a hand-built payload so it passes a broken path.\n\nFix: extend harness/add-custom-message to (customType content &opt display); wrap as {role:'custom', customType, content, display:true} matching pi's CustomMessage shape (messages.ts:48). UI consumer reads customType at top level. Add bridge/UI-equivalent test that walks the full LoopMessage::Custom -> AgentEvent::CustomMessage -> renderer-resolve path so future drift is caught.

title: Path traversal via .. survives lexical-fallback when both canonicalize calls fail
description: permission/checker.rs:495-513 — when canonicalize(joined) AND canonicalize(parent) both fail (nonexistent subdir + ..), falls through to lexical joined.to_string_lossy(). Path::starts_with matches components, so /cwd/nonexistent/../../etc/passwd classifies as internal. Need lexical .. normalization in fallback.

title: Provider SSE stream has no per-chunk timeout
description: agent/runner.rs:259 stream.next().await with no tokio::time::timeout — stalled provider hangs agent forever. opencode chunk-timeout pattern: per-chunk read deadline.

title: ANSI injection in permission ALERT prompt
description: ask_req.tool / ask_req.input rendered un-sanitized at mod.rs:2584-2585. Reopen path already sanitizes — asymmetric. Sec impl: ANSI at the permission-decision moment.

title: Chat history ignores 120-col content_width cap
description: max_line_width and wrap_line use raw content_cols, so on wide terminals scrollback overflows the centered band into divider/panel margin.

title: R1: fix 3 critical plugin bugs (FFI panic, dialog deadlock, init hang)
description: From the plugin subsystem audit: (1) wrap JanetCFunctions in catch_unwind so Rust panics don't unwind across the C-FFI boundary into Janet; (2) cancel send_dialog's reply_rx.recv() on worker shutdown so the worker thread doesn't block forever when the UI exits mid-dialog; (3) add timeout to the init handshake so a worker panic before init_tx.send() doesn't hang the main thread. Also: (4) bounds-assert wrap_string's i32 cast for the unlikely >2GB case, (5) make take_string_slot atomic to close the race window, (6) don't eat unrelated user events in the dialog arm.

title: Loop and steering improvements from the comparison survey
description:
Umbrella for the loop/steering improvements identified by surveying a comparison harness against dirge. Eleven children, filed on their own terms: what is wrong today, what the change does, what measurement justifies it.

ALREADY DONE, no child issue: a uniform per-tool dispatch budget with a structured error (shipped as dirge-9tl3 + dirge-8cbm). One deliberate deviation — the error message avoids the word 'timeout' so tool_error_class does not route a runaway call into the Transient bucket and retry it unchanged.

SURVEYED AND REJECTED, so nobody re-derives them:
  - The plugin/waterfall architecture itself. dirge is a single binary with a static tool registry; the extension-point machinery solves a problem dirge does not have and is the bulk of what is there.
  - Package-owned runtime invariant registration. dirge's equivalent is debug_assert plus the test suite.
  - Per-agent default model. Subagent profiles (.dirge/agents/) already cover it.
  - Three-way input targeting (next-turn / next-step / non-waking inject). dirge's turn-boundary injection with All/OneAtATime is adequate, and mid-turn steering is an axis where dirge is already ahead.
  - A generic per-model config map. The wire SHAPES are per provider-type and correct; only the effort default has a demonstrated need (dirge-l0jt). Revisit if one alias ever serves both a chat and a reasoner model.
  - Session-local scheduled reminders, model-facing session query, and a generic background-job registry: dirge already has session_search, background/bg_shell, and task_status covering the substance.

MEASUREMENT — this is the part that binds all children. scripts/loop-ab.sh reports steering signals (turns, tool calls, errored calls, storm suppressions, failure streak, every gate_*/nudge_* count, turns-to-first-write, correctness) AND cost (input tokens, cached tokens, cache-creation tokens, hit rate) on ONE line, because a change measured for one but not the other lets 'improved steering by destroying the cached prefix' read as a clean win. Every child therefore needs a CONFIG FLAG to be an A/B arm — that is a constraint on the implementation, not an afterthought.

Four rules this codebase has already paid to learn, and every child is subject to them:
  1. Write the must-not-fire half of each assertion FIRST. Two of three scorer bugs in the compaction round surfaced the moment the negative half was written down, before any model was called.
  2. Check the premise against the code before building. Four of seven rounds in the steering epic had premises the measurements killed, and the premise check itself turned up two P1 bugs that were in no plan. Three round-2 hypotheses died this way too.
  3. A mechanism gate reading zero in BOTH arms means the run measured nothing — discard it, do not report a null result.
  4. Report the tail beside the mean, and read the model's actual output at the first disagreement before believing any number.

ORDER: dirge-gxdn first. It is the least interesting item and everything depends on it — dirge-027e and dirge-ue37 are both bets about uncached input tokens, and without prefix-change attribution neither is falsifiable.

title: Oversized tool output is truncated with no way to retrieve what was cut
description:
A large tool result is bounded by throwing bytes away. read and grep cap individual lines at 4-16KB and mark the cut; llmtrim's toolout stage windows the result to a line budget. What was elided is gone — the model cannot ask for it, and neither can a later turn, a summary, or a person reading the session back.

That makes the cap a genuine loss of information rather than a presentation choice, and it pushes the size limits upward: every cap has to be generous enough that the common case survives it, because exceeding it is unrecoverable. A 40k-line grep and a 300MB log get the same answer — a truncated middle and no way back.
design:
Persist the full result to a session-scoped artifact and replace the model-facing content with a head/tail preview plus a locator and a retrieval hint, above a byte threshold. The model keeps the shape of the output and gains a way to go back for the rest; the transcript keeps the whole thing.

Details that are not optional, each of which is a way to get this wrong:
  - Reserve the notice's own byte cost INSIDE the cap. A preview that spends the whole budget and then appends the locator produces a replacement LARGER than the cap, and for a marginally-oversized result larger than the original.
  - Exempt read. Otherwise read -> spill -> read the spill file is a loop the model will find.
  - Best-effort, always. No session, no store, a write failure, or a notice that does not fit under the cap => keep the original inline content. A spill failure must never turn a successful tool call into an error or hide a result.
  - Plain-text results only; leave anything carrying non-text blocks alone.
  - Preview is head AND tail. The head says what the command was doing, the tail usually says whether it worked.

Interacts with dirge-ahx6 (pruning stale results from history), and the ordering matters: spill bounds a result on the way IN, ahx6 shrinks one already in history. Spill first — it reduces what ahx6 ever has to deal with, and gives ahx6 somewhere to point when it prunes.

title: Nothing records when the cached request prefix changes, or why
description:
Nothing records when the cached request prefix changes or why. The prefix is system prompt + tool schemas + config; any of them moving invalidates the provider's cache from that point on, and the only visible consequence is a worse cached_tokens number several turns later with no way to attribute it.

This is load-bearing for three separate pieces of work. dirge-027e (per-request prompt sections) deliberately makes the prefix vary and cannot be evaluated without seeing how often. dirge-ue37 (reasoning passback) is a bet about uncached input tokens. And a tool registry that reorders — MCP tools arriving late, a prompt deny list changing, a skill appearing — would silently cost the cache on every session with no signal at all. Right now nobody would notice any of it.
design:
Canonicalise the request head (system text, tool schemas in order, and the config fields that reach the wire) into a hash, and emit a tracing event on the dirge::gates target when it differs from the previous request's — with a reason: initial, resume, or changed, and for changed, WHICH component moved.

Deliberately cheap: a hash per request and one line only when it changes. Not a diff of the prompt, not a copy of it.

Two things fall out of it immediately, and both are the point:
  - A test that the tool schema list is emitted in a deterministic order. If it is not, every session is paying for it today and this is a bug fix, not a diagnostic.
  - scripts/loop-ab.sh gains a prefix_changes column, so any treatment that shifts the prefix is visible in the same table as the tokens it costs.

Reference for what to record: the request head is already assembled in rig_stream_factory.rs around the filter_tool_defs / builder.tools path.

title: Retry counts and backoff are global; only the chunk timeout is per provider
description: ProviderEntry already carries stream_chunk_timeout_secs per alias, but the retry policy — attempts, backoff ceiling — is one global setting. A flaky local vLLM and a strict hosted API therefore share it: tuning retries up for the local endpoint loosens them for the hosted one, where aggressive retry costs money and can trip rate limits.
design: Optional retry object on ProviderEntry (max_attempts, backoff ceiling) falling back to the global defaults, matching how stream_chunk_timeout_secs already resolves. Keep the global as the default rather than requiring the key everywhere.

title: Thinking level resets to the global default on every new session and model switch
description: Reasoning effort is a per-request steering choice with one global default. Switching to a reasoning-class model, or starting a fresh session, starts from that default rather than from anything the model wants — so a chat-class model and a reasoner-class model in the same config get the same effort until the user changes it by hand, every time.
design:
ProviderEntry.thinking_level: Option<ThinkingLevel> — the default effort for that alias's default model, applied when the user has not chosen one this session.

The motivating case is provider-specific and concrete: a chat-class model and a reasoner-class model want different defaults (chat-class off or low; reasoner-class high or max, and DeepSeek is one of the few backends that accepts 'max' at all — see the xhigh -> max mapping already in adapter.rs). Today both start from one global default, so whichever model is not the one the default was chosen for runs at the wrong effort until someone fixes it by hand, every session.

Deliberately NOT a generic per-model map. The wire SHAPES for reasoning are already per provider-type and correct; this is a per-model PREFERENCE, and it is the only one with a demonstrated need. If one alias later serves both a chat and a reasoner model, add ProviderEntry.models at that point and not before.

Also add optional thinking to the .dirge/agents/ profile schema, so a reviewer subagent can pin low effort while the coordinator runs high.

title: Repeated identical tool calls jump straight to suppression with no advisory tier
description:
The storm breaker's only response to a model calling the same tool with the same arguments repeatedly is to SUPPRESS the call and answer with a first-person explanation. There is nothing between 'no reaction' and 'your call did not run'. The common case on smaller models is milder than a storm — the model forgot it already ran this — and a nudge would resolve it without the veto, which costs a turn and can confuse a model that then argues with the harness instead of moving on.

NOT part of this work: argument canonicalisation is ALREADY correct. storm.rs signature() runs arguments through message::canonical_json, which deep-sorts object keys and normalizes integers-stored-as-floats, so a model that reorders keys does not defeat detection today. Only the advisory tier is missing.
design:
An advisory tier in the existing failure-tracker/storm path: a short reminder at 3 consecutive identical calls, a detailed one (tool, run length, argument preview) at 5 and 8, none of which blocks the call. Reuse storm.rs's existing canonical_json signature — it already deep-sorts keys, so the chain key is a solved problem.

Two details decide whether it works. Count AFTER execution, so a permission-denied call still counts — a model hammering a denied call is exactly the loop worth breaking. And reset the chain on user interjection: the user changing the subject is precisely when a repeat stops being a mistake.

Cap the argument preview (500 chars is a reasonable start) but key the chain on the FULL canonical string — a write body or a long command would otherwise ride into the next request unbounded, in exactly the loop scenario where context is already under pressure.

MEASURE: the existing storm counters already record suppressions; the bar is fewer SUPPRESSIONS at equal or better task completion, not merely more nudges fired. Provider-agnostic — this is a loop-control change, not a wire change.

title: Session persistence failing is invisible in the TUI
description: persist_turn_to_db returns early when the session DB cannot be opened, so with a damaged or unwritable database the session silently stops being saved. Found alongside #769. It now reports once at warn! with the reason (which names the file and the recovery steps when the database is damaged), but during a TUI session stderr is redirected to the log, so a user without --verbose still sees nothing while their history is being dropped.
design: Needs a UI notice path into a function that has neither renderer nor event channel today. Options: hand persist_turn_to_db a notice sink like the code-review advisory path (dirge-kdwz) already uses, or have the caller check store health once at session start and render a line there.

title: last_init_error is written in three places and read nowhere
description: SessionDb::open records a diagnostic via set_last_init_error on three paths, and last_init_error() is called by nothing outside its own tests. The one that matters is the WAL fallback: WAL being unavailable is the signature of a network or cloud-synced filesystem (NFS, SMB, Dropbox, iCloud), which is the classic way a SQLite file gets corrupted. dirge detects that precondition and throws it away — the tracing::warn goes to a log nobody captures without --verbose. A filter whose reject path has no reader.
design: Surface it once at startup, next to the other startup warnings.
close_reason: last_init_error deleted — written in three places, read nowhere, and a dirge-w4i7 test already warned against reading it because a successful open clears it. The WAL-fallback notice shared that slot and was wiped by the same open that recorded it; it has its own drained, deduplicated list now, surfaced at startup. Also fixed the two swallowed failures found alongside: the memory store's Err(_) => None and persist_turn_to_db's per-turn debug!.

title: Database corruption is stumbled into, never detected
description: SessionDb::open does no integrity check and SQLITE_CORRUPT is recognised nowhere in the codebase, so corruption surfaces at whatever random write hits a bad page — mid-session, after work has been done. Every later write then fails the same way, for the rest of that session and every future one. quick_check on the largest real state.db here (3.6MB) takes about 30ms, which is a fair price for finding it at open instead.
design: PRAGMA quick_check after open; a failure becomes the same corruption error as (1), naming the file and the recovery step.
close_reason: SessionDb::open runs PRAGMA quick_check, so damage is found at open rather than at whatever write touches a bad page. ~30ms on the largest real state.db.

title: A corrupt database reports neither which file nor what to do
description: Reported as issue #769: 'Failed to demote entry: database disk image is malformed' on every memory write. That is SQLITE_CORRUPT surfacing from memory_db.rs, and the message names neither the database nor a recovery step — there are two candidates (the per-project .dirge state.db, shared with session persistence, and the global memory db) so the user cannot even find the file. They replied 'Please advise' because the message does not.
design: One helper that maps a rusqlite error to a user-facing string, recognising SQLITE_CORRUPT / SQLITE_NOTADB and adding the database path and the recovery step. Connection::path() recovers the path, so no plumbing through the call sites.
close_reason: db_health::describe recognises SQLITE_CORRUPT and NOTADB and adds the database's path plus recovery steps (salvage first, start over second, and the likeliest cause — a WAL-less filesystem). Every other error is passed through unchanged.

title: Ctrl+C does not escape the question modal
description: Every modal in the UI treats Ctrl+C as 'I want out' — Permission maps it to Deny, DialogConfirm/DialogSelect cancel, PlanSwitch and PlanApproval bail, and PlanApproval's free-text entry explicitly guards Char(c) on !CONTROL with a comment saying it matches the rest of the UI. The question modal, the other text-entry modal, has neither guard. In option-select, option_select_action takes only a KeyCode so Ctrl+C falls to Ignore and nothing happens. In the custom-answer field, KeyCode::Char(c) is pushed unguarded, so Ctrl+C types a literal 'c' into the user's answer. A user hammering Ctrl+C to get out of a question they do not want to answer gets silence or corrupted text; Esc works, but it is not what the rest of the UI taught them to reach for. Same shape as every other missing-guard-on-a-parallel-implementation bug in this codebase: the guard was written for one text-entry modal and not the other.
design: option_select_action takes the modifiers so the mapping stays pure and testable (dirge-72h2 made it pure for exactly that reason); Ctrl+C and Ctrl+D map to Reject. The entry branch guards Char(c) on !CONTROL and bails on Ctrl+C, mirroring PlanApproval.
close_reason: option_select_action takes the modifiers and maps Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D to Reject; the custom-answer field guards Char(c) on !CONTROL and bails on Ctrl+C, matching PlanApproval and the permission deny-note field. A rule test asserts every modal text field ignores control chords. 4 mutations killed.

title: Scavenged tool-call syntax is printed to the user as prose
description:
When a model emits a tool call as TEXT (the llama.cpp/ollama shape dirge-56vo exists to handle), the raw call syntax is streamed to the user as the assistant's answer, whether or not the scavenger lifts a call out of it.

Reproduction (mock SSE provider returning one text-mode call, dirge -p --yolo):
  stdout = '<tool_call>\n{"name": "shell", "arguments": {"command": "echo ALIASWORKS"}}\n</tool_call>DONE'
The call ran correctly; the syntax was shown anyway.

Not fixable where the scavenger runs. run.rs pushes LoopMessage::Assistant at ~2802 and scavenges at ~2955, and the text has already been streamed to the UI by then, so stripping after the fact cannot unprint it. The fix belongs in the streaming display layer and has to distinguish a leaked call from a model legitimately showing JSON in a fence -- RE_FENCED_CALL matches any ```json block, so a naive strip would eat legitimate content.

Found while measuring tool-name misses (dirge-e31n.8); deliberately NOT folded into that work because the fix is in a different layer and is materially larger.
notes: Only strip regions that actually became calls -- stripping call-shaped regions that did NOT become calls would leave an empty answer, which is worse than raw syntax. Scavenger would need to report the consumed source spans (DsmlInvoke has no raw field; extract_tagged_regions returns inner bodies, not full matches).
close_reason: Fixed. Display and dispatch now read one region definition (agent_loop/call_syntax.rs); syntax that runs is withheld, syntax that runs nothing is left visible. Two further bugs from the same gap fixed with it: the dangling tool_result (scavenged call never reached the assistant message) and the empty call id. Write-up in docs/text-channel-calls.md.

title: The in-loop compaction summarizer never sees tool calls; /compact does
description:
The two compaction paths disagree about whether the summarizer sees tool CALLS.
Found while fixing dirge-tmex; sibling of dirge-tgb9, where the same two paths
disagreed about prompt-injection fencing.

  provider::summarize::serialize_conversation  (the /compact path)
    emits, per message: "[Tool: <name>(<args json>)]" and "[Result: ...]",
    with args and result each capped at PER_TOOL_CAP = 2048 chars.
    So the summarizer SEES what the agent called and with what.

  compression::serialize_turns_for_summary  (the automatic in-loop fold)
    emits "[i] <role>: <content_text(...)>", and content_text keeps only
    `type: "text"` blocks. A toolCall block contributes NOTHING.
    So the summarizer sees "assistant: <prose>" with no record of the call.

CONSEQUENCE: on the path that actually runs unattended, a fold summarizes a
stretch of work without any record of what the agent DID -- which file it wrote,
which command it ran, what arguments it passed. The prose around a tool call
often does not restate it ("done", "that worked"). The summary then becomes the
session's record for every later turn.

Note the tool RESULT does survive on both paths (it is a separate `toolResult`
message whose content is text), so this is specifically the call side: the
summarizer can see an outcome with no idea what produced it.

BEFORE FIXING, MEASURE. src/agent/compaction_bakeoff.rs now exists and can
answer this directly -- but NOT with the current fixture, whose planted facts
all live in text content. It needs a fixture that plants facts in tool-call
ARGUMENTS (a write's path and content, a bash command line) and scores whether
they survive the fold. If they do not survive today and do with the call
serialized, that is the evidence to change it. Uncapped args would blow the
summarizer prompt, so any fix wants serialize_conversation's 2048-char cap or
similar.

Do not assume the /compact shape is the right one just because it is richer:
[[steering-premises-die-on-measurement]] records three rounds where the
plausible-looking richer prompt measured null or worse.
acceptance_criteria: a bake-off fixture plants facts in tool-call arguments; measured whether they survive a fold today; change made only if the measurement supports it
close_reason: Fixed at 99b06845. Measured before/after with a tool-call-argument fixture: 0/6 reached the prompt and 0/6 survived, now 6/6 and 6/6, with the text-content fixture unchanged at 20.0/20. Args capped at 512. Mutation 4/4. Also fixed the harness bug it exposed: unwrap_or_default() scored a failed provider call as a 0/20 summary.

title: Carry unresolved effects across a real interrupt, and fence partial assistant text
description:
The two dirge-e31n.5 acceptance criteria that did not land.

1. Facts live in a run_agent_loop LOCAL, so an unresolved effect survives across TURNS within a run but not across a true interrupt — a new run_agent_loop call starts with an empty list. That is exactly the case the bead was named for: the user hits Ctrl-C mid-write, comes back, and the next turn has no idea what landed. Needs the fact list on session state rather than a stack local.

2. handoff_marks_partial_assistant_text_unverified: on an interrupt the partial assistant text should be carried into the next turn fenced verified=false, so the model does not read its own half-finished reasoning as settled fact.

Both are cross-run persistence problems; the within-run half shipped in 776a0dda.
design: Fact list moves to session state (or a LoopConfig Arc<Mutex<..>> like truncation_notes, if that is per-session rather than per-run — CHECK, it may be rebuilt per run). Partial text needs capturing at the cancellation site in stream_assistant_response, not at the tool layer.
notes:
COMPLETE (52fe6f15 + this). Both halves landed, neither by the route this bead proposed.

HALF 1 -- cross-run unresolved effects (52fe6f15). The bead planned to persist a fact list to session state. Unnecessary: heal.rs::fix_tool_call_pairing already finds tool calls whose results never arrived and synthesizes one per missing id, so interrupted calls are DERIVABLE from the persisted history. Reading it first also found a live bug -- that synthetic result told the model "treat as a transient failure and retry if needed" for EVERY tool, which for bash/write/apply_patch/task is the duplicate-effect advice the taxonomy exists to prevent. Now chosen by side_effect::classify_effect.

HALF 2 -- partial assistant text fenced (this commit). Premise verified before building: a cancel or non-retryable mid-stream error preserves the partial with stop_reason=Error and error_message set, and assistant_to_value serializes both -- but those are TRANSCRIPT-ONLY. default_convert_to_llm passes the value through, and the rig conversion to a provider body keeps role and content only. So the model reads a sentence that stops mid-thought, indistinguishable from a finished answer.
  Marker goes in the CONTENT (stream::INTERRUPTED_NOTICE), appended in the terminal Error arm, only when something streamed.
  Covers BOTH the resume path and the same-session continue -- doing it at heal time would have missed the second, since an in-memory continue never reloads.
  NOT named *_TAG: reserved by intervention::HARNESS_TAGS, whose registry test scans source for the shape. This is not a harness-injected message.

TWO EXISTING TESTS BROKE and were updated rather than loosened: they asserted the exact text of a truncated message. Kept exact (now asserting text == partial + fence) because a `contains` there would stop noticing anything else that began appending to a truncated turn.

PROCESS NOTE: the first mutation run reported 3 kills against a RED tree -- those two tests were already failing from my change. mutate_control caught it and voided the run. That is the whole reason the harness has a control step; without it I would have recorded three meaningless results.

3 mutations killed with a clean control. 5314 tests, clippy clean. NOT measured -- this is a resume/interrupt path and loop-ab.sh runs single non-interactive prompts, so it cannot interrupt and resume. Unit + mutation tested only.
close_reason: Both halves landed (52fe6f15, partial-text fence); neither needed the session-state persistence the bead proposed

title: Weight MissingInfo tool errors into the capability tier
description: dirge-61sv classified tool errors but capability.rs still scores every errored call at weight 1, so the measured blowups (7 errored of 26 calls = 269 per-mille) sat below the 333 Struggling bar and nothing tightened. Split the tally's errored count by ErrorClass and weight MissingInfo above the rest, so a run operating on a wrong picture of the tree escalates without lowering the bar for genuine friction.
design: Per-class counters derived from ErrorClass::ALL so the emitted line cannot drift from the enum. errored_tool_calls becomes the sum, not a second field. Weight chosen by sweep against every run whose counters are on record.
notes:
SHIPPED (0df85394). W_ERRORED_MISSING_INFO=2, uniquely pinned by the five runs on record.

WHAT MOVED
- GateTally.errored_by_class[ErrorClass::ALL.len()] replaces errored_tool_calls; the total is now the SUM, derived, so it cannot drift from its parts. Same in CapabilityCounters.
- record_tool_call takes Option<ErrorClass>: an errored call with no class is unrepresentable rather than discouraged.
- capability::errored_weight is an exhaustive match, so a new class cannot compile without stating its weight. Defaulting a new class to the floor would silently restore the blindness.
- Class split emitted on dirge::gates (errored_misuse/missing_info/transient/fatal/unclassified), scraped as loop-ab col 27.

THE SWEEP, because the number is the whole change
Constraint set = 2 blowups (must Struggle) + 3 grounding runs that COMPLETED (must not). At 1 both blowups escape (235 and 269 per-mille vs the 333 bar) -- that is today's behaviour. At 3 the glm and qwen runs cross it. 2 is the only integer that satisfies all five. Grounding runs predate classification so their mix was never recorded; they are scored worst-case (all missing-info), which makes the upper bound as tight as it can be. Test walks weight-1/2/3 through the REAL raw_tier via raw_tier_at, so it cannot go stale against a copy.

WHY ONLY MissingInfo
Transient/Fatal are the environment, not the model -- raising them lowers the bar for genuine friction, the mistake this is meant to avoid. Misuse is already on the repair axis (repair_invalid 4, repair_successful 1); raising it double-counts. Unclassified at 1 IS the non-regression criterion.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN THE PROCESS
An invented tool name errors as 'Tool X not found', which the classifier reads as MissingInfo -- so it would have scored 2 (missing-info) + 2 (hallucinated) = 4, counting one failure twice on the same axis and re-ranking it against repair_invalid. Now classed Misuse at the tally site: keeps the documented 1/3/5 ordering and is the honest label. Test asserts its own premise (that the real text does classify as MissingInfo) so it cannot go vacuous, plus the other-side test that a real tool reporting a missing path IS still missing-info.

HARNESS BUG FOUND AND FIXED
Adding col 27 reported '0.0 (..)' in both arms: the report's numeric-column list (nnum = split("4 5 6 ...")) is hand-maintained and never had it. A column missing from that list renders (..) where an absent-but-accumulated column renders (0..0) -- distinguishable, which is the only reason it was caught. Three source-level guards added, each mutation-tested: every column a row reports must be accumulated; every get_field/sum_fields assignment must reach results.tsv (this is the denied_tool_attempts failure mode -- a gate reading zero forever while the report looks healthy); the results.tsv printf's conversions must match its arguments (bash printf REUSES the format on excess args, writing a second row from the leftovers).

VERIFICATION
8 Rust mutations + 7 harness mutations, all killed, both with no-op controls. 5229 tests, clippy clean, 109 selftest checks.

STILL OPEN: the weighting has not run against a live model. The mechanism gate is the whole point -- if errored_missing_info reads 0 in both arms on the next A/B, the change did nothing observable and the sweep's premise (that the blowups' errors were missing-info) is unconfirmed. That premise could not be checked directly: the blowup work dirs were mktemp'd and are gone.
close_reason: Shipped in 0df85394; live A/B validation of the mechanism gate still outstanding

title: R6/F7: labelled-slot compaction schema
description:
F7 + F8 + F9 (Medium / Low-Med). Three independent cleanups that share a file.

F7 - COMPACTION_PROMPT asks for five narrative sections (Goal, Progress, Key Decisions, Relevant Files, Critical Context). A better shape asks for eleven labelled slots: TASK, CONSTRAINTS, STATE, DONE, DECISIONS, FILES_IDS, COMMANDS_TESTS, OPEN_NEXT, RISKS, ACTIVE_CONTRACT, SOURCE_COVERAGE - with rules to quote identifiers verbatim, mark anything inferred as 'unverified'/'inferred', treat incomplete assistant messages as unreliable, cap at 1200 words, and emit a coverage sentinel. A weak summarizer loses far less against slots than against prose. dirge's injection fencing is BETTER and must stay.

F8 - prompts are include_str! blobs. No version marker, no segment identity, no shadow path. A steering change is a code change with no A/B route and no way to bisect a behavioural regression to a prompt revision. dirge already runs an A/B harness for code_mode_rubric, so the missing piece is identity, not infrastructure.

F9 - truncation is ad hoc: heal.rs caps tool results at 40k chars, llmtrim has its own accounting, the preamble is unbounded. One approach runs one CJK-aware estimateNormalizedTokens through every budget, with an explicit degradation ladder per block and a throw when the floor cannot be met. The LADDER matters more than the estimator: it makes truncation ordered and observable rather than arbitrary.
design:
F7: rewrite the section list toward labelled slots. Keep COMPACTION_DELIMITER_* fencing and input_contains_compaction_delimiter exactly as-is.

F8: segment markers in the prompt sources + a POLICY_VERSION constant, recorded in session metadata, with active/shadow/rollback gated on env. Assembly asserts all required segments are present rather than silently shipping a truncated policy.

F9: one estimator, one budget type, a declared degradation order per injected block, and a budget_fallbacks list surfaced in telemetry so a silent truncation becomes a visible one.

Splittable into three if the A/B wants them separated.
acceptance_criteria:
- compaction_prompt_has_all_labelled_slots
- compaction_retains_injection_fencing_and_collision_check
- policy_version_recorded_in_session_metadata
- missing_segment_fails_assembly_loudly
- budget_degrades_in_declared_order
- budget_fallbacks_visible_in_telemetry
notes:
RESULT: the slot rewrite is CUT; one section from it SHIPS.

MEASURED with a new bake-off (src/agent/compaction_bakeoff.rs) driving the real
window + prompt builder + summarizer, transcript/window/budget/scorer held
identical across arms so the only difference is the section template. Fixture is
20 facts buried in noisy tool output (compaction_recall::hard_facts +
noisy_session), sized so summary_budget is set by its 20% ratio rather than
clamped up by its 2000-token floor.

RECALL -- NULL. deepseek-v4-flash, verbatim recall of 20 planted facts:
  n=20  sections 19.6/20 (lost 8/400)   slots 19.6/20 (lost 9/400)
  n=10  sections 19.2      sec+cov 20.0      slots 19.7
  n=8   no-cov 19.8        sections 19.9     slots 19.8
  floor (qwen3.6-27b local, n=3): sections 19,19,20; slots 19,20,...
A schema that does not move recall is not worth a schema change. Note the
FLOOR did not fail either -- ~19.3/20 -- which is the same finding as
[[steering-helps-only-a-failing-model]]: there was no failing summarizer to
rescue.

COVERAGE -- NOT NULL, and decisive. With the assembled prompt clipped the way
oneshot_with_model clips it, "did the summary tell its reader the material was
partial":
  without the section  1/12 runs
  with the section    12/12 runs
  slots               11/12 runs
p ~ 3e-6. The slot rewrite buys nothing over the single section.

WHY IT MATTERS: the clip is real, not hypothetical (dirge-5zca, fixed at
1c5e81d3 -- the budget was a fixed 128 KB and dropped most of the conversation
on any model over ~70k tokens). Even with the budget now derived from the
model's window, a turn-start fold on a large window can still hand over more
than fits. A summary built from a clipped transcript reads exactly like one
built from the whole thing.

SHIPPED (b1dcf46e): "## Source Coverage" in the summary template, added to
SUMMARY_SECTIONS, with a test pinning the list against the template's headers
both ways. SummarySchema::{Slots, SectionsWithoutCoverage} stay as bake-off
arms so the comparison is reproducible; neither is reachable from config.

THREE SCORER BUGS found along the way, each on course to produce a confident
false answer. Written up in docs/verification-discipline.md ("When the scorer is
the thing that is wrong"): verbatim matching against needles the model
reformatted in markdown; a coverage detector sharing the keyword "truncat" with
a planted fact, so the better the summary the more certainly it misreported; and
a keyword scan with no negation handling, which read "COMPLETE -- no truncation
marker" as a declared gap and thus inverted the healthy case for the whole arm
under test. Two of the three surfaced the moment a "must NOT fire" assertion was
written down, before any model was called.
close_reason: Slot rewrite cut on a null recall result (n=20 level, floor did not fail either). The one part that measured -- a source-coverage section -- shipped at b1dcf46e: 1/12 -> 12/12 on declaring a clipped transcript. Bake-off harness kept.

title: R5: stream-level loop/leak detection + per-turn generation overrides
description:
F5 + F6 (Medium).

F5: storm.rs covers repeated tool CALLS only. A model that degenerates into repeating a paragraph, or that starts reciting the system prompt, runs unchecked to the output cap. Both are common on the model class dirge targets and both are cheap to detect on the stream.

a reference implementation LoopDetector: SimHash-64 over 350-char sliding windows, FNV-1a over 4-grams, Hamming <= 5, and - the part that makes it usable - it requires BOTH a near-match count >= 3 AND regular spacing (period variance <= 50% of mean) before firing, so a genuine repeat cycle is distinguished from incidental similarity. PromptLeakDetector compares output windows against the system prompt (window 200, Hamming 8) and fires a hard non-recoverable error. Plus maxAgentTurns 200.

F6: tool_choice is read in llmtrim but never set on the agent path. There is no way to force a call or forbid one for a single turn. a reference implementation forbids tools on turns where the user is correcting behaviour rather than requesting work.

dirge already depends on gaoya::simhash in llmtrim/stages/dedup.rs, so the primitive is in-tree.
design:
New module src/agent/agent_loop/loop_detect.rs fed from the streaming text. Both detectors abort the turn with typed errors carrying recoverable/retryable metadata (a reference implementation ERROR_META table is a good shape: loop = recoverable+retryable with 1s delay, leak = non-recoverable, user action required).

Separately thread TurnOverrides { tool_choice } from the loop through the stream factory. Start with tool_choice only; temperature and reasoning-effort overrides can follow.

Do NOT port a reference implementation Chinese-regex correction-turn detector as-is - it is language-specific and brittle. The plumbing is the deliverable; the trigger policy is a separate decision.

Flags: [harness] stream_loop_detect, [harness] prompt_leak_detect (both default off).
acceptance_criteria:
- repeated_paragraph_trips_loop_detector
- varied_prose_does_not_trip
- irregular_repeats_do_not_trip (periodicity gate works)
- preamble_echo_trips_leak_detector
- normal_output_quoting_a_prompt_line_does_not_trip
- tool_choice_none_suppresses_calls_for_one_turn
- typed errors carry recoverable/retryable metadata
notes:
BOTH HALVES IMPLEMENTED at the user's direction (53175716, 757217d9), overriding this bead's earlier "hold / do not build yet" recommendation.

1. PROMPT-LEAK DETECTOR -- src/agent/agent_loop/prompt_leak.rs, config prompt_leak_detect, DEFAULT OFF.
   Modes reuse GateMode: advisory records and warns; blocking also stops consuming the stream and keeps the answer given BEFORE the recitation.
   SimHash-64 over sliding 16-CONTENT-word windows vs the same windows of the prompt, Hamming<=8, tripping on 12 consecutive matches.

   THREE THINGS I ASSERTED AND THE TESTS DISPROVED:
   a) Hashing raw words false-positived on ordinary prose. In a 24-word English window 10+ tokens are the/and/in/a, so unrelated windows land inside a Hamming-8 radius -- the detector was measuring "is this English". Content words only now (reuses llmtrim's language-detected stopword set).
   b) TRIP_RUN=6 was justified as "far past anything a quotation produces". It is not: a verbatim TWO-SENTENCE quote reaches 6 and tripped, because windows straddling a quote's edges mix in surrounding prose and still match. Raised to 12 (~55 words verbatim). The doc now states the MEASURED margin.
   c) Blocking discarded the whole turn. A bare break falls through to the stream-closed fallback, which synthesizes an EMPTY message -- so it threw away the model's real answer to suppress the recitation, worse than not detecting it. Now finalizes at leak.start_offset.

   MUTATION TESTING DROVE ALL OF THAT. The run gate, the run reset and the partial-word escape each had a SURVIVING mutation because the false-positive fixtures produced zero matching windows and passed for the wrong reason. Fixtures are now derived from the tokeniser (verbatim_span) and assert they actually matched something. 7 mutations killed with a control.

   ALSO: a mutation swapping the tokeniser back still survives -- lex_words and the output path agree on ASCII prose. The unification is DEFENSIVE, not a fix for an observed bug, and the comment says so rather than claiming credit.

2. tool_choice -- ToolChoice{None} on StreamOptions -> provider body, WITH A CONSUMER.
   Consumer: the permission checkpoint, whose own text says "retrying, rephrasing, or switching to another tool will not clear it". Until now that was advice the model could answer with another blocked call; it is enforced on exactly the turn that reads it. One turn only by construction (take() at the stream call).
   Required splitting BoundaryNudge::PermissionCheckpoint out of ReflectionCheckpoint -- opposite advice, and previously indistinguishable on the emitted line.
   NO ToolChoice::Auto: Option::None already means that, and an explicit "auto" must not be sent (some OpenAI-compatible backends reject tool_choice on a request with no tools array, and dirge makes plenty of those).
   4 mutations killed; two initially survived because no fixture had a non-permission nudge firing and the run ended before the turn after the constraint.

3. TEXT-LOOP DETECTOR -- STILL DROPPED. Unchanged by this work: both observed blowups were varied-call wandering with no repeated output for SimHash to see, and that failure is now handled by dirge-s9ry's MissingInfo weighting. Nothing here reopens it.

NOT MEASURED. Neither half has an A/B. The leak detector's condition has never been observed in dirge (which is why advisory exists), and the tool_choice consumer fires only on a permission-denial streak, which loop-ab.sh's scenarios do not produce. Unit + mutation tested only, and stated rather than implied.

5305 tests, clippy clean, 109 selftest checks.
close_reason: Both halves implemented per user direction (53175716, 757217d9); text-loop detector remains dropped on the evidence

title: R4: side-effect taxonomy + interrupted-turn handoff
description:
F4 (Med-High). dirge's tool results are success/error text. After an interrupt or a crash the next turn cannot distinguish a write that committed from one that never ran. recovery.rs classifies transport errors for retry and heal.rs repairs unpaired tool calls on load, but neither tells the MODEL what actually landed - so it either re-runs a committed effect or assumes work it never did.

One approach classifies every tool result committed | unknown | no_effect, and on interrupt renders <trusted_turn_facts type="interrupted_turn_handoff"> carrying, per fact: ordinal, tool name, tool id, status, side-effect state, a safe summary, and artifact refs including sha256 - plus unresolved effects, plus the partial assistant text fenced as verified="false". That taxonomy is what lets its prompt assert 'interruption does not roll back committed side effects' and have the model act on it.

This is where dirge's existing safe_state and recovery work finally has something to say to the model rather than only to the harness.
design:
Add SideEffect::{Committed, Unknown, NoEffect} to the tool result type.

Classification at each tool, not centrally: write/edit/apply_patch that returned success -> Committed; bash that produced output -> Committed; bash aborted or timed out -> Unknown; read/grep/glob/list_dir/semantic -> NoEffect.

On interrupt, render confirmed + unresolved facts into the next turn's envelope (R1). Add the 'interruption is not rollback' rule to the prompt alongside it - the rule without the facts is noise.

Related: dirge-61sv classifies tool ERRORS into recovery classes. This classifies tool EFFECTS. Complementary, same recording site (failure_tracker::record_result already sees is_error/tool_name/excerpt), worth landing together.

Flag: [context] turn_facts (default off). Depends on R1.
acceptance_criteria:
- write_tool_reports_committed
- successful_bash_reports_committed
- aborted_bash_reports_unknown
- timed_out_bash_reports_unknown
- read_tool_reports_no_effect
- interrupt_renders_handoff_into_next_turn_envelope
- handoff_marks_partial_assistant_text_unverified
- handoff_omitted_when_no_facts
notes:
VERDICT: CUT. Four model configurations across the full supported range, two scenarios, 53 informative runs. Control never fails.

  deepseek-v4-pro   6/6 control   (handoff)
  glm               6/6 control   (handoff), 6/6 (handoff-fold)
  deepseek-flash    6/6 control   (handoff-fold)
  qwen-local        3/3 control   (handoff-fold)  <-- capability.rs's documented LOW BOUND

qwen ran the scenario properly: every run reported unresolved_effects=1 and compactions=2-4, so the condition WAS produced and folded away. It is a real measurement of the population the feature was built for, not a broken run. (The n=3 batch hit its wall-clock cap at 5 of 6 runs; the missing run is a treatment run, which cannot change a control-never-fails finding.)

THREE ROUNDS, EACH FIXING A FLAW IN THE LAST, ALL NULL:
  R1 handoff -- measured the case where the block is REDUNDANT (compactions=0 in all 24 runs; the model can see the timeout in its own transcript).
  R2 handoff-fold -- forced a fold so the tool result is compacted away, which is the block's only non-duplicative job. Also fixed the fixture: the task had ended "report how many lines out.txt contains", FORCING the read that reveals the truth. Answer is now the sum over modules; out.txt's line count is a hidden dependent variable.
  R3 same scenario against weaker models, down to the documented low bound.

The failure the block prevents -- re-running a command whose effect you can no longer see -- does not occur in any supported model.

WHAT REPLACES IT. The cross-run case that motivated this bead is covered by two mechanisms that carry information the model genuinely LACKS, both landed since:
  - heal.rs interrupted-call note, per-tool via side_effect::classify_effect (52fe6f15)
  - partial assistant text fenced in the CONTENT (b1c9f109)
The envelope block's remaining role was summarising effects the model can already see.

REMOVAL PLAN (keep the parts that earn their place):
  DELETE: envelope::Section::TurnFacts + TurnFact + MAX_TURN_FACTS + HANDOFF_RULE + push_fact/trim_facts + to_envelope_with_facts; config turn_facts and resolve_turn_facts; LoopConfig/LoopSpawnConfig/AnyAgent turn_facts plumbing; run.rs fact recording and the re-render block; the associated tests and the docs/config.md row.
  KEEP: side_effect.rs (heal.rs depends on it), GateTally::unresolved_effects + its emitted field (free observation, and the mechanism gate that made these three rounds legible), loop-ab.sh's handoff and handoff-fold scenarios and their column.
close_reason: Taxonomy kept and in use by heal.rs; envelope block cut on 53 runs across 4 model configs where control never failed (252ba776)

title: 1h prompt-cache TTL default is unmeasured; /cache can't answer whether it pays
description:
Writes cost 2x base input at 1h vs 1.25x at 5m; reads are 0.1x and refresh the entry either way. Break-even is 2 requests at 5m, 3 at 1h.

In an active agent loop turns are seconds apart, so a 5m entry never lapses and the 0.75x surcharge is paid on every write for nothing — roughly 2-3k extra token-equivalents per turn on the delta automatic caching writes each turn. It flips on idle gaps: one lapsed 5m entry on a 150k prefix costs about what 80 turns of surcharge do.

So it genuinely depends on usage, which is what prompt_cache.rs already says. The gap is that dirge cannot settle it: /cache reports cumulative totals but not the TTL in force, so an A/B via DIRGE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL leaves no record of which arm produced which numbers.

For reference, opencode never sets a 1h TTL anywhere.

Scope here is instrumentation only — surface the active TTL in /cache so the A/B is runnable. Do NOT flip the default without data; that is a pricing change.

title: No visibility into per-turn cache misses (20-block lookback, concurrent fan-out)
description:
Two documented ways to lose the cache that dirge cannot currently detect:

1. 20-block lookback. Each breakpoint walks back at most 20 content blocks to find a prior entry. The system prompt encourages parallel tool calls; ten of them is assistant(text + 10 tool_use) + user(10 tool_result) = 21 blocks in one turn, which pushes the previous breakpoint out of the window and silently misses. A single automatic breakpoint has no redundancy here (opencode's two sliding message breakpoints do).

2. Concurrent fan-out. A cache entry only becomes readable once the first response BEGINS STREAMING. K subagents launched simultaneously share the same preamble and tool block, so all K pay the write instead of 1 write + K-1 reads.

Neither is confirmed to fire in practice — and neither should be 'fixed' blind. Add the instrument first: warn when a turn deep into a session reports cache_read_input_tokens == 0, carrying the message-block count so the lookback case is distinguishable from a cold start.

Then decide on evidence whether either needs a code change.

title: dirge sandbox check pkg-config probe never fires on macOS
description:
check.rs:333 derives the pkg-config package name with name.trim_start_matches("lib").trim_end_matches(".dylib"), turning libkrun.dylib into 'krun' — but the metadata file is libkrun.pc and the package is 'libkrun'. So pkg-config --exists krun always fails. Worse for libkrunfw: LIBKRUNFW_LIB is libkrunfw.5.dylib, which becomes 'krunfw.5'.

build.rs:19-23 carries a comment warning about exactly this ('strip only the extension, NOT the lib prefix, or pkg-config always misses'); check.rs never got the fix. Not fatal — the probe falls through to the brew --prefix and fixed-dir checks — but it is dead code on every macOS machine, and it is the drift check.rs:30-35 already warns about, invisible because CI has no macOS runner (dirge-u35k).

title: microVM runner link failure is an opaque wall of undefined symbols
description:
When libkrun is absent, build.rs emits no link directives and dirge-microvm-runner fails to link with ~40 lines of 'Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: _krun_create_ctx, _krun_set_exec, ...'. Documented as intended in docs/microvm/SETUP.md:59-62, but it is a terrible first contact — nothing in the output names libkrun as the cause.

Fix: build.rs emits cargo:rustc-cfg=krun_linked (plus cargo:rustc-check-cfg) when both libraries are found; src/bin/dirge-microvm-runner.rs gates its real main on #[cfg(krun_linked)] and compiles a stub under #[cfg(not(krun_linked))] that exits nonzero with 'built without libkrun — install libkrun and rebuild'. Build always succeeds; the failure becomes legible and moves to runtime where sandbox check already explains the fix.

title: Harness interventions have no uniform voice or visibility contract
description:
little-coder routes every scaffold override through one helper emitting 'harness intervention: <consequence>'. They built it after a single thinking-budget abort surfaced as several stacked warnings in different voices.

dirge has far more guards than they do, each with its own notice — and we already hit the sharper version: a work-tracking backstop that was SystemNotice, i.e. UI-only, so the model never saw it (types.rs:148).

Two wins:
  1. one shared constructor for the user-facing intervention line
  2. an explicit model-visible vs UI-only classification on every intervention, so 'the model never saw it' cannot recur silently

title: scavenge misses <tool_call> and fenced tool-call text formats
description:
scavenge.rs handles DSML invoke blocks and three JSON shapes. It does not handle:
  - <tool_call>...</tool_call> — Qwen/Hermes native text channel, the exact thing that leaks when llama.cpp is served without --jinja
  - fenced ```tool / ```json blocks

dirge supports ollama/lmstudio/llama.cpp, so the Qwen tag format is the most likely text-leak in practice and it currently falls through to no tool calls at all.

Port the extra patterns from little-coder's output-parser/parser.ts. Keep dirge's existing advantage: scavenged calls are validated via tool_input_repair at promotion and dropped when invalid (little-coder does not do this).

title: Compaction does not keep user messages verbatim
description: serialize_turns_for_summary (compression.rs:800) truncates user turns at 2000 chars before the summarizer sees them; apply_summary (:870) then deletes them entirely. Only the first user prompt survives, and only in the stored session. Mid-session constraints survive as paraphrase only -> small-model drift.

title: [bug] validate_summary too weak — a stub summary destroys the middle
description: compression.rs:829-836 passes any non-empty string containing one of four substrings. '## Active Task\nNone.' validates and apply_summary then drops the folded region for good. Needs section-coverage + non-trivial Active Task + length floor.

title: Compaction summary has no breadcrumb to the folded raw turns
description: SUMMARY_PREFIX (compression.rs:59-72) frames compaction as total loss; never names session_search or the parent session id. Model cannot know the raw turns are recoverable.

title: Syntax-gate reject message doesn't say the gate is universal — models escalate to a full-file rewrite
description:
DIAGNOSIS of a live trace: a model blocked by the pre-write syntax gate concluded 'the project tree-sitter parser does not understand doctest macro syntax and flags the whole file as invalid', then planned to 'bypass the guard by writing the entire file with write (which may or may not have syntax guard)', reconstructing a 385-line file from context.

Three findings, two of them refutations.

1. THE CLAIM IS FALSE. Added semantic::syntax_validator::tests::rust_doctest_and_macro_shapes_pass_the_guard covering seven shapes: doctest with hidden lines and asserts, a doctest fence containing unbalanced delimiters in prose, a fence containing a macro invocation, macro_rules! with repetition, a macro that generates doc comments, #[doc = include_str!(..)], and a raw string containing unbalanced delimiters. All pass. Its companion the_doctest_guard_check_can_still_fail confirms a broken body under a doctest is still rejected, so the check is not vacuous. The rejection the model hit was about its edit.

2. THE ESCAPE PLAN IS ALSO FALSE, AND THE TOOL NEVER SAYS SO. agent/tools/mod.rs:451 documents syntax_gate as 'the single choke point shared by EVERY content-writing edit tool (write/edit/edit_lines/edit_minified/apply_patch)', and write.rs:127 does call it. Switching from apply_patch to write cannot bypass anything. Nothing in the reject message or in any tool description says the gate is universal, so 'try the other tool' is the obvious next move and it is wrong — and the specific wrong move it leads to (rewrite the whole file from context) is the most destructive action available, and interacts badly with any read trimming (cf. dirge-09e8).

3. THE LEGITIMATE STAND-DOWN IS INVISIBLE. dirge-ytu1 already handles the case the model was afraid of: if the file ALREADY failed the check before the edit, the gate steps aside, writes verbatim, and returns GateNote::PreExisting. So a genuinely unparseable file is not uneditable. But that note only exists on the stand-down path; the REJECT path (format_errors, syntax_validator.rs:917) says only 'Syntax check failed ... Fix and re-submit. (This is a pre-write guard — the file was NOT modified.)'. A model facing a reject has no way to learn the guard is conditional, so it infers the guard is absolute and goes looking for a way around it.

PROPOSED FIX (small, deterministic, no model in the loop): extend the reject message with two facts it already knows — that this gate applies to every file-writing tool so switching tools will not avoid it, and that a file which was already failing before the edit is passed through automatically, so a reject means the edit introduced the error. Regression test asserting both sentences appear on a reject. This is a deterministic error string, not a prompt edit.

SEPARATE LATENT ISSUE FOUND WHILE READING, NOT VERIFIED: apply_patch.rs:161 hands the gate  as the baseline (LF-normalized, BOM-stripped) while judging  (BOM and original line endings restored by SourceText::reencode). If tree-sitter errors on a leading BOM, then on a BOM-carrying file the candidate would reject while the baseline reads clean, defeating the dirge-ytu1 stand-down and making the file permanently uneditable via apply_patch. edit.rs and edit_lines.rs pass the pre-edit content directly and are not obviously affected. Needs a test with a BOM'd fixture before it is treated as real.
notes: SEPARATE LATENT ISSUE, NOT VERIFIED (restating the paragraph mangled by shell backtick expansion on create): apply_patch.rs:161 hands the gate the variable "normalized" as the baseline -- LF-normalized, BOM-stripped -- while judging the variable "candidate", which is the text after SourceText::reencode has restored the BOM and the original line endings. If tree-sitter errors on a leading BOM, then on a BOM-carrying file the candidate rejects while the baseline reads clean, which defeats the dirge-ytu1 pre-existing stand-down and makes the file permanently uneditable via apply_patch. edit.rs:350 and edit_lines.rs:258 pass the pre-edit content directly and are not obviously affected. Needs a test with a BOM-carrying fixture before it is treated as real.
close_reason: Reject message now states the gate is universal and that a pre-broken file is passed through; BOM hypothesis refuted by test

title: loop-ab.sh mechanism check is blind to gates — nudges_fired is structurally 0 for every gate-only change
description:
docs/verification-discipline.md makes the mechanism check the first rule of measuring a loop-control change: 'A treatment arm showing zero did not exercise the change, and its deltas are noise.' The harness implements it as ONE number, nudges_fired (TSV col 17), built in run_arm by summing eight hardcoded nudge_* field names (loop-ab.sh:545-551).

Two gaps, both under-reporting:

(a) No gate_* field is scraped at all. The dirge::gates line carries gate_verifier, gate_critic, gate_goal, gate_todo, gate_open_issues (and should carry gate_claim_gate / gate_source_gate — see dirge-l8l7.1), and the TSV has no column for any of them. So an A/B of a FINALIZATION GATE — claim_gate, source_gate, publish_guard, the verifier gate — reads nudges_fired=0 in both arms. The mechanism check then says the change never fired, when in fact the harness cannot see the thing that fired. Read literally per the doc, every gate A/B ever run should have been discarded as noise.

(b) The eight nudge names are a hand-maintained copy of the emit() field list. They match today. A ninth BoundaryNudge variant would be silently excluded from the total, with nothing to notice — the identical failure mode as dirge-l8l7.1 one layer out.

Partial cover: boundaries= (col 19) does carry gate names, so co-occurrence sees gates. It is not summed into the mechanism check and is not what the report's 'mechanism' rows read.

FIX: derive both totals from the line itself — sum every field matching nudge_*= and every field matching gate_*= — and report gates_fired alongside nudges_fired. No hardcoded name list on either side. TEST: a synthetic gates line with an unknown nudge_/gate_ field must be counted.

title: loop-ab.sh: control-vs-treatment comparison has no absent-arm guard — one missing arm aborts the whole report
description:
scripts/loop-ab.sh reporting awk, per-model two-arm section (lines 764-767): success_rate and green_rate divide by n[ck] and n[tk] unguarded. A model present in the results TSV under one arm and not the other kills awk with 'division by zero' at that record and NO report is produced at all — after a multi-model, multi-repeat run that can take hours. The raw TSV survives (run_arm appends), so the data is recoverable; the run's output is not.

The N-arm block twenty lines below has exactly this guard, with a comment naming the hazard: 'every rate below divides by n[ek], so proceeding would divide by zero and abort the whole report. Reporting the absence rather than skipping silently is the same discipline as tally=missing.' The guard was written for the extra arms and never applied to the primary pair.

MEASURED: a fixture with control+treatment for m1/m2 and control-only for m3 gives 'awk: division by zero, input record number 7, source line number 93' and no output.

Not reachable through a clean run of the script today (run_arm always appends a row for both arms), which is why it has never been seen. Reachable on an interrupted run, a re-run appending into an existing results.tsv, or a hand-assembled TSV.

FIX: apply the same absent-arm guard to the primary pair, reporting the absence. TEST: the fixture above must produce a report.

title: loop-ab.sh: co-occurrence events reported in awk hash order, not run order — and the selftest locks in the scrambled order
description:
scripts/loop-ab.sh:660, 'for (i in evs)' after split($19, evs, ";"). awk's in-operator iteration order is unspecified, so the order events are first seen — which is the order evlist keeps and the report prints — is hash order, not run order.

MEASURED on BWK awk 20200816, the macOS default and the only awk on this box: a boundaries field of 'A;B;C;D;E' reports as 'B x1, C x1, D x1, E x1, A x1'.

boundaries_encoding() documents its output as 'in run order', and the tally records members in order deliberately (gate_tally.rs:183-216). The reporter throws that away.

Worse: loop-ab-selftest.sh:76 asserts '^  co-occurrence allgates: Critic x2, Verifier x2$' for a fixture whose input is 'Verifier;Critic'. The expected value IS the scrambled order — the assertion encodes the bug as the contract, and would fail on gawk or mawk, which hash differently.

FIX: iterate 'for (i = 1; i <= n; i++)' over the split count. TEST: assert reported order matches input order, which is the assertion that currently fails.

title: Replan instead of stopping when the /plan reviewer exhausts its fix cycles
description:
agent/plan/workflow.rs:390 next_review_step returns ReviewStep::Exhausted when the fix-cycle budget runs out, and the loop simply stops with the work unfinished. The plan itself is never revisited — if the plan was wrong, repeated implement-retries against it cannot converge.

The data4sci writeup's PlannerAgent.replan() feeds structured failure context (which node failed, with what args, and the error) back to the planner for an amended plan. dirge already has the fork for this: revise_plan_prompt (workflow.rs:291) was built for user edits at the approval gate and takes request/findings/prior-plan/feedback. Pointing it at reviewer feedback instead of user feedback reuses the whole path.
design: On Exhausted, if a replan budget remains: run the revise fork with the reviewer's accumulated 'missing' punch-lists as FEEDBACK, then restart the implement+review loop against the amended plan. Cap replans separately from fix cycles so the two budgets cannot multiply into an unbounded run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exhausted triggers one replan pass when budget remains, rather than stopping
- Reviewer punch-lists are carried into the revise fork as feedback
- Replan budget is separate from and does not multiply the fix-cycle budget
- Exhausting the replan budget stops cleanly, as today

title: Classify tool errors into recovery classes, not one undifferentiated streak
description:
Provider errors get six-way classification (recovery.rs:45 ErrorKind, with Retry-After parsing). Tool errors get none: every failure funnels into failure_tracker.rs as an undifferentiated consecutive-failure streak that produces one generic reflection nudge.

The data4sci writeup's four classes map onto machinery dirge already owns:
- TOOL_MISUSE (bad args) -> tool_input_repair (exists)
- TRANSIENT (timeout, EAGAIN) -> retry with backoff. Exists for provider errors, ABSENT for tools: a timed-out tool result goes straight back to the model with no retry.
- MISSING_INFO (file not found, unknown symbol) -> should trigger re-explore/re-plan, currently just increments the streak
- FATAL (permission denied, policy) -> should stop, currently just increments the streak

failure_tracker already weights timeouts 2x, which is the first step of this by another name.

Related: dirge-opdt (cross-turn failure recovery + better error feedback for weaker models).
design: Classify at the point the tool result is recorded (failure_tracker::record_result already sees is_error, tool_name, excerpt). Route by class rather than counting uniformly, and make the nudge text specific to the dominant class — '3 file-not-found errors in a row, your path model is wrong' beats '3 tool calls have failed'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool errors classified into at least transient/misuse/missing-info/fatal
- Transient tool failures retried with backoff before reaching the model
- Fatal (permission-denied) failures do not accumulate toward the reflection streak
- Nudge text names the dominant failure class
- Unclassified errors behave exactly as today
notes:
FIRST SLICE LANDED (228605d9). Classification + class-aware checkpoint.

Done:
- ErrorClass {Misuse, MissingInfo, Transient, Fatal, Unclassified} with a
  conservative classifier anchored on wording the tools and OS actually emit.
- Precedence is explicit and tested: Fatal > Transient > Misuse > MissingInfo.
  Real error strings routinely match two patterns -- a permission error usually
  contains a path, a timeout can name a file -- so first-match ordering IS the
  rule, and each pair has a two-pattern test.
- The recovery checkpoint names the dominant class and gives the instruction
  that fits it. A missing-info streak is told to stop calling and go look, which
  is the one thing the previous three generic questions never suggested.
- Dominance is a STRICT MAJORITY. A plurality would give confident direction
  about a minority of the streak.
- Unclassified never dominates; an unrecognised streak is byte-identical to
  before, which was the non-regression criterion.

ALREADY DONE BEFORE THIS, found while reading rather than rebuilt:
'Fatal (permission-denied) failures do not accumulate toward the reflection
streak' was closed by dirge-iwwq -- Outcome::Denied already has its own streak
and its own permission checkpoint. The ErrorClass::Fatal added here is the
OS-level EACCES case, which is a different thing from a policy denial.

SECOND SLICE LANDED as dirge-s9ry (0df85394, closed): ErrorClass feeds
capability.rs. MissingInfo weighted 2 against 1 for every other class, the
weight swept rather than guessed -- 2 is the only integer that catches both
measured blowups without branding the three grounding runs that finished the
task. See dirge-s9ry notes for the sweep, the tally restructure, and two bugs
found on the way (invented tool names double-counting into missing-info; the
A/B report's hand-maintained numeric-column list).

STILL NOT DONE:
- Transient retry-with-backoff before the result reaches the model. That is a
  behaviour change to the dispatch path rather than a classification change, and
  it wants its own slice with its own test for the retry budget. This is the
  only acceptance criterion still open.
THIRD SLICE LANDED (ff7882b8): transient retry-with-backoff. ALL acceptance criteria now met.

Gated on the TOOL, not the error. A timeout does not mean the work did not happen -- a bash command killed at its budget may have run to completion (the dirge-e31n.5 Unknown state) -- so only Operation::Read is eligible: read/grep/glob/list_dir plus the whole LSP family, which is where transient tool failures actually come from (a server still indexing).

Positive allowlist over an exhaustive match on Operation, so a new variant is non-retryable until someone argues otherwise. Deliberately does NOT reuse Operation::is_side_effecting -- that answers 'should the loop guard gate repetition of this', and under it Operation::Other (unknown MCP/plugin tools) and Operation::Memory both read non-side-effecting. Borrowing a predicate that answers a neighbouring question is the same error class as reading a Strong tier to relax a verification guard.

3 attempts, 250/500ms backoff (short: it sits inside a turn the user waits on), backoff races the abort signal.

MEASUREMENT: retry_stats on LoopConfig beside repair_stats (dispatch cannot reach the tally), latched at run end, emitted as tool_retries_attempted/tool_retries_recovered. Deliberately NO loop-ab column: the A/B scenarios do not produce transient read failures, so it would read zero forever and look like a healthy mechanism gate. This slice is verified by tests, not by A/B, and that is stated rather than papered over.

MUTATION TESTING FOUND A REDUNDANT GUARD. An is_cancelled() early-return after the call survived its mutation -- the backoff cancel-race already covered every path reaching it, AND the early return was slightly wrong: it discarded the recovery attribution for a retry that HAD succeeded before the run was cancelled. Deleted; the race is the single encoding. Same lesson as dirge-2m68: a mutation that changes no behaviour finds a redundant condition, not a missing test. It also exposed that the first cancellation test could not discriminate (the abort message is not transient, so the class gate refused it regardless); replaced with a tool that cancels from inside execute and returns transient text.

7 mutations killed with controls. 5246 tests, clippy clean.
close_reason: All four acceptance criteria met across three slices (228605d9, 0df85394, ff7882b8)

title: Structured per-step trace export (--trace out.jsonl)
description:
GateTally::emit and the dirge::gates tracing target give good aggregate signal, but there is no durable per-step record. Nothing answers 'which tool dominated wall time this run' or lets the A/B harness diff two harness versions on the same task.

From the data4sci advanced-harness writeup: a flat TraceEvent schema is enough — you do not need a proprietary format to get real observability, just a sufficient schema.
design:
One JSONL record per step with: step_id, parent_id (links a tool call back to the turn/gate that spawned it), timestamp, role (turn|tool|gate|critic|subagent), action {type, tool, args-digest}, result digest, latency_ms, tokens, cost_usd, budget_pressure, verdict (for gate/critic steps).

The events already exist (AgentEvent, GateTally, verifier/critic verdicts) — only the schema and the sink are missing. Gate behind a --trace <path> flag so default runs are unchanged.

Depends on dirge-i2st for the cost_usd and budget_pressure columns to be non-zero; the rest can land first.
acceptance_criteria:
- --trace <path> emits one flat JSON record per step
- Records carry parent_id so tool calls attribute to their turn
- Latency and token columns populated; cost/pressure populated once dirge-i2st lands
- No trace flag = no file, no measurable overhead

title: Give the critic an evidence block and have it check claims against it
description:
run_unified_review (src/agent/agent_loop/critic.rs:624-630) ALREADY receives the transcript, the run diff, and the final VerificationStatus, and renders a verification_block into its prompt. What is missing is the instruction to use them as a check on the assistant's factual claims about its own actions.

CRITIC_PREAMBLE (critic.rs:232) says 'Judge ONLY whether the task is actually complete and correct within those constraints — not style.' Nothing asks whether the claims are supported.

Two changes:
1. Add a deterministic evidence block to the critic prompt: files mutated this run, verification commands observed and their outcomes, tool-call count.
2. Extend CRITIC_PREAMBLE to flag claims the evidence does not support.

This covers what the deterministic sibling gate cannot: 'I applied the two awk fixes' when the diff shows no edit to that file.

Sharpen the existing critic pass rather than adding a second one — dirge-1elu's ablation finding is that stacked gates competing for the same turns give back most of their individual gains.

title: Deterministic claim/evidence gate: unsupported verification claims at finalization
description:
At finalization, compare the final answer against observed run state and fire when a specific claim has no supporting evidence:

- the answer asserts a verification outcome (a test count like 'N passed'/'N tests', or an explicit 'clippy clean' / 'tests pass' / 'all green' / 'fmt clean') AND the verifier recorded no verification command this run
- the answer asserts having applied/fixed/changed something AND zero files mutated this run

Deliver as a model-visible tagged LoopMessage::User, one-shot, matching the existing verifier nudges. Per dirge-1elu.4 it must NOT be a bare SystemNotice — the model never sees those.

Deterministic and no LLM, deliberately: a model asked to detect lying can be talked out of it or can invent accusations. A regex over 'N passed' conjoined with 'the verifier observed zero verification commands' cannot.

Over-detection is the bounding risk and the conjunction is what controls it. A specific numeric or named-gate claim together with zero observed verifications is very unlikely to be innocent. The plausible false positive is the model quoting someone else's earlier output; carve that out if it shows up in practice.

Needs measuring with scripts/loop-ab.sh before it goes anywhere near default-on, per docs/verification-discipline.md's mechanism check.

title: [bug] h7_cerebras smoke test asserts on live-model phrasing — flaky 1-in-5 on a clean tree
description:
`h7_cerebras_tool_dispatch_completes_round_trip` asserts on the wording a LIVE model
returns, so it fails whenever the model paraphrases instead of quoting the tool result.

Measured on a CLEAN tree (no local changes), 5 consecutive runs: 4 passed, 1 failed.
Reproduced during unrelated work on dirge-1elu.1; confirmed pre-existing by stashing all
changes and re-running.

Failure:

    thread '...h7_cerebras_tool_dispatch_completes_round_trip' panicked at
    src/agent/agent_loop/h7_smoke.rs:1220:
    expected final response to use the completed tool result:
    "The word has been echoed successfully."

The tool round trip actually SUCCEEDED — the transcript shows `[tool_result] 15 bytes`,
then the model summarized the result in prose rather than echoing the literal token the
assertion greps for. So the assertion tests the model's phrasing, not dirge's dispatch.

This is docs/verification-discipline.md's own pattern, one row over from
"Prerequisite as outcome": a check whose red does not mean what it says. The dispatch
mechanism under test worked; the gate went red on a stylistic coin flip. Per that page,
"A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, because it is trusted" — and its inverse
applies here too: a gate that fails for reasons unrelated to its subject trains everyone
to ignore it.

Fix direction: assert on the STRUCTURE the test is actually about — that a tool_result
was produced, consumed, and that a final assistant turn followed it — not on whether the
model quoted a specific string. If the literal echo genuinely matters, the model must be
instructed to echo verbatim and the assertion should say so.

Two related observations while in there, worth deciding on separately:

- These h7_smoke tests hit live providers on a plain `cargo nextest run --bin dirge`.
  Observed runtimes in the same 5-run sample ranged 0.5s to 62s, i.e. real network
  latency. A default test run should probably not depend on a paid third-party endpoint
  being up and fast; consider gating behind a feature or an env check that SKIPS (not
  fails) when unset.
- dirge-8kag already tracks a different breakage in this same module (DeepSeek retired
  the deepseek-chat model name). Same root shape: live-provider coupling in the default
  suite. Consider handling both together.

title: Advisory gates emit SystemNotice only — the model never sees them
description:
Some harness gates emit a bare LoopEvent::SystemNotice and nothing else. SystemNotice is
a UI/stream event — the model never sees it. Those gates fire, render to the user, and
change nothing about what the model does next.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4 §C.1.4, §C.2.4)

This is the exact failure AHE measured and fixed at iteration 8, and it is worth reading
closely because the WARNING TEXT WAS ALREADY CORRECT:

  "polyglot-c-py and pytorch-model-recovery failed at iteration 7 with a different but
  related symptom: the iteration-6 middleware had already emitted the right warnings
  about clean-layout violation and inline-helper validation, but the warnings were
  appended only to the tool output, and on the very next model turn the agent ignored
  them and published."

The iteration-8 fix (§C.2.4 chg-2) added a `before_model` hook that promotes any risk note
