emitted on the previous step into a FRAMEWORK reminder visible in the next model turn,
"so the warning becomes part of the reasoning context rather than text appended after the
tool output." polyglot-c-py, polyglot-rust-c, pytorch-model-recovery and mteb-retrieve all
flipped via that path. Same detector, same text, different delivery.

The paper's own summary of the pair: "chg-1 prevents the destructive shell command itself,
chg-2 fixes the salience gap of the iteration-6 middleware."

## dirge status

dirge has already learned this once. The general mechanism is right:
- src/agent/agent_loop/run.rs:191 `emit_harness_notices` — messages injected as
  USER-role LoopMessages get MIRRORED to a SystemNotice for headless consumers. Model
  sees the message, user sees the notice. Correct.

But there are emit sites that send the notice with no accompanying message:
- src/agent/agent_loop/run.rs:950 — open-issues gate, GateMode::Advisory arm
- src/agent/agent_loop/run.rs:1013 — untracked-work advisory

And GateMode::Advisory is the DEFAULT (src/agent/agent_loop/types.rs, `#[derive(Default)]`
on the Advisory variant), documented as "surface findings/reminders as a non-blocking
SystemNotice". So the default configuration of every advisory gate — code-review,
open-issues, and per the doc comment "any future opt-in finalization gate" — has the
salience gap the paper measured.

Note: the sibling publish-state issue must not be built on a notice-only path, or it
reproduces iteration 6 rather than iteration 8.

## Scope

Audit every LoopEvent::SystemNotice emit site. For each, decide deliberately: is this
FYI-for-the-human (a notice alone is right) or is it steering the model (needs a
model-visible message, which then mirrors to a notice for free)?

Do not blanket-convert. A notice that becomes a message costs a turn's attention and
prompt budget, and the epic's non-additivity finding says stacking closure-style nudges
has a real cost — the paper's three positive single-component swaps summed to +11.1pp but
stacked delivered only +7.3pp. Each conversion needs its own justification.

Then document the distinction so the next gate author picks correctly. GateMode's doc
comment currently describes Advisory purely in terms of SystemNotice, which is what
steered these sites wrong.

## Acceptance

- An enumeration of every SystemNotice emit site with a per-site verdict (steer vs FYI).
- For each site converted: a test that the model-visible message is actually present in
  the next request's messages, not merely emitted as an event. Per
  docs/verification-discipline.md's "Signal never fed" row — test the function the
  production path calls. A test that constructs the message and asserts on it directly
  would pass while the wiring stays broken.
- For each site left as a notice: a one-line rationale in the code or the doc.
- No change to what the human sees in either the TUI or headless output.
notes:
Enumeration done (2026-08-04). Four real LoopEvent::SystemNotice emit sites; bridge.rs:161 and message.rs:748 only handle/name the variant.

1. run.rs:199 emit_harness_notices — MIRROR of an already-injected LoopMessage::User. Correct by construction. FYI. No change.
2. run.rs:950 open-issues gate, GateMode::Advisory arm — NOTICE-ONLY. Text is a steer ('close or defer them when done'). GAP.
3. run.rs:1013 untracked-work advisory — NOTICE-ONLY. Text is a steer ('add it with write_todo_list and mark it in_progress'). GAP.
4. run.rs:3090 max_turns truncation — notice-only and CORRECT: the run is ending, there is no next model turn to steer. No change.

CORRECTION to this bead's premise: code-review's Advisory arm does NOT have the gap. run.rs:735-737 is explicit — 'Any finding — even medium/low — re-enters the loop so the model actually sees and acts on it, rather than a display-only notice it never reads.' dirge already learned this for code review. Scope is sites 2 and 3 only.

Root cause of the two wrong sites: GateMode's doc comment in types.rs describes Advisory as 'surface findings/reminders as a non-blocking SystemNotice. It never re-enters the loop' — but code_review's Advisory arm DOES inject messages. The sites that followed the doc comment literally got it wrong. The doc comment needs fixing as part of this.

title: Masked-command guard misses non-fail-fast multi-step validation blocks
description:
dirge's masked-command guard catches the exit-status-hiding shapes (`| tail`, `|| true`,
`;`-chained). It does not catch a multi-step validation block whose exit status is
honestly 0 while a mismatch scrolled past in the output.

## The shape

    diff expected.txt actual.txt
    cmp -s a.bin b.bin
    test -f out/report.json
    echo "all checks passed"

Every assertion runs, one of them prints a mismatch, none of them stops the block, and
the exit status belongs to the `echo`. dirge records VerifiedGreen. The existing guard is
looking for a pipeline or a `|| true` and finds neither, because there isn't one — the
status is genuinely 0.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4, evolved harness middleware)

Shipped as an execution-risk pattern in the evolved harness
(experiments/evolved_harness/middleware/execution_risk_hints.py,
`_looks_like_non_failfast_validation`, priority 46). The note it emits:

  "This validation script chains diff/cmp-style assertions inside a multi-step shell
  block without an explicit fail-fast guard. One hidden mismatch can still be followed by
  a misleading 'passed' line and exit 0."

The detection is conjunctive and deliberately narrow, which is what keeps it from firing
on ordinary work: validation-ish description or command, AND a diff/cmp/test -f/grep -q
assertion, AND no `set -e` / `|| exit` / `trap ... exit`, AND multi-step (newline, `;`,
or a loop), AND a success sentinel or echo/printf at the end.

The same rule reached the evolved system prompt as an explicit line (systemprompt.md:28):
"Custom validation scripts must fail fast. Use `set -e` or explicit non-zero exits for
every diff/cmp/assertion, and if any expected-vs-actual mismatch appears in the output,
treat the validation as failed even if the script later prints `passed` or exits 0."

## dirge status

docs/verification-discipline.md, "Masked-command guard" — the closest existing machinery,
and the right place to extend. Its stated design rule applies directly here: "A masked
command reporting success is now not recorded at all: the status stays Unverified... 'We
don't know' is the honest answer." Same treatment fits this shape.

Note the doc's own warning against over-detection: "Over-detecting would decline good
verifications and nag forever, which is the same harm pointed the other way." Keep the
conjunction narrow. `&&`-chained assertions are NOT this shape — `&&` short-circuits, so
a failing assertion IS the exit status, exactly as the existing guard already reasons.

## Scope

Extend the masked-command detection to the non-fail-fast multi-step validation block.
Same failure direction as the existing guard: success is not recorded, failure still is.

## Acceptance

- A test with the exact failing shape above (newline-separated diff + trailing echo,
  exit 0) that currently latches VerifiedGreen and must not after.
- A test that `diff a b && echo passed` STILL latches green — short-circuit means the
  status is honest, and declining it would be the over-detection the doc warns about.
- A test that a block carrying `set -e` still latches green.
- A test that an ordinary non-validation multi-step command (a build script, a
  multi-line cargo invocation) is untouched.
notes:
Spec deviation (reviewed 2026-08-04): after reading src/agent/agent_loop/verifier.rs:551 masks_failure, the defect is narrower and more certain than this bead assumed. masks_failure handles ';' but not its exact bash synonym '
' — the segment splitter feeding is_verification_command already treats '& | ; 
' as separators (comment at verifier.rs:839); masks_failure was written against the same grammar and missed one. So the fix is to treat '
' as ';' (with a backslash-continuation carve-out), NOT the broader conjunctive pattern matcher from the AHE middleware. The narrow fix subsumes the target shape and is far less likely to over-fire. See scratchpad spec-3.md.
Same defect found in a SECOND place during review of dirge-1elu.1: publish_guard.rs tokenize()/detect_discard() splits segments on '&&','||',';','|' but treats '
' as ordinary whitespace, so 'echo hi
rm out.json' returns Pass — the guard is bypassed by a newline. Proven with a failing probe test. Both sites are the same bash-grammar oversight and are being fixed together.

title: [bug] 'allow always' on a substitution/subshell command saves a rule that can never fire
description:
SessionAllowlistPolicy::decide (permission/engine/policies.rs:193-200) returns None for any complex command (command/process substitution, subshell, arithmetic expansion) — by design, dirge-g9qj: the inner command is invisible so a broad head grant like 'echo *' must not cover 'echo $(rm -rf ~)'.

The UI doesn't know that. Pressing 'a' on 'echo $(date)' still renders '-> will allow: echo *' and 'allowed bash echo * (saved to session)', writes the entry to the session allowlist and persists it — and the identical command prompts again on the very next invocation, forever. The affordance lies, and the dead entry accumulates in the saved session.

Same user-visible symptom as dirge-mirm (found alongside it), different root cause: there the pattern was subsumed by an existing rule, here no pattern of that shape is honored at all.

Fix: detect the complex case at suggestion time and downgrade to allow-once with an honest reason, reusing the existing placeholder path the empty-input case already takes.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing 'allow always' on a substitution/subshell command allows once and says why, rather than saving an entry that cannot match.

title: eval_waits_for_an_in_flight_confirm_past_the_base_timeout is still flaky on loaded CI
description:
src/plugin/worker.rs. Failed 'build (all-features)' on PR #740 (run 30720225929), then PASSED on --failed rerun of the SAME commit with no changes. Identical input, different outcome -- a flake by demonstration, not by inference.

    assertion `left == right` failed: eval must wait for the confirm answer
    instead of timing out, got Err("janet worker did not reply within 1s")
      left: Err(...)  right: Ok("true")

Passes 10/10 locally in isolation, which is the wrong environment: isolation removes exactly the parallel load that causes it.

## This is the second time

Fixed once already in #720 (ec88f762), which warmed up the worker, raised CONFIRM_BASE_BUDGET from 100ms to 750ms, and stated 'passes 12/12 with all cores saturated'. It flaked again anyway. The first failure reported 'did not reply within 0s' at a 100ms budget; this one 'within 1s' at 750ms. Same shape, one order of magnitude up.

## Why no constant fixes it

The timeout extension only engages if `dialog_pending` is already set when the base budget expires. So the test requires the worker to receive Cmd::Eval, start Janet, and enter harness/confirm within CONFIRM_BASE_BUDGET. That latency is unbounded under nextest parallel load on a shared runner -- it is scheduler-dependent, not work-dependent. Raising the budget lowers the failure RATE and cannot reach zero, and every raise also lengthens the test (CONFIRM_ANSWER_DELAY must stay above the budget, so the test's floor is budget + delay; it is already ~1.5-2.2s).

The test is racing a wall clock against work whose latency has no bound. #720's own commit message says precisely this about the tests it fixed, then fixed this one by picking a bigger number.

## Recommended fix

Stop racing. Split the two things the test currently conflates:

1. THE DECISION -- 'when the base budget expires and dialog_pending is set, extend rather than time out.' That is a pure predicate over (elapsed, dialog_pending) and can be unit-tested with no worker, no Janet VM, and no wall clock. This is the pattern the repo already uses for exactly this reason (should_advise_untracked_work, should_nudge_fast_verify, option_select_action).
2. THE WIRING -- one end-to-end smoke that a confirm round-trips, asserting only the RESULT, never a duration.

Then no test asserts 'the worker got somewhere within N milliseconds', which is the unbounded quantity.

## Why it is worth doing rather than re-raising the budget again

A gate that goes red for reasons unrelated to the change trains people to re-run instead of read -- which is the same failure this repo documents in docs/verification-discipline.md from the other direction. A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate; a gate that fails at random is how you get there.

Found on PR #740 (capability tier), unrelated to that change -- filed rather than folded in, since a fix touches the Janet worker's concurrency and does not belong in a capability-estimator PR. See also dirge-ntjh for adjacent worker-lifecycle work.
notes: If the pure-predicate split turns out to need worker internals exposed, an acceptable interim is to gate the test behind an ignore-by-default flag and run it in a serial nextest profile -- but that is second best, since it stops guarding the extension on every CI run.
close_reason:
Fixed in b6feee2c on branch fix-worker-timeout-flake.

Split the test into the two things it conflated, as recommended:

1. THE DECISION -> timeout_action(dialog_active, elapsed, ceiling) -> KeepWaiting | GiveUp. A free function, total over three values, no worker/VM/clock. Truth table is exhaustive: the one extending case, both no-dialog cases, past-ceiling with a dialog pending, the strict-< boundary at exactly the ceiling, and a zero ceiling.

2. THE WIRING -> dialog_pending_is_set_while_a_confirm_is_in_flight. Samples the flag at the instant the helper receives the DialogRequest. Clock-free, because DialogPendingGuard::enter() (worker.rs:1654) happens-before tx.send(req) (:1657), so holding the request proves the counter is incremented. Also asserts the guard is released afterwards. This half matters: without it the predicate could be perfectly correct and the security gate still fail open, which was the original dirge-hwzs bug.

VERIFIED BY MUTATION rather than by a green run -- #720 claimed 12/12 under saturation and still flaked, so a passing hammer proves little. Three mutations, each caught:
  - ceiling comparison < -> <=            FAILS (boundary case)
  - dialog_active && -> ||                FAILS
  - DialogPendingGuard::enter() deleted   FAILS with the fail-open message
The old test caught only the third. So this is strictly better coverage as well as deterministic.

Also 15/15 with all 10 cores saturated, and the end-to-end half drops from ~1.5s to ~0.03s.

NOT changed, deliberately: the other two duration assertions in the file are a different shape. eval_without_a_dialog_still_times_out_at_the_base bounds a give-up expected at ~150ms against a 5s bound (the alternative outcome is the ~630s dialog ceiling, so the bound is nowhere near tight) and load pushes it the SAFE way -- load makes a timeout more likely, not less. The shutdown test starts its clock only after the dialog request has landed, so the unbounded part is already over. The flaky shape is specifically 'require unbounded work to complete inside a tight bound'; neither of those does that.

title: Release process silently skips channels: 0.20.0 never reached crates.io or the site
description:
v0.20.0 shipped to 4 of 6 distribution channels and nobody noticed until the 0.21.0 release.

Measured 2026-08-01:
  tag v0.20.0            YES
  GitHub release+binaries YES (workflow, automatic)
  nix/bin.nix            YES (workflow, automatic)
  homebrew formula       YES (manual, was done)
  crates.io publish      NO  -- registry goes 0.19.29 -> 0.21.0, no 0.20.0
  site brand-ver         NO  -- index.html still read v0.19.29, so it had ALSO missed 0.20.0

Net effect: 'cargo install dirge-agent' users never got 0.20.0 (the DS1 agent-loop work). 0.21.0 contains it, so there is no outstanding user-facing gap, but the failure was silent in both directions -- nothing failed, nothing warned, and the two skipped channels are exactly the two that are MANUAL.

The automated channels (release.yml binaries, the nix bump action) both fired correctly. The manual ones are where it went wrong, and the same shape as the fmt miss in dirge-5mtx.6 FM-6: a checklist that is a habit rather than a gate, where the steps that get skipped are the ones nothing checks.

## Change

Either automate the two manual steps or make skipping them loud:
  - crates.io publish is a natural release.yml job (cargo publish on tag, needs CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN as a repo secret). This is the important one -- it is a real distribution channel.
  - the site bump could be a repository_dispatch to dirge-code.github.io from the same workflow, or just dropped in favour of reading the version from the GitHub API at page load.
  - homebrew is currently manual because it needs the release sha256s; it could be a post-release job that reads them back from the release assets.

If any stay manual, publishing.md should carry a checklist that lists all six and the release should not be considered done until each is ticked -- but automation is better than a longer list, since the list existing is not what failed.
notes: publishing.md documents crates.io publish (steps 3-5) and the site bump (step 7) but as prose, not a checklist. Homebrew and nix are not mentioned in it at all.
close_reason:
Landed on branch z85a-failure-threshold-per-poll (d5d195ea).

Both manual channels automated in release.yml, per the corrected 3-for-3 / 0-for-2 split in the comment:
  - crates-io: cargo publish on tag. Gates on the tag matching Cargo.toml first (a mismatch would put the wrong version on the registry PERMANENTLY, and no later check can undo it). Idempotent -- 'already uploaded' is treated as success so re-running a completed release is clean. needs: build, because publishing is permanent and a tag that does not compile on all five targets should not become an immovable registry entry. Secret: CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN.
  - site: rewrites the brand-ver span in dirge-code.github.io, mirroring the homebrew job. Secret: SITE_REPO_TOKEN. (You picked automate-the-bump over dropping the channel via a GitHub API fetch at page load.)

Third job, and the one that actually closes the issue: verify-channels. Automating the two manual steps only converts 'someone forgot' into 'a job silently no-opped' -- both the homebrew and site steps rewrite markup with sed, and an unmatched sed exits 0, after which 'nothing to do' reads as success. verify-channels ignores job status and reads PUBLISHED STATE back: crates.io sparse index, tap formula, site span, nix/bin.nix on main, and every expected release asset with its checksum. Any disagreement with the tag is a red X on the release run.

Verified against real releases rather than assumed (FM-3: a check whose inputs are all defaults cannot discriminate):
  - v0.21.1 -> exit 0, all six channels ok
  - v0.20.0 -> exit 1, names crates.io specifically. That is this bug, reproduced.
  - site sed guard -> exit 1 when the span's class is renamed
  - tag/manifest guard -> exit 1 on v0.99.0 against a 0.21.1 manifest, exit 0 on v0.21.1

One bug found and fixed in the verification job while writing it: 'gh api ... | grep -q' looks correct and is not. grep -q exits on first match, gh takes SIGPIPE, and pipefail reports the pipeline as failed -- a missing-channel error for a channel that is fine. It only surfaced on index.html, the one input long enough to still be streaming when grep exits; the nix and homebrew files are small enough to complete first. Fixed by fetching to a file, then matching. Worth remembering: it is the same shape as the failures in docs/verification-discipline.md -- a check that reported the wrong thing for a reason unrelated to what it was checking.

publishing.md rewritten. It documented a manual process that no longer exists; it is now a channel table, the two-step release (bump Cargo.toml, push the tag), the secrets, and a by-hand fallback for when the workflow is broken.

Note the new jobs cannot run until CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and SITE_REPO_TOKEN exist as repo secrets on dirge-code/dirge. Without them those jobs fail loudly on the next tag; the binary release is unaffected.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the description: Homebrew is NOT manual. Every formula bump back through 0.19.26 is authored by github-actions[bot], including 0.21.0, which landed on its own with sha256s identical to the ones I fetched and verified against the tarballs by hand. I inferred 'manual' from the plain 'dirge 0.20.0' commit subjects without checking the author, and pushed a redundant duplicate commit before noticing (reset, not on the remote).

That makes the finding SHARPER, not weaker. Corrected channel status for v0.20.0:

  tag                     manual   OK
  GitHub release+binaries automated OK
  nix/bin.nix             automated OK
  homebrew formula        automated OK
  crates.io publish       MANUAL   SKIPPED
  site brand-ver          MANUAL   SKIPPED

Every automated channel fired. Both manual channels were skipped. It is a clean 3-for-3 and 0-for-2 split, so the fix is unambiguous: automate the remaining two rather than write a better checklist. cargo publish on tag in release.yml is the important half -- it is the only skipped channel that is a real distribution path.

The homebrew workflow is also the working model to copy: it already reads the release assets back after the binary jobs finish, which is exactly the shape a publish job or a site-bump dispatch would need.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION on v0.21.2 (released 2026-08-02, run on tag eb136f9d).

All six channels landed on the first fully-automated release. Verified independently of verify-channels rather than taking its green at face value:
  crates.io   0.21.0 0.21.1 0.21.2  (contiguous — contrast the 0.19.29 -> 0.21.0 gap this issue is about)
  homebrew    version "0.21.2"
  site        brand-ver">v0.21.2
  nix on main version = "0.21.2"
  release     11 assets (5 archives + 5 checksums + sbom)

The two jobs that had never run before — crates-io and site — both succeeded unattended. verify-channels emitted all 15 'ok:' lines, so it ran its checks rather than passing vacuously; that mattered to check, since a job that silently no-ops is the exact failure it was written to catch.

STILL UNEXERCISED: the crates.io sparse-index retry loop. The index had 0.21.2 on the first probe, so the CDN-lag path (10 attempts, 30s apart) has never run. If a future release fails verify-channels on crates.io alone while the publish job succeeded, suspect that loop before suspecting the publish.

title: awaiting_user_response: replace hand-rolled heuristic with a classifier
description:
Depends on .3 (ClassifyFn).

`awaiting_user_response` (run.rs:3060-3115, plus `is_option_list_line`
run.rs:3121 and `option_marker_len` run.rs:3131) answers "is the model blocked
on the user?" with ~55 lines of text heuristics: join Text blocks, bail on an odd
number of ``` fences, walk backwards past blank and option-list lines, strip
trailing `*_`)]"'>` decoration, then test whether what's left ends in `?`.

It is gate 0 in `poll_finalization_follow_up` (run.rs:563-601) and outranks
everything except the goal gate. When it returns true the run finalizes
immediately — the verifier, critic, todo, and open-issues gates are all skipped
for that boundary. The doc comment says exactly why that's wanted (run.rs:563-
567): a model blocked on the user shouldn't be re-entered until it "gives up
waiting and guesses".

The failure is asymmetric and invisible. A false positive silently disables the
entire finalization gate stack, and skipping a gate produces no output, so
nothing in the transcript shows it happened. Cases that trip it today:

  - work finished, turn closes with "Want me to add tests too?"
  - any turn ending on a rhetorical question
  - a summary whose last meaningful line happens to be a question

"Blocked on the user" vs "offering a next step" is a semantic distinction. It is
the paper's §4.2 argument for a model-scored predicate over a hand-written one,
and this is the single highest-leverage gate in the loop to get right.

## Change

1. FIRST, instrument. Land the `BoundaryNudge`/`GateTally` counters from .1 and
   get real numbers on how often `AwaitingUser` fires before changing it. If it
   fires rarely, this drops to P3 — say so and stop. Do not skip this step.
2. Replace the predicate with a two-way ClassifyFn call (BLOCKED / OFFERING)
   over the final assistant text, when a judge is configured.
3. Keep the heuristic as the fallback when no judge is configured, and as a
   cheap pre-filter: no `?` anywhere in the final text -> definitely not
   blocked, skip the classifier call entirely. Costs nothing on the common path.

## Acceptance

- Corpus test: hand-label ~30 final assistant turns (blocked vs offering vs
  neither), pulled from real session history. Assert the classifier beats the
  heuristic on it. Keep the corpus in-repo as a fixture; it's the regression
  test for every future change to this gate.
- No-judge config uses the heuristic and behaves identically to today.
- The `?`-free fast path is asserted to make zero judge calls.
- A/B (.1 harness): the clarifying-question scenario must still hand control
  back to the user (no regression), while the finished-work-plus-offer scenario
  should now run its gates instead of skipping them.

title: Verifier edit counting and headless visibility of harness injections (found by A/B)
description:
Both found by end-to-end A/B runs against DeepSeek, not by unit tests.

1. edits_since_verify counted TOOL CALLS, not code files. A model asked to change four files emitted one apply_patch with four operations, which registered as a single edit — so the mid-run fast-check threshold of 3 was effectively unreachable for any model that batches, which is most of the capable ones. Now counts distinct code paths per call (deduped, docs excluded).

2. Harness-injected messages were invisible to headless consumers. They are user-role messages that the TUI attributes to the system by matching their [tag]; --print shows only the final answer and the stream-json user event carries tool results only. So a --print/--loop user saw the model abruptly change course with nothing explaining why, and could not distinguish an injected steer from the model's own judgement. Now mirrored as SystemNotice at every injection site, keyed off a single HARNESS_TAGS list with a test pinning that every tag is recognized.

title: Snapshot bash file mutations, then enable safe-state abort auto mode
description:
Blocks 'auto' mode for the R3 safe-state abort (dirge-uw2l.4), which shipped advisory-only for this reason.

snapshots::capture / capture_bytes is called ONLY from edit.rs, write.rs, apply_patch.rs, edit_lines.rs, edit_minified.rs. bash is not wired in at all (verified by grep). So sed -i, echo > file, tee, and in-place formatters mutate files with no pre-state captured.

Consequence for auto mode: restore_after_green_turn reverts the captured edits but leaves the bash mutations in place, producing a tree in a state that never existed — half green, half post-green, likely uncompilable. The model then debugs a self-inflicted broken tree while the failure streak keeps climbing, which is the exact opposite of a safe state. /rewind carries the same gap but is user-chosen and visible; auto would be neither.

Options: capture bash file writes (hard — needs to know which paths a command touched), or detect-and-refuse auto when a mutating bash ran since the green turn (cheap, conservative, probably enough).

Also tracked here: the (a-prime) per-file green checkpoint. snapshots store PRE-mutation state only, so they structurally cannot restore to a green POST-state for files edited to reach green. Option (b) (restore from the turn AFTER green) handles the cross-turn case; the within-turn case is handled by declining. A true per-file green checkpoint would close that but needs new capture machinery.

title: RAX R4: horizon replanning, goal triage, residual-objective handoff
description:
Three related paper findings:
- Paper 2/3.2 (MM): plans are per-horizon, folding in EXEC's projected state; the second plan contains an activity to generate the third. dirge's write_todo_list is bulk up-front, afterwards items are only checked off — nothing folds what was learned in items 1-3 into items 4-10.
- Paper 3.1b (PS): rejecting low-priority unachievable goals is a VALIDATION OBJECTIVE, not a failure. dirge todo items carry no priority and the nudge pushes completion of everything; cancelled is supported by the store but not invited by guidance.
- Paper 3.4/5: the 2-day scenario aborted at ~70% of objectives; within ~10 hours they built a 6-hour scenario targeting precisely the remaining 30% and reached 100%. dirge emits a truncation notice with no met/outstanding breakdown, so a resumed session re-derives scope.

- todo priority field; nudge reworded to close/re-scope/cancel-with-reason
- horizon boundary: after M complete with K remaining, one bounded replan checkpoint
- early termination emits residual-objectives block into the session digest (met/outstanding/evidence)
notes:
RAX R4 decision (session bc3fc90a):

(A) Horizon replanning — SKIPPED. Structural premise doesn't hold in dirge. In RAX, PS's plan was a fixed ahead-of-time artifact computed from a long-range profile, and EXEC's projected state changed between horizons, so the second plan had to CONTAIN an activity that generated the third, folding in the new state. dirge's todo list is re-surfaced in the prompt every turn and freely re-writable, so there is no stale plan store to refresh and nothing to fold back in. The only concrete trigger (a boundary at 'M complete, K remaining') has no failure signal behind it, and R3's progress monitor already covers the detectable case (stall checkpoint + 60%/85% budget notices both already invite re-scope). A boundary that fires whether or not anything is wrong can only ever add messages under the no-op-default constraint. Decision recorded rather than forgotten.

(B) Goal triage — SHIPPED (narrow). Two of the issue's premises were stale: priority already existed and is required (TodoItem.priority, issues.priority NOT NULL), and R3's stall/budget notices already invite cancellation citing the RAX validation objective. The real gap was that priority was collected then discarded (unfinished_count was a flat usize). Shipped: unfinished_by_priority() -> (high,normal,low) in todo.rs; todo_nudge_message(unfinished, low) names low-priority items as cancel candidates when low>0, byte-identical to the old wording when low==0.

(C) Residual-objective handoff — SHIPPED. New src/agent/agent_loop/residual.rs: residual_block(&[TodoItem]) -> Option<String> (outstanding-only — the board mirror excludes terminal items, so it reports what remains, not a done/remaining split it can't honestly compute). Appended to the max-turns truncation notice via max_turns_notice(cap, board) AFTER the prefix (provider/run.rs headless detector at starts_with(MAX_TURNS_NOTICE_PREFIX) guarded by max_turns_notice_keeps_truncation_prefix_with_residual_block); reused in session_digest render. Always on, NO config gate — no-op by data (None on empty board), per the approved change.

Verify: 4738 tests pass (4729 baseline + 9 new), cargo clippy --bin dirge -- -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --check clean.

title: RAX R3: safe-state abort — restore last-green tree and replan
description:
Paper 2 (EXEC): failure ladder is alternate method -> request recovery -> cleanly abort the plan, bring the spacecraft to a safe state, request a new plan. dirge's ladder stops at rung 2 (storm reflect-then-pivot, failure_tracker checkpoint) — both keep the model digging in a possibly half-mutated tree.

Machinery exists (snapshots::restore_from) but is user-driven via /rewind only.

- new rung above failure_tracker: at 2x failure threshold WITH code mutations since last green verification
- restore files via snapshots::restore_from, inject replan message carrying the reflexion log + failure excerpts
- REAL WORK: last-green marker. snapshots key on user turn today; needs a verification-green checkpoint id stamped by the R1 tier verifier. Depends on R1.
- modes: advisory (tell the model the option exists) | auto (harness restores). Default advisory.

title: ProjectPaths::new in tests resolves through DIRGE_PROJECT_ROOT — leaked a shared $TMPDIR/.dirge session DB
description: Curator/skill/memory tests built ProjectPaths::new(&temp_dir), which consults the process-global DIRGE_PROJECT_ROOT that dirge_paths' own env-override tests set concurrently. Their writes landed in $TMPDIR/.dirge instead; the leaked sessions/state.db accumulated 12 rows and then failed first_run_gates_on_session_count intermittently on every later run. Added ProjectPaths::at() (literal root) and switched the scratch-dir test sites.

title: deny_tools does not filter tool defs out of the request
description: GH #734. Prompt frontmatter deny_tools is enforced only at the permission layer, so --prompt ask still ships all 34 tools including write/edit/bash/apply_patch (verified off the wire). The model burns attention on tools it will be refused, and users have no way to shrink the toolset for a weak model. Fix: drop prompt-denied names in filter_tool_defs.

title: Todo nudge can't fire on a plan-only turn (gated on turn_made_file_edits)
description: GH #734. run.rs:589 gates the unfinished-todo nudge on turn_made_file_edits, and write_todo_list is not an Edit op. Verified with a scripted model: two write_todo_list calls then stop -> dirge finalized with 2 open todos, zero files written, no nudge. Fix: also fire when todos were written this turn and no edits happened, with wording that says start the work.

title: System prompt mandates write_todo_list before work; tool description lacks when-not-to-use
description: GH #734. prompt.rs:108 tells the model to put a non-trivial task on the active list FIRST. opencode never mentions its todo tool in the system prompt and puts full when/when-not guidance (with negative examples) in the tool description instead. Weak local models substitute planning for the work. Fix: drop the ordering mandate, move guidance into the description with negative examples.

title: Kimi OAuth: 15-minute tokens refresh with no skew margin, and 401 is non-retryable
description:
epoch_ms_is_expired (src/auth/file_store.rs:22) is 'now_ms >= expires_at_ms' with no early-refresh margin, and Kimi stores expires_at = now + expires_in with expires_in = 900s (src/auth/kimi_device.rs:463).

So RefreshableToken::bearer() (src/provider/kimi_http.rs:45) considers a token fresh right up to the millisecond it expires. A request issued just under the boundary can reach Kimi after the token has actually expired — network latency plus any client/server clock skew — and come back 401.

That 401 is not recoverable: retry.rs classifies auth errors as non-retryable (does_not_retry_auth_error, src/agent/agent_loop/retry.rs:441), so the turn dies rather than refreshing and retrying.

Why Kimi specifically: the same margin-free helper backs the OpenAI and Anthropic OAuth paths, but those tokens are far longer-lived, so the boundary is crossed orders of magnitude less often. At 15 minutes it is crossed roughly every 15 minutes of an active session, and each crossing is a chance to land in the window.

Two independent fixes, either sufficient, both cheap:
1. Refresh early. Treat a token as expired N seconds before expires_at (30-60s is the usual choice). Cleanest as an optional margin argument on epoch_ms_is_expired, or a Kimi-specific wrapper so the OpenAI/Anthropic paths keep their current semantics.
2. Make a 401 on an OAuth provider retryable exactly once, forcing a refresh first. Bigger change, but it also covers server-side revocation and clock skew larger than any fixed margin.

Found while reviewing #724 for the 0.19.27 release. Not a release blocker: the window is small and the failure is a visible error rather than corruption.

title: dirge exits 101 (panic) on terminal hangup instead of 129; children may not be reaped
description:
When the terminal goes away, dirge exits with 101 (Rust panic) instead of the intended 128+SIGHUP = 129. Something panics writing to the dead tty before signal.rs's clean teardown runs.

Reproduced end-to-end with a Python harness that runs dirge on a real
controlling pty via `pty.fork()`, then closes the master:

    PASS phase 1: alive after 4s
    closed pty master (terminal is now gone)
    exited 0.2s after tty close, code 101

0.2s is faster than the 250ms dead-tty watchdog tick, and 101 is rustc's
panic exit status, so neither the watchdog nor the SIGHUP handler is what
ends the process — a panic beats both.

Pre-existing, NOT introduced by the 0.19.24 spin fixes. Verified by
stashing the input_reader change, rebuilding, and re-running the same
harness: baseline behaves identically (phase 1 pass, 0.2s, code 101).

Why it matters beyond the wrong exit code: `src/signal.rs` exists
specifically so a terminal hangup reaps the detached child process groups
(LSP servers, MCP servers, DAP adapters, bash subtrees) via
`reap_all_groups()` before exiting, since those are `setsid`-detached and
never receive the terminal's signal themselves. A panic path likely skips
that, which is the exact orphaned-rust-analyzer scenario dirge-6klk was
filed for. Worth confirming whether the panic hook reaps.

Next step: capture the panic message and backtrace. Redirecting the
child's stderr to a file changes behaviour (it panics immediately, before
the tty is even closed — a different path worth understanding on its own),
so the message has to be captured on the pty itself, before the master is
closed, or via the panic hook's log file.

The harness used is in the 0.19.24 investigation; it can be rebuilt from
the description above in a few lines of Python.

title: crossterm input reader spins at 100% CPU on a dead tty; poll() never returns
/agent <name> doesn't cross-provider route its pinned model (sibling of GH #711)
description:
Same root cause as dirge-t665 / GH #711, different consumer. src/ui/slash/cmd/agent/switch.rs:32-37 sets session.model to the profile's pinned model via resolve_model_alias (same-client only) and never rebuilds the client, so /agent researcher with model: glm-5.2 on a Codex/ChatGPT client makes every MAIN-session turn 400. It also resets session.provider to the CLI/config default (switch.rs:35), which /model explicitly documents as wrong — the next routing decision then reasons from the wrong active provider.

Fix is the same shape as the task path (see resolve_profile_model / resolve_model_route added for #711): route via resolve_model_route, rebuild the client on ModelRoute::Provider, set session.provider to the switched alias, mirror /model's refuse-and-warn for Unroutable.

Needs one extra piece the task path doesn't: /agent off (clear.rs:20-25) restores model_before_agent but never restores the CLIENT, so a switch-back would leave the restored model on the profile's provider. Needs a provider_before_agent sibling to model_before_agent.

title: h7_smoke tests broken: DeepSeek retired deepseek-chat model name
description:
The three h7_smoke scenarios call the live DeepSeek API with model 'deepseek-chat', which the provider retired: 'The supported API model names are deepseek-v4-pro or deepseek-v4-flash, but you passed deepseek-chat.' All three fail on every local 'cargo test'.

Pre-existing, not from #717 — verified by stashing and re-running on a clean tree. Invisible in CI (no DeepSeek key there), so it only bites local runs, where it makes a green suite look red and trains people to ignore failures.

Fix: update the model name in src/agent/agent_loop/h7_smoke.rs, or gate the scenarios on a reachable provider so they skip rather than fail when unconfigured.

title: Syntax gate has no pre-edit baseline: already-broken files can't be edited at all
description:
syntax_gate(path, candidate) validates the WHOLE candidate file with no reference to what was on disk before. If the file was already unparseable, every edit is rejected with an error pointing at a region the model never touched, and there is no opt-out (write goes through the same gate).

Two classes hit this:
1. Legitimately unparseable files that carry a lisp extension - templates (luminus-template/resources/leiningen/new/luminus/core/src/core.clj has <% %> markers), linter fixtures (clj-kondo/corpus/invalid_literals.clj), REPL transcripts. dirge can never edit them.
2. A file broken by something outside the edit tools (bash/sed, a partial apply_patch, the user's own WIP). Recovery requires one edit that fixes ALL syntax at once.

Repro: a .clj file with an unclosed form near the top + 40 valid defns after it -> any edit rejected with 'the ( opened at line 3, col 1 is never closed'.

Fix direction: compute the gate on the pre-edit content too, and only block when the edit INTRODUCED errors (or increased the error count). Pre-existing breakage should downgrade to a warning appended to the success message. Same shape as the SQL carve-out reasoning already documented in language_for_path.
acceptance_criteria: Editing an already-broken file succeeds with a warning when the edit does not make it worse; an edit that introduces a new error is still blocked; regression tests both ways

title: Delimiter hint points at the outermost unclosed opener, not the innermost
description:
delimiter_summary (src/semantic/syntax_validator.rs) reports stack[0] - the OUTERMOST unclosed opener. In a lisp that is almost always the enclosing top-level form, i.e. column 1 of a defn, which is nowhere near the actual mistake. The innermost unclosed opener (stack.last()) sits at or next to the dropped closer.

Repro: file with (defn broken [x] / (let [y (inc x)] / (println y  -> message says 'the ( opened at line 3, col 1 is never closed' (the defn) when the actionable pointer is (println at line 5, col 5.

Effect: the message tells the model 'do not count by hand - fix this delimiter' while pointing it at the top of the form, so it re-reads the whole form and counts anyway. This is the reported 'Whole-file balance N (unbalanced) yet reader loads' flailing.

Fix direction: lead with the innermost unclosed opener (deepest, closest to the error), keep the count, and optionally mention the outermost as context.
acceptance_criteria: Summary names the innermost unclosed opener's line/col; existing wording tests updated; count unchanged

title: ACP does not expose slash commands (gh#714)
description: Dirge's ACP bridge never announces its slash commands, so editor clients (Zed, etc.) can't offer them. Advertise a curated ACP-appropriate subset via available_commands_update after session/new, and intercept invocations (/help, /clear, /cd, /model, /mode) in run_prompt so they execute locally instead of being fed to the LLM. TUI-only commands are not advertised.

title: Linux build: document toolchain prereq + add no-plugin feature alias (#712)
Build-time follow-ups: nextest in CI, opt-in cranelift+sccache scripts

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: Implemented in PR #692 (branch perf/build-time-followups). nextest in CI (verified locally: 4406 passed), scripts/fast-build.sh (opt-in sccache/cranelift), plans/compile-time-improvements.md. Measured: sccache 85->52s clean rebuild only; cranelift marginal (4.9 vs 5.5s) + can't link plugin on macOS arm64. Close on merge.

title: No always-on completeness backstop for default (no critic_provider) runs; critic is one-shot + fail-open
close_reason: Both gaps fixed: critic one-shot now spent by a verdict (bounded retries), plus a deterministic completeness_gate at advisory by default. Shipped 0.21.13, PR #759.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
From the headless-stall investigation. Separate from the u6zc 429 fix.

Two distinct gaps:
1. No-critic default: when critic_provider is unset, the completeness judge (Gate 4, poll_finalization_follow_up) is inert. Remaining always-on gates are narrow mechanical detectors (verifier=edited-code-not-run; resume=last-tool-call-failed; todo=only if model tracked todos). A model that stops with a plausible-but-incomplete answer after successful tool calls hits nothing -> loop ends.
2. Configured-but-weak: even with critic_provider set, in advisory mode (default) the critic is ONE-SHOT (critic_done flips regardless of verdict, run.rs:475) AND fails open on judge timeout/error (critic.rs:393). A slow/stalling judge silently drops the backstop; a flash judge can rubber-stamp COMPLETE.

Proposed (two small, safe pieces):
(a) Harden critic one-shot-vs-fail-open: a judge timeout/error should NOT consume the one shot (retry it) — strictly helps every configured user.
(b) Bounded no-LLM completeness nudge for autonomous/headless runs: promote the existing track-work advisory to re-drive ONCE when a run made real edits/tool-calls but produced a short final answer with no tracked todos and no critic. Must be one-shot + narrowly triggered + soft (false re-drives waste turns) — needs its own tests.

Note: user's config HAS critic_provider=deepseek-flash, so gap #2 is the live one for them; gap #1 matters for default installs.
