title: Discovery 'anchored window around match' is actually anchored at session's first message
description: search_messages never selects m.id, so find_message_id_near reconstructs the anchor via get_anchored_view(session,1,0) which returns exactly the session's first message regardless of timestamp -> every discovery hit's window/anchor_index describes the session opening, not the FTS match. Also get_anchored_view's anchor_row.saturating_sub(1) wraps -1 to usize::MAX for foreign anchor ids. Fix: return m.id from the FTS join and pass it as the anchor; clamp anchor_row-1 at zero before cast. Files: src/extras/session_search.rs:359, session_db.rs:1288,1582. Round R2.
close_reason: search_messages returns m.id; discovery anchors on the match; anchor_row-1 clamped at 0 before usize cast

title: get_session_meta only finds metadata for the 50 most-recent sessions
description: Discovery-hit metadata looked up by scanning list_sessions_rich(None) = LIMIT 50 ORDER BY last_active DESC. An FTS hit in an older session gets empty source/model/title/started_at silently (Ok with blanks). Also does a throwaway get_anchored_view probe just to 404-check. Fix: direct SELECT source,model,title,started_at FROM sessions WHERE id=?1. Files: src/extras/session_search.rs:344, session_db.rs:1243. Round R2.
close_reason: Direct SELECT source,model,title,started_at WHERE id=?1; discovery meta no longer blanks out for sessions past the recent 50

title: Multi-line harness/add-steering/add-followup splits into multiple user messages
description: Unlike add-custom-message and every other registry (which use harness/-escape), the steering/followup queues append content unescaped into a newline-delimited blob. (harness/add-steering 'step 1\nstep 2') arrives at the loop as two separate LoopMessage::User entries -> a formatted multi-line instruction is shredded. Fix: escape on append, unescape on drain, matching the custom-message wire format. File: src/plugin/worker.rs:287,296, mod.rs:547. Round R4.

title: Worker timed-out evals still execute later; late harness/block wiped by next pre-clear
description: eval_with_timeout enqueues Cmd::Eval and abandons only the reply on timeout; the command still runs later. After a fail-open timeout the next dispatch's pre-clear (set harness-block nil) is queued behind the blocked hook; when the user finally answers deny, the plugin's harness/block executes and is immediately erased by that queued pre-clear -> denial vanishes silently. No interrupt facility, so one (while true) hook permanently wedges all future hooks/tools/commands. Fix: tag each Eval with a generation, skip stale queued commands; longer-term wire janet interrupt/recreate worker after repeated timeouts. Files: src/plugin/worker.rs:1137, mod.rs:657. Round R4.
notes: Scope finding (deferred pass): confirmed two coupled problems on the single Janet worker thread (worker.rs worker_loop:1407-1418 runs client.run(&code) serially, no interrupt). (1) STALE SIDE-EFFECT: eval_with_timeout (worker.rs:1208) abandons only the reply on timeout; the Eval stays queued/running. A hook that blocks without a registered dialog (dialog_pending==0, e.g. while-true or a blocking syscall) times out fail-open at 5s, then its late harness/block lands and the NEXT dispatch's pre-clear (dispatch_tool_hook pre-clear, mod.rs) wipes it -> denial vanishes. (2) PERMANENT WEDGE: a (while true) hook never returns, so every subsequent Eval queues behind it forever -> all future hooks/tools/commands freeze. SECURITY-ADJACENT: this is the permission-gate (harness/block) path; a wrong fix can make the gate fail OPEN. Recommended design (needs supervision): (a) add a shared AtomicU64 generation; tag each Cmd::Eval with the generation at send; on host timeout bump it; worker skips/ignores side-effects from a stale-generation eval so a late block from an abandoned eval can't corrupt a newer generation. (b) For the wedge, Janet has no safe cross-thread fiber interrupt, so recreate the worker thread after N consecutive timeouts (kill+respawn+re-init, accepting plugin-state reset) rather than trying to interrupt. Do NOT fire-and-forget; pair with the user.

title: /graph search swallows --compress/--depth flags into the FTS5 query
description: Query built with take_while(s != --kind && s != --tier), so --compress (usage line) and --depth (parsed later) are included in the search string. '/graph search auth --compress' searches FTS5 for 'auth --compress' -> wrong results while compress mode still activates. Fix: extend the terminator set to all known flags or split flags from positionals in a shared parser. File: src/ui/slash/cmd/graph.rs:40. Round R8.
close_reason: positional_query helper terminates the /graph search query at the first --flag; --compress/--depth no longer leak into FTS5. Delegated to dirge, reviewed+verified (fmt fixed).

title: /compress always prints 'prompt cleared (back to default behavior)'
description: install_compaction unconditionally writes this line after rebuilding the agent, but nothing in the function clears the prompt layer -> users falsely told their active /prompt was reset on every compaction incl. automatic ones. Fix: delete the line or replace with an accurate 'agent rebuilt' note. File: src/ui/slash/mod.rs:453. Round R8.
close_reason: Removed misleading 'prompt cleared' line from install_compaction; compaction doesn't reset the prompt layer and the result is already reported below.

title: DAP attach stalls full timeout then records running debuggee as Stopped
description: attach waits timeout(30s) for a stopped event that usually never comes on a running process, racing the Janet bridge 30s DAP_CMD_TIMEOUT, then unconditionally sets status=Stopped -> debug panel and summaries misreport a running debuggee. Fix: set Running when no stopped event arrived; use a short grace wait (~1s) not the full request timeout. File: src/dap/session.rs:462. Round R7.
close_reason: attach waits a 1s grace (ATTACH_STOP_GRACE) not the full request timeout, and records Running when no stopped event arrives instead of a fabricated Stopped; split out attach_with_client for testing

title: DAP pause can never interrupt continue (active mutex held across stop-wait)
description: continue_ holds self.active.lock().await through its tokio::select! stop-wait; pause starts by acquiring self.active. Continue a free-running program then pause -> pause blocks on the mutex up to continue's 30s timeout, the one window where pause is meaningful. Fix: clone the client handle out of the lock before waiting for the stop event so other requests issue concurrently. File: src/dap/session.rs:571,707. Round R7.
close_reason: continue_ hands the event receivers off and releases the active lock before parking on the stop-wait, so a concurrent pause/snapshot no longer blocks for continue's full timeout

title: DAP stale queued stopped events satisfy later step/pause waits
description: stopped events accumulate in an unbounded channel drained only on demand; nothing clears pre-existing events before issuing next/pause. Multi-threaded debuggee where two threads stop -> the next step 'completes' instantly consuming the stale event; reported reason/thread belong to the previous stop, every subsequent op skewed by one. Fix: drain the stopped channel immediately before step/continue/pause (mirror drain_output/drain_termination). File: src/dap/session.rs:196. Round R7.
close_reason: drain_stopped() clears stale queued stopped events before each continue/step/pause, mirroring drain_output/drain_termination, so ops no longer complete on a previous stop

title: apply_patch failures return Ok('FAILED:...'), invisible to recovery machinery
description: Mid-batch failure pushes 'FAILED: {e}' into results and returns Ok(results.join). Not an error, so the consecutive-failure recovery checkpoint, repeat-loop guard, and critic transcript labeling (which key off errored tool results) never see apply_patch failures -> a model looping on a failing update op gets none of the documented recovery interventions. Fix: return Err when the batch ends in failure (keep per-op text as message), or when no op succeeded. File: src/agent/tools/apply_patch.rs:404. Round R3.
close_reason: apply_patch batch ending in failure now returns Err (keeps per-op text), so recovery checkpoint/repeat-guard/critic labeling see the failure

title: Relay summary points at a never-written file when the disk write fails
description: wrote_ok is tracked but format_summary is unconditionally handed &path, so on create_dir_all/fs::write failure the LLM-facing text still says 'Full output stored at ... Use the read tool', contradicting the doc comment ('summary with no path'). Model then burns turns reading a nonexistent file. Fix: when !wrote_ok omit the path sentence and say the full output could not be stored. File: src/agent/tools/output_relay.rs:286. Round R3.
close_reason: format_summary now takes Option<&Path>; on a transient-write failure relay_if_large passes None and the trailer says the output could not be stored instead of pointing the model at a nonexistent file

title: BOM files: edit_lines deterministically false-rejects any range including line 1
description: read strips U+FEFF from line 1 before hashing; edit_lines recomputes hashes from raw disk with only CRLF normalization, so line 1 still carries the BOM and its hash never matches what the model echoed -> any edit_lines touching line 1 of a BOM file rejected 'line(s) changed since you read them', unfixable model-side. Fix: strip a leading U+FEFF in edit_lines before hashing/splicing, re-prepend on write. Files: src/agent/tools/read.rs:347, edit_lines.rs:219. Round R3.
close_reason: decode_for_edit strips a leading BOM before hashing (matching read.rs) and re-prepends on write, so edit_lines on line 1 of a BOM file no longer false-rejects

title: Mixed-line-ending files wholesale rewritten to CRLF by edit/edit_lines/apply_patch
description: has_crlf = any CRLF anywhere; on write-back every \n becomes \r\n. A mixed-ending file (common after cross-platform edits) has all its LF-only lines flipped to CRLF incl. lines nowhere near the edit, despite comments claiming 'so we don't silently rewrite line endings'. Noisy unintended diffs. Fix: detect mixed endings and preserve per-line (splice bytes), or at least report the normalization. Files: edit.rs:179,324, edit_lines.rs:220, apply_patch.rs:130. Round R3.
close_reason: line-ending shape detected at decode; mixed-ending files normalize to the dominant ending and report it, instead of has_crlf=any flipping every LF to CRLF

title: edit/edit_lines write from_utf8_lossy output; pre-existing non-UTF-8 bytes -> U+FFFD
description: File decoded lossily, edit applied, whole lossy buffer written back -> invalid bytes far from the edit (latin-1 comment, or bytes appended externally after the session read) silently become replacement chars. Read gate mostly prevents but mark_read is session-lifetime, so read-then-externally-modified reaches it. Fix: detect from_utf8_lossy produced Cow::Owned and refuse with 'not valid UTF-8' instead of writing mangled bytes. Files: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:180,350, edit_lines.rs:221,252. Round R3.
close_reason: edit/edit_lines/apply_patch now decode via shared text_io::decode_for_edit which refuses non-UTF-8 instead of from_utf8_lossy mangling bytes to U+FFFD

title: /spec anchors store at process cwd while sibling commands use session.working_dir
description: spec.rs builds ProjectPaths from cwd; issues.rs/graph.rs/clear.rs use session.working_dir. swap_to_session replaces session.working_dir but never set_current_dir, so after /sessions <id> into a session saved elsewhere, /issues reads that project's state.db while /spec reads the cwd project's -> two commands over the 'same' session DB disagree. Fix: standardize all slash ProjectPaths on session.working_dir. File: src/ui/slash/cmd/spec.rs:11. Round R8.
close_reason: /spec now builds ProjectPaths from ctx.session.working_dir (via resolve_project_paths helper) like /issues, /graph, /clear — no longer anchors at process cwd, so commands over the same session agree

title: DEFER_* slash sentinels are colon-delimited and break on paths containing ':'
description: handle_slash signals deferred work via anyhow error-string prefixes; DEFER_WT_MERGE packs 5 fields (branch:target:main:wt:repo) parsed with splitn(5,':'), DEFER_WT_EXIT splitn(2,':'). A repo path with ':' (legal on macOS/Linux) shifts every field -> wrong branch/paths or truncated chdir; user-typed merge target unvalidated; on field-count mismatch both arms have no else -> silent no-op. Fix: replace the string protocol with a typed SlashOutcome enum stashed in UI state. Files: src/ui/slash/cmd/worktree.rs:131, ui/mod.rs:2529. Round R8.

title: /loop start <prompt> leaks the verb 'start' into the loop prompt
description: Dispatch requires parts[1]=='start' but the handler only strips '/loop' from raw text, so tokens include 'start' which isn't --max and lands in prompt_tokens. '/loop start fix the tests' -> LoopState prompt 'start fix the tests', corrupting every iteration. Fix: strip the start verb too (or build from parts[2..] with --max handling); add a unit test on the parsed prompt. File: src/ui/slash/cmd/loop_cmd/start.rs:15. Round R8.
close_reason: Strip leading 'start' dispatch verb before parsing /loop prompt; extracted testable parse_loop_start helper. Delegated to dirge mcp, reviewed+verified.

title: Invalid permission config block silently drops all rules instead of failing fast
description: RuleConfig is deny_unknown_fields, so one misspelled field makes the whole permission block fail to deserialize; build_channels prints a stderr warning (scrolls away under TUI) and continues with PermissionConfig::default(), discarding every rule incl. hard denies (rm ** deny, external_directory denies). Exactly the failure the config loader hard-exits for elsewhere. Fix: make an unparseable permission block a startup error, or refuse-to-run when the discarded config had deny rules. Files: src/main.rs:149, config/mod.rs:1028. Round R1.

title: Cross-process auth-store race clobbers rotated refresh token
description: save_openai/Anthropic save are unlocked load-modify-write. Two dirge processes with an expired credential both refresh with the same refresh token; OpenAI rotates on use, so the loser persists a now-invalid refresh token over the winner's fresh one -> next expiry fails refresh, forces re-login. Fix: advisory file lock (flock on auth.json) around load->refresh->save, re-check freshness after acquiring. Files: src/auth/store.rs:148, src/provider/client.rs:457, auth.rs:194. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed in R1 security cluster (audit-p2-r1-security branch): https-only guard extended to Anthropic OAuth; independent OAuth state vs PKCE verifier; advisory file lock around OAuth refresh; ChatGPT/Codex mid-session bearer refresh.

title: Explicit --model gpt-4o silently rewritten to gpt-5.5 under Codex
description: codex_model_name replaces any name equal to default_model_for('openai') (='gpt-4o') with gpt-5.5, so it can't tell 'user never set a model' from 'user explicitly asked for gpt-4o' -> explicit choice overridden with no warning. Fix: resolve the Codex default earlier where explicit-vs-default is still known (CLI/config layer) instead of pattern-matching the default string at dispatch. Files: src/provider/dispatch.rs:134, resolve.rs:35. Round R5.
notes: Scope finding (deferred pass): far more invasive than framed. codex_model_name is load-bearing at ~40 runtime completion_model() sites — session.model is persisted as 'gpt-4o' for a default-codex session and every runtime rebuild (ui/mod.rs slash cmds, compaction, /model, run_handlers, resume, acp) relies on the central rewrite to remap gpt-4o->gpt-5.5. Removing/relocating the rewrite regresses EVERY codex user unless: (1) the resolved codex default is stored INTO session.model at startup (needs the built client for codex-detection, which is created after Session::new, plus context_window reconciliation), and (2) already-persisted old default-codex sessions are migrated on resume (they carry model='gpt-4o'). Recommend a dedicated scoped pass with the user, not a quick fix. Doing the other 4 deferred issues first.
close_reason: Resolved the Codex default once (resolve_model_name) with the explicit-vs-default signal and stored it as session.model; removed the in-completion_model remap so the ~40 sites read one correct name. Role clients + ACP resolve the same way. Fresh + resume + test harness covered.

title: PKCE code_verifier reused as OAuth state parameter
description: append_pair('state', &verifier): the PKCE secret is embedded in the authorize URL (terminal, browser history, URL-logging proxy) and echoed in the localhost redirect. An observer of either URL obtains code + verifier and can complete the exchange. state-mismatch check gives CSRF protection but not disclosure mitigation. Verify whether the endpoint requires state==verifier; if not use an independent random state kept only in memory + back-channel POST. File: src/provider/anthropic_oauth.rs:67. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed in R1 security cluster (audit-p2-r1-security branch): https-only guard extended to Anthropic OAuth; independent OAuth state vs PKCE verifier; advisory file lock around OAuth refresh; ChatGPT/Codex mid-session bearer refresh.

title: Anthropic OAuth token may be sent over plaintext http
description: The https-only guard (token too sensitive for allow_insecure) is gated on is_chatgpt_auth||uses_openai_oauth only; the AnthropicOauth branch accepts any validated base_url. providers.anthropic={auth:anthropic, base_url:http://..., allow_insecure:true} sends sk-ant-oat bearer in Authorization over plaintext. Same argument the code makes for the Codex token. Fix: extend the https-only bail to also fire when auth==Anthropic. File: src/provider/client.rs:267. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed in R1 security cluster (audit-p2-r1-security branch): https-only guard extended to Anthropic OAuth; independent OAuth state vs PKCE verifier; advisory file lock around OAuth refresh; ChatGPT/Codex mid-session bearer refresh.

title: Escalation stream route bypasses the retry wrapper
description: Default and review-fork routes wrap in retrying_stream_fn; the escalation StreamFn is threaded raw (build.rs:602 returns model.build_stream_fn, spawn.rs:202 clones unwrapped, stream.rs uses it directly). Escalation fires once after repair-exhaustion; a transient 503/rate-limit on that single call surfaces immediately, wasting the escalation the user paid a second provider for. Fix: wrap escalation StreamFn in retrying_stream_fn. Files: src/provider/build.rs:602, spawn.rs:202. Round R5.

title: File store and salience DB diverge on delete: ghost active rows re-enter curator
description: Tool delete removes the directory but leaves the skills row status='active' + FTS row. render_candidate_list builds from list_active filtered to source='learned' -> next curator pass handed a skill that no longer exists; its skill(load) fails mid-consolidation. Same when curator dir-move succeeds but the ignored s.archive() fails. Fix: tool delete arm also calls store.archive (best-effort, logged); log the curator's DB-archive error instead of discarding. Files: src/agent/tools/skill.rs:242, src/extras/skills/curator.rs:152. Round R6.

title: restore_entry can demote the eviction-exempt overview
description: restore_entry re-implements hot-tier compaction with bare least_salient_index, unlike insert_into_hot which never picks 'overview' and honors the working reserve. Small hot tier + restoring a large entry demotes the overview to breadcrumb (contradicts 'never an eviction victim'); a demoted overview then renders twice (project_overview block filters by kind, breadcrumb index by tier). Fix: restore_entry reuses insert_into_hot victim-selection; exclude kind='overview' from breadcrumb render. File: src/extras/memory_db.rs:1268. Round R2.
close_reason: restore_entry reuses make_room_in_hot (overview-exempt victim selection); breadcrumb render excludes kind=overview

title: Restored skills stay status=archived in DB forever
description: Recovery = moving the dir back out of .archive/. On next startup register_file_skill update branch refreshes description/content/updated_at but never status, so the row keeps status='archived' -> permanently excluded from list_active (preamble salience), invoke (AND status='active'), and search. Skill works only as an unranked file. Fix: register_file_skill update branch resets status='active' (directory presence is ground truth). File: src/extras/skill_db.rs:417. Round R6.
close_reason: register_file_skill UPDATE branch now resets status='active'; recovered skill dirs re-activate. Delegated to dirge, reviewed+verified.

title: Legacy MEMORY.md import can index FTS under wrong rowid; partial import strands rest
description: INSERT OR IGNORE + last_insert_rowid(): if an insert is ignored (dup uid), last_insert_rowid returns the previous rowid and the following INSERT INTO memories_fts attaches new text to the wrong row -> search returns mismatched content. Also no transaction: mid-loop error leaves earlier rows committed, COUNT>0 gate blocks re-import of the rest, files never parked to *.imported -> part of legacy memory stranded. Fix: one transaction + check execute row count (skip FTS when 0) instead of trusting last_insert_rowid after OR IGNORE. File: src/extras/memory_db.rs:2000. Round R2.

title: skill_db multi-step writes lack transactions (row + FTS)
description: create (INSERT skills then INSERT skills_fts) and register_file_skill (UPDATE/INSERT + DELETE fts + INSERT fts) run bare, unlike memory_db which wraps every row+FTS mutation in a txn. Failure between statements (crash, or SQLITE_BUSY past 5s while a post-session background writer holds state.db) leaves a skill row with no FTS row (unsearchable) or stale/duplicate FTS, no self-heal. Fix: conn.transaction() around create and register_file_skill. File: src/extras/skill_db.rs:238,417. Round R6.

title: insert_message runs 4 statements with no transaction; can corrupt external-content FTS
description: INSERT messages + messages_fts + messages_fts_trigram + UPDATE sessions run as separate autocommit statements. Crash after the first leaves a message row with no FTS projection (invisible, message_count drifts); later delete_session_messages issues the external-content FTS5 'delete' with a recomputed projection for a never-indexed rowid -> FTS5-documented index corruption. delete path already uses a txn; insert doesn't. Fix: wrap insert_message in unchecked_transaction(). File: src/extras/session_db.rs:1145. Round R2.

title: is_verification_command substring markers count git checkout/npm install as green
description: Markers matched with contains: 'check' matches 'git checkout main', 'npm' matches 'npm install', 'test' matches 'ls tests/'. After a code edit any of these succeeding sets ran_verification=true, verification_failed=false -> VerifiedGreen fabricated: verify nudge silenced and critic told a build/test passed when nothing was verified. Fix: tokenize (reuse tree-sitter bash segmenting) and match markers on command words, excluding checkout/install/add. File: src/agent/agent_loop/verifier.rs:181. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed on audit-p2-r5-gates: anchored exit-code failure signal + tokenized verification-command match. Tests in verifier.rs.

title: Verifier failure signal 'Exit code:' is an unanchored substring scan
description: result_indicates_failure returns true if 'Exit code:' appears anywhere in tool text. A green 'make test' whose wrapper echoes 'Exit code: 0' marks the run VerifiedRed -> wrong FAILED_NUDGE and feeds the critic 'Don't pass a red build - INCOMPLETE', blocking a correct green run. Fix: anchor to the harness marker (parse N != 0 on the final line) or thread the real exit status. File: src/agent/agent_loop/verifier.rs:171. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed on audit-p2-r5-gates: anchored exit-code failure signal + tokenized verification-command match. Tests in verifier.rs.

title: Verify pass can't drop a FALSE_POSITIVE-annotated (vs omitted) finding
description: Pass 2 asks for VERIFIED/FALSE_POSITIVE but re-parses with parse_findings which has no notion of those tokens. A common LLM shape (re-list every candidate with inline verdict, e.g. '- High - SQLi. FALSE_POSITIVE: not in diff') still carries a severity label -> parsed as a survivor and can wrongly BLOCK finalization. Only omission works; all tests use omit-style. Fix: discard blocks containing FALSE_POSITIVE before severity detection; add annotate-style test. File: src/agent/agent_loop/code_review.rs:832,896. Round R5.
close_reason: Fixed on audit-p2-r5-gates: verify_pass now discards FALSE_POSITIVE-annotated blocks before parse_findings; annotate-style tests added.

Slots into poll_finalization_follow_up near the critic as a SEPARATE gate.

Thin git shell-out (reuse git_worktree git() pattern); pure formatting/truncation/exclude logic unit-tested.

Port from ~/src/roborev: Severity{Critical,High,Medium,Low} with ordering; Finding{severity,location,harm,fix}; parse_findings() ported from internal/storage/verdict.go:51-305 (severity-label detection, --- splitting, legend/rubric skip); REVIEW_PREAMBLE + SECURITY_PREAMBLE ported verbatim from prompt/templates/default_review.md.gotmpl and default_security.md.gotmpl (evidence discipline, don't-report list, severity defs, toolchain-from-manifest). Fires at finalization when a run edited code, reviews the actual git diff, verifies findings to drop false positives, then blocks on critical/high and surfaces medium/low as advisory. Also /review on demand. Ports prompt craft + finding/verdict model from ~/src/roborev (Go); none of its daemon/queue/sqlite infra. Decisions: finalization+/review trigger, severity-gated blocking, two-pass from the start.

The code reviewer is a sibling gate to the completeness-critic, built on the same CriticFn plumbing + build_judge_fn, but with its own preamble + a findings pipeline. New module: src/agent/agent_loop/code_review.rs; tag [code-review]; distinct from [critic]/[verify-before-done].

title: Flaky test: last_init_error_tracks_open_failures races on global LAST_INIT_ERROR
description: extras::session_db_tests::last_init_error_tracks_open_failures asserts the process-global LAST_INIT_ERROR is Some after a failed SessionDb::open, but a concurrent successful open() in another parallel test clears it to None, so the assertion flakes. Passes in isolation. Fix: isolate the global for this test (serialize, or assert on the returned Err rather than the shared global).

title: Compaction OAuth fallback gaps: /compress hard-errors + fragile error matcher
description: Follow-up to PR #529. Two gaps for Anthropic-OAuth users without summarization_provider: (1) explicit /compress hard-errors with no prune-only fallback unlike reactive overflow; (2) is_anthropic_oauth_compaction_disabled_error matches err.to_string() which breaks if error is wrapped with context — would silently disable the prune-only routing.
notes: Fix in PR #530 (branch fix/compaction-oauth-prune-fallback). Awaiting review/merge.

title: No request-establish timeout on model client / wrap_rig_stream
description: Latent robustness gap noted in #523: wrap_rig_stream wraps only the established stream body's .next(); the request-establish phase and the provider clients (client.rs:355) set no timeout, so a stalled connection/handshake can hang a run with no bound. Not the cause of the #523 headless deadlock (that was ask_rx undrained, fixed in 0.13.1). Add a request/response timeout to the provider client build and/or bound the stream-establish phase.
notes: Scope finding (deferred pass): the establish phase IS unbounded — invoke_one_stream (src/agent/agent_loop/rig_stream_factory.rs:275) does model.stream(request).await with no timeout; chunk_timeout only guards reads AFTER establishment. StreamOptions.request_timeout (stream.rs:83) is threaded from LoopConfig but carries #[allow(dead_code)] — never read; defaults to None (types.rs:656) with NO config key, so nothing sets it (only a unit test does). retry.rs:60's comment that 'request_timeout already aborts a stuck/hung stream' is currently false. features.md documents request_timeout as a whole-run 'thinking-stall watchdog' backstop — a DIFFERENT semantic from a connection/handshake establish bound. So a correct fix needs a design decision: (a) bound establish at rig_stream_factory.rs:275 via tokio::time::timeout — mechanism is a ~10-line contained change; (b) decide whether establish-timeout is a new config concept or reuses request_timeout (semantic clash with the watchdog); (c) pick a default (establishment is fast, so a generous 120-180s bounds only genuine stalls without killing long legit streams). Recommend the user choose the policy; the mechanism is ready to wire once decided. NOT the cause of the #523 deadlock (that was ask_rx undrained, already fixed).
close_reason: Bounded the establish phase with a consistent named timeout (timeouts.request_establish, default 300s); removed the dead request_timeout field

title: TUI: tool chambers + chat don't span to right pane edge (dead band + artifacts)
description: chamber_widths uses content_width()=line_width().min(120)-1 which is gutter-blind and capped at 120, while ChatPane paints to Layout::chat.width-1 (reclaims hidden-panel gutters). At ~122-151 cols (panels hidden until 152) the box is ~119 wide in a ~145-col paint area -> ~26-col dead band on the right where stale glyphs from earlier/wider frames survive (resize, picker overlay). USER DECISION: full pane width for BOTH chambers and chat text (un-cap, no centering). Fix: derive chamber/content width from the actual chat paint area (Layout::chat.width-1, panel-aware) instead of content_width()'s 120 cap; chat wraps to chamber width so both follow. Add a test asserting chamber frame width + 1 == Layout chat.width across panel-hidden/shown widths. Root cause detail in PR #524 thread / agent analysis. Files: src/ui/tool_display.rs:347, src/ui/renderer.rs:1335, src/ui/tui/chat.rs:91-110, src/ui/tui/layout.rs:129-147.

description: save_session (serialize+fsync) and persist_turn_to_db across done/interjected/context_compacted/overflow/error handlers, /sessions switch/delete/list dir-scan+JSON parse (storage.rs), and the git diff --stat HEAD in the post-done digest (done.rs:490 -> session_digest.rs:225) are awaited inline. Remaining candidates (save_session, persist_turn_to_db, /sessions scans) are sub-100ms local ops where offloading needs storage-layer refactors with poor risk/benefit — left by design; reopen if profiling shows one is slow in practice.

title: Round 3b: run /wt-merge git merge off-thread
description: DEFER_WT_MERGE handler (mod.rs:2287) runs merge_worktree synchronously (several git invocations, no timeout) then build_agent. Spawn the merge.

title: Round 3a: run shell !cmd off-thread with abortable handle
description: run_shell_command().await (mod.rs:2142/2173, 120s cap) is awaited inline; long commands freeze the UI + Ctrl+C. Spawn with a phase handle so render continues and Ctrl+C aborts.

title: Round 2b: run /btw LLM call off-thread (non-blocking)
description: cmd/btw.rs:16 model.btw_query().await is a direct inline LLM completion (with retries) on the UI loop. Only slash command with a raw inline LLM call. Spawn it; render the result via a select! arm or a spawned task.

title: Non-blocking compaction: wire the two AUTO sites (post-turn auto-compact + overflow recovery)
description:
dirge-dtyn stages 2a/2b made the two USER-INITIATED compaction paths non-blocking (explicit /compress; preemptive pre-prompt compaction) via ui::compaction + the compaction_phase select! arm. Two AUTO-triggered sites still run the summarizer inline (freeze):

1. Post-turn auto-compact: run_handlers/done.rs:361 handle_compress().await (inside handle_done, agent_rx Done arm). Continuation = Nothing. Needs &mut ui.compaction_phase threaded into handle_done + its call site (mod.rs:2790); prepare_compaction + spawn(Nothing); is_running stays true; the 'AUTO-COMPACT FAILED' framing moves to the arm's Failed branch. Low risk.

2. Reactive overflow recovery: run_handlers/context_overflow.rs compress().await. DIVERGENT continuation — only retry on Compacted && !tools_already_ran (tool-side-effect safety), drops the trailing User message from history, NO add_message (prompt already in session), resets last_collapsed. Needs a CompactionThen::RetryAfterOverflow { prompt, tools_already_ran } variant + outcome-aware (Compacted vs NoOp) branching in the compaction_phase arm. Higher risk; correctness-sensitive (must not strand users on overflow). Deferred from the first pass to avoid rushing it untested.

The machinery (ui::compaction::{spawn, CompactionThen, CompactionPhaseHandle}, slash::{prepare_compaction, install_compaction}) is in place; this is wiring the two run_handler sites through it.
notes: Item 2 (reactive overflow recovery) DONE in branch nonblocking-compaction commit 32af163. Only item 1 (post-turn auto-compact in done.rs) remains. NOTE: item 1 is NOT as low-risk as originally written — the auto-compact at done.rs:345 runs before the turn-finalization tail (post-done action 458, loop continuation, reviewer 530, idle drain 597), each of which may spawn a follow-up runner that MUST run against the compacted context. A plain async spawn(Nothing) only works when the turn truly ends with no follow-up; the loop/reviewer/plugin/queued-interjection cases need the tail deferred until after install, OR the eager compaction dropped in favor of the now-async preemptive+reactive paths.
close_reason: Item 2 (reactive overflow) wired in 32af163; item 1 (post-turn auto-compact) resolved by dropping eager compaction in favor of the now-async preemptive+reactive paths. All four compaction triggers are now non-blocking — no inline summarizer call remains in the event loop.

title: Observability: opt-in dump of outgoing provider requests (which prompt, which provider, why)
description:
Local users debugging multi-provider/secondary-call behavior (e.g. a mystery mid-turn side completion that thrashes a single-slot KV cache) have no way to see what prompts dirge sends. dirge only logs cache-prefix HASHES (emit_cache_prefix_event), never payloads, and -v just sets dirge=debug.

Add DIRGE_DUMP_REQUESTS env: =1 logs a summary line per outgoing request (purpose label, provider, tool count/names, reasoning flag, byte sizes); =full also logs the system prompt / one-shot prompt body. Emitted at INFO on target dirge::wire so it lands in dirge.log (-v/RUST_LOG/DIRGE_LOG) or via RUST_LOG=dirge::wire=info. Instrumented at both request-build choke points: provider::summarize::oneshot_with_model (side-LLM: summarizer/critic/approval, carries the 'why' label) and agent_loop::rig_stream_factory (main turn/escalation/subagent/forked review). Off by default, no behavior change.
close_reason: DIRGE_DUMP_REQUESTS scaffold already existed (wire.rs, both choke points wired); completed it by adding provider+model+messages_bytes to the summary/full log lines — the provider field the issue explicitly required was missing. Implemented via dirge delegation, reviewed + fmt/clippy/test verified.

title: Scrollback (esp. markdown tables) does not reflow on terminal resize
description:
Chat scrollback is a flat Vec<LineEntry> of already-WRAPPED physical rows (renderer.rs:356). Markdown -> rows happens once at arrival width (markdown_to_styled, markdown.rs:326; render_table at markdown.rs:183 takes max_width but is only called at append time). On resize the handler (mod.rs:1364) only calls request_repaint(), which redraws the SAME stored rows — there is no re-wrap at draw time. Result: nothing in scrollback reflows on resize; tables are the most visible casualty (box borders overflow/mangle at narrower widths, don't expand at wider), while prose just over-runs or stays narrow.

Fixing 'tables reflow' therefore means 'scrollback reflows', which requires re-rendering from retained SOURCE at the new width. Complication: in-flight content (streaming assistant response + tool-call chambers) is not yet in session.messages, so re-rendering from history alone would drop it.

Options:
A. Full reflow: retain per-block logical source (text + color + kind, incl. table source) so the whole buffer can be regenerated at any width. On resize: regen buffer at new width, preserve scroll anchor. Also re-render in-flight buffer. Cleanest result, largest change; must handle streaming + eviction + scroll restore + perf on huge scrollback.
B. History-only reflow: on resize rebuild the buffer from session messages via the existing history-render path at the new width; accept that a resize mid-stream loses the in-progress turn until it finalizes. Much smaller; degraded during active streaming.
C. Table-targeted: tag table row ranges with their source markdown; on resize re-render only those ranges via render_table at the new width (buffer has a truncate+extend splice already at renderer.rs:1280). Narrow blast radius; only tables reflow (matches the report literally) but adds block metadata to a flat buffer.
design:
Full scrollback reflow (user-chosen scope). Make buffer a derived cache over a retained source log.

Stage 1 — source log + rebuild:
- Add blocks: Vec<ChatBlock> to Renderer + ChatSnapshot; buffer becomes derived.
- ChatBlock::{ Plain{text,color}, Markdown{src,base_color,handle}, ToolChamber{tool,banner,output,max_chars,max_lines}, Blank }.
- Route write_line/commit_partial -> Plain; the 5 markdown_to_styled sites (events.rs:238 history, agent_io.rs:88 stream, done.rs:298, interjected.rs:47, btw.rs:21) -> Markdown; render_tool_output (tool_display.rs) -> ToolChamber.
- rebuild(width): clear buffer, replay blocks through existing width-taking renderers (markdown_to_styled, chamber rendering, soft_wrap).

Stage 2 — reflow on resize:
- mod.rs:1364 Resize -> renderer.rebuild(content_width()). Preserve scroll anchor (offset-from-bottom; re-clamp to new max_offset). 

Stage 3 — streaming + edges:
- In-flight response (response_buf/response_start_line owned by event loop) re-renders at new width after mid-stream resize; reset start_line to new buffer_len on rebuild.
- Reconcile replace_from streaming, eviction (MAX_SCROLLBACK=20000, drain 2500, eviction_generation), Ctrl+O expansion absolute-index anchors, selection indices, multi-chat save/load_active.

Choke points are few: all ~90 write_line callers funnel through write_line/push_buffer_line; 5 markdown sites; tool chambers via render_tool_output. Width via content_width() = line_width().min(120).
acceptance_criteria: After a terminal resize, markdown tables in scrollback are re-laid-out to the new width (borders aligned, columns refit). Scroll position is preserved across the reflow. No regression to streaming, eviction, or selection. Tests cover render-at-width-A then reflow-to-width-B.
close_reason: Scrollback now reflows on resize: plain text + markdown (tables) re-wrap to new width via a source-block model + rebuild(). Chambers preserved verbatim (no border fracture); chamber re-boxing tracked as dirge-ghpf.

title: Keybinding rebind across contexts requires explicit unbind (ctrl-r)
description:
User keybinding config is supposed to merge OVER the built-in config: rebinding an existing key to a new command should override the default with no explicit unbind. Today a cross-context rebind silently fails unless you unbind first.

Repro:
  "keybindings": [ { "key": "ctrl-r", "command": "reverse_search" } ]
does NOT take effect; you must prepend { "key": "ctrl-r", "command": "unbind" }.

Root cause — Keymaps::from_config (src/ui/keymap.rs:344-372): there are TWO keymaps, global (KeyAction) and input (InputAction). 'unbind'/'none' removes the chord from BOTH maps. A real rebind inserts into only ONE map: global.map if the command resolves via KeyAction::from_command, else input.map via InputAction::from_command. reverse_search is an InputAction, but the DEFAULT ctrl-r is a global KeyAction. So binding ctrl-r->reverse_search inserts into input.map while the default stays in global.map. The chord is now bound in both contexts; global wins at dispatch, so the user binding never fires. unbind 'works' only because it clears both maps.

So override is 'last wins' only WITHIN the same context, not across global<->input. Any rebind whose new command lives in a different context than the default leaves the default live.

Fix direction: when applying a user (and plugin) binding for a chord, remove that chord from BOTH keymaps first, then insert into the resolved context — so a user rebind is authoritative for the chord regardless of which context old/new commands live in. The dispatch model already treats a chord as single-purpose (see the dirge-fl57 prefix/terminal conflict resolution), so clearing both then inserting one is consistent. Verify plugin layering (defaults < plugins < user, src/ui/mod.rs:209-225) still resolves correctly, and that the same-context override tests (override_rebinds_and_keeps_other_defaults, override_on_an_occupied_chord_replaces_it) plus unbind tests still pass.
acceptance_criteria: Binding an existing default chord to a command in the OTHER context (e.g. ctrl-r -> reverse_search) takes effect without an explicit unbind. New test: a global-default chord rebound to an input command fires the input command and the global default no longer fires (and vice versa). Existing override/unbind tests still pass.
close_reason: from_config now clears the chord from both keymaps before inserting; cross-context rebind works without explicit unbind. Tests for both directions; plugin path covered.

title: Minimal running project context: pinned, eviction-proof project overview
description:
At session start we inject a flat, salience-ranked BAG of individual facts (format_for_system_prompt, memory_db.rs:605). There is no single always-present high-level 'what is this project' orientation — stack, architecture in 3-5 lines, the gestalt the model should read before granular facts. No pinning exists ('No pinned concept yet — every entry is in scope' in memory_curator), so foundational orientation can be demoted to breadcrumb and drop out of the hot block as facts accumulate.

This is Recall's context.md Goal+Summary idea as a durable tier: a curated, pinned project-overview entry that (1) is never salience-evicted, (2) renders FIRST in the system prompt, (3) is REFRESHED (overwritten) by the background review rather than appended to, keeping it minimal. Distinct from the fact bag and from identity-kind (which is who the user is).

Open design questions: new kind 'overview' vs a pinned flag on existing rows; single-entry cap; how the review maintains it (replace, not add).
acceptance_criteria: A pinned/overview project-context entry exists that is exempt from salience eviction, renders first in the system prompt, and is refreshed (not duplicated) by the review. Tests: overview survives a budget-pressure compaction that evicts ordinary hot facts; review updates it in place rather than appending.
close_reason: overview kind: singular, eviction-exempt, rendered first, review-maintained; tests cover singularity, flood survival, render order

title: Session-resume / open-threads digest (cold-start carry-over)
description:
dirge has session replay (--session <id> rehydrates panels) and durable MEMORY.md facts, but nothing produces a compact 'where we stopped + open threads' handoff for the IN-PROGRESS task. working-kind exists but the review prompt says 'prefer not to persist it' and it is first to be evicted, so current-task state has no carry-over between sessions.

Idea from ~/src/recall: a cheap next-step cue regex (still need|todo|blocked|follow-up|trailing '?') + uncommitted git files, used to seed working-kind 'open threads' at session end, surfaced at the next session start. Fills the cold-start-of-the-current-task gap that durable facts don't cover. Pairs with the git/todo signals from the ground-truth layer (sibling issue).
acceptance_criteria: At session end, open threads are extracted (cue regex + uncommitted files + unfinished todos) and persisted as a resume digest; at next session start in the same project the digest is surfaced to the model. Tests cover cue extraction and the round-trip persist/surface.
close_reason: Review-maintained open-thread carry-over via working entries, fed by the deterministic digest; prompt guard test added

title: Deterministic ground-truth capture layer for background review
description:
Memory formation today is entirely LLM-mediated: run_background_review (src/agent/review.rs) forks an agent over build_transcript(session) and asks it to NOTICE facts like 'what build/test commands ran'. This is lossy (LLM omits non-salient facts), rate-limited (15-min claim_review_slot throttle; can return early with zero captures), and costs tokens to rediscover facts the transcript already carries verbatim.

Idea from ~/src/recall: pull deterministic ground-truth straight from the transcript+git WITHOUT an LLM — files touched, commands run (Bash args), git diff --stat, todo deltas, first-goal/last-state. rehydrate.rs already computes modified_files + todo_list; tool calls carry file_path/command args.

Two uses:
(a) Prepend this structured digest to COMBINED_REVIEW_PROMPT so the LLM ranks/classifies KNOWN facts instead of hunting — better recall, fewer tokens.
(b) Use it as a zero-LLM fallback write (working/episodic) when claim_review_slot is throttled or the review errors, so a session's learnings are never fully lost.

Highest-leverage of the set. Puts a deterministic floor under LLM formation, not a replacement.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic session digest (files touched, commands, git diff --stat, todo deltas) is computed without an LLM call; it is fed into the review prompt; and a fallback path persists it when the LLM review is skipped/throttled. Unit tests cover digest extraction from a synthetic transcript and the throttled-fallback path.
close_reason: 1a shipped: deterministic digest module wired into both review entry points. 1b (deterministic fallback persist) declined — carry-over chosen as review-maintained (dirge-hcv8), no deterministic floor wanted.

title: Phase 2: LSP-verify the auto-repair, roll back on error
description: After repair_delimiters auto-closes a trailing truncation, verify the written result with the language server (where one exists). If the repair introduced error-severity diagnostics, roll the file back to its pre-write state and return the diagnostics + relevant code so the model fixes its own un-repaired content. Repair-path only: a clean write is never rolled back (keeps surface-don't-block for WIP). Catches semantically-wrong-but-parseable repairs tree-sitter can't (e.g. nested #[test]).
close_reason: Implemented in #499 — write/edit LSP-verify the auto-repair and roll back on error.

title: Critic/verifier nudge vanishes from chat log after next turn streams
description: A finalization nudge (critic/verifier/todo) re-enters the loop as a user-role message WITHOUT a Done/ToolCall event, so the prior turn's stream anchor (response_start_line) stays live. The AgentEvent::UserMessage handler rendered the <critic> line but didn't reset the anchor, so the next turn's render_agent_stream replace_from(stale anchor) truncated the buffer and overwrote the nudge — it disappears on screen though the model still has it in context. Fix: finalize the in-flight response + reset the anchor before rendering the message (mirrors ToolCall/Done).

title: Prototype: feed verification status into the critic
description: Extend the in-loop LLM critic to be pickier about compile/lint/test. Reuse VerifierGate's existing signal (edited_code/ran_verification/verification_failed) as a read-only status, gate on edited_code as the precondition, and pass it into the critic prompt so it treats unverified/red code edits as concrete INCOMPLETE when verification is runnable and not forbidden.

title: Undo (Ctrl+Z) in the input editor
description: The input editor has no undo. Add a Ctrl+Z undo that reverts the last edit (especially pastes). Snapshot buffer/cursor/pastes before edits, coalesce runs of typing, discrete steps for paste/kill/delete. Reset on submit.

title: Copy wrapped prose as one line
description: When selecting prose in the chat that the renderer soft-wrapped across multiple display rows, copying inserts a newline at every wrap boundary. User has to manually re-join. selected_text() should join soft-wrap continuation rows back into one line (hard newlines/paragraph breaks preserved).

title: /sessions delete unusable when ids share a prefix (compacted-*)
description: Compacted sessions get ids 'compacted-<uuid>' (storage.rs:307). The /sessions list/switch/delete views truncated the id to a fixed 8 chars ('compacte'), identical for every compacted session, so on ambiguity 'be more specific' was impossible — the user couldn't tell them apart or type a distinguishing prefix. Fix: show each id at the shortest length that's unique among the shown set (distinct_id_len), floored at 8.
acceptance_criteria: With multiple compacted-* sessions, /sessions and /sessions delete show distinguishable id handles the user can retype to target one.

title: Keybindings phase 5: docs + close #476/#234
description: Rewrite docs/config.md 'Key bindings': remove the 'input-editor keys not rebindable' note, add the input-command table + their default chords, document sequence syntax ('ctrl-x ctrl-s'), pending-prefix/cancel behavior, and chord_timeout_ms. Add a docs/plugins.md section on creating AND overriding keybindings via plugins (register-shortcut + new bind-key), with the merge/precedence order. Close GitHub #476 and #234 with a summary comment.
acceptance_criteria: docs/config.md and docs/plugins.md reflect the unified system; #476 and #234 closed with comments.

title: Keybindings phase 4: emacs-style chord sequence runtime (#234)
description: Add the pending-prefix state machine to the dispatch loop so multi-key sequences (e.g. 'ctrl-x ctrl-s') fire. On a keypress: extend the pending sequence; complete match -> dispatch + clear; valid prefix -> hold pending and echo it in the footer, swallow the key; no match -> cancel pending and fall through. Esc and Ctrl+G cancel a pending prefix (only while pending). Optional config chord_timeout_ms (default: none, wait like emacs). No sequence bindings ship by default — capability only.
design: Pending state lives in the UI key handler (src/ui/mod.rs). Prefix/terminal conflict resolved phase-2-side: sequence wins, terminal dropped with a startup warning. Footer echo reuses existing status rendering. Applies to both global and input keymaps via the same matcher.
acceptance_criteria: Binding 'ctrl-x ctrl-s' to a command fires only after both keys; footer shows the pending prefix; Esc/Ctrl+G cancels; a non-matching second key cancels and falls through; optional timeout works when set.

title: Keybindings phase 3: Target::{Builtin,Plugin} model + plugin remapping (#476)
description: Make the keymap value a Target enum: Builtin(action) or Plugin(handler_name). Fold today's separate plugin_shortcuts list (harness/register-shortcut) into the unified keymaps so plugin bindings and built-ins resolve through one table. Add a Janet harness/bind-key (keys command) that lets a plugin bind/rebind a built-in command name (or 'none' to unbind), collected after plugin load (like list_shortcuts) and merged at precedence defaults < plugins < user-config. Closes the remapping half of #476 (the adding half already works).
design: Plugin bindings merged through the SAME from_config layering as user config, applied before user config so user always wins. register-shortcut stays for chord->plugin-handler; bind-key is chord->built-in-command. Reserved keys (Ctrl+C/D/Esc) still non-overridable. Document precedence and conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin can rebind a built-in command to a new chord and unbind one; user config overrides a plugin binding; existing register-shortcut plugins keep working; #476 remapping path covered by tests.

title: Keybindings phase 2: sequence-native unified keymap + config surface
description: Build the keymap data model as sequence-native (Vec<Chord> keys; defaults all length-1) so #234 is a later runtime addition, not a retrofit. Unify config: one keybindings array whose command vocabulary = global (KeyAction) UNION input (InputAction). Keymap::from_config routes each {key, command} to the right context keymap by command-name lookup across both registries; unknown commands still warn. Add prefix/terminal conflict detection (a chord that is both a terminal binding and a prefix of a sequence). Wire the input keymap from config in src/ui/mod.rs alongside the global keymap.
design: Chord parser extended to parse space-separated sequences ('ctrl-x ctrl-s' -> Vec<(KeyCode,KeyModifiers)>); single chord = length-1. Keymap stores bindings keyed on Vec<Chord> plus a prefix set for fast pending-prefix checks. resolve() still works for length-1 (the only defaults). Command-name uniqueness across KeyAction+InputAction is required (validate at startup).
acceptance_criteria: A config.json keybindings entry can rebind an input-editor command (e.g. move cursor_line_start off Ctrl+A); global rebinding unchanged; conflicting/unknown entries warn; sequence parsing is in place though no sequence runtime yet.

title: Keybindings phase 1: input-editor command layer (table-driven, behavior-preserving)
description: Convert src/ui/input.rs's hardcoded text-editing key match into resolve-then-apply: add an InputAction enum + InputAction::ALL default-chord table (mirroring KeyAction::ALL in src/ui/keymap.rs), resolve each KeyEvent to an InputAction via a lookup, then apply the existing logic bodies behind the enum. Single-chord only this phase. Behavior-preserving: defaults reproduce today's keys exactly. Intrinsic keys stay direct (char insertion, Backspace, Enter/submit, @ file-picker, Tab slash-completion). Riskiest phase — touches the editor core, so it lands isolated and green before anything else.
design: Rebindable input actions = named editing commands only: cursor_left/right, cursor_line_start/end (Ctrl+A/E, Home, End), word_left/right (Alt+B/F, Alt+arrows), kill_to_line_end/start (Ctrl+K/U), kill_word_back/forward (Ctrl+W, Alt+D, Alt+Backspace), yank/yank_pop (Ctrl+Y/Alt+Y), history_prev/next (Ctrl+P/N), reverse_search (Ctrl+F), up/down line/history. Preserve subtle behaviors: marker-block aware Left/Right, wrap-aware Up/Down (dirge-5w9v), kill accumulation reset, paste placeholder delete, slash-ghost accept on Right. NOT rebindable: Char insertion, Backspace, Delete, Enter/Shift+Enter, Tab, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+C/D/Esc.
acceptance_criteria: input.rs dispatches via InputAction lookup; full input test suite green; new tests assert each InputAction maps to its default chord and that a remapped table changes behavior.

title: Unified, data-driven keybindings (input + global + plugin remap + chord sequences)
description: Replace the split, partly-hardcoded keybinding handling with one data-driven system: a built-in default keymap that user config (and plugins) merge on top of, covering BOTH the global command keys (already table-driven) and the input-editor keys (currently a hardcoded match in src/ui/input.rs). Adds plugin remapping of built-ins (#476) and emacs-style multi-key chord sequences (#234). Nothing hardcoded except the Ctrl+C/D/Esc panic gesture and intrinsic editing (char insertion, Backspace, Enter-submit, @ picker, Tab completion). Defaults stay as in-code declarative tables (KeyAction::ALL pattern); user config wins over plugins wins over defaults.
design: Two contexts (global/chat + input-editor), one mechanism: action enum + default-chord table + chord parser + config layering. Keymap value becomes Target::{Builtin,Plugin} so plugin shortcuts and built-ins share one resolution table. Keymap is sequence-native (Vec<Chord> keys) so #234 chording is a runtime/UX addition, not a data-model retrofit. Closes #476 and #234; supersedes the 'not rebindable' note in docs/config.md.
acceptance_criteria: Input-editor keys rebindable via config.json; plugins can add AND remap built-in bindings; multi-key sequences (e.g. 'ctrl-x ctrl-s') work with a pending-prefix indicator and Esc/Ctrl+G cancel; docs updated; #476 and #234 closed.

title: Critic: treat permission-denied capabilities as out of scope
description: The critic (src/agent/agent_loop/critic.rs) already respects constraints expressed in the system prompt ('NEVER flag the absence of an action the instructions forbid'), but it's blind to runtime permission denials — a separate constraint channel. It sees the transcript (build_critic_transcript, first/last tool results) but is never told that a denial means the capability is out of scope rather than a failure to fix. Result: it flags 'commit+push missing' as concrete incompleteness and the model complies by routing around the guardrail. Fix: add one rule to CRITIC_PREAMBLE — 'if the transcript shows a tool was permission-denied, treat that capability as out of scope; do not demand it.' Smallest of the consumer fixes and useless on its own if denial still looks like a generic error string, hence depends on the root.
design: Depends on dirge-c7sd so the denial is legibly marked in the transcript (build_critic_transcript can label Denied results distinctly). Then add the preamble rule.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transcript containing a permission-denied commit/push, the critic does not return INCOMPLETE solely for the missing denied action.

title: approval_provider Deny should fall through to human prompt (advisor, not final authority)
description: With an approval_provider configured, try_auto_approve (src/agent/tools/mod.rs:409) short-circuits on Ok(ApprovalDecision::Deny) via ?, so the denial never reaches the human prompt at ~line 559. Only an evaluator *error* (None) falls through. Net effect: the LLM evaluator is the final authority on denials and the user is designed out of the loop — even when they'd have approved. Fix: a Deny from the approval_provider should fall through to the human prompt (treat the LLM as advisor for denials), and/or the denial message should carry the exact '/allow add <tool> <pattern>' string so recovery is one paste. Hard rule-based Effect::Deny stays terminal.
design: Depends on dirge-c7sd for the suggested_allow string. Decision needed: always fall through to human on approval_provider Deny, vs. surface the deny + /allow hint without auto-prompting. Lean: fall through to human prompt, prefilled with the evaluator's reason, since a configured human is present in interactive mode.
acceptance_criteria: An approval_provider Deny in interactive mode results in the user being prompted (or shown a one-paste /allow hint), not a hard ToolError with no recourse.

title: Failure tracker: don't treat permission denials as mechanical failures
description: The recovery-checkpoint escalation (src/agent/agent_loop/failure_tracker.rs) is built for mechanical recovery. A permission/approval denial lands in Outcome::Error with escalation weight 1 (activity.rs), indistinguishable from a wrong-args error, so it feeds the same streak. The emitted checkpoint text ('What root cause — wrong arguments, wrong tool, or wrong approach? Re-read its description and parameter schema... take a DIFFERENT next step') is wrong for a well-formed-but-denied call, and the 'take a DIFFERENT next step' instruction is exactly what drives the model to route around the guardrail (e.g. writing a .sh wrapper). Fix: exclude Denied outcomes from the mechanical-recovery streak, OR emit a distinct checkpoint — 'blocked by permissions; you cannot route around this — ask the user to /allow or stop.'
design: Depends on dirge-c7sd (Outcome::Denied). Once classify() can yield Denied, FailureTracker::record either skips escalation weight for Denied or accumulates it into a separate bucket with its own format_checkpoint branch.
acceptance_criteria: A run of N consecutive permission denials does NOT emit the 're-read the parameter schema / take a different approach' recovery checkpoint; it either stays silent or emits a permission-specific message.

title: Model permission/approval denials as a first-class tool outcome
description: A permission/approval denial is currently flattened into ToolError::Msg(String) (src/agent/tools/mod.rs:155). Downstream subsystems (failure tracker, critic, approval flow) can only re-infer 'this was a policy denial' from a string, so each one mistakes it for a generic execution error. Root fix: give denial a typed identity — e.g. ToolError::Denied { reason, suggested_allow } and/or an Outcome::Denied variant in src/agent/agent_loop/activity.rs — that the failure tracker, critic, and approval path can key off. This is the prerequisite for the three consumer fixes.
design: Two flatten points to fix: (1) ToolError in tools/mod.rs — add Denied variant carrying reason + a suggested '/allow add <tool> <pattern>' string. The denial site is try_auto_approve (tools/mod.rs:409) which today returns ToolError::Msg. (2) Outcome::classify in activity.rs:58 currently maps to Ok|Error|Timeout — add Denied so record_result can route it. Keep hard Effect::Deny (rule-based, terminal) distinct from approval_provider Deny (advisory).
acceptance_criteria: A permission/approval denial is distinguishable from a generic ToolError at the type level; failure tracker and critic can each branch on it.

title: /sessions: explicit verbs instead of overloaded positional
description: parts[1] does double duty as both subcommand sentinel ('delete') and session id, so a session id can never be 'delete'. Move to explicit verbs: /sessions list | /sessions switch <id> | /sessions delete <id>, keeping bare /sessions <id> as a switch shortcut. A bare positional is then only ever a session id.
close_reason: Deleting current session now boots to a fresh session; /sessions uses explicit verbs (list/switch/delete) so a bare positional is only ever a session id

title: Deleting the current session leaves a zombie; boot to a fresh session
description: Deleting the session you're currently in (/sessions delete <current-id>) removes the file but the in-memory session keeps running, pointing at a now-deleted file. Decision: when the deleted session is the active one, swap the live session for a fresh empty one (new id, same model/provider/cwd) and rebuild the agent, mirroring the switch path.
close_reason: Deleting current session now boots to a fresh session; /sessions uses explicit verbs (list/switch/delete) so a bare positional is only ever a session id

title: Goal gate doesn't strip compaction summary from rules (critic does)
description: critic::strip_compaction_summary keeps the critic from treating a resumed session's [CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY] summary (its stale ## Active Task) as an outstanding requirement. The sibling goal gate (goal::build_goal_prompt) receives the same merged system_prompt as rules but does NOT strip the summary, so it shares the stale-state bug. It also byte-slices rules (&rules[..N]) which can panic on a non-char boundary.
close_reason: Footer now shows compaction-trigger budget; goal gate strips compaction summary like the critic

title: Footer shows model window, not the compaction budget
description: The status-line footer uses session.context_window (raw model window, e.g. 200k/1M) as the token-usage denominator. That misrepresents how much room is actually left: the loop folds/compacts at effective_fold_threshold * effective_ctx_max, where effective_ctx_max = min(model_window, context_target). Show the compaction-trigger budget instead so the percentage reflects 'how close to a fold'.
close_reason: Footer now shows compaction-trigger budget; goal gate strips compaction summary like the critic

title: Q&A custom-answer paste leaks into main prompt
description: When typing a free-form custom answer in the question modal, pasting routes to input.handle_paste (main compose box) instead of the question's custom-answer buffer. Root cause: dispatch_modal! only matches UserEvent::Key, so Paste falls through to the compose Paste arm.
close_reason: Fixed in #468 — pastes route to the Q&A custom-answer field

title: Config flag to show thinking output by default
description: GH #461: add a config setting (show_reasoning) to make model thinking/reasoning visible by default, like show_tool_details/show_edit_diff. Defaults to false (current behavior).

title: Cost-aware loop guard: consolidate storm + failure tracker behind shared activity log
description: Storm breaker and failure tracker are count-based and cost-blind: a single 120s timeout counts the same as a 5ms error, so neither escalates on expensive failures. Consolidate bookkeeping behind one ToolActivityLog/LoopGuards facade recording {call, outcome, cost_ms}; keep storm's suppress + failure tracker's nudge as two policies reading it. Add cost-awareness: timeouts are a stronger 'stuck' signal — escalate the nudge faster and lower storm's effective threshold for a call that previously timed out.
close_reason: Fixed: setsid detaches the controlling terminal so tty prompts fail fast; non-interactive env defaults added. Loop guard made cost-aware behind a LoopGuards facade (timeout weighting in failure tracker + lowered storm threshold). All tests + clippy -D warnings pass.

title: Expanded thinking block: wrapped rows escape the box (lose the │ bar)
description: In the Ctrl+O expanded thinking panel, render_thinking_block formats each line as '  │ {line}' and lets write_line wrap it. write_line wraps with an empty continuation indent, so continuation rows drop the '  │ ' bar and start at column 0, escaping the bounding box. Fix: pre-wrap each line to content_width-4 and carry the '  │ ' bar onto every wrapped row (same pattern as the blockquote/code-block wrap fixes).

title: Unify Anthropic + OpenAI OAuth onto shared machinery, add /login
description: #455 added OpenAI device-code OAuth as a parallel src/auth/ subsystem that duplicates the Anthropic OAuth machinery in src/provider/ (PKCE, 0600 credential storage, expiry/refresh). Extract shared OAuth primitives so both providers share one base; add a /login TUI slash command mirroring the dirge auth CLI. Follow-up to merging #455.

title: Long lines in fenced code blocks are clipped, not wrapped
description: The chat painter (ChatPane::render in tui/chat.rs) draws one screen row per LineEntry and clips to width. markdown_to_styled wraps prose via word_wrap but emitted code-block lines as one unwrapped LineEntry per source line, so a long line inside a fenced code block was clipped at the window edge (user saw 'only one sentence'). Fix: wrap each code line's colored content to the content width, carrying the gutter onto every wrapped row.

title: Compaction: Active Task can hold an already-completed task, confusing the model (#443)
description: GitHub #443: after compaction the model re-derives/expresses confusion about the original task when it's already done and only follow-up work remains. Root cause: build_summary_prompt's '## Active Task' biases toward the user's original verbatim request, and SUMMARY_PREFIX tells the model to 'resume exactly from there' without warning the original task may be complete. Fix: reframe Active Task to the immediate next action / emergent follow-up and require stating the original done; add a completion guard to SUMMARY_PREFIX; add a supersession probe to the recall harness.

title: Quoted headings/code blocks render without the blockquote bar
description: The #446 fix bars quoted prose via flush_blockquote at TagEnd::Paragraph, but TagEnd::Heading and TagEnd::CodeBlock ignore in_blockquote, so a quote mixing prose with a heading or fenced code reads as disconnected blocks. Also separator-guard misfires after list/heading; inner_w can be 0; flush_blockquote duplicates flush_acc.

Re-add confidence REAL (schema v13) WITH a producer (natural/harsh contradiction classification on replace, harsh lowers confidence + marks old entry superseded_by/superseded_at) and a consumer (confidence factors into search rank + eviction). Superseded entries filtered from snapshot but restorable. Branch feat/memory-confidence-supersession.
