title: Route all edit tools through one syntax_gate choke point; edit_minified was missing auto-repair
description: Code review of dirge-p5fu found edit_minified.rs still used the old reject-only check_syntax/format_errors path — it was never migrated to the delimiter auto-repair, because the repair was wired at ~5 near-identical call sites instead of one choke point (the per-site copies had also drifted: note separator was a leading space in apply_patch vs newline elsewhere). Extracted syntax_gate + append_repair_note into agent::tools and routed write/edit/edit_lines/apply_patch(create+update)/edit_minified through it. Uniform note format; no tool can drift out of the contract now. No behavior change for the four already-wired tools; edit_minified gains the repair.
close_reason: Extracted syntax_gate + append_repair_note choke point; all 5 edit tools (incl the previously-missed edit_minified) route through it. Uniform note format. Full suite green (2750).

title: Auto-repair unbalanced delimiters in code edits (parity with JSON truncation repair)
description:
Inconsistency: a truncated tool-call JSON argument is mechanically repaired (tool_input_repair::repair_truncated_json closes braces/brackets, reports notes), but an unbalanced delimiter in code that the model write/edit/apply_patch is only DETECTED (semantic::syntax_validator::check_syntax) and the edit is REJECTED — forcing a wasteful model round-trip for a mechanical fix.

Make code-delimiter handling consistent with JSON: mechanically close and report, rather than bounce to the model.

Design (safety-aware):
- Refactor the comment/string/char-aware scanner into a structured delimiter_balance returning the unclosed-opener stack (with exact positions) OR a stray/mismatched-closer location. delimiter_summary formats from it; existing messages/tests unchanged. This preserves the semantic, exact-position summary the user wants to keep.
- repair_delimiters: ONLY the pure-unclosed case (no stray/mismatched closer). Append the matching closers (top-of-stack first). Then RE-VALIDATE the repaired content with check_syntax — tree-sitter for grammared langs (the oracle that rejects nonsense closes like fn main( { -> })), the scanner for lisps. Apply only if it now parses clean; else fall back to the current reject-with-summary.
- Only available where we have comment/string/char-aware lex rules (lex_rules_for_path) so we never miscount a delimiter inside a string/comment.
- Report the repair as a note on the SUCCESS result (mirrors JSON repair notes), so it is never silent and the model can correct a wrong guess.
- Wire into write/edit/edit_lines/apply_patch.

TDD: structured scan distinguishes unclosed vs stray; comment/string/char-literal awareness (a ) inside a string/comment is not counted); truncated lisp form + truncated brace get closed and validate; stray/mismatched closer is NOT auto-repaired (still rejected with summary); the re-validation gate rejects a close that does not actually produce valid syntax; success note is surfaced. delimiter_summary tests stay green.
close_reason: Added repair_delimiters + validate_or_repair on the structured delimiter_balance scan. Edit tools (write/edit/edit_lines/apply_patch x2) now mechanically close a purely-unclosed delimiter imbalance and report it, instead of rejecting — parity with JSON truncation repair. Safety: only with comment/string/char-aware lex rules, never a stray closer, and the close is re-validated by check_syntax (tree-sitter oracle) before applying. delimiter_summary preserved; existing tests green.

title: Curator bulk view: annotate entries with kind + use count + id
description:
Follow-up to dirge-26h1. The memory curator LLM pass reads two things: the flagged candidate tables (which carry Target/Age/Uses/Id) and the bulk MEMORY.md/PITFALLS.md dump it actually consolidates from. The bulk dump comes from store.rendered(target), which joins raw entry CONTENT only — no kind, no usage, no id. So for any entry not in a candidate table the LLM has zero usage/kind signal to weigh consolidation, removal, or inline promotion.

rendered() must NOT change — it is also the system-prompt injection path and is kept byte-stable for the frozen snapshot. Add a separate store.rendered_for_curator(target) that prefixes each entry with its kind, use_count, and urn id (so the LLM can target it precisely with replace/remove). Wire review.rs run_background_review to pass the annotated text to render_curator_input, and add a one-line legend so the model knows how to read the annotation. Do NOT turn low use-count into a removal trigger — keep the existing keep-bias; usage is context, not a delete rule.

TDD: rendered_for_curator includes kind + uses + id + content; plain rendered() stays metadata-free (regression); curator input carries the legend.
close_reason: Added rendered_for_curator(target) prefixing each entry with [kind | N uses | id]; review.rs feeds it to the curator instead of the content-only render. render_curator_input gained a legend. Removed the now-unused rendered() (it was curator-only, not the prompt path — that's the frozen snapshot, untouched). Tests lock annotation + delimiter join + legend.

title: Promote durable working memory to procedural/semantic via the curator's LLM pass
description:
Working-kind entries (salience 0.3) are first-evicted by design. A working insight that turns out durable (e.g. the test command is cargo test --bin dirge) currently never graduates — it decays/demotes and the knowledge leaks away, not because working crowds out long-term but because nothing re-kinds it. There is no promotion path.

Fix (decided): extend the memory curator LLM consolidation pass (memory_curator.rs MEMORY_CURATOR_PROMPT + spawn_memory_curator_runner, memory-only allow-list) to identify durable working entries and re-kind them to procedural (default) or semantic. The store already supports this: replace_entry(target, old, new, Some(kind)) re-classifies in place, preserving uid/created_at/usage lineage and bumping salience. Runs between sessions, so HOT stays prefix-cache-frozen within a session.

Work: (a) confirm the memory tool surfaces the kind param on replace so the forked curator runner can actually re-kind (add to the tool schema if missing — must stay within the memory-only allow-list); (b) update MEMORY_CURATOR_PROMPT to instruct: promote working entries that are demonstrably durable (aged + repeatedly consulted) to procedural/semantic, with the bias-toward-keeping caveat; (c) surface promotions in LLM_REPORT.md.

TDD: prompt contains the promotion instruction (string test); replace_entry re-kind path covered (working to procedural updates kind + salience, preserves uid/usage); LLM_REPORT renders a promotion action. Depends on the memory-tool kind affordance being reachable from the curator runner.
close_reason: Curator now surfaces aged working entries as promotion candidates (separate from the stale/removal table) and the LLM pass is instructed to re-kind durable ones to procedural/semantic via replace. CurationEntry carries kind; MechanicalReport.promotion_candidates + render table + REPORT.md count added. replace already preserves uid/usage and bumps salience — locked by promote_working_keeps_usage_lineage. Memory tool needed no schema change.

title: Working-memory HOT reserve: cap long-term in-context footprint so working keeps a toehold
description:
Today the 'memory' target HOT budget (DEFAULT_MEMORY_CHAR_LIMIT=2200) is shared by all kinds; add_entry's compaction loop demotes strictly least-salient. Because salience is kind-derived (working 0.3 < procedural 0.5 < semantic 0.6 < identity 0.75), working is always demoted first — which prevents working from diluting long-term, but as long-term knowledge grows a project full of recently-used invariants STARVES working memory of any HOT space.

Fix (decided): reserve a small slice of the memory HOT budget for working-kind entries (DEFAULT_WORKING_HOT_RESERVE ~400 chars, memory target only; pitfalls reserve 0). Make eviction kind-aware so two invariants hold: (1) anti-dilution — adding/keeping working never demotes a long-term entry; (2) anti-starvation — long-term is capped at char_limit - reserve, so it can never evict working below the reserve. Long-term overflow demotes to breadcrumb (already searchable/expandable on demand). Edge: a single long-term entry between (limit-reserve) and limit still fits by using reserve slack (no infinite demote).

TDD: working entries within the reserve survive a flood of high-salience long-term adds; a working add never demotes a long-term entry; long-term overflow lands in breadcrumb not tombstone; existing snapshot/budget tests stay green (adjust any that assumed working-demoted-first within the reserve). Lock both invariants explicitly. Reframes the 'salience floor' idea into a two-sided guarantee.
close_reason: Implemented conditional working HOT reserve (400 chars, memory target). Eviction victim selection is now kind-aware: long-term demoted while it exceeds char_limit-reserve; working overflow past the reserve demoted otherwise. Long-term still uses full budget when working is absent (not a proactive cap). Two-sided guarantee locked by tests; existing eviction tests green.

title: Snapshot store: move process-global STORE to per-session ownership
description:
The /rewind file-snapshot store (src/agent/tools/snapshots.rs) is a process-global `static STORE: LazyLock<Mutex<Store>>`. dirge runs one interactive/headless session per process today, but subagents spawned by the `task` tool run IN-PROCESS and share this global: their file mutations land in whatever turn bucket is current (the parent's), and a parent /rewind can restore subagent-edited files; concurrent subagents can interleave captures. Also blocks multiple top-level sessions per process and forces the test-only global TEST_GATE.

DECISION GATE FIRST: assess whether this is worth the churn. dirge is single-session-per-process; subagent edits to the same repo arguably SHOULD be rewindable by the parent. Legitimate outcomes: (a) per-session refactor, or (b) decide global is acceptable, harden tests, and document. Decide before refactoring.

If refactoring: mirror ToolCache. ToolCache (src/agent/tools/cache.rs) is an Arc<Mutex<..>> handle constructed once per session in src/agent/builder/loop_tools.rs and passed to each tool via with_cache(); it ALREADY holds a per-session read_files set (Arc<Mutex<HashSet<PathBuf>>>). Options: put the snapshot store INSIDE ToolCache, or add a sibling per-session SnapshotStore handle threaded the same way. capture/capture_bytes move to methods on that handle; begin_turn/restore_from/clear operate on the session's store (UI: src/ui/mod.rs begin_snapshot_turn, src/ui/search_rewind.rs restore_from, src/ui/slash/cmd/clear.rs). Resolve: do subagents share the parent store (rewindable by parent) or get their own? Removing the global also lets tests drop TEST_GATE.

Touch points: snapshots.rs (all pub fns), edit.rs/edit_lines.rs/write.rs/apply_patch.rs (capture call sites), loop_tools.rs (construction/threading), ui/mod.rs + search_rewind.rs + slash/cmd/clear.rs.

TDD: keep the existing snapshots tests green; add a test proving two independent stores don't cross-contaminate (replaces the global TEST_GATE serialization).
notes: DECISION: keep the process-global STORE (outcome b), do not refactor. Rationale: dirge is single-session-per-process, so the global IS the session store — no second top-level session to collide with. Subagents run in-process and never call begin_turn (only the UI does, per user message), so their edits intentionally fold into the parent's turn bucket and are parent-rewindable; a per-subagent store would break that, and a per-session handle would behave identically to the global for a much larger surface. No current correctness bug; only blocks a multi-session-per-process mode that is not on the roadmap. TEST_GATE stays as the accepted cost of the global. Documented the contract in snapshots.rs module doc + TEST_GATE doc; added regression test subagent_edits_fold_into_parent_turn_and_are_parent_rewindable locking the shared-store contract.
close_reason: Decision: keep process-global (outcome b). Documented intentional shared-store contract + added regression test; no refactor — global is correct for single-session-per-process and gives parent-rewindable subagent edits.

title: File-state rewind via content-addressed snapshots
description:
Article gap (howardchen DeepSeek V4 piece): dirge's /rewind (src/ui/search_rewind.rs) only truncates the conversation history; it does NOT roll files back to their pre-turn state. The article's content-addressed snapshot makes multi-hour autonomous loops safe (worst-case rollback = minutes + ~$1). Pairs with --goal autonomous runs.

Scope: before any file mutation (write/edit/apply_patch), capture pre-state content of touched files keyed by turn (content-addressed, SHA-256, dedup). Extend /rewind N to restore those files alongside the existing message truncation. Decide storage location (.dirge/sessions/<id>/objects/ analog) + retention.

TDD plan (round 3):
1. Test: snapshot/restore roundtrip for a single mutated file.
2. Test: /rewind N restores files for all turns >= N and truncates history together.
3. Test: partial-turn safety (mutation applied mid-turn still captured).
4. Test: interaction with git worktrees (don't double-restore).
close_reason: Implemented with tests; committed on branch hash-anchored-editing (article gap-closing rounds 1-4)

title: Harness: cross-turn failure recovery + better error feedback for weaker models
description: Audit of how the harness handles model mistakes found that mechanical repair is strong (tool_input_repair, scavenge, fuzzy edit, truncation closer) but cross-turn failure handling and non-mechanical feedback are thin. Adopt proven techniques (structured reflection arxiv 2509.18847/2509.25238, did-you-mean a la aider, tool-doc re-injection arxiv 2510.17874). Three rounds.

title: Memory guidance: explain frozen snapshot so the model doesn't re-add facts

Fix the guidance to explain the snapshot is frozen + writes land next session; make the add tool response signal 'active from next session'; sharpen breadcrumb/tombstone guidance.

title: Phase 3: Non-destructive supersession + bi-temporal time for memory
description:
Add UMP-compatible non-destructive supersession and bi-temporal time model to memory entries.

## Current State
Memory replace() mutates entries in-place via substring match. No history, no supersession chain, no valid time tracking. Remove() deletes entirely.

## Goal
- Add supersedes/superseded_by fields to track replacement chains
- Add time model with valid_from/valid_to (bi-temporal)  
- Replace operations create successors rather than mutating
- Superseded entries are tombstoned, not deleted
- Remove() tombstones by default (optional hard erase)
- Backward-compatible: existing entries get valid_from=now, valid_to=null

## Files
- src/extras/memory_store.rs — add time/supersession fields, update replace/remove logic
- src/extras/memory_provider.rs — update trait signatures if needed
- src/agent/tools/memory.rs — update tool definition for new semantics
- src/extras/memory_usage.rs — track tombstoned entries
notes: Implement against the SQLite memories table (dirge-18ks), not memory_store.rs markdown files. superseded_by column already planned in the v7 schema.
close_reason: tombstone-on-remove/evict + restore + id addressing implemented on sqlite-memory-store branch; replace deliberately stays update-in-place (lineage preserved on the row), bi-temporal valid_from/valid_to dropped as unneeded — reopen if true supersession history becomes a requirement

title: Phase 2: Injection-resistant rehydration framing for memory
description:
Add UMP-style injection-resistant framing wrapper when memory is injected into the system prompt.

## Current State
Memory entries are injected as raw text blocks wrapped in  XML tags. No explicit untrusted-data framing, no sanitization against fence-breaking.

## Goal
- Wrap injected memory in an explicit untrusted-data frame with structural fencing
- Sanitize entry content to prevent fence-breaking (strip forged frame tags, collapse newlines)
- Add a preamble directive that recalled memory is reference data, not instructions

## Files
- src/extras/memory_store.rs — update format_for_system_prompt to use framed output
- src/agent/builder/preamble.rs — ensure framing survives preamble assembly

title: Phase 1: Record identity + kinds + lifecycle for memory entries
description:
Add UMP-compatible record identity, memory kinds, and lifecycle fields to the memory system.

## Current State
Memory entries are plain strings separated by § delimiters in MEMORY.md / PITFALLS.md. No per-entry IDs, no kind classification, no lifecycle tracking.

## Goal
- Add stable, unique record IDs (URN format) per entry
- Add 5 memory kinds: semantic, episodic, procedural, working, identity
- Add lifecycle fields: confidence (0-1), salience (0-1), status (active/candidate/tombstoned)
- Backward-compatible: existing plain-text entries get auto-assigned IDs and default kind=procedural

title: Unified input mechanism: InputMode state machine, dissolve nested modal loops (#387 follow-up)
description: Follow-up to the rendering refactor. User input is handled in 7 scattered places: the main user_rx arm (compose) + 6 nested blocking loops (permission, question options, question custom-input, dialog confirm, dialog select, plan accept/reject) + rewind picker. The nested blocking loops are the root cause of the questionnaire-freeze class of bug and the input-priority concern. Introduce InputMode enum on UiState + one dispatch_input router; dissolve each nested loop into a mode state driven by the central loop; make select! biased so user events take priority. Branch: refactor/unified-rendering-387.
close_reason: Dissolved all nested modal blocking loops into a unified InputMode state machine on UiState + dispatch_modal! router in the single biased user_rx arm. Converted plan-switch, question (incl. custom-text), dialog confirm/select, and permission; rewind picker was already event-driven. Modal-triggering arms gated on !is_modal() so siblings can't clobber an in-flight reply channel. Full --all-features suite green (2603). Commits on refactor/unified-rendering-387; needs interactive smoke-test of each modal before merge.

title: Unified state-driven rendering: single paint per event + UiState struct (#387)
description: GitHub issue #387. Phase 1: centralize all rendering into a single paint per event — add a needs_paint dirty flag + flush() to Renderer, make mutators set the flag instead of inline tui_redraw, build the StatusLine once per event at the loop bottom, collapse ~85 inline render_viewport/draw_bottom/StatusLine call sites. Phase 2: decouple rendering from state by moving the ~37 event-loop state locals into a UiState data structure that RunCtx + the status line read from. Branch: refactor/unified-rendering-387.
notes: DONE on branch refactor/unified-rendering-387 (5 commits). Phase1: UiState data model + Renderer single-paint mechanism (needs_paint/flush/set_bottom). Phase2: migrated 34 event-loop locals into UiState; render_frame! is the single per-event paint effect (builds StatusLine once, dirty-on-change coalescing preserved); collapsed ~85 inline draw_bottom/render_viewport sites (StatusLine::render now appears once in mod.rs, net -300+ lines). Full --all-features suite green. User verified live behavior. Ready for PR.

title: transform-context/on-compact block a tokio worker (no spawn_blocking); message-end skipped in headless
description: agent_loop/plugin_hooks.rs:451-468,498-535: transform_context_from_plugin_manager, on_before, on_compact call mgr.dispatch() directly in the async block while holding the PluginManager std-Mutex, blocking the OS thread up to INTERACTIVE_EVAL_TIMEOUT (30s) per LLM call — unlike tool hooks which use spawn_blocking + timeout (LOOP-8). Separately, message-end / harness/rewrite-message is dispatched only on the interactive done.rs path (:180), never on the headless provider/run.rs path — a silent no-op under --print/--loop/ACP. Fix: wrap these dispatches in spawn_blocking; fire message-end on the headless path too (or document TUI-only).
close_reason: transform-context/on-before-compact/on-compact now run via spawn_blocking + 10s timeout (no tokio-worker stall, PM mutex not held across a slow hook). message-end now also dispatched on the headless apply_response_hooks path with the rewrite stored. Tests added.

title: Phased /plan forks receive the full session transcript, not just explore findings
description: cmd_plan.rs:147-162 + spawn.rs:353 + review.rs:687: both explore and plan forks are passed transcript=build_transcript(session) (entire session history) embedded as <session_transcript>; the plan fork additionally gets findings. The in-code comment 'the ONLY thing carried over is the findings report — a true context reset between phases' is inaccurate: phases are isolated from each other's intermediate tool chatter but NOT from prior session history. Fix: either restrict the plan fork to findings-only as documented, or correct the comment/docs.
close_reason: Plan fork now spawned with an empty transcript (findings-only via plan_prompt) instead of the full session transcript — matches the documented 'true context reset between phases'. Explore fork keeps the transcript as entry context. Plan suite green.

title: context-depth tracker counts per tool-call, not per turn, contradicting its docs/reminder
description: context_depth.rs docstring, Inner.consecutive, and the emitted reminder all say 'consecutive turns', but record_tool_call is invoked once per tool call (tools.rs:170 sequential, :879 parallel -> :443). Test touches_same_files_increments_consecutive confirms 3 calls => consecutive=3. A single turn with 5 edits to one file bumps consecutive by 5, so the reminder fires far earlier than 'N turns' implies and reports an inflated count. Fix: count per turn, or correct the wording/threshold.
close_reason: Wording corrected across module docstring, Inner field comments, the emitted reminder, features.md, and config.md to say 'consecutive tool calls' (the real per-call unit) instead of 'turns'. Behavior unchanged; test updated.

title: DAP has no session-end teardown; relies on Drop of a static that never runs
description: dap/session.rs:29: DAP_MANAGER is a static Option<Arc<DapSessionManager>>. Debuggee/adapter teardown depends on DapProcessGuard::drop -> kill(-pgid, SIGKILL), but a static is never dropped on normal process exit, and there is no exit hook calling terminate_active/disconnect (contrast LSP's close_all_files at main.rs:1273). Within a session terminate_active runs before each new launch, but on dirge exit a setsid-isolated adapter+debuggee can be orphaned. Fix: add a session-end/atexit hook that terminates the active DAP session.
close_reason: Added dap::session::shutdown_active_session() (terminates the active session via terminate_active) and called it on the interactive exit path beside the LSP close_all_files step, so a DAP adapter+debuggee isn't orphaned when the static manager is never Dropped.

title: /panel auto real threshold is ~152 cols, not the documented 100; PANEL_AUTO_MIN_COLS is dead
description: renderer.rs:1103-1110: side_panel_visible for Auto requires cols>=100 AND content_indent()>=15. content_indent (=:1163) only reaches 15 once cols>=152 (content_width capped at 120). So between 100 and ~151 cols /panel auto (and /panel on) show nothing, and PANEL_AUTO_MIN_COLS=100 (:108) is effectively dead — the indent>=15 gate always binds. README:126 says '>=100 cols'. Fix: reconcile the constant + docs with the real threshold.
close_reason: PANEL_AUTO_MIN_COLS set to 152 (the real cols at which content_indent reaches 15); README/config/features docs corrected from >=100 to >=152. Test pins the constant to the gutter math.

title: --no-color is bypassed by hardcoded diff +/- background ANSI escapes
description: ui/run_handlers/tool_result.rs:310-315 -> box_render.rs:283-290 bake \x1b[48;5;22m (green) / \x1b[48;5;52m (red) directly into diff rows. write_line stores the string verbatim; theme::no_color() (theme.rs:481) only collapses colors routed through theme::*() accessors. Under --no-color, diff lines still paint green/red backgrounds — the one stray-escape bypass of the single-chokepoint design. Fix: source the diff backgrounds from the theme chokepoint.
close_reason: row_with_bg now sources its +/- background escapes via diff_bg_escapes(bg_idx, theme::no_color()) — empty under --no-color. Pure helper tested.

title: apply_summary/compute_compress_window can orphan a tool_use/tool_result pair (latent 400)
description: compression.rs:691-742: the compaction window is message-count based (end = n - protect_tail). assistant tool_calls and each tool_result are separate messages (run.rs:1071,1104,1117). The tail/head boundary can leave an orphaned tool_result (or retain an assistant tool_call whose result was folded), producing an unbalanced history that 400s Anthropic/OpenAI. heal/fix_tool_call_pairing runs ONLY on session load (integration.rs:628), never after a fold. The handle_compress path guards this via align_cut_to_user_boundary (mod.rs:91) — the two compaction impls diverged. LATENT today only because summarize_fn is unwired; becomes live HIGH if that is wired. Fix: snap the window to tool-pair/user boundaries or re-run fix_tool_call_pairing after every fold.
close_reason: compute_compress_window now snaps both cuts to user-message boundaries (head forward, tail backward) so the fold can't orphan a tool_use/tool_result pair. Test: compute_window_snaps_off_tool_pairs.

title: prune_tool_outputs silently no-ops on production block-array tool results
description: compression.rs:419 reads msg content via as_str(); production tool results are block arrays (message.rs:289-298, content = Vec<ContentBlock>). Array content => None => never pruned. So the only compaction that runs in the live loop does nothing to real tool results; headroom is held solely by cap_oversized_tool_results (run.rs:912). The estimator and the cap were widened for blocks (dirge-el3n); this pass was not. Fix: handle block-array content in prune_tool_outputs. (Closely tied to the summarize_fn-dead issue.)
close_reason: prune_tool_outputs now reads text from both scalar-string and block-array content and preserves the array shape on rewrite; the in-loop prune pass (run.rs:378) is no longer a no-op on real tool results. Tests: prune_handles_block_array_content, prune_leaves_small_block_array_untouched.

title: allow_tools does not restrict MCP or plugin tools (reads as a whitelist, only caps built-ins)
description: context/agent_defs.rs:72-83: ToolPolicy::Allow is realized as 'deny every built-in not in the allow-list' over BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES. MCP/plugin tools are not enumerable there, so a profile allow_tools: [read, grep] leaves every MCP/plugin tool fully callable. Users reasonably read allow_tools as a hard whitelist. Fix: extend allow_tools to deny non-listed MCP/plugin tools (e.g. deny mcp_tool umbrella + unlisted plugin tools), or document the limitation prominently.
close_reason: Added plugin_tool to BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES so ToolPolicy::Allow->deny denies the plugin umbrella (mcp_tool was already covered). allow_tools is now a genuine cap over built-ins + MCP + plugin; listing an umbrella re-allows that class. Doc corrected, test added.

title: edit_minified is invisible to the verifier gate and misclassified by the storm breaker
description: verifier.rs:76 hardcodes match tool_name { write|edit|apply_patch }, so an agent editing exclusively via edit_minified (a registered built-in, tools/mod.rs:97) never sets edited_code and the 'verify before done' gate stays silent on unverified code changes. Separately, permission/engine/build.rs:42-62 maps edit/apply_patch/write to Operation::Edit but edit_minified falls through to Operation::Other, so storm (storm.rs:209) does not treat it as mutating (a verify-read after a minified edit can be miscounted). MITIGATED: edit_minified presents as 'edit' to enforce, so plan-mode permission denies still cover it. Fix: derive verifier + storm classification from tool_operation and add edit_minified to the Edit mapping.
close_reason: Added edit_minified->Edit and read_minified->Read to tool_operation (fixes storm default_mutating/default_exempt) and edit_minified to the verifier gate's edit arm. Tests added.

After /agent architect (model->opus) then /agent off, the session stays on opus. Also profile->profile switches where the new profile has no model leave the prior profile's model active. title: Config-driven, opt-in multi-agent mechanism (unify role-routing + critic + user agents)
description: dirge already routes ROLES to different models via config (provider / review_provider[critic] / escalation_provider / compact_model / subagent). Forge generalizes this: user-defined agents in .forge/agents/*.md (id, system prompt, tools, model, reasoning), lazy-loaded into a registry, each overriding model/provider, layered CWD->global->builtin; agents become /agent-<name> commands. DESIGN GOAL for dirge: a UNIFIED, OPT-IN, config-driven agent mechanism where the existing roles (critic/escalation/summarizer/subagent) are special built-in agents and users can define custom ones (name + prompt + tools + model + reasoning) in config.json or .dirge/agents/. Opt-in: absent config = today's single-agent behavior unchanged. Brings: /agent-<name> commands, per-agent model override. Reuse: adapt Forge's agent_definition.rs schema + agent_registry.rs (forge_repo/forge_services). HIGH value, needs a design spike first. Source: ~/src/forgecode.
design:
UNIFIED AGENT MECHANISM (opt-in, config-driven). Generalize the existing ConfigRole (Default/Review/Escalation/Summarization/Subagent/Critic/Approval — each a config key routing to a providers-alias model via resolve_role) into a named AGENT = { prompt, model, tools, reasoning, temperature }. Built-in roles become reserved built-in agents (today model-only); users can define custom agents and override built-ins (e.g. give the critic a custom prompt). role->model becomes the model slice of agent->{model,prompt,tools}.

CONFIG SOURCE (decided: BOTH, layered): (a) .dirge/agents/<name>.md — YAML frontmatter + prompt body, SAME shape as dirge skills (reuse the skill frontmatter parser), project dir + global ~/.config/dirge/agents/; (b) config.json agents:{ name: { model, prompt, tools:{allow|deny}, reasoning, temperature } } for inline one-offs. PRECEDENCE: project file > global file > config.json > built-in. No agents configured => today's single-agent behavior unchanged (fully additive/opt-in). The existing *_provider keys stay as backward-compat sugar that sets a built-in agent's model.

AGENT FIELDS: name; prompt (inline | @file | named dirge prompt | none->default); model (Option<providers alias>; None->default, reuses resolve_role plumbing); tools (all | {allow:[..]} | {deny:[..]} — reuse prompt deny_tools enforcement at the permission layer); reasoning effort/budget; temperature.

INVOCATION: /agent interactive picker + dynamic /agent-<name> tab-completable commands that switch the active agent (prompt/model/tools) for the session (reuse Forge's sanitize+register from plans/2025-09-13-dynamic-agent-slash-commands-v3.md). Later: /plan phases + the task subagent can target a named agent.

REUSE (port, don't rewrite): Forge crates/forge_repo/src/agent_definition.rs (schema/frontmatter) + crates/forge_services/src/agent_registry.rs (lazy-load + layering + precedence) + plans/2025-09-08-agent-loader-cwd-extension-v1.md (CWD->global->builtin precedence) + plans/2025-09-13-dynamic-agent-slash-commands-v3.md. dirge side: reuse src/skill.rs frontmatter parser, config resolve_role plumbing, prompt deny_tools enforcement.

PHASED DELIVERY: (1) AgentDefinition + loader (both sources) + registry with precedence + guardrail test — LOAD ONLY, no behavior change. (2) /agent picker + /agent-<name> commands switch active agent. (3) fold built-in roles (critic/review/escalation/summarizer/subagent/approval) into the registry; *_provider keys become sugar. (4) optional — route /plan phases + task subagents to named agents.
notes: Phases 1-3 implemented in PR #385 (branch feat/agent-profiles), all CI green: AgentDefinition/AgentRegistry loader (3 layered sources), /agent <name> switching (model+prompt+tools, same-client), /agents unified view incl. built-in role routing. Built-in critic/role routing untouched (opt-in preserved). Phase 4 (route task/subagent + /plan to named profiles; cross-provider /agent client switch) filed as separate follow-up.

title: /compact (explicit) should force compaction, not be gated by threshold
description: When the loop auto-compacts it correctly checks context is over threshold (should_compress / decide_after_usage). But an explicit user /compact command is currently treated like a suggestion — it appears to be gated by the same threshold check, so /compact below the threshold is a no-op. Explicit /compact must be definitive: force the compaction pass regardless of current context fraction. Separate the 'auto' path (threshold-gated) from the 'user-commanded' path (forced).

title: Unify the mid-loop interjection layer (5+ inject sites)

Notably verifier silently blocks critic via 'if follow_up.is_empty()' so the critic verdict never surfaces on a turn that also has a red build, and MID_TURN_STEER_WRAPPER is applied at two independent sites. Design + build one interjection abstraction with explicit priority and a single wrap-once point. MED — top consolidation target for a smoother loop.

title: Single context-budget authority (estimate+thresholds+action)
description: Three modules independently decide 'context is filling': compression.rs (pre-send per-result caps + should_compress), context_manager.rs (post-response fold/exit tiers), context_depth.rs (ambient reminder). Pre-send uses a chars/4 ESTIMATE while post-response uses the API's ACTUAL prompt_tokens — two disagreeing numbers — plus a snip-feedback override living only in run.rs that's invisible to the decision engine. Consolidate into one ContextBudget owning the estimate, all tier thresholds, and the chosen action. MED.

title: Permissions: configured 'deny' rules are not terminal — overridable by session allow-always
description:
FORMAL FINDING (chiasmus_verify/Z3 on the Stage-A decider precedence in permission/engine/policies.rs).

Decider precedence (first-claim-wins): 1 prompt-deny, 2 yolo, 3 session-allow, 4 configured-rule, 5 builtin-allow, 6 external-dir, 7 default. A user's configured 'deny' rule sits at precedence 4 — BELOW session-allow (3) and yolo (2). Only frontmatter prompt-deny (1) is truly terminal.

Z3 results:
- SAT: configured-rule votes Deny yet final=Allow, witnessed by session-allow claiming Allow at precedence 3 (above 4).
- UNSAT (proven): absent yolo+session-allow, a configured Deny IS terminal — so the override path is EXACTLY yolo + session-allow.
- UNSAT (proven): prompt-deny is unconditionally terminal (good).

Aggravator: ui/permission_ui.rs::suggest_pattern defaults session allow-always grants to BROAD globs (path tools -> '<parent>/**', e.g. editing /etc/foo suggests /etc/**), confirmable with one 'a' keypress. So a NARROW config deny (e.g. 'deny edit /etc/secret') is shadowed once the user allow-always-es a sibling path /etc/foo -> pattern /etc/** (session precedence 3 > configured deny 4). yolo>configured-deny is documented + startup-warned; session-allow>configured-deny is not.

Impact: explicit user deny guardrails in config are silently defeatable by a one-keypress, broad-by-default session grant.

Fix options (need decision): (a) move SessionAllowlistPolicy below configured DENY rules; (b) split configured rules so DENY is a terminal decider above session-allow/yolo (makes 'deny' absolute like prompt-deny); (c) at Engine::allow_always, refuse or narrow a session grant whose pattern overlaps a configured deny. TDD + Z3 re-verify after.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #310: ConfiguredDenyPolicy terminal above session-allow (below yolo). Z3-verified: configured deny terminal absent yolo (UNSAT); yolo still overrides (SAT). Covers main + external_directory rules; last-match-wins preserved.

title: Plugin notification/custom-message buffers grow unbounded per turn (no backpressure)
description: harness-notif-list and harness-custom-messages are Janet strings appended to by harness/notify and harness/add-custom-message, drained only at the per-turn boundary. A plugin that calls notify/add-custom-message in a hot hook (on-message-update fires every ~16 tokens) accumulates these strings without bound within a turn — an untrusted-producer memory leak (same trust model as the os/exit hardening). Fix: cap per-turn accumulation; once over the cap, append a single 'dropped' marker and stop appending until the host drains (clears to ""), which resets the marker.
close_reason: Fixed in #285: per-turn cap on harness-notif-list (64KiB) and harness-custom-messages (128KiB) with a single drop-marker and reset-on-drain. Tests + full plugin suite green.

description: default_model_for(alias) matches parse_provider on the bare alias (built-in names only); a custom alias with no model falls to the OpenRouter default, sending an invalid model id to OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. Callers: main.rs:406, build_escalation/critic/approval/review_stream_fn. Fix: resolve provider_type_of(alias, entry) before default_model_for.
close_reason: Fixed in round 4 provider/MCP batch (TDD): config-alias collision skip, default_model_for_entry/alias provider-type resolution, StderrLineSplitter drain. Full suite green.

title: Aliasing a built-in provider name with base_url rejected as collision (contradicts docs)
description: resolve_provider_info rejects a config entry that aliases a built-in backend name with a custom base_url as a BUILTIN_PROVIDER_NAMES collision, but docs/config.md documents exactly that (e.g. ollama: provider_type openai + base_url). Fix: skip the collision check for config-declared aliases; keep it only for plugin providers.
close_reason: Fixed in round 4 provider/MCP batch (TDD): config-alias collision skip, default_model_for_entry/alias provider-type resolution, StderrLineSplitter drain. Full suite green.

title: Concurrent dirge processes trigger false memory drift, renaming MEMORY.md to .bak
description: reload_and_detect_drift treats a disk mismatch with both in-memory entries AND the load-time snapshot as external corruption; two sessions in one project make a legit write look like corruption -> file renamed to .bak and write refused. Fix: accept disk as truth when superset/compatible, or compare a persisted last-written content hash under the lock.
close_reason: Fixed in round 3 stability batch (TDD): LSP SpawnSlotGuard, edit keep_disjoint_ranges, memory superset-drift, per-attempt lock staleness. Full suite green.

title: Non-semantic-bash build does not gate bash redirect/mutation targets
description: On --no-default-features (semantic-bash off), check_bash_segments only does quote_aware_split for Execute claims and never scans redirect/mutation targets, so echo > /etc/passwd is ungated. Fix: add a regex/byte-scan fallback for redirect targets + known mutator path args in the cfg(not(semantic-bash)) branch.
close_reason: Fixed in round 2 security batch (TDD): invisible-char typo, atomic_write umask split, coarse bash redirect/mutation gating, MCP nested-arg path walk. Tests pass default + no-default-features.

title: Agent-created files get 0600 instead of umask 0644
description: fs_atomic::atomic_write_sync sets new files to 0o600 (owner-only); it is the shared write path for write/edit/apply_patch tools, so agent-created project files are owner-only instead of umask 0644. The 0600 was meant only for session/memory JSON. Fix: do not force 0600 for new files in the shared path; gate it behind a param used only by session/memory callers.
close_reason: Fixed in round 2 security batch (TDD): invisible-char typo, atomic_write umask split, coarse bash redirect/mutation gating, MCP nested-arg path walk. Tests pass default + no-default-features.

title: BOM/ZWNBSP invisible-char guard typo: U+0FEF should be U+FEFF (2 sites)
description: INVISIBLE_CHARS lists \u{fef} (U+0FEF, Tibetan) where it intends the BOM/zero-width-no-break-space U+FEFF, so BOM injection is never blocked. Sites: skills/guard.rs:23 and memory_store.rs:99. Fix: \u{fef} -> \u{feff}.
close_reason: Fixed in round 2 security batch (TDD): invisible-char typo, atomic_write umask split, coarse bash redirect/mutation gating, MCP nested-arg path walk. Tests pass default + no-default-features.

title: Session tests leak fixtures into the user's real session store (recent-sessions noise)
description: The runtime new_session handler calls save_session; its hook tests build sessions with model 'm' and 'stale'/'outgoing' messages and trigger it WITHOUT isolating DIRGE_DATA_DIR, persisting fixtures into ~/.../dirge/sessions and polluting the user's recent-sessions list on every cargo test. Fix: under cfg(test), route dirs_path() to a per-process temp dir so tests can never write to the real data dir.

title: Loop: max_turns kills active human steering; reset budget on fresh user steering
description: The per-run turn counter (max_turns, default 100) accumulates across the whole run and is never reset when the user interjects/steers. A user actively steering a progressing agent gets killed by the cap as if it were a runaway loop. Runaway loops are caught by the storm breaker; the cap is a cost ceiling for AUTONOMOUS runs. Fix: reset turns_taken when a fresh USER steering message is consumed (not file reminders or plugin/critic follow-ups).

title: Memory: compact (evict oldest) instead of failing the write when budget is full
description: When a memory add() would exceed the per-file char budget, it returned 'Char budget exceeded' and the model gave up. Instead, compact: evict the oldest entries until the new one fits. Only a single entry larger than the whole budget is a real error (split it). Surface the compacted count in the success message.

title: Add approval_provider: LLM auto-approves permission prompts
description: Optional config approval_provider. When set, a permission Ask is routed to that LLM (with a clear safety prompt explaining dangerous ops: deleting files, committing/modifying outside project or /tmp, network code-exec, sudo) instead of prompting the human; the LLM returns ALLOW/DENY and the system acts on it. Mirror critic_provider wiring. Document in docs/permissions.md.
close_reason: approval_provider added: per-session evaluator on the checker; only intercepts Ask; fail-safe to human; shared one-shot LLM helper. Merged in PR.

title: Make background-injected MCP tools search-gated under dynamic_tool_search
description: Follow-up to dirge-ffwa. The shortcut fix marks injected MCP tools as always-loaded (always shipped in the request) which erodes dynamic_tool_search's token savings for heavy-MCP users. Proper fix: make ToolSearchTool.registry an Arc<Mutex<Vec<ToolMeta>>>, store the handle on AnyAgent, and have extend_loop_tools append the injected tools' meta to it (discoverable via tool_search, hidden until requested) instead of marking them loaded. Keeps behavior identical to build-time MCP tools.
close_reason: ToolSearchTool registry is now Arc<Mutex<Vec<ToolMeta>>>; extend_loop_tools appends injected MCP tools' meta to it so they're search-gated (discoverable via tool_search, not always-shipped). Merged in PR #268.

title: Startup: load MCP tools in background so the TUI draws immediately
description: Even with parallel connect_all, the interactive UI still blocks on MCP before the first frame because the slowest server (e.g. 'npx -y chiasmus' cold start) gates build_agent's collect_tools. Build the interactive agent with NO MCP tools, draw the UI immediately, and connect+collect MCP in a background task; deliver (manager, wrapped tools) over a channel to run_interactive's select loop, which injects the tools into the live agent (next clone picks them up) and stores the manager so the panel lights up. Non-interactive (--print/--loop) keep connecting synchronously.
close_reason: Interactive TUI now builds the agent without MCP tools and draws immediately; a background task connects+collects+injects MCP tools into the live agent and lights up the panel when ready. --print/--loop unchanged. Merged in PR #266.

title: Startup: parallelize MCP connect_all to cut time-to-first-frame
description: connect_all (src/extras/mcp/mod.rs:32) connects MCP servers sequentially in a for-loop, so startup pays the SUM of every server's spin-up. With several servers each doing an 'npx -y <pkg>' cold start (seconds) and a 10s per-server init timeout, the UI takes several seconds to appear. Parallelize the connects with futures::join_all so startup waits only for the slowest server, not all in series. Keep bookkeeping (insert/log order, failure handling) deterministic.
close_reason: MCP servers now connect concurrently (futures::join_all); startup waits for slowest server, not the sum. Merged in PR #265.

title: Right panel: MODIFIED box tall when empty + bash file mutations don't propagate
description: Two right-side-panel bugs. (A) The MODIFIED sub-panel takes all remaining vertical space even when empty, rendering very tall; it should be one line tall like TODOS '(none)' and grow with content. (B) Files created/deleted via bash (heredoc 'cat > f', 'rm', 'mv') do not appear in MODIFIED because bash.rs never calls mark_modified; only write/edit/apply_patch do. Reuse extract_redirect_targets + extract_mutation_paths (already computed for permission checks) to mark bash mutations.
close_reason: Fixed: empty MODIFIED collapses to 1 line; bash heredoc/rm/mv mutations now propagate. Merged in PR #264.

title: Generalize syntax-error feedback: missing-token + per-language delimiter localization
description: Make pre-write syntax errors mechanically useful for all tree-sitter languages: (1) name the expected token from tree-sitter MISSING nodes; (2) generalize the Lisp delimiter-balance scanner to brace languages via per-language lexing rules.

title: Lisp paren feedback + retry budget + additive LSP extensions
description: (1) Enrich tree-sitter pre-write errors for Lisp with a delimiter-balance summary so the model stops counting parens. (2) Increase retry budget for transient LLM API failures. (3) Additive lsp extensions config (extend builtin list).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #261 (paren feedback, retry budget, lsp extend_extensions)

title: UI/permission tweaks: whitespace, autocomplete, double-click, compound-bash perms
description: Batch of minor fixes: (1) trim/collapse whitespace in slash command args; (2) ghost-text slash autocomplete with right-key accept; (3) double-click word select; (4) compound bash command re-prompts because allow-rule covers only the first segment.

title: F6.3: bounded in-loop LLM critic (tier 3)
description: Optional critic_provider role; when configured, run one bounded LLM critique at finalization on substantive runs. CriticFn callback mirrors SummarizeFn; reuses summarize_with_model. Off unless critic_provider set.

title: F6.2: outcome-aware verifier (tier 2)
description: Upgrade VerifierGate to track whether a build/test command ran and PASSED or FAILED (via bash exit-code marker). At finalization: red build → fix-it nudge; edited-but-no-verification → verify nudge; verified-pass → silent. Records post-execution at finalize_executed_tool_call.

title: Phase D: cross-feature integration tests + consolidated docs
description: Prove all 6 guidance features compose: base-prompt cohesion (F2+F3+F5) + combined loop test (F1+F6 in one run). Consolidated docs section.

title: F6: pre-finalization verifier gate
description: Cheap signal-based in-loop critic: nudge to verify before done when code edited but no shell command ran. Reuses get_followup_messages finalization seam + FileTouchTracker pattern. Bounded once per run, no LLM call.

title: F4: in-session reflexion memory
description: Accumulate abandoned approaches across a run and re-surface them in the repeat-loop guard. Reuses storm detection + reflect-then-pivot injection. Reflexion (Shinn 2023) episodic buffer.

title: F5: uncertainty-calibrated ask-vs-assume
description: Base-prompt calibration for when to ask the user vs proceed: weigh cost/recoverability/inferability/divergence; otherwise proceed with the most reasonable interpretation and state the assumption. Self-assessed (no logprobs available). Research: Ask or Assume?

title: F3: progress / tool-preamble narration
description: All-models base-prompt guidance: brief up-front plan for multi-step tasks + terse progress notes between major steps. Scoped to long tool runs, NOT the final reply (reconciled with the terse-output ethos). Research: GPT-5.1 tool preambles.

title: F2: definition-of-done + pre-reply self-check + stop conditions
description: All-models base-prompt guidance: a single fast self-check before claiming done, an explicit definition of done, and stop conditions (when to stop vs hand back). Research: GPT-5 prompting guide.

title: F1: few-shot tool-use exemplars via lexical (nucleo) retrieval
description: Curated exemplar corpus; query-aware retrieval by token overlap using nucleo-matcher (reuse in-repo dev-dep, promote to dep). Inject top-k exemplars for the user's task into the turn context. All models.

title: Epic: close harness-guidance gaps (few-shot, self-check, progress, reflexion, ask-calibration, critic)
description: 6 general-purpose model-agnostic guidance features from the research gap analysis. TDD, branch-per-feature, sequential merge, reuse existing infra, integration tests at the end.

title: P4: structured tool-error self-repair hint
description: On malformed/failed tool call return structured repair hint so model self-corrects. Wire into tool-result seam.
close_reason: Already implemented: tool_input_repair.rs (validate_and_repair + format_structured_error wired into dispatch). No new work needed.

title: P3: dual-encode load-bearing rules into tool descriptions
description: Fold read-before-edit, no-repeat-failed-call, parallel-vs-sequential into tool descriptions at the action boundary. Helps all models.

title: P2: DeepSeek-gated guidance markdown fragment
description: prompts/steering/deepseek.md embedded via include_str!, appended to preamble only when vendor==Deepseek. Structural framing, plan-execute-verify, success/never contract, anti-repetition.

title: Epic: DeepSeek-aware harness steering for better reasoning
description: Add model-family detection + DeepSeek-gated guidance + cross-model tool-description hardening + structured tool-error self-repair. Baked-in/automatic, no config keys. Research-backed: structural prompting, plan-execute-verify, anti tool-call drift/repetition.

title: nrepl plugin: fix try-body compile error, bencode framing, eval timeout; correct docs
description: The bundled nrepl plugin never loaded (multi-form try bodies are a Janet compile error). Also: bencode reader dropped coalesced/partial TCP messages; os/time timeout math was 1000x off; README wrongly required external janet on PATH.

title: Hidden side panels don't give freed space to chat
description: The /display feature hides side panels but Layout::new always reserves symmetric gutters regardless of show_left_panel/show_right_panel. Hidden panels leave blank reserved space instead of expanding the main chat pane. Fix: thread panel visibility into layout so a hidden panel's gutter is reclaimed by the chat band.
close_reason: Layout is now visibility-aware via Layout::with_panels; hidden panel gutters are reclaimed by the chat band

title: /display command + config to choose visible TUI panes
description: Add /display left|main|right slash command and 'display' config key to control which side panels show, independently per side. Main pane always shown.

title: harness/lsp: (harness/lsp?) reports available when LSP runtime-disabled
description: Predicate checks compile-time symbol existence, not runtime manager. When lsp_manager is None (config-disabled), predicate is true but queries return nil -> plugin json/decode crashes. Make availability reflect a live bridge.

title: Input box: Up/Down arrow nav across soft-wrapped display rows
description: After the scroll fix (dirge-5w9v), Up/Down still move by HARD newlines only (prev_line_start/next_line_start); in a wrapped paragraph with no \n, Up falls through to history recall. Make vertical motion wrap-aware: map the cursor to its display (row,col) via wrap_editor's projection and move to the adjacent display row, then back to a raw byte offset (handling the editor's paste-marker display projection). Reuse wrap_editor; don't duplicate wrap logic.

title: MED: cancelled tool future keeps running detached (work leak)
description: Dispatcher races wait_for_cancel vs tool future; on cancel returns an aborted result but lets the tool future continue (tools.rs:515-529 comment confirms no force-kill). In-process work (MCP call) leaks. bash converts abort->process kill; MCP/LSP rely on Drop. 3 cancellation primitives (AbortSignal atomic, CancellationToken, killpg). Fix: standardize one token + race-then-drop/kill helper. tools.rs:515-543, tool.rs:41.
close_reason: Fixed + merged in PR #210: Notify-backed AbortSignal (instant cancel) + drop-contract regression test; verified drop-on-cancel is sound

title: MED: data/config dir overrides honored inconsistently; web-enable precedence duplicated
description: DIRGE_DATA_DIR honored in storage.rs:15 but ignored by loop transcript.rs:5 (uses dirs::data_dir directly) -> split state. DIRGE_CONFIG_DIR honored in storage.rs:23 but plugins(main.rs:574)/themes/prompts re-derive ~/.config/dirge. Also webfetch/websearch enable precedence (cfg||env_true) copy-pasted builder.rs:457 & :905. Fix: export storage::dirs_path/config_path as the single base; add Cli::resolve_web*_enabled.
close_reason: Merged in PR #212: exa_api_key/web-enable helpers, DIRGE_DATA_DIR transcript + DIRGE_CONFIG_DIR plugin routing

title: MED: no tool-result boundary pipeline (truncation x3, no shared cap)
description: LLM cap (~12000 chars, compression.rs) and UI cap (500/tool_result_max_chars, tool_display.rs:251) are separate codepaths w/ different markers; plus 5 per-tool caps (bash 256KB, background 3000 silent, grep 4096, review 2000, list_dir 200). A bash result truncates up to 3x w/ 3 markers; config knobs only bind UI. Fix: one TruncationPolicy / boundary layer (redact->cap->format). Pairs with dirge-tkyn.
close_reason: Merged in PR #214: shared head_cap (output byte caps, fixes silent drop) + required_nonblank (per-action arg checks)

title: MED: conditional required-for-action validation hand-rolled per multiplexer tool
description: memory/skill/lsp re-derive which fields are required for the chosen action with bespoke ok_or/is_none + divergent messages, no repair. JSON Schema can't express conditional-required. Fix: dirge-hints conditional_required rule ({when:{action:add},require:[content]}) in validate_and_repair. memory.rs:129, skill.rs:131, lsp.rs:197.
close_reason: Merged in PR #214: shared head_cap (output byte caps, fixes silent drop) + required_nonblank (per-action arg checks)

title: MED: absolute-path enforcement duplicated across 4 tools despite semantic tag
description: read/write/edit/apply_patch each re-implement Path::is_absolute() with divergent error strings, though a semantic:'absolute_path' dirge-hint tag (tool_input_repair.rs:710) is designed to own it (only read declares it; only used for md-link unwrap). Fix: validate_and_repair rejects AbsolutePath-tagged fields failing is_absolute, one message. read.rs:184/write.rs:94/edit.rs:137/apply_patch.rs:276. Part of chokepoint-A.
close_reason: Fixed + merged in PR #207: shared require_absolute_path helper

title: MEDIUM: op:* config rules use path-style globbing
description: pattern_for_op maps OpSpec::Any to path-style Pattern::new, so blanket {op:*} rules with a single * silently under-match commands/mcp keys (git * misses git push origin/main).
close_reason: Fixed + merged in PR #204 (TDD, 4 new tests); 2104 tests pass at -D warnings

title: Central MemoryProvider hook dispatcher (audit finding A)
description: The 4 MemoryProvider hooks (on_memory_write, on_session_end, on_pre_compress, on_session_switch) fire from 40 callsites across 11 production files: main.rs, ui/mod.rs, ui/plugin_tree.rs, ui/slash/cmd_session.rs, ui/slash/mod.rs, provider/mod.rs, agent/review.rs, agent/tools/memory.rs, agent/agent_loop/run.rs, agent/agent_loop/integration.rs, extras/memory_provider.rs. Adding a 5th hook requires hunting every site; easy to forget one → silent inconsistency. Build a central dispatcher (single 'fire_hook' helper or a HookBus) so every callsite goes through one path. Foundation for future hooks (after_turn, post_review, etc).

title: Memory curator + lifecycle (audit finding B)
description: MEMORY.md and PITFALLS.md have no consolidation, no stale-detection, no audit. Skills get the full ops surface (curator, 30d/90d lifecycle, .usage.json telemetry, pinning, .curator_reports/, LLM consolidation via dirge-odv3). Memory entries get none of it — MEMORY.md grows forever with no path to merge overlapping facts or retire stale ones. Build a memory curator that mirrors src/extras/skills/curator.rs for memory entries: mechanical lifecycle pass + LLM consolidation pass. Reuse the review.rs runner infrastructure where it fits.

title: Auto-compaction / Phase 3: turn-end per-tool-result cap
description: Reasonix shrinks every tool result >3000 tokens at every turn-end (TURN_END_RESULT_CAP_TOKENS). Dirge only shrinks via prune_tool_outputs INSIDE a fold pass triggered at 75% context — a single 50KB tool output stays verbatim until fold fires. Add per-result cap at every turn boundary, independent of fold.

title: more descriptive session summaries in /sessions listing
description: Current /sessions preview is the last 30 chars of the last message — useless for tests/empty sessions ('...stale', '...outgoing'). Derive a better preview: (1) compaction summary's Active Task / Goal line if present, (2) first user message truncated, (3) fall back to last message.

title: CI matrix: build each feature group at least once
description: Default cargo build doesn't compile acp/plugin/lsp/loop/semantic-* code paths. Recent regressions slipped through: ACP build broke when build_agent gained session_id, plugin_hooks_tests broke when run_agent_loop gained memory_provider. Add CI matrix exercising each feature group.

title: on_session_switch fires in inconsistent state window
description: ui/mod.rs:2241 fires after DB rotation + messages drain, but BEFORE save_session (line 2245). A provider that queries DB or on-disk JSON during the hook sees inconsistent triple state. Move the hook to after save_session OR move save_session to before the rotation.

title: compaction handler doesn't rebuild agent — SessionSearchTool stale
description: ui/mod.rs:2236 fires on_session_switch + updates session.id but does NOT rebuild agent. The agent's SessionSearchTool was constructed with the pre-rotation session_id; after rotation it excludes the wrong session. dirge-502b fixed this for /session swap but not for compaction rotation.

title: --print save_session? short-circuits past on_session_end fire
description: main.rs:816 uses ? which propagates save errors up, skipping the on_session_end fire at line 823. Failed save is exactly when plugin providers need the hook (their backend is the only durable record). Fix: fire before save OR handle save error inline.

title: /session swap fires on_session_end but never on_session_switch
description: cmd_session.rs:105 rotates session.id via *ctx.session = s after firing on_session_end. The incoming id never triggers on_session_switch — exactly the case the trait docstring describes ('cache per-session state, document ids, counters').

title: fire on_session_end on clean CLI exit
description: No call site fires on_session_end when the user exits the program normally (loop terminates). Add a shutdown hook in run_interactive or main.rs after the loop exits cleanly.

title: fire on_session_end on compaction-driven session rotation
description: ui/mod.rs:2224 changes session.id after compaction — the OLD session has effectively ended. Fire on_session_end with the pre-rotation transcript before the id assignment so plugin providers receive the session boundary.
notes: On reflection this is on_session_switch (mid-process id change), not on_session_end. Add the hook to the trait and fire it at the compaction rotation point.

title: fire on_session_end on /clear (session reset)
description: cmd_clear truncates session messages without firing on_session_end. /clear is a genuine session-reset boundary; hermes fires the hook on /reset analog. Wire it before the clear.

title: use MemoryProvider trait through builder.rs preamble
description: builder.rs:212 still calls the concrete MemoryToolStore::format_for_system_prompt. A plugin provider's prompt block won't appear. Change builder.rs to hold Option<Arc<dyn MemoryProvider>> and call through the trait.

title: subagent session_id propagation
description: Subagents spawn via task tool. If they get session_id=None, their session_search includes the parent's transcript + their own. Audit task spawn path and decide policy: inherit parent (excludes parent's transcript) vs distinct id vs explicit None for fresh subagents. Add test.
close_reason: not-a-bug, invariant pinned with regression test

title: wire MemoryProvider::on_session_end + on_pre_compress hooks
description: PR 157 added the lifecycle hooks but no call site invokes them. Plugin providers that override on_session_end (end-of-session fact extraction) or on_pre_compress (preserve insights through compaction) get no signal. Invoke provider.on_session_end at the same point as spawn_background_review in done.rs, and provider.on_pre_compress in the compression path.

title: add: MEMORY_GUIDANCE and SESSION_SEARCH_GUIDANCE to system prompt
description: Hermes injects tool-gated guidance at session start (system_prompt.py:105-186) telling the model when to persist and when to search past sessions. Dirge has none in prompt.rs. Add equivalents.

title: add: in-session skill creation/patching guidance to system prompt
description: Model only learns about skill create/patch from post-session review. Hermes injects SKILLS_GUIDANCE telling model to save skills after complex success and patch outdated skills mid-task. Add equivalent to prompt.rs:88.

title: background subagent completion: main agent not notified
description: When a background subagent completes, the main agent doesn't see the result until the user prompts again. The completion event should surface into the parent's context as a system reminder OR the parent should poll task_status. Investigate the LifecycleReceiver flow and whether completions inject a follow-up message.

title: subagent output truncation: 'The subagent's output was truncated'
description: Task tool returns 'The subagent's output was truncated' for non-trivial subagent runs. The truncation point is too aggressive — full subagent output should be returned to the parent (or at least configurable). Check the task tool's response assembly + any inline char/line caps.

title: subagent UI: stream output in subagent tab + kill command
description: Subagent chats currently show only '<you> prompt' and '(subagent running…)' — the assistant's streaming tokens and tool calls aren't surfaced in the tab. Users have no way to see what a subagent is doing OR to abort one. Stream the subagent's AgentEvents into its chat slot, and add a /kill <id> (or Ctrl+K on focused tab) to abort.

title: permission: accept-mode prompts for in-cwd writes; same-folder re-prompts
description: Accept mode is supposed to auto-approve work inside the cwd. Users report (a) edit/write on files in cwd still pops the permission dialog, and (b) when 'Allow always' is selected for a folder, subsequent writes to the same folder re-prompt instead of being remembered. Investigate the rule eval + session allowlist persistence.

title: memory tool: add without prompting
description: The memory tool currently prompts for confirmation on add. Should auto-approve memory adds (low-risk, scoped to ~/.dirge/memories), or accept the user's standard/accept/yolo mode without re-prompting on top.

title: spawn_review_runner ignores review_provider config role
description: src/provider/mod.rs:1228 builds the review-runner's stream_fn from self (the main agent's client + model). The Config refactor in 42e778f added ConfigRole::Review and the review_provider key, but spawn_review_runner doesn't consult it — so setting review_provider in config.json silently has no effect on which model runs background review. Fix: when ConfigRole::Review resolves to a different provider than ConfigRole::Default, build_agent should construct a review-specific stream_fn (mirroring the Phase 4 escalation pattern) and stash it on AnyAgent for spawn_review_runner to pick up. When equal, fall back to the current self-built stream_fn (no duplicate client construction). Surfaced during audit of dirge-7ls (cache isolation fix landed correctly, but exposed this independent drift).

title: Phase 4 background_review: fires on EVERY Done event with no rate limiting or cost gating — could cause massive LLM API costs for users on paid plans with frequent session completions
close_reason: Fixed: review now rate-limited to 15-minute intervals via AtomicU64.

title: Phase 8 integration: last_user_prompt tracking misses several input paths — shell bang command path, loop iteration path, plugin followup path, and interjection queue drain path do NOT update last_user_prompt, causing stale prompts in session DB
close_reason: Fixed: last_user_prompt now updated at all 10 spawn_runner call sites: main text submission, shell bang command, worktree merge, loop iteration start, loop iteration continue, plugin followup, both interjection drain paths (Done + Interjected), ContextOverflow respawn, and question response.

title: Phase 6 curator: CuratorState atomic_write_sync may fail if .archive/ parent dir doesn't exist — atomic_write_sync writes to a temp file in the same directory and renames, but doesn't create missing parent dirs
close_reason: Already handled — CuratorState::save() calls create_dir_all(parent) before atomic_write_sync, and archive_skill() calls create_dir_all(archive_dir) before rename. No missing parent directory issue.

title: Phase 4 background_review: review fork shares the same ToolCache as main agent. Review writes to memory/skills can pollute the main agent's tool cache.

Phase 5 session_search: FTS5 query input is not sanitized — user-provided search terms are passed directly to FTS5 MATCH without escaping special FTS5 syntax chars (*, AND, OR, NOT, NEAR, parentheses, quotes)
close_reason: Fixed: added sanitize_fts5_query() function in session_search.rs that wraps queries in double quotes and strips FTS5 special characters (*, ", (, )). 5 new tests verify normal queries pass through, special chars are stripped, quotes are removed, empty-after-clean returns empty, and whitespace is trimmed.

title: Phase 2 memory_store: locking performed INSIDE reload_and_detect_drift + add/replace/remove — but reload opens the file BEFORE acquiring the lock. TOCTOU exists between file existence check and lock acquisition. FileLock uses create_new not flock — two processes could both pass the exists check before either creates the lock file.
close_reason: Already fixed — the lock (acquire_lock) is called before duplicate/budget checks in add(), before substring match in replace(), and before substring match in remove(). Drift detection (reload_and_detect_drift) runs under the lock. No TOCTOU window.

title: find_git_root doesn't canonicalize paths — symlinks in the path chain can cause incorrect root detection
close_reason: Fixed: find_git_root now calls cwd.canonicalize() before walking up, resolving symlinks in the path chain.

title: FileLock uses create_new which leaves stale lock files on crash — no deadlock detection or PID-based staleness check
close_reason: Fixed: FileLock now writes PID into lock file on creation. On contention, is_lock_stale() reads the PID and checks if the process still exists via kill(pid, 0) on Unix. Stale lock files from crashed processes are detected and cleared automatically on first contention check.

title: find_git_root doesn't handle git worktrees (.git as file)
close_reason: Fixed: find_git_root now checks for .git file with gitdir: prefix (worktree marker) in addition to .git directory. is_git_root_marker() helper handles both cases.

title: run_print max_turns wired to agent_loop LoopConfig
plugin hook contract tests (currently zero)
agent_loop integration tests (zero outside h7_smoke)
App-level mouse selection working through modal UI
description: Implement char-granular drag-to-select with auto-copy. Must work through alerts, dialogs, pickers, permission prompts. Renderer scaffolding (selection_active/start/end, buffer_pos_at, selected_text, copy_to_clipboard) already exists from previous incarnation; this wires events, adds ratatui REVERSED highlighting, and adds a cross-cutting selection::handle() helper consumed by every user_rx.recv() site so modal loops can't block it.

title: UI: subagent overview in left panel
description:
The left panel area (between col 0 and the chat content_indent) is mostly empty space today, used only for the bottom-row avatar (5 chars wide). Reclaim it as a real-time subagent overview.

Content per subagent:
- short task id
- status (Running / Completed / Failed)
- truncated prompt
- elapsed time

Source: BackgroundStore::list() + subagent_chat_map (Phase E). The UI loop pushes a fresh PanelData::SubagentList on each lifecycle event; render_viewport paints it in the gutter.

Requires PanelData / PanelMode extension: today PanelData carries todos + modified files for the RIGHT panel. Either extend with a Left field or add a separate LeftPanelData + render path. Coordinate with the existing avatar — should sit ABOVE the avatar, leaving the bottom 3 rows for it.

title: UI: subagent multi-chat-window (Ctrl-N/P, /tasks picker) — port from maki
description:
Each subagent task gets its own chat window; navigate via Ctrl-N (next) / Ctrl-P (previous) and /tasks slash command opens a picker. Maki: maki-ui/src/app/mod.rs:317-322 (open_tasks), :341-352 (Ctrl-N/P), components/keybindings.rs:135-136 (NEXT_CHAT/PREV_CHAT), components/command.rs:22-23 (/tasks).

Bigger refactor: dirge's renderer holds ONE buffer. Need to model Vec<Chat> with active_chat index, swap renderer buffer on switch. Conflict: dirge's Ctrl-X currently drops queued interjections — would need a different binding for next-task, or rebind interjection-drop. Coordinate with user before starting.
notes:
## Design (post-scope-decision: user picked Heavier refactor)

Five phases, each independently committable so we can ship partial
progress if needed.

### Phase A: Multi-buffer in Renderer (~200-300 lines)

Per-chat state extracted into a `ChatBuffer` struct:
- buffer: Vec<LineEntry>
- partial: CompactString + partial_color
- scroll_offset, lines, col
- selection_active, selection_start, selection_end

Global state stays on Renderer:
- input_rows, monochrome
- panel_mode, panel_data
- avatar_state, avatar_tick

Renderer gains:
- chats: Vec<ChatBuffer>
- active_chat: usize
- add_chat(name) -> ChatId
- switch_chat(id)
- chat_names()

All existing public methods (write_line, write, replace_from,
render_viewport, scroll_*, selection_*) route to chats[active_chat].

Backward compat: Renderer::new() creates one default chat (active=0).
Single-chat usage = existing behavior.

### Phase B: Keybinds + /tasks (~80 lines)

- Ctrl-N: next chat
- Ctrl-P: prev chat
- Ctrl-X: open /tasks picker (rebind interjection-drop to Alt+X
  per ov2 plan)
- `/tasks` slash command: same picker

Picker shows chat names; selection switches active.

### Phase C: Per-chat UI state (~150 lines)

ui/mod.rs has 10+ state variables that are currently per-session:
- response_buf, response_start_line
- reasoning_buf, reasoning_start_line
- last_tool_name, last_tool_call_id
- tool_chamber_open, agent_line_started
- was_reasoning, tool_calls_buf

Move to a `ChatUiState` struct, one per chat. The UI loop reads
state from `chat_states[active_chat]` on each event.

### Phase D: task tool refactor (~200 lines)

Currently `task` tool calls `model.btw_query(prompt)` — one-shot,
no tools. Refactor to:
- Spawn a sub-runner using same provider but limited tool set
  (read-only? or same as parent? — needs decision)
- Subagent emits AgentEvents to its own mpsc channel
- task tool returns the chat_id; UI routes events from the channel
  to chats[chat_id]

### Phase E: Event router (~80 lines)

UI loop selects across multiple agent_rx channels (one per active
subagent). Each event lands in chat_states[event.chat_id] and
renders via chats[event.chat_id].

## Open question for Phase D

Should subagent inherit parent's tool set, or be restricted to
read-only? Maki gives subagents full tools by default. Dirge's
permission system already gates per-tool, so safety isn't broken
either way. Inheriting is simpler.

title: CLI: --output-format stream-json headless mode (port from maki)
description:
dirge has --print boolean but no output format selector. Port from maki:
- maki/src/main.rs:32-58 (Cli with --print + --output-format)
- maki/src/print.rs:44-49 (OutputFormat enum: Text | Json | StreamJson)
- maki/src/print.rs:51-110 (PrintResult / InitEvent / AssistantEvent / UserEvent structs — Claude-Code-compatible JSON schema)
- maki/src/print.rs:126-388 (headless run loop with NDJSON event serialization at lines 280, 285, 304, 325, 334)

Adapt: dirge's run_print already exists at src/provider.rs:572. Extend it with format dispatch. For stream-json: serde-serialize each AgentEvent (or a JSON-shaped envelope) and println! one object per line.

title: Perm review F3: space-star pattern optional-arg semantics
description:
LOW-polish gap found in opencode-vs-dirge review. Opencode's wildcard matcher (util/wildcard.ts:13-15) rewrites trailing ' *' as '( .*)?' — making the trailing args optional. So 'ls *' matches BOTH 'ls' and 'ls -la'. Dirge's pattern.rs glob_to_regex requires the args (' *' becomes ' .*' which needs at least the space).

Concrete UX friction: a user accepts 'ls *' from a session allowlist after the agent runs 'ls -la', then the agent runs bare 'ls' — re-prompted because the saved pattern doesn't match. Port the optional-suffix rewrite to src/permission/pattern.rs's glob_to_regex.

title: B3-9: edit tool fuzzy-match cascade
description: edit.rs:155-160 returns 'old_text not found' on whitespace/indent/CRLF drift. LLMs frequently hit this. opencode edit.ts:222-432 has simple → lineTrimmed → whitespace-normalized → indentation-flexible → levenshtein. pi edit-diff.ts:91-132 has fuzzyFindText. Port the cascade.

title: B3-10: LSP pull-diagnostic fallback for lazy servers
description: lsp/client.rs:261-289 wait_for_push is push-only. clojure-lsp/jdtls/clangd may not push on demand. 10s timeout = 'clean' diagnostic block reported when errors exist. opencode lsp/client.ts:540-582 races push-wait against requestDocumentDiagnostics. Add pull fallback.

title: B3-8: soft-wrap + mouse selection display-width awareness
description: renderer.rs:1457-1496 wrap_input measures chars().count() instead of UnicodeWidthChar. Cursor mis-lands on CJK/emoji wrapped lines. Mouse selection columns map 1:1 char-to-display rather than width-aware. Pi interactive-mode.ts uses string-width per cell.

title: B3-7: Python find_callees captures method calls
description: semantic/adapters/python.rs:280 only matches (call function:(identifier)); misses obj.method(). Go/Java/C++ all capture selector_expression equivalent. Python users get hollow callee lists.

title: B3-5: doom-loop + allowlist reset on /cd
description: permission/checker.rs:568-571 only updates cwd. recent_calls and session_allowlist survive across /cd — 'cd *' allowlist follows user to new project. Clear both on set_working_dir.

title: B3-6: bash background & in fallback splitter + AST recurse
description: bash.rs:401-473 fallback splitter (no semantic-bash feature) doesn't split on bare &. Also semantic-bash should recurse so background commands get checked individually.

title: B3-4: /loop max-iterations default cap
description: ui/slash.rs:778 passes None for max_iterations; LoopState::should_stop returns false forever. Runaway API spend until user notices. Default cap 20; accept '/loop --max N <prompt>'.

title: B3-3: provider env-var fallbacks beyond GLM/ZHIPU
description: provider.rs:210-219 only chains ZHIPU. Add ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN as fallback for Anthropic, GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY for Gemini. Pi handles both.

title: B3-2: HTTP 500 retry + robust status patterns
description: recovery.rs:261-269 only retries 502/503/504. Add 500 + any 5xx. Patterns require literal ' NNN ' spaces; accept 'status: NNN', 'status=NNN', 'NNN ' too. opencode retries all status >= 500.

title: B3-1: memory tool atomic writes
description: extras/memory.rs:118 uses std::fs::write (truncate-in-place). Switch to crate::fs_atomic::atomic_write to match write.rs/edit.rs/apply_patch.rs pattern. Crash mid-write currently leaves truncated .md.

title: Batch2-3: session save lockfile to avoid two-instance data loss
description: session/storage.rs:55-74 uses atomic-rename per save but no advisory lock or version check. Two dirge instances on the same session id: last write wins, the loser's in-memory state silently overwritten. Add per-session-file fs2/fd-lock advisory lock OR version-stamp + reload-conflict warning. opencode uses lockfile; pi serializes through a process-local session manager.

title: Batch2-2: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md ancestor walk depth cap
description: context/mod.rs:90-103 walks parent chain to /, reading both AGENTS.md AND CLAUDE.md at every level. Deep project under /Users/foo/work/x/y/z/... = 6-10 stat+open calls per startup plus unintended files under /Users/yogthos / /Users. opencode caps at git root + /Users/yogthos. Cap walk at: (a) git root if found, (b) max 8 levels otherwise. README claim 'ancestors + global fallback' preserved.

title: Batch2-1: pre-emptive compaction guard before user prompt dispatch
description: Auto-compact only fires on AgentEvent::ContextOverflow (ui/mod.rs:2543-2545 in Done arm). A new user prompt is sent against a near-full window → request fires → ContextOverflow → reactive compact + respawn. Costs an extra round-trip + provider error every slow recovery. opencode/pi compact BEFORE dispatch when needs_compaction() returns true. Add pre-flight check on user-prompt submit.

title: H-R1: try_lock at loop-top PM acquisitions to avoid UI freeze during plugin tools
description: ui/mod.rs event-loop top does std::sync::Mutex::lock() multiple times per iteration (list_shortcuts, drain_notifications, drain_entries, drain_tree_ops). During a plugin tool execution inside spawn_blocking holding the same mutex, these acquisitions block the runtime worker thread — UI freezes. Switch all four to try_lock; on contention, skip the refresh this iteration. drain_* semantics tolerate the one-tick delay; list_shortcuts gets refreshed on the next idle tick after the tool returns.
