title: H3: expose prepareArguments on harness/register-tool
description:
LoopTool::prepare_arguments default no-op; JanetLoopTool doesn't override. Plugin authors wanting to normalize args before schema validation (pi's prepareEditArguments is the canonical example) have no surface.

Pi: prepareArguments?: (args: unknown) => Static<TParams> on ToolDefinition (types.ts:443); pi forwards through the wrapper.

Fix: optional prepare-arguments field on harness/register-tool (Janet fn name). Host calls it before parsing args into the loop's typed shape. Mutate result back into Value and feed to handler.

title: H4: dedup plugin-tool names + emit diagnostic on shortcut/renderer collisions
description:
harness/register-tool appends to harness-tools-list unconditionally. Two plugins (or one plugin reload pattern) registering the same name produce two entries; both are wrapped as JanetLoopTool and the agent loop has two same-name tools with undefined dispatch order.

Pi: extension.tools is Map<name, RegisteredTool> (loader.ts:219) — second set replaces first. Across extensions runner.ts:378 uses first-extension-wins.

Fix: dedup in list_plugin_tools (last-load-wins per name, matching the Map semantics) with tracing::warn on duplicate. Same for list_shortcuts; pi emits a diagnostic per duplicate (runner.ts:451). list_message_renderers already first-match-wins via .find().

title: H5: surface plugin shortcut handler errors instead of swallowing
description:
UI shortcut dispatch goes through invoke_command which catches Janet errors to Ok(None). UI only displays on Ok(Some(msg)). A handler raising an exception is indistinguishable from one returning nil — no chat notification, no tracing::warn, plugin authors get zero feedback.

Pi parallel: Promise.resolve(...).catch(err => this.showError(...)) (interactive-mode.ts:1666).

Fix: use the same DIRGE_HOOK_ERR catch wrapper that dispatch() uses (mod.rs:1956) — tracing::warn + harness/push-hook-err notification. Either inline in invoke_command (with backward-compat), or add a new invoke_command_traced variant.

title: 9b: align harness/register-command + harness/register-provider to ExtensionApi
description: The existing harness/register-command and harness/register-provider were added ad-hoc. Refactor them to route through ExtensionApi (added in 9a) so all register-* APIs share one shape. Keep backwards compatibility for any in-tree plugins by leaving the old call sites as thin wrappers. Acceptance: provider/command registration goes through ExtensionApi; no behavior change for users.
acceptance_criteria: Provider + command registration both route through ExtensionApi. Existing tests still pass. No new Janet API breakage.
notes: On closer review, the wire-format difference between register-command (name|handler), register-provider (name|type|base|env), and register-tool (tab-escape) is cosmetic. Existing parsers are stable, no user surfaces are affected, and the Rust-side return types are already shaped per their use site. Aligning them would be churn for marginal gain. Deferring in favor of 9c (registerShortcut) which delivers new capability.

title: 9a: ExtensionApi surface + harness/register-tool
description: Build foundation + first feature together. Add an ExtensionApi struct in src/plugin/extension.rs that exposes register_tool/register_command/register_provider/register_hook in a uniform shape. Wire it into PluginManager. Add harness/register-tool helper in Janet that lets plugins register a LoopTool whose execute() callback runs a named Janet function. The plugin-tool list must be discoverable by build_loop_tools() so the agent loop picks them up alongside built-ins. Acceptance: a Janet plugin can declare a tool with name+description+parameters+handler, and the LLM can call it. Tool parameters use JSON Schema (matching pi's TypeBox shape semantically).
acceptance_criteria: Janet plugin can call (harness/register-tool ...) with name, description, parameters, handler-fn. Tool appears in build_loop_tools(). Test invokes the registered tool via run_agent_loop and checks the Janet handler ran with correct args.

title: Phase 9 epic: pi-style extension API for plugins
description: Refactor dirge's plugin architecture to mirror pi's extension API. Goal: a unified ExtensionApi surface (in Rust + Janet harness) that lets plugins register tools, commands, providers, shortcuts, and message renderers using one consistent shape. Current state: dirge has harness/register-command, harness/register-provider, harness/register-hook (string-based slot-setters). Missing: registerTool (biggest gap), registerShortcut, registerMessageRenderer. Sub-phases tracked separately.

title: H10/H17/M7b/M13 followup — reviewer flagged incomplete
description: Reviewer caught 4 partial/missing fixes after R-batch: H10 needed agent interject too; H17 needed AgentEvent::ContextOverflow + auto-respawn; M7b grep had no per-line cap; M13 still .write() on the outer RwLock.
close_reason: Addressed in this commit. H10 also fires interject; H17 emits AgentEvent::ContextOverflow → UI auto-compacts + respawns; grep adds 4 KiB per-line cap with UTF-8-safe truncation marker; SymbolIndex now uses Mutex<FileCache> so all 5 semantic tools hold .read() on the outer RwLock.

title: Plugin hooks have no timeout; can hang every tool
description: plugin/hook.rs:101 mgr.dispatch_tool_hook runs synchronously under a Mutex with no time bound. A plugin that loops or makes a blocking net call hangs every subsequent tool. Wrap in tokio::time::timeout(5s).

title: (H12 followup) apply_patch should also pin to canonical path
description: read/edit/write now use check_perm_path_resolve. apply_patch has per-op iteration with multiple check_perm_path calls; refactor to use the resolve variant for each op's file I/O.
close_reason: Closed by C1 fix in commit c70b757 — apply_patch now routes every PatchOp through check_perm_path_resolve and uses the resolved path for the apply_* calls. Verified with the new test in src/agent/tools/apply_patch.rs.

title: No auto-continue after auto-compaction
description: ui/mod.rs:2043+ auto-compact runs after is_running=false but doesn't re-submit the user's last prompt or continue the in-flight stream. Also ContextLength errors in runner just emit and break, no in-flight compact-and-retry.
close_reason: Superseded by followup dirge-fqo — needs proper compact-and-resume runner plumbing, deferred to dedicated round

title: ACP build_agent passes None for bg_store
description: extras/acp/mod.rs:163-181 — background tool degrades silently under ACP. Provide a real BackgroundStore (with no UI sink is fine).

title: Skill discovery: outer monorepo skills override inner
description: skill.rs:24-97 — find_project_ancestor_dirs walks cwd→parents (inner first, outer last). map.insert at line 69 is last-write-wins so outer wins, opposite of 'more specific wins'. Reverse the iteration.

title: MCP servers never reconnect after initial connect
description: extras/mcp/mod.rs:17 connect_all once. If transport dies mid-session, cached peer returns errors with no recovery. Add a reconnect-on-error path.

title: TOCTOU symlink swap between permission check and file open
description: checker.rs:476 resolve_absolute canonicalizes following symlinks. read.rs:215+227 re-opens raw path; OS dereferences symlink AGAIN at open time. If swapped between, the file actually read differs from the authorized one. Need to use the canonicalized path from check_perm_path for the open.

title: Yolo mode silently bypasses explicit deny rules
description: checker.rs:162 — SecurityMode::Yolo returns Allowed BEFORE rule lookup. A user who configured deny rules for rm -rf etc. has them silently ignored under Yolo. Surface a one-time warning at session start when Yolo + non-empty deny rules.

title: external_directory rules ignored in Standard/Restrictive modes
description: permission/checker.rs:278-296 — match_ext_dir invoked only in SecurityMode::Accept. Standard + Restrictive never consult ext_dir_rules so a config like external_directory={'/external/safe/**'='allow'} does nothing in Standard.

title: No cascading reject when one pending tool is denied
description: ask.rs + ui/mod.rs — denying one tool only sends to its single oneshot. Other queued AskRequests pop fresh alerts. Add Deny-all-pending option or auto-deny remaining when user picks Deny.

title: edit tool ambiguous-match error blob unbounded
description: agent/tools/edit.rs:186-213 pushes one line per match into error message. A pattern matching 50k lines produces a 50k-line error blob fed back to LLM, blowing context. Cap at first 20 + '...and N more matches'.

title: Zombie process trees on Ctrl+C abort (bash tool)
description: agent/tools/bash.rs sets kill_on_drop(true) which SIGKILLs the immediate bash child only, not its descendants. On task abort, grandchildren survive. timeout path correctly killpg's -pid. Drop guard should also killpg the whole group.

title: Tool outputs without per-tool caps overflow LLM context
description: agent/runner.rs collects ToolResultContent::Text with no global cap. Self-capped tools: bash (256 KiB), read (per-line), websearch, background notify. Uncapped: find_files, grep already capped MAX but emit total list; list_dir not capped; MCP tool outputs; apply_patch results. Add a final post-tool-call cap (e.g. 100 KiB) so any tool's runaway output can't blow context.

title: Compression summarizer has zero retry
description: provider.rs run_summarizer single stream_chat.multi_turn(1); first Err returns Compression failed. A transient 503/rate-limit permanently fails /compress instead of retrying.

title: No HTML response detection from proxies/gateways
description: recovery.rs classify_error doesn't recognize Cloudflare/nginx 502/503 HTML pages or captive-portal interception. Falls through to ErrorKind::Other, no retry. Detect <html / DOCTYPE / 'Bad Gateway' / 'Service Unavailable' and reclassify as Network.

title: run_print one-shot mode has zero retry
description: agent/runner.rs run_print builds stream once, on first Err prints and breaks. Non-interactive mode arguably needs retries MORE than interactive. Wrap in same RecoveryPolicy + should_retry loop spawn_agent uses.

title: Missing Retry-After HTTP-date parsing
description: recovery.rs retry_after_from_error_msg supports seconds/ms/JSON forms but not RFC 7231 HTTP-date (Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT). Falls back to exponential backoff when provider/proxy emits an explicit date.

title: Only 4 context-length error patterns in classify_error
description: agent/recovery.rs:209-215 matches only 4 substrings (context_length_exceeded, maximum context length, reduce the length of the messages, request too large). Misses Anthropic 'prompt is too long', OpenAI o-series 'token limit', Gemini, GLM, DeepSeek variants. Add the missing variants from opencode's pattern list.

title: Background subagent tasks not cancelled on session switch
description: task.rs spawns via tokio::spawn with no JoinHandle tracked; /clone, /fork, session swaps leave tasks running, consuming API budget until 10-min timeout. Process exit IS handled by runtime drop. Need per-session task registry + cancel on session lifecycle events.

title: Deny path leaves orphan chamber rows
description: On Deny last_tool_name=None but the tool's ToolResult (with denial error) still goes through render_tool_output, writing chamber body + bottom for a chamber whose top no longer exists.

title: @-picker doesn't trigger after multibyte char
description: input.rs:923 uses bytes[cursor-1] which is a UTF-8 continuation byte after é, etc. Picker silently fails to open.
close_reason: False positive on review. Current byte check correctly implements 'open picker iff @ follows space or buffer start' — multibyte prior char produces continuation byte ≠ space, so the picker stays closed which is the intended mid-word behavior. Added regression tests to lock in.

title: Denied trailer prints unsanitized tool/input
description: mod.rs:2692 — same ANSI-injection class as ALERT, post-deny.

title: chamber_row uses chars().count() instead of display width
description: Tool output with CJK/emoji misaligns right border. chamber_row_centered already uses UnicodeWidthStr::width.

title: Terminal escape sequences leak to shell on quit
description: On exit, dirge prints raw responses (OSC 11, DSR 63;1R, primary DA ?64;...) to the shell. Suggests a terminal query was sent during init but its response wasn't consumed before leaving raw mode.

title: MCP panel shows (none) on startup
description: Right-hand info panel shows MCP servers as (none) when the app starts, only populates after first key press.

title: Permission alert chamber overlaps previous chamber
description: When the permission prompt renders, it draws on top of the just-written tool chamber instead of below it.

title: Input soft-wrap overflows when content_width is capped
description: On wide terminals (>120 cols), bottom_indent is non-zero but wrap_width is computed as cols-3 instead of cols-3-bottom_indent. Resulting input text overflows the centered content band and the terminal hard-wraps unpredictably, looking like 'wrap is broken'.

title: P4d: harness/set-label, harness/fork, harness/navigate-tree, etc.
description: Plugin-level access to the session tree: bookmark labels (harness/set-label), programmatic branching (harness/fork, harness/new-session, harness/switch-session, harness/navigate-tree). Mirrors pi's ctx.fork / ctx.newSession / ctx.navigateTree.

title: P4c: /tree, /fork, /clone slash commands + UI
description: Interactive picker for /tree navigation. /fork [entry-id|HEAD] branches off (restores prompt into editor). /clone [entry-id] duplicates the path. ASCII tree renderer; label badges in chat view.

title: P4b: switch session storage to node-based (parent links)
description: Replace Session::messages: Vec<SessionMessage> with a node-based SessionTree { entries: HashMap<id, entry>, leaf_id, root_id, parents }. convert_history walks the parent chain from leaf_id. Update compaction, undo, retry to be branch-aware. Backwards compat: legacy linear sessions auto-convert to a degenerate root→...→leaf chain on load.

title: P4a: per-message timestamps + IDs (data model enrichment)
description: Add timestamp: i64 and id: String fields to SessionMessage. Backwards compat via serde defaults (existing sessions load with default IDs and zero timestamps). Update render_session to interleave messages and extra_entries by timestamp, closing the known P2 limitation. Unlocks P4b's node-based addressing.

title: P4: session tree (fork / clone / tree navigation)
description: Switch Session::messages from Vec<Message> to a node-based SessionTree { entries: HashMap<EntryId, Entry>, leaf_id, root_id, parents }. convert_history walks back from leaf_id. New slash commands: /tree (interactive picker), /fork [entry-id], /clone [entry-id]. New harness APIs: harness/set-label, harness/navigate-tree, harness/fork, harness/new-session, harness/switch-session. Versioned session file format with legacy linear-to-tree auto-convert. UI: ASCII tree renderer + label badges. Largest blast radius of the pi parity work — touches Session, persistence, compaction, undo, retry.
close_reason: split into dirge-45n / dirge-wdc / dirge-3va / dirge-16l

title: P1: plugin-registered custom providers
description: (harness/register-provider name spec) lets plugins add LLM providers at startup. Spec carries base-url, api-key-env, api (e.g. :openai-completions), and an explicit models array. After plugin load, main.rs merges plugin specs into the runtime provider registry (same place cfg.custom_providers feeds in). --list-models and /model see plugin-registered models alongside built-ins. Plugins re-register every startup (matches pi's no-persist behavior).

title: P3: granular streaming events (message_start/update/end + turn_start/end)
description: Wire new plugin hook events from the post-P0 turn loop: on-message-start, on-message-update (batched to ~100ms or N tokens), on-message-end (with replace-message slot), on-turn-start, on-turn-end carrying message + tool-results context. on-message-end can return a replacement Janet table that the host re-serializes and uses as the persisted assistant message.

title: P2: custom message renderers via plugin
description: Plugins can register typed message renderers and append typed entries. New harness APIs: harness/append-entry, harness/register-renderer. Session::messages gains extra_entries: Vec<PluginEntry> with custom_type, data (JSON), display flag. UI render_session walks both regular messages and extra entries in timestamp order, calling registered renderer (returns [color text] pairs) per plugin entry. Persists across session save/load. Fallback renderer for unknown custom_type from a no-longer-installed plugin.

title: P0: runner turn-boundary detection (TurnStart/TurnEnd events)
description: Refactor run_stream in src/agent/runner.rs to detect turn boundaries within rig's multi_turn stream and emit AgentEvent::TurnStart / AgentEvent::TurnEnd between iterations. Preparatory for P3 (granular streaming events) and P4 (session tree branch-aware accounting). One Turn = assistant message + tool calls + tool results before the next LLM call.

title: R2: add top-5 missing plugin tests + FFI edge cases
description: From the plugin coverage audit: worker init-failure path, load_file with missing path, store_response round-trip, on-tool-end fires when inner returned Err, concurrent dispatch_tool_hook serialization. Plus FFI edge cases for read_string_arg (keyword/symbol/buffer), read_string_array_arg (empty + tuple-vs-array), wrap_string (empty / multibyte UTF-8). Depends on R1 so the worker init / dialog code is stable.

title: Phase 3b: Janet worker thread + harness/confirm + harness/select
description: Move JanetClient onto a dedicated OS thread so harness/confirm and harness/select can block synchronously from Janet without deadlocking the current_thread tokio UI. Replaces the unsafe impl Send/Sync on PluginManager with a real worker channel. Adds DialogRequest channel the UI loop drains via tokio::select to render confirms and selects. Was originally part of Phase 3 but the refactor is large enough (~2 days) to warrant its own phase.

title: Phase 4: plugin input transform via on-prompt return
description: on-prompt hook returning a string can now replace (not just prepend) the user prompt. Backwards-compat: only replace when a new harness flag (harness/replace-prompt) is set. TDD: replace-prompt fires verbatim; default behavior preserved.

title: Phase 3: UI primitives from Janet (notify/confirm/select)
description: (harness/notify msg level), (harness/confirm title question), (harness/select title opts). Notify drains into a renderer queue. Confirm/select piggyback the existing AskRequest/QuestionResponse channels. Janet's !Send lock must be released around the oneshot await. TDD: notify queue ordering, confirm/select via mock channel.

title: Phase 1: plugin tool hooks (block / mutate-input / replace-result)
description: Wrap each rig Tool in a HookedTool<T> that calls into PluginManager before/after T::call. New harness APIs: harness/block, harness/mutate-input, harness/replace-result write to PluginManager slots that Rust reads after dispatch. TDD: slot read tests, integration test that block returns ToolError, mutate replaces args via JSON roundtrip, replace-result swaps output. Touches src/plugin/mod.rs and src/agent/builder.rs. Closes gap with pi's tool_call/tool_result mutation extension API.

title: Phase 2: plugin-registered slash commands
description: (harness/register-command "mycmd" "my-handler-fn") records {cmd -> fn} in PluginManager. handle_slash falls through to plugin command dispatch when not a built-in. /help lists registered commands. TDD: registration at load, dispatch via slash, /help inclusion.

title: Phase 2B: true mid-execution interjection (turn-boundary inject)
description: Builds on 2A. Wire interject_rx into runner. Convert run_stream/multi_turn into a manual turn loop so between stream iterations we can drain queue and inject as a user message into history. Touches src/agent/runner.rs:138-225 and the rig multi_turn flow. Depends on dirge-qq2 wait, the 2A issue.

title: Phase 3: right-side info panel (cwd, MCP, LSP, todos, modified files)
description: Carve right ~32 cols (auto-hide when terminal narrower than ~100). Sources: cwd from env, MCP from McpClientManager.handles, LSP via new public accessor on LspManager, todos from TODO_LIST mutex, modified files via new shared Arc<Mutex<IndexSet<PathBuf>>> populated by Write/Edit/ApplyPatch tools. New /panel on|off toggle. Default on when wide enough.

title: Phase 2A: queue user input while agent is running
description: Remove 'agent is busy' guard at src/ui/mod.rs:663 and :720 for plain text. Push to VecDeque<String> interjection_queue. Show queue count + dim preview above input. Esc/Ctrl-X drops most recent. Ctrl-C still aborts. Slash commands stay gated to current allow-list. On AgentEvent::Done, drain queue and run as next turn.

title: Phase 1: soft-wrap input box instead of horizontal scroll
description: Replace horizontal scroll logic in src/ui/renderer.rs::draw_bottom (lines ~500-660) with display-column wrap. Drop input_scroll_offset; compute visual rows from logical lines wrapped to visible_width; keep MAX_INPUT_VISIBLE_LINES cap with vertical scroll keeping cursor visible. Move or guard the token counter so it doesn't collide with wrapped text. Add a unit test for cursor (logical -> visual) mapping.

title: A tool's model-facing description and its validator can state different rules
description:
When a tool's model-facing description states a rule and the tool's validator enforces it, the two are written in different places and nothing ties them together. They drift: the prompt can promise what the validator forbids, or describe a restriction the validator does not apply.

This is the same family as the divergences already on record in this codebase — a guard added to one of two parallel implementations, a prompt section shipped to one of two compaction builders. The failure mode is quiet: the model follows the description, the validator rejects the call, and the model has no way to tell a real error from a stale instruction.
design:
Where a tool has a configurable rule that is BOTH described to the model and enforced in code, derive both from the same value, so the description cannot say one thing while the check does another.

Scope this by finding the real instances first — this is a discipline, and filing it as a sweep would be worse than not filing it. Start by grepping tool descriptions for rules stated as absolutes ('only one', 'must not', 'at most') and check each against its validator. Fix the ones that have drifted; couple the ones that are configurable.

The cheap general guard, if the instances turn out to be a family: a source-scan test in the shape already used for reply_rx.await marking and modal control-chord handling, so a new site cannot be added uncoupled.

title: A goal has no way to report that it is blocked, only met or out of re-entries
description:
A goal in dirge is run-local. goal.rs re-enters the model with the objective, an independent judge checks the stop condition each round, and MAX_GOAL_REACT bounds the re-entry. There is no vocabulary for a goal that is legitimately stuck: the only outcomes are met, or the backstop runs out.

A model that cannot proceed because it needs a credential, a decision, or an answer therefore has no way to say so as a STATE. It either keeps burning re-entries against a wall until the bound is hit, or it declares completion it has not reached — and the judge is the only thing standing between those two, on a question the judge cannot answer because the blocker is outside the diff.
design:
Explicit goal verbs — pause, resume, block with a reason code and an explanation, complete, clear — with block as a durable state that ends the round loop cleanly and surfaces the reason, rather than a bound being exhausted.

LOW PRIORITY, and honest about why: the independent judge already covers 'did it actually do the work', which is the harder and more valuable half, and the re-entry bound already covers runaway. This buys the distinction between 'gave up' and 'ran out', which matters mostly for unattended runs and for resumable goals — neither of which is a current use case. Worth filing so the gap is on record; not worth building ahead of the P1s.

If it is built: the reason code must be a closed set the harness owns, not free text from the model, or it becomes another thing nobody can count. Revision fencing (a mutation carries the revision it was based on and a stale one is rejected) is the right shape if goals ever become concurrently mutable, and unnecessary until then.

title: Verify an empty completion with finish_reason=stop is retried
description: One-shot summarize bails on an empty response, history conversion drops empty assistant turns, and stream retry covers mid-stream aborts — but nothing confirms end to end that a chat-completions provider answering with an empty completion and a clean stop reason gets retried rather than surfacing as a finished, empty turn. Believed covered; unproven.
design: A wire-level test through the mock provider: return one empty completion with finish_reason=stop, then a real one, and assert the run produces the real answer and records a retry. If it is already covered the test costs nothing and pins it; if it is not, the test is the bug report.

title: Stale tool results ride in history until a full compaction
description: llmtrim has a whole stage pipeline for INCOMING tool results, but a large result already in history stays at full size until compaction folds the whole conversation. Compaction is expensive (an LLM call) and destructive (the turns are replaced by a summary), so the only tool for a 200KB grep output from twenty turns ago is the heaviest one available.
design: A deterministic pre-compaction stage that prunes stale tool results in place — keep the head and tail of each, replace the middle with an explicit marker, above a char threshold and below the compaction threshold. Deterministic and model-free is the whole point: the same history must serialize to the same bytes on every request or it moves the cached prefix, which costs more than the pruning saves. Prune oldest-first so the recent results a model is actually reasoning about stay whole.

title: Loopback-server tests raced the process-global rate-limit gate
description: reqwest_streaming_keeps_headers_on_429 failed once in a full parallel run with 'the response headers must have latched the gate', passing in isolation on both the pre-change and post-change tree. rate_limit_gate is a process-global keyed by host:port; serve_once binds whatever ephemeral port the OS hands out, and the send path clears an endpoint's entry on ANY successful response. Two concurrent serve_once tests where the second is handed the port the first just released means its 200 clears the first's latch between the request and the assertion. Pre-existing and rare — it needs exact port reuse inside a narrow window.
design: A tokio::sync::Mutex serializing the tests that stand up a loopback server. Sequential runs cannot collide because each assertion completes before the next test starts; only concurrency opens the window.
close_reason: Loopback-server tests serialized behind a mutex. The rate-limit gate is a process-global keyed by host:port and cleared by any 2xx, so two concurrent serve_once tests could collide on a reused ephemeral port.

title: Two leftovers from the token-budget review: a second estimator and a dead const
description:
Split out of dirge-e31n.7 after the premise check. Most of F9 was already built
and better (single estimator, five-tier ladder in context_manager.rs, and the
"throw when the floor cannot be met" was considered and deliberately rejected).
Its telemetry half turned into dirge-5zca, which is fixed.

TWO RESIDUALS, both small and both real:

1. Session::estimate_tokens (src/session/mod.rs:371) is a SECOND token
   estimator: (text.len() / 4).max(1), per-message FLOOR division, against
   compression::estimate_messages_tokens's sum-then-div_ceil. compression.rs:184
   documents itself as "the project's single token estimator", which is not
   true. The two measure different collections (SessionMessage vs Value) so they
   do not contradict each other directly, but the session one drives the UI
   context meter, the /compact threshold (ui/slash/mod.rs:328) and session fold
   accounting, so a user reading the meter and the loop deciding to fold are
   working off different arithmetic. Establish whether the divergence has an
   observable consequence BEFORE unifying — if it does not, fix the comment
   instead of the code.

2. compression::MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH (compression.rs:192) is
   #[allow(dead_code)] — written, never wired to anything. Either wire it or
   delete it.
close_reason: Both leftovers done, and the review found a bigger one. estimate_messages_tokens ignored tool-call ARGUMENTS entirely (a 40 KB write argument measured 4 tokens) — fixed at 7aad6662 via block_chars, mutation suite 3/3. MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH deleted. The Session::estimate_tokens divergence is rounding-only with no observable consequence, so the false 'single estimator' comment was corrected and a test pins that the two keep agreeing on method. Filed dirge-czg9 for the sibling divergence found on the way.

title: Record which prompt revision produced a session
description:
Split out of dirge-e31n.7 after the premise check. F8 as written proposed
segment markers, a POLICY_VERSION constant, shadow/rollback gating, and an
assembly assertion that all required segments are present.

THE ASSEMBLY ASSERTION HAS NOTHING TO GUARD. assemble_base_preamble
(src/agent/builder/preamble.rs:55) concatenates compile-time consts
unconditionally; build_agent_inner layers AGENTS.md / prompts / skills / memory
on top. No path truncates the preamble, so "silently shipping a truncated
policy" is not a reachable state. No observed failure motivates the rest.

WHAT IS REAL, and it is much smaller: nothing in a session records which prompt
produced it. A session stores source, model, title, started_at. If a user
reports that behaviour changed between two builds, there is no way to bisect
that to a prompt revision — and this epic changed the system prompt repeatedly
(capability projection shipped WORSE first, turns 4.0 -> 8.5, and only an A/B
found it).

Cheapest useful version: hash the assembled preamble and record the hash in
session metadata. Diagnostic value only — it does not change behaviour, so
there is nothing to A/B. Judge it on whether a real diagnosis would have used
it, not on a measurement.

DO NOT build the shadow/rollback machinery without evidence. See
[[steering-premises-die-on-measurement]].
close_reason: session.preamble_digest at 5cf2b2f5 — 12 hex chars of SHA-256 over the assembled preamble, stamped and logged at agent build, serde-defaulted for old files. SHA-256 not DefaultHasher because the value crosses builds and machines. Shadow/rollback machinery deliberately not built: no observed failure behind it. Mutation 3/3.

title: A model-supplied bash timeout silently overrides timeouts.bash_secs without bound
description:
src/agent/tools/bash/mod.rs resolves the command deadline as args.timeout.unwrap_or(Timeouts::get().bash), so a model asking for timeout=600 gets 600 however low the user set timeouts.bash_secs. Found while building the dirge-e31n.5 handoff scenario: with bash_secs pinned to 5 the model passed timeout=60 and the command ran to completion, so the scenario measured nothing.

This is NOT obviously a bug — the field is documented as a default 'when the call omits one' (timeout.rs:110, docs/config.md:912), and that is what it does. The question is whether a user lowering it wants a DEFAULT or a CEILING. A user who sets 30 to keep runs snappy currently gets whatever the model asks for.

Needs a decision, not a unilateral change: making it a cap changes behaviour for anyone relying on long model-chosen timeouts.
design: Options: (a) leave as-is, document more loudly that it is a floor-less default; (b) clamp to min(args.timeout, configured) and rename the doc to 'maximum'; (c) add a separate timeouts.bash_max_secs so default and ceiling are distinct knobs. (c) is the only one that does not change existing behaviour for someone.
notes: RELATED FIX ALREADY LANDED: the bash tool's schema description for the timeout parameter was wrong twice and is now rendered from the resolved config. It said 'default 120, or 600 when background' — the 120 ignored timeouts.bash_secs entirely, and the 600 background default has never existed (an omitted background timeout runs unbounded, which the adjacent 'background' description states correctly). Same schema, two accounts. Test: agent::tools::bash::tests::timeout_description_reports_the_resolved_default_not_a_literal.
close_reason: Implemented as a separate bash_max_secs ceiling (option c), default 3600, per user authorization to change behaviour

title: R7: tool-name alias table for commonly-guessed names
description:
F10 (Low). dirge exposes ~35 tools flat. One approach collapses ~40 browser tools behind one browser_use tool with an action parameter, a help action, category grouping, and an alias table mapping the names models actually guess (evaluate / execute_script / exec / js -> inject_script; open / open_tab / new_tab -> navigate with newTab: true).

dirge's capability estimator weights hallucinated_tool_names at 2x, which is the same signal from the other end: a near-miss name is currently scored as the model being out of its depth when it is really the harness refusing a synonym.

Cheapest useful slice: an alias table consulted at dispatch before a name is rejected. Count an alias hit as a repair, not a hallucination, so the capability tier stops being poisoned by near-misses.

Full unification behind action-dispatch tools is a much larger change and is NOT proposed here - tool_search already addresses surface breadth from a different angle.
acceptance_criteria:
- known alias dispatches to the real tool
- alias hit counted as repair_successful, not hallucinated_tool_names
- unknown name still rejected exactly as today
- alias table covers at least the observed near-misses from benchmark runs
notes:
PREMISE CHECK (before building):

The bead's framing -- "collapse the tool surface, alias the names models guess"
-- was checked against measurement first. Two of its three claims did not hold,
and the one that did pointed somewhere else.

DEAD: "models guess tool names at dispatch". With a tools array in the request,
90 native calls across 4 models (3 hosted + the qwen3.6-27b floor) produced 0
off-registry names. The providers constrain the name to the advertised set. 60
tasks, deliberately worded to tempt synonyms.

DEAD: "the capability tier is poisoned by near-misses". It cannot be, because
the counter that feeds it reads 0 -- for the same reason.

ALIVE, and not where the bead pointed: the name is only in play when the model
writes the call as TEXT, from memory rather than from the schema. Asked with NO
tools array, 111 of 175 names models produced (63%) were not dirge tools --
shell/execute_command/terminal for bash, ask_user for question, read_file for
read. Those calls were silently DROPPED by the scavenger's allowed-name gate:
no result, no error, no counter, and the turn then ended with no tool call at
all, so the raw call syntax became the final answer. Confirmed end to end
against the real binary with a mock provider.

BUG FOUND BY THE PREMISE CHECK (P1-ish, not in the plan): suggest::closest
allowed len/2 edits capped at 3, and of eleven plausible guesses it resolved,
SIX pointed at an unrelated tool -- exec->spec, shell->skill, open->spec,
ls->lsp, ask->task, search->websearch -- with no hedge in the message. The
harness was steering models wrong and then scoring the result as the model
being out of its depth, which is the exact shape capability_cards.rs documents.

SHIPPED:
- tool_aliases.rs: exact, normalized, evidence-counted table; case/separator
  variants resolve against the real registry with no entry. Ambiguous names
  (search/find/open/plan) deliberately excluded.
- one resolution site in run.rs over the final call list, so native and
  scavenged calls are handled identically and before storm dedup.
- scavenger gate widened to aliasable names (was the silent-drop path).
- closest: transposition = 1 edit, budget = 25% of the longer name. 8 wrong
  suggestions -> 1 on the measured sample, keeping every real typo.
- three counters on dirge::gates (hallucinated / dropped_unknown / aliased),
  all three scraped by loop-ab.sh as mechanism rows -- hallucinated_tool_names
  was emitted but never scraped, so every A/B on it read nothing in both arms.
- dirge::tool_miss logs the guessed name and its nearest real one on both
  paths, so the table's next entry is an observation, not a guess.

DEVIATION FROM ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: "counted as repair_successful" -- an alias
hit gets its own counter (aliased_tool_names) rather than a RepairKind variant.
RepairKind is the ARGUMENT-repair pipeline; a name is a different axis, and the
three name outcomes only read as one story when they sit together.

FILED, NOT FIXED HERE: dirge-n00z -- raw call syntax is streamed to the user as
prose whenever a model emits a call in text. The text is streamed before the
scavenger runs, so it cannot be fixed at this layer.

Evidence: docs/tool-name-misses.md.

title: Direct Gemini gets no prompt caching (only the OpenRouter google/gemini-* route is marked)
description:
Only the Anthropic and AnthropicOauth arms call automatic_caching! in stream_dispatch.rs, so every other provider relies on llmtrim's CacheStage.

llmtrim's set_router_cache_breakpoint (src/llmtrim/stages/cache.rs:110) classifies by ROUTER model id — it needs a vendor/model shape and returns early when router_model() is None. So openrouter google/gemini-* correctly gets a SystemBlock breakpoint, but a directly-addressed Gemini model id (no slash) gets nothing.

Gemini caches nothing without an explicit breakpoint, so a direct Gemini session re-bills the full system prompt and tool block every single turn. This is the same hole dirge-607 closed on the direct Anthropic path.

opencode misses this too (its applyCaching covers anthropic/openrouter/bedrock/openaiCompatible/copilot/alibaba — no google), so there is no reference implementation to copy.

Needs care: the marker shape and where Gemini accepts it differ from the OpenAI chat shape mark_system_message writes, and dirge addresses Gemini through rig's native Gemini client, not the OpenAI-compatible one. Verify against the Gemini wire format before sending anything — an unrecognized field is a 400, not something ignored.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
Investigated for the v0.21.18 patch — NOT fixable as scoped, deferring.

The issue assumed direct Gemini needed a cache_control-style marker like the OpenRouter google/gemini-* route gets from mark_system_message. It doesn't. Gemini has no per-request cache breakpoint field at all:

- Explicit caching goes through a separate CachedContent RESOURCE: POST to cachedContents to create it, get back a name (cachedContents/abc123), reference that name in the request's cachedContent field, then manage its TTL and delete it. It is a resource lifecycle, not a marker.
- rig 0.41 does not implement it. GenerateContentRequest (providers/gemini/completion.rs:2116) carries 'cachedContent: Optional<String>' as a COMMENTED-OUT placeholder — the field does not exist on the struct. rig only reads cached_content_token_count back off the response (completion.rs:1433).
- Gemini 2.5+ ships implicit caching that is automatic and free, so the direct path is not getting zero benefit today — it just gets no explicit control.

Doing this properly means owning the CachedContent lifecycle: when to create, how to key it to a prefix, TTL, invalidation when the prefix changes, deletion. That is a feature, and guessing at the wire format risks 400ing every Gemini request — the exact failure mode accepts_prompt_cache_key was written to avoid.

Reclassified P3 and left for a feature release. The OpenRouter google/gemini-* route is unaffected and keeps its SystemBlock breakpoint.

title: Library search logic duplicated between build.rs and check.rs
description:
build.rs::find_library_dir and check.rs::check_shared_library are near-copies of the same pkg-config → brew --prefix → fixed-dir-list search, with divergent details (pkg-config name derivation, fallback dir lists, return type). dirge-vij7 is exactly the drift that produced.

check.rs's own doc comment (lines 30-35) notes drift goes invisible here because CI has no macOS runner (dirge-u35k). Hoist the search into one module both consume so there is a single place to fix and a single place to test.

title: build.rs gates linking on libkrunfw, which nothing links against
description:
build.rs requires find_library_dir(libkrunfw) to succeed before emitting -lkrun. But per check.rs:24-35, libkrun carries no LC_RPATH and dlopens libkrunfw by bare versioned name at runtime — the runner references no krunfw_* symbol (the reported link error lists only krun_*). So a machine with libkrun but not libkrunfw cannot link, for no link-time reason.

The two files also disagree on the leaf name: build.rs looks for the unversioned libkrunfw.dylib, check.rs for libkrunfw.5.dylib. That split is actually correct — link-time wants the symlink, runtime dlopen wants the versioned name — but it is undocumented on the build.rs side and reads as drift.

Fix: link on libkrun alone, keep libkrunfw as a warning, and document why the two names differ.

title: No env escape hatch for libkrun in a non-standard prefix
description:
build.rs::find_library_dir searches pkg-config, brew --prefix, then a fixed list (/opt/homebrew/lib, /usr/local/lib, /usr/lib). Anyone with libkrun outside those has no override. Setting PKG_CONFIG_PATH does not help either: build.rs emits no cargo:rerun-if-env-changed, so a changed PKG_CONFIG_PATH does not retrigger detection (compounded by dirge-zsi8).

Fix: honour LIBKRUN_LIB_DIR / LIBKRUNFW_LIB_DIR as a first-priority override, and emit rerun-if-env-changed for those plus PKG_CONFIG_PATH.

title: edit and apply_patch can truncate a file the way write no longer can
description:
dirge-m8d0 stopped 'write' from replacing a file with a fraction of its content. The same destruction is available through edit with a large old_text and a tiny new_text, and through apply_patch with a big deletion hunk — neither is shrink-checked.

Less likely than the write case (an edit has to match existing text exactly, so the model demonstrably read it), which is why it was not in the original fix. But 'demonstrably read it' is not 'meant to delete it'.

write_guard::shrink_verdict is already a pure function over (before, after) text, so wiring it into the edit tools is mostly plumbing. Decide first whether the ratio should differ — a deliberate deletion is far likelier through edit than through write, so the same 50% may be too aggressive there.

title: Revisit the write shrink-guard threshold with benchmark data
description:
The guard (write_guard.rs) refuses when a 30+ line file would keep under half its lines. Both numbers are judgement calls with no data behind them yet.

Known friction: condensing a doc or plan file — a 100-line PLAN.md refined down to 40 — is legitimate and now costs a turn. The refusal names the way through (edit, or remove-then-write), so the model recovers, but it is friction on a real workflow.

Now that benchmarks/polyglot.py exists, this is measurable: run with the guard at several ratios and compare. That is the whole point of having the harness — these thresholds stop being taste.

Also consider whether markdown should be exempt, or whether the ratio should scale with CapabilityTier after all (deliberately not done initially — see the module doc for why).

title: write path guards: reserved device names, root-bare path rewrite, injected-block dedupe
description:
Three small ones from little-coder:

1. Reserved Windows device names (nul, con, prn, aux, com1-9, lpt1-9, extension-insensitive). Writing one creates an undeletable file on Windows and is a near-certain mistake everywhere else.

2. Root-bare path rewrite: /foo.md -> cwd/foo.md. write.rs:89 says 'must be absolute, not relative', which is precisely what induces the failure — the model anchors at / because it was told to be absolute. Genuine system writes always have an intermediate directory.

3. Injected-block dedupe (their makeDedupe): a tail-injected block persists in the conversation, so re-sending a byte-identical block each turn is pure context waste. Applies to exemplar and reminder injections.

title: Compaction: llmtrim kill switch undocumented; no CLI flag
description: [compression].enabled + DIRGE_COMPRESSION already work (client.rs:978) but docs/config.md:236-251 documents only the four sub-flags. Add --no-compression CLI flag + docs + test.

title: loop-ab.sh: consistency summary calls unanimous-flat 'MIXED', and iterates a hardcoded 10 against a split
description:
Two smaller reporting defects in the same awk END block.

(a) loop-ab.sh:841. held = (b == nm) ? 'better in every model' : ((w == nm) ? 'worse in every model' : 'MIXED'). There is no f == nm arm, so a metric that came out FLAT in every model is labelled MIXED — the label for a disagreement. MEASURED on a healthy 2-model fixture: 'turns  better 0, worse 0, flat 2 of 2 models — MIXED'. A unanimous no-effect reads as an inconsistent result, which is the opposite of what it means and the exact reading an A/A calibration is supposed to produce.

(b) loop-ab.sh:836-837. split(...) builds the metric-name list, then 'for (i = 1; i <= 10; i++)' walks it against a hardcoded 10. split() returns the count; nothing checks it. Adding a metric name to the string silently drops it from the summary — same hand-maintained-count class as the rest of this epic.

FIX: add the f == nm arm; iterate to the value split() returned.

title: Add cost_hint to the Tool trait
description:
dirge tools carry no cost annotation, so the budget can only charge after a call returns. The data4sci TypedTool dataclass carries a cost_hint float used for pre-dispatch budget accounting (a cheap lookup is 0.1, an LLM-backed tool is 1.0-2.0).

Small change; mainly useful as an input to dirge-i2st (charge before dispatch, and let a pressured run prefer the cheap tool).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool trait exposes a cost_hint with a sane default so existing tools need no change
- LLM-backed tools (task, websearch, webfetch) annotated above the default
- Budget charges the hint at dispatch time

title: Verification-keyed memory expectations need the verifier status plumbed out of run_loop
description:
dirge-1elu.5 shipped MemoryExpectation with only the CommandRan variant. A VerificationGreen variant was built and then removed before merge because it could not fire: ExpectationSignals.final_verification was hardcoded None at both production call sites (ui/run_handlers/done.rs and context_compacted.rs), since the VerifierGate is a run_loop local and is gone by the time either handler runs. SessionDigest carries commands as bare strings with no exit statuses, so the status is not derivable there either.

Shipping it inert would have been the 'gate that cannot fail' pattern the parent epic exists to remove, so it was dropped rather than left settable-but-dead.

To add it back, the run's final VerificationStatus has to reach the post-session pass. Options considered, neither costed:
- return it from run_agent_loop (currently returns Vec<LoopMessage>; signature change ripples)
- stash it in a process-global the way tools/snapshots.rs and tools/modified.rs already do, with the concurrency caveat those carry

gate_tally already holds the value (final_verification, gate_tally.rs:118) and emits it on the dirge::gates line, so a third option is reading it back from the tally rather than re-deriving it.

Whichever path: from_wire already treats an unknown expectation string as None, so a DB written by a future version that sets verification_green stays inert on an older binary. That property must survive.

title: gate_tally records per-run totals, not gate co-occurrence at a boundary
description:
scripts/loop-ab.sh compares one arm against one control. Nothing measures what happens
when several gates fire in the same run — which is the configuration every real user is
in, and which the paper measured as the place the ceiling lives.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4 §4.4.1, Table 3)

The component ablation swapped ONE evolved layer into the seed at a time, holding the
other three at seed defaults:

  seed                 69.7%   (Easy 87.5 / Med 78.2 / Hard 51.7)
  + memory only        75.3%   (Easy 50.0 / Med 83.6 / Hard 63.3)
  + tool only          73.0%   (Easy 75.0 / Med 87.3 / Hard 46.7)
  + middleware only    71.9%   (Easy 100  / Med 81.8 / Hard 50.0)
  + system_prompt only 67.4%   (Easy 75.0 / Med 78.2 / Hard 46.7)
  AHE full             77.0%   (Easy 100  / Med 88.2 / Hard 53.3)

Two things fall out. The three positive single-component gains sum to +11.1pp; stacked
they deliver +7.3pp. And on Hard tasks the MEMORY-ONLY variant (63.3%) beats full AHE
(53.3%) by a wide margin — adding the other three components made Hard tasks worse.

The paper's diagnosis: "memory, middleware, and the system prompt all push toward the same
closure-style verification, so stacking them spends turns on redundant re-checks within
the long-horizon budget." And on why the loop converged there anyway: "Since the evolve
agent optimises an aggregate dominated by 55 Medium tasks, it converges to a Medium-heavy
trade-off that returns part of the Hard memory effect."

Note also the per-difficulty inversions in that table: memory-only takes Easy from 87.5%
DOWN to 50.0% while taking Hard from 51.7% UP to 63.3%. An aggregate-only comparison
would have reported that component as a clean +5.6pp win and hidden both halves.

## Why this matters for dirge specifically

dirge ships more finalization gates and boundary nudges than AHE ever had: the verifier
gate and its tier escalation, the critic, code review, the goal gate, open issues, the
storm breaker, the failure tracker, safe-state abort, the progress/stall monitor, budget
notices, the file-touch tracker, the exploration-prologue cap. Several of them push toward
the same closure-style re-verification the paper found interfering. This epic adds more.

docs/verification-discipline.md already states the measurement constraint honestly: an A/A
on recon-real produced 18 vs 36 turns on one model and 15 vs 33 on another, so "at n<=3
against a ~2x floor, effects justified by 'this reduces turns' are not measurable at any
sample size worth paying for. Prefer changes whose success criterion is STRUCTURAL — did
the mechanism fire when it should, and stay silent otherwise — because those hold at n=1."

That constraint is not an argument against this issue; it shapes it. The measurable
question is not "does gate X reduce turns" but "do gates X and Y fire on the same
boundary, on the same run, for the same underlying condition."

## dirge status

src/agent/agent_loop/gate_tally.rs already records which finalization gate fired
(GateSource) and which boundary nudges fired (BoundaryNudge), and emits per-run counts on
the `dirge::gates` target. It is pure instrumentation with no control-flow effect. Its
module doc already names two consumers (the A/B harness and the capability estimator).

What it does not record is CO-OCCURRENCE — which gates fired at the same boundary, and in
what order. The counts are per-run totals, so two gates that always fire together and one
that never does are indistinguishable from the aggregate.

## Scope

Make gate interaction visible, then look at what it says. Two parts, in order:

1. Extend the tally to record co-occurrence at a boundary, not just per-run totals. Stay
   observation-only — gate_tally has no control-flow effect and must keep none.
2. Extend scripts/loop-ab.sh to report the co-occurrence, and add a mode that measures
   more than two arms so a "all gates on" configuration can be compared against
   "one gate on" configurations, which is the shape of the paper's Table 3.

Do not act on the results in this issue. Finding that two gates redundantly fire is a
separate decision with its own evidence bar; this issue is about being able to see it at
all. The paper's own loop got this wrong in the other direction — it optimized an
aggregate and silently gave back the Hard-tier gain.

## Acceptance

- A run in which two gates fire at the same boundary produces a tally line that says so,
  distinguishably from the same two gates firing at different boundaries.
- loop-ab.sh reports co-occurrence per arm, and its existing mechanism check still holds:
  "A treatment arm showing zero did not exercise the change, and its deltas are noise."
- Per-model reporting is preserved. The doc is explicit that a single-model result is not
  evidence for a steering change.
- gate_tally still has zero control-flow effect — a test that the loop behaves
  identically with the tally's new fields populated and ignored.

title: Learned memories carry no falsifiable prediction; effectiveness is self-reported
description:
dirge's post-session learning writes memories and skills with no prediction attached and
no measured verification that they helped. The `memory mark success|failure` action exists
but is agent-discretionary self-report, in-band, and nothing forces it to be called.

## Paper evidence (arXiv:2604.25850v4 §3.3, §4.4.2, Appendix D)

Decision observability is AHE's third pillar and the one that keeps the loop from
collapsing into trial-and-error. Every edit ships a manifest entry naming four things:
failure evidence, root cause, targeted fix, and PREDICTED IMPACT (expected fixes plus
at-risk regressions). The next round intersects those predicted sets with the observed
task-level deltas to produce a per-edit verdict, and edits whose predictions do not
materialize get rolled back at file granularity. "Each edit thereby becomes falsifiable by
the next evaluation, which replaces rationale-driven self-justification with a measurable
contract between rounds."

The calibration result is the part to take seriously, and it cuts both ways (§4.4.2):

- FIX predictions are informative. Cross-iteration precision 33.7%, recall 51.4% — about
  5x the random baselines of 6.5% and 10.6%. "each harness edit lands on a real,
  agent-anticipated target rather than on an arbitrary subset of the panel."
- REGRESSION predictions are near-worthless. Precision 11.8%, recall 11.1%, only about 2x
  the random baselines of 5.6% and 5.4%. Appendix D gives the raw counts: across 9 rounds
  the agent issued 43 unique regression predictions and 5 landed, while 40 regressions it
  did not foresee actually occurred.

The paper's own reading: "The agent can justify why an edit should help, but it cannot
reliably name the tasks the same edit is about to break." It names closing this gap as
"the clearest direction for future self-evolution loops."

The design consequence for dirge is specific: ASK for the fix prediction and act on it.
Do NOT ask a model to predict what its learned memory will break and then trust the
answer — that number is barely above chance, and treating it as a safety signal would be
worse than having none.

## dirge status

The substrate is all there and unconnected:
- src/agent/review.rs — background review at session end, writes memories + skills
- src/agent/post_session.rs — the ordered orchestrator around it
- src/agent/session_digest.rs — deterministic ground truth (files touched, commands run,
  where we stopped) with no model call
- src/extras/memory_db.rs:211 `effectiveness_bonus(kind, success_count, failure_count)`,
  procedural-only, signed and bounded, already feeding salience at :740
- src/agent/tools/memory.rs:86 the `mark` action

The missing piece is the contract. A procedural memory today asserts a rule; it does not
state what it expects to change, so nothing can ever falsify it. `effectiveness_bonus`
reads counters that only move when the agent volunteers a `mark`.

## Scope

When post-session review writes a PROCEDURAL memory, have it also record a falsifiable
trigger: the observable condition under which the memory should have applied. Later
sessions that meet the trigger settle it against measured signal rather than self-report.

The measured signal already exists per-run: src/agent/agent_loop/gate_tally.rs emits gate
and nudge counts plus capability signals on the `dirge::gates` target, and
scripts/loop-ab.sh already scrapes exactly that line.

Deliberately out of scope: asking for a regression prediction. See the calibration data
above.

Start narrow. This is the least-proven item in the epic and the one whose blast radius
touches persisted user state, so prefer a shape that is inert when the trigger never
fires and that cannot corrupt existing memories.

## Acceptance

- A memory written with a trigger, a later session meeting that trigger, and the
  effectiveness counter moving WITHOUT an agent-issued `mark`. This is the whole point;
  if the counter only moves on self-report, nothing changed.
- A test that a memory whose trigger never fires is left exactly as it was — no decay, no
  phantom failure. Inert by default.
- Existing memories with no trigger keep working unchanged (migration safety).
- Per docs/verification-discipline.md "Signal never fed": the test must drive the
  PRODUCTION path that records the outcome, not call the recorder directly. That row
  exists because a counter with zero production callers passed its unit test while being
  structurally always 0.

title: nREPL plugin: babashka users can't auto-connect (bb prints the port, never writes .nrepl-port)
description:
Found while fixing dirge-hli5. .nrepl-port is the plugin's only port-discovery mechanism. clojure -M:nrepl and lein repl :headless write it; 'bb nrepl-server' does NOT — it prints 'Started nREPL server at 127.0.0.1:<port>' to stdout and writes nothing. Verified locally with bb 1.x.

So babashka users get no auto-connect and must call nrepl_connect with an explicit port (which does work). Not a regression — the plugin never supported bb — and the README comparison table already says 'Port discovery: .nrepl-port only'.

Options: lsof fallback (what clojure-mcp-light does), or parse a known server log. Neither is obviously right; needs a decision.

title: [bug] Relay tests write ~126KB of debris into the real ~/.dirge/transient
description:

title: check_microvm_includes_kvm_check fails on macOS: expects libkrunfw.dylib, gets libkrunfw.5.dylib
description:
src/sandbox/check.rs:490. Fails on macOS under --all-features on clean main (verified by stashing unrelated changes and re-running):

    should include libkrunfw.dylib check, got: ["Hypervisor.framework",
    "libkrun.dylib", "libkrunfw.5.dylib", "gzip", "tar", "ssh-keygen",
    "dirge-microvm-runner", ...]

The test looks for an unversioned 'libkrunfw.dylib' entry; the code emits the versioned 'libkrunfw.5.dylib'. Either the check list or the assertion drifted -- worth deciding which is correct rather than just relaxing the assertion, since the string is what a user is told to install.

sandbox::microvm::tests::integration::dyld_fallback_library_path_valid_on_macos fails in the same run and is probably the same drift.

NOT caught by CI because the all-features job runs on ubuntu; see dirge-u35k (no macOS CI coverage). So this is invisible to the gate and only shows up when someone runs the suite locally on a Mac -- which means it reads as 'the suite is red' to anyone doing that, and trains them to ignore it.

Found incidentally while fixing dirge-h3dw; unrelated to that work and not folded in.
close_reason:
Landed on branch z85a-failure-threshold-per-poll (1138e13f). The issue guessed the second failure was 'probably the same drift' -- it isn't, they have different causes and needed different fixes.

FAILURE 1 (check_microvm_includes_kvm_check) -- real drift, and the CODE was right. check.rs:142 deliberately emits the versioned libkrunfw.5.dylib, with a comment saying why: libkrun carries no LC_RPATH and dlopens libkrunfw by bare versioned name at runtime, so the unversioned libkrunfw.dylib symlink is never consulted by the loader and can exist on a machine where the dlopen still fails. Checking for it would report OK on a broken install. The test's assertion had drifted to the unversioned name.

Answering the issue's 'decide which is correct rather than just relax the assertion': the check is correct, the assertion was wrong. But the real cause is that the string was spelled out in FOUR places (check.rs:143, microvm/mod.rs:322, microvm/tests.rs:2027, and the wrong one in check.rs:486), so it is now a single LIBKRUNFW_LIB const (plus LIBKRUN_LIB) that all four read. Both are gated on sandbox-microvm, or they are dead_code under default features and -D warnings fails the default build.

De-duplication alone would make the decision unfalsifiable -- with one const feeding both the check and its assertion, changing it to the unversioned name moves the test with it and nothing objects. So there is also a separate macOS-only test pinning LIBKRUNFW_LIB == 'libkrunfw.5.dylib' with the reason.

FAILURE 2 (dyld_fallback_library_path_valid_on_macos) -- NOT drift. It hard-fails whenever libkrunfw is not installed, which is any Mac that has not run 'brew install libkrun libkrunfw'. That is the 'trains them to ignore red' half of this issue, and it is an environment prerequisite, not a code defect.

What the test actually guards is our brew-prefix RESOLUTION, using the installed library as the oracle: formula installed but not found under any prefix we resolve => resolution broken => fail. Formula absent => nothing to resolve to => skip, matching the ~20 sibling tests in that file that skip on missing virtualization or PTY allocation.

The precondition asks brew directly ('brew list --formula libkrunfw') rather than looking for the file under a prefix WE resolved. Using our own resolution would make the skip condition identical to the assertion, turning the guard vacuous instead of red -- the FM-3 shape from dirge-5mtx.6.

Verified: macOS 'cargo test --bin dirge --all-features' is now 5158 passed / 0 failed, first time green on this machine. Confirmed with --nocapture that the dyld test SKIPS with its message rather than vacuously passing (libkrunfw is genuinely not installed here). All four clippy configs clean, fmt clean, default suite 4866 passed.

Does not close dirge-u35k (no macOS CI coverage) -- that is still the reason this class of drift is invisible to the gate.

title: FailureTracker threshold is fixed at construction, so it can never adapt
description:
FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESHOLD (run.rs:275, value 3) is consumed exactly once, at FailureTracker::new(FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESHOLD) (run.rs:2053), which runs at run start. At that point the capability estimator is always Nominal by warm-up (MIN_CALLS_FOR_ESTIMATE = 5 tool calls), so deriving the threshold at the construction site is inert by construction -- it would read the neutral tier every time.

This matters because FAILURE_REFLECTION_THRESHOLD is the single BEST-MATCHED candidate for capability derivation in the whole audit (see dirge-5mtx.7). The estimator is literally built from failure counts and streaks, and this guard fires on consecutive errored results -- signal and trigger are the same thing, which is the test the audit says a derivation must pass. Every other movable constant fails that test.

## Change

FailureTracker needs its threshold to be re-readable per turn rather than baked in at construction: either a set_threshold(u32), or have poll/record take the effective threshold as an argument (mirroring how should_nudge_fast_verify takes the tier). Prefer the argument form -- it keeps the tracker stateless about policy and matches the pattern already used for the tier-derived nudge.

Then derive it: Struggling -> reflect after 1 consecutive failure instead of 3. Strong and Nominal stay at 3, per the one-directional policy (the tier may add support, never remove it).

## Acceptance

- The effective threshold is read per evaluation, not at construction, with a test that changes tier mid-run and observes the guard firing earlier.
- Nominal and Strong remain bit-identical to today.
- No A/B claim. Per dirge-5mtx.6 FM-5 the ~2x noise floor makes this unmeasurable; it ships on the structural argument that signal and trigger match, or not at all.
notes: Found while auditing dirge-5mtx.7 rather than from a failure. Low priority: it only affects Struggling, which is rare (1 of 6 runs at the supported low bound) and n=1.
close_reason:
Landed on branch z85a-failure-threshold-per-poll (adef66e1).

poll_reflection now takes the tier and derives its threshold per evaluation via CapabilityTier::scale_threshold, mirroring should_nudge_fast_verify. The tracker keeps the base constant; the caller supplies the observed tier.

Deviation from the issue text: Struggling gets 2, not 1. scale_threshold is 2/3, so 3 -> 2, and a threshold of 1 would violate the tracker's own '>= 2' construction invariant and fire the checkpoint on the first errored call -- which contradicts the module's premise (repeated, DISTINCT failures). The derived value is floored at MIN_EFFECTIVE_THRESHOLD = 2 so a future smaller base can't produce it either.

Two things deliberately left on the base threshold, both inside the same tracker:
  - the permission checkpoint (dirge-iwwq). A denial streak is a policy wall; nothing in CapabilityCounters measures how often the user's rules block a call, so the tier has no standing to pull it forward.
  - safe_state_due's 2x signal. That rung spends one of two hard-capped aborts per run and, in auto mode, restores files on the tree. Firing it sooner is not 'adding support' in the one-directional sense, and there is no evidence for it.

Acceptance:
  - threshold read per poll, with tier_flip_mid_streak_moves_the_guard_both_ways changing tier mid-streak and observing the guard move in BOTH directions (fires at 2 under Struggling; re-arm reverts to the base interval when it flips back)
  - nominal_and_strong_are_bit_identical pins the no-op property
  - no A/B claim, per dirge-5mtx.6 FM-5

Verified red-then-green: neutering effective_threshold to ignore the tier fails exactly the three tier tests, the other 26 pass. Full gate green -- 4866 passed, RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo clippy --all-targets clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean.

docs/verification-discipline.md now carries the table of what the tier actually derives (two thresholds) and what it deliberately doesn't.

title: clippy -D warnings fails under --all-features and --features dap
description:

Measured 2026-08-01: 'RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets' exits 101 with 17 findings, mostly collapsible_if:

  6  src/agent/tools/debug.rs
  3  src/ui/run_handlers/done.rs

Same shape as dirge-xw43 (sandbox-microvm, 50 findings): an ungated feature combination accumulates lint debt silently. The fix is both halves — clear the findings AND add the config to the clippy job, since clearing without gating just restarts the clock.

Found while landing dirge-5mtx; not caused by it (all 8 files are untouched by that work). Filed rather than folded in to keep an unrelated 8-file diff out of PR #739.
notes: Check whether --features dap is also dirty before deciding the job layout; the clippy job already runs three configs sequentially and a fourth/fifth adds CI time. May be worth one --all-features pass instead of per-feature ones.
close_reason:
Landed on branch z85a-failure-threshold-per-poll (d2b74019). Both halves done, per the issue.

All 17 findings cleared across the 8 files listed. The collapsible_if ones became let-chains (edition 2024), which is how the loop code already reads -- run.rs:1966 was already written that way. Two needed hand fixes: graph.rs:229 took &PathBuf where &Path does (deref coercion means no caller changed), and entity_compress.rs:587 indexed 'kinds' by a loop counter that existed only to index it.

Job layout, answering the NOTES question: --features dap alone is CLEAN once the all-features findings are fixed, so no separate dap step is warranted. Added ONE '--all-features --all-targets' step instead of per-feature ones -- it subsumes dap, plugin, semantic and the rest for one config's worth of CI time.

Kept the three existing narrower configs rather than replacing them with --all-features. --all-features cannot reach a cfg(not(feature = ...)) path, and windows-default is subtractive (--no-default-features), not additive, so it is not a subset of anything --all-features compiles. Dropping them would lose the coverage dirge-xw43 added.

Verified all four configs clean: default, windows-default, sandbox-microvm, all-features. cargo fmt --all --check clean.

Tests: default suite 4866 passed. The --all-features suite is the one that actually exercises the changed dap/plugin/graph code -- 5155 passed, 2 failed, and both failures are the known macOS sandbox drift in dirge-jbhz (check_microvm_includes_kvm_check, dyld_fallback_library_path_valid_on_macos), in files this change does not touch.

title: State-derived gate preconditions; unify the nine gate budgets
description:
The largest and last child. Mostly refactoring; the behavioural win is that
several hand-tuned budgets stop being load-bearing.

Paper §A.2 (implicit sequence): attach a readiness PRECONDITION to each step and
re-evaluate every tick. In a static world it behaves identically to a fixed
sequence; in a changing one it's reactive and self-recovering, because a step
whose precondition stopped holding simply doesn't fire.

dirge's gate predicates evaluate over `new_messages`, which ACCUMULATES across
re-entries. So a condition that was true once stays true forever, and each gate
needs a counter to stop it re-firing. The code diagnoses this itself at
run.rs:795-800:

  "`new_messages` accumulates across re-entries, so the triggering
   `write_todo_list` call stays in the list and the condition would hold on
   every later pass. A behavioral nudge that didn't land the first time doesn't
   land on the third identical repeat — it just spends round-trips."

The compensating counters, all separate, all hand-tuned, all threaded through
`poll_finalization_follow_up`'s argument list (run.rs:536-561 — nine `&mut`
counters, already `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`):

  critic_done, code_review_reacts, goal_reacts, todo_nudges, resume_nudges,
  open_issues_nudges, track_nudges, verify_nudges, plus the verifier's own
  internal one-shot and `last_reviewed_fingerprint` / `last_review_findings`.

Same root cause produces the documented priority inversion at run.rs:528-532:
"a red build surfaces the verifier nudge now and the critic runs at the *next*
finalization once the build is fixed (the verifier won't fire twice)". That's a
one-shot budget standing in for reactive re-evaluation.

And it produces two already-filed bugs, both of which .5 should fix or close:
  - dirge-q7vw: a judge ERROR records `last_reviewed_fingerprint`, so the retry
    is suppressed and the diff never gets reviewed.
  - dirge-mu46: the dedup skip keys on the diff fingerprint but also skips
    transcript-based completeness re-judgment.

## Change

1. Evaluate gate predicates over the DELTA since the last finalization, not the
   whole accumulated `new_messages`. Most gates want "did this happen since I
   last looked", which is what a precondition means.
2. Introduce one `GateBudget { max: u8, spent: u8 }` (or a small `GateState`
   holding budget + per-gate memo) and a single `GateStates` struct replacing
   the nine `&mut` parameters. Collapses the argument list and puts every
   lifecycle in one place.
3. With state-derived predicates, relax the budgets that only existed to
   compensate. Some are genuine cost ceilings and MUST stay — MAX_GOAL_REACT
   and MAX_REVIEW_REACT bound LLM calls, MAX_TURNS bounds spend. Distinguish
   the two kinds explicitly in the type: a cost ceiling vs a re-fire guard.
   Getting this wrong in the unsafe direction means an unbounded loop, so a
   budget stays unless the precondition demonstrably subsumes it.

## Risk

Highest-risk child in the epic; it touches every gate's lifecycle. Land it last,
behind the A/B harness, and expect to keep more budgets than the theory says are
needed. "Refactored into one place" is a real win on its own even if few budgets
actually relax.

## Acceptance

- `poll_finalization_follow_up` takes one state struct, not nine `&mut u8`s;
  the `too_many_arguments` allow comes off.
- dirge-q7vw and dirge-mu46 have failing tests first, then pass.
- Every existing gate test passes unchanged — this must be behaviour-preserving
  except where a linked bug says otherwise.
- Each budget is documented as cost-ceiling or re-fire-guard, and every relaxed
  budget has a test showing the precondition now stops the re-fire.
- A/B (.1 harness): all scenarios show no regression. This child is not expected
  to improve the numbers; if it moves them, something changed that shouldn't
  have.
close_reason:
Refactor landed (a6573055). poll_finalization_follow_up now takes &mut GateStates + GateInputs instead of 17 positional args; the too_many_arguments allow is off. Behaviour-preserving: both structs are destructured at the top of the fn so gate bodies are byte-identical, and the 30 existing gate tests pass with no assertion changes (only building a GateStates instead of loose locals). Full gate green: fmt --all --check 0, clippy -D warnings 0, 4852 tests.

The tractable order recorded on the previous attempt turned out to be unnecessary — the destructure trick meant the fn body never changed, so the only work was the 30 call sites, done with a transformer written to ABORT on any shape it did not fully recognize rather than guess. It aborted twice (once on a real parser bug of mine, once correctly flagging that tests seed non-default values like todo_nudges=MAX_TODO_NUDGES that a lenient transform would have silently dropped). That refusal is why this attempt landed and the last one did not.

Acceptance: one state struct + allow removed DONE; q7vw and mu46 fixed earlier (be8738be); existing gate tests pass unchanged DONE; every gate budget documented cost-ceiling vs re-fire-guard on GateStates DONE. Budget relaxation and delta-based predicates stay DROPPED per the descope. The broader constant taxonomy (MAX_RULES_CHARS, MAX_DIFF_BYTES, MAX_SCAVENGE_INPUT, context_manager fold fractions) belongs to dirge-5mtx.7.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text: REVISED by dirge-5mtx.7. Unifying the nine budgets into one struct is still the refactor, but the budgets should end up DERIVED from the capability estimate rather than being constants in a tidier container. Also: this issue must draw the line between capability-tuned thresholds (adaptive) and true invariants that stay fixed — context_manager fold fractions are memory pressure, MAX_RULES_CHARS / MAX_DIFF_BYTES are token budgets, MAX_SCAVENGE_INPUT is a DoS bound. Right now both kinds of constant sit side by side looking identical, which is half of why this is confusing to change.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
DESCOPED on the evidence.

Original premise: with state-derived preconditions, most of the nine hand-tuned budgets could be relaxed because the precondition would stop the re-fire on its own. That claim cannot be verified. Run-to-run variance on the recon-real scenario is ~2x on turns and tool calls (dirge-5mtx.6, FM-5), so 'this budget can be relaxed without hurting anything' is exactly the kind of statement our A/B cannot distinguish from noise at any sample size we can afford — provider spend is the binding constraint.

Also, the empirical work found no benefit to point at. Every failure this epic surfaced was a VERIFICATION failure, not a steering one; nothing suggested the budgets were mis-set.

REMAINING SCOPE (pure refactor, no behavioural claim):
  - collapse the nine &mut counters threaded through poll_finalization_follow_up into one GateStates struct, and drop the too_many_arguments allow
  - fix the two linked lifecycle bugs, dirge-q7vw and dirge-mu46, each with a failing test first
  - document every constant as cost-ceiling vs re-fire-guard (dirge-5mtx.7 needs that line drawn anyway)

DROPPED:
  - relaxing any budget
  - evaluating predicates over the delta since last finalization, which was only worth doing to enable the relaxation

Priority drops to P3: it is tidying with two small bug fixes attached, not a behavioural improvement.

comments.author: Yogthos
comments.text:
Attempted the GateStates collapse and REVERTED it.

The struct itself was fine — nine &mut params into one place, with the cost-ceiling vs re-fire-guard distinction documented per field. Production code compiled cleanly. What killed it was the 30 test call sites: they pass a mix of named locals and inline `&mut 0u8` defaults and then assert on those locals afterwards, so collapsing the signature means rewriting each site to build a GateStates, call, and copy values back out. My mechanical transformer got most of them and mangled the rest.

Judgement: not worth it. This is tidying with no behavioural claim (already descoped for that reason), and pushing a fragile 30-site rewrite through at the end of a long session risks breaking real coverage for zero user-visible gain. The two bugs attached to this issue — dirge-q7vw and dirge-mu46 — were the valuable part and are fixed and committed (be8738be).

If it gets picked up later, the tractable order is: add GateStates and a `from_legacy`-style test helper FIRST so existing sites keep compiling, migrate sites in small batches with the suite green between each, then delete the helper. Doing the signature and the sites in one pass is what made it fragile.

title: [bug] cargo check --no-default-features fails: task.rs references git_worktree unconditionally
description:
Pre-existing on main (verified against origin/main in a clean worktree), not a regression from the RAX branch.

src/agent/tools/task.rs:77 calls crate::extras::git_worktree::repo_is_dirty unconditionally, but the module is behind the git-worktree feature. So:

  cargo check --no-default-features
  error[E0433]: cannot find `git_worktree` in `extras`

Not covered by CI — the matrix is acp / all-features / dap / default / loop+git-worktree / lsp / mcp / plugin / sandbox-microvm / semantic-bash / windows-default, none of which is bare --no-default-features. Release artifacts build with default features, so shipped binaries are unaffected.

Fix is presumably a cfg gate on the call site (or on the containing fn) with a no-op fallback when git-worktree is off. Worth deciding whether --no-default-features is a supported configuration at all; if it is, it should be in the CI matrix so this can't regress again.

title: llmtrim capability: 191 of 299 model_context entries are unreachable (prefix stripped from query but kept in key)
description:
capability::context_window_for (src/llmtrim/capability.rs:156) normalizes the QUERY by dropping a 'provider/' prefix:

    let id = model_id.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let id = id.split_once('/').map_or(id.as_str(), |(_, rest)| rest);
    CONTEXT.get(id).copied()
